10.1126/science.adq6530.title: Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe 2 /WS 2 moiré superlattices
10.1126/science.adq6530.abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal-dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

10.1126/science.ady7647.title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
10.1126/science.ady7647.abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane-localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.
authors: Keyi Huang, Jingni Wu, Yu Cao, Yingying Cao, Zhongji Pu, Aoshen Xu, Wenzhao Wang, Xue Zhou, Ming Li, Min Zhang, Yuhua Wang, Jinbiao Ma, Yulin Du, Qin Wang, Yingqiao Wan, Shangyu Gao, Dacheng Wang, Guangzheng Sun, Qin Gu, Huan Chen, Guosheng Xiong, Heng Yin, Yiwen Deng, Wensheng Zhao, Zhengguang Zhang, Shengben Li, Xiquan Gao, Sun Tae Kim, Gang Li, Baolei Jia, Jijie Chai, Kenichi Tsuda, Zheng Qing Fu, Yiming Wang

10.1126/science.adz4903.title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
10.1126/science.adz4903.abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA-chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA-DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.
authors: Lu Han, Yuxiang Yuan, Yujie Liu, Yan Li, Yijun Qi

10.1126/science.adz5323.title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
10.1126/science.adz5323.abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.
authors: Yuan Zhang, Yanhe Liu, Yachuang Hu, Zhenkun Zhang, Jie Du, Lele Cui, Qi Liu, Lin Zhong, Yu Xin, Ruiming Chai, Li Deng, Jingwei Pan, Jackie Schiller, Ning-long Xu

10.1126/science.aee0658.title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
10.1126/science.aee0658.abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.
authors: Caroline Needell, Catherine C. Walker, Jeremy N. Bassis

10.1126/science.aeh1409.title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
10.1126/science.aeh1409.abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel-based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect-confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.
authors: Andreas Bezold, Manuel Köbrich, Jan Vollhüter, Longsheng Feng, Lukas Amon, Nicolas Karpstein, Yunzhi Wang, Erdmann Spiecker, Mathias Göken, Michael J. Mills, Steffen Neumeier

10.1126/science.aeh4273.title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
10.1126/science.aeh4273.abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.
authors: Dian Tan, Guixu Xie, Libo Zhang, Yang Xu, Chilong Liu, Haolan Yuan, Zhihua Chen, Chang-Kang Hu, J. Q. You, Song Liu, Eric Lutz, Tobias J. Kippenberg, Dapeng Yu

10.1126/science.aeh6251.title: Stereoselective polysubstituted bicyclo[1.1.0]butane synthesis by rhodium-catalyzed kinetic resolution
10.1126/science.aeh6251.abstract: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) are a distinctive class of strained small-ring carbocycles of growing importance in synthetic and medicinal chemistry. However, the enantioselective synthesis of polysubstituted BCBs remains a largely unsolved challenge. In this study, we report a general chemical platform for the stereoselective assembly of chiral or meso 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted BCBs from internal alkynes and carbenes through stepwise [2+1+1’] or one-pot [2+1+1] cycloaddition reactions, respectively. Successful execution of these transformations exploits the combination of triftosylhydrazones (carbene precursors) and chiral dirhodium catalysts. The sterically hindered catalyst Rh 2 ( R -3,5- di PheTPCP) 4 features a confined chiral microenvironment that enables exquisite discrimination between cyclopropene enantiomers, affording highly enantioenriched polysubstituted BCBs through kinetic resolution upon reaction with chiral rhodium carbenes. This chemistry operates under mild reaction conditions, uses readily available starting materials, and exhibits broad substrate scope.
authors: Xiaolong Zhang, Rongkai Wu, Zhaohong Liu, Ge Yin, Jiaqi Tang, Paramasivam Sivaguru, Xin Hong, Edward A. Anderson, Xihe Bi

10.1126/science.aei2693.title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
10.1126/science.aei2693.abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide-semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.
authors: Seok Young Min, Hyunje Cho, Suk-Ho Lee, Jaeho Choi, Taeho Kim, Jong Yun Choi, Heewon Park, Junsoo Yoon, TaeJoon Mo, Chumki Nayak, Gi-Yeop Kim, Sung-Hyuk Her, Chul-Ho Lee, Yong-Sung Kim, Si-Young Choi, Cheol-Joo Kim, Moon-Ho Jo

10.1126/science.aei5957.title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia
10.1126/science.aei5957.abstract: The ciliary transition zone (TZ) regulates ciliary proteome composition, yet its molecular architecture, protein content, and contribution to motile ciliopathies remain poorly defined. We applied in situ cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to human multiciliated epithelial cells. This approach resolved TZ-specific doublet microtubules at subnanometer resolution and identified nine constituent proteins. We found that epithelial cell transforming 2 like (ECT2L) and double zinc ribbon and ankyrin repeat-containing protein 1 (DZANK1) form the major linker complexes between adjacent TZ doublet microtubules. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia. ECT2L and DZANK1 deficiency disrupted TZ architecture, caused microtubular abnormalities and abnormal bulbous ciliary tips, and impaired mucociliary clearance. These findings establish a direct genetic link between TZ defects and human motile ciliopathy and illustrate how in situ structural biology can uncover mechanisms of human disease.

10.1126/science.adt1928.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
10.1126/science.adt1928.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type-specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)-signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.
authors: Sonja D. C. Weterings, Hiromune Eto, Jan-Daniël de Leede-Scheven, Amir Giladi, Jooske L. Monster, Mirjam E. Hoekstra, Wouter F. Beijk, Esther J. M. Liefting, Karen B. van den Anker, Jacco van Rheenen, Alexander van Oudenaarden, Katharina F. Sonnen

10.1126/science.adz4600.title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
10.1126/science.adz4600.abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

10.1126/science.aee6550.title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
10.1126/science.aee6550.abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

10.1126/science.aeh4015.title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
10.1126/science.aeh4015.abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

10.1126/science.aen0122.abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability-it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.

10.1126/science.aei0498.title: A noncontiguous code for RNA-guided DNA recognition at the origin of CRISPR-Cas
10.1126/science.aei0498.abstract: CRISPR-Cas provides RNA-mediated adaptive immunity, but how its first RNA-guided effector arose is unclear. In this study, we report the discovery of Viral Interference Programmable Repeat (VIPR) systems consisting of a Vipr protein ancestral to the earliest CRISPR-Cas effectors and VIPR RNAs (vrRNAs) comprising alternating GGY/NN motifs. Unlike canonical guide RNAs that pair with target nucleic acids through contiguous complementarity, vrRNAs recognize double-stranded DNA through a noncontiguous code in which the variable NN dinucleotides collectively specify a gapped target sequence. Natural vrRNA targets suggest that VIPR systems act against competing phages, and we demonstrate programmable phage defense by redirecting the complex for transcriptional repression. These results suggest that adaptive immunity originated from ancient warfare between viruses, revealing a previously unidentified logic for encoding information in sequence.

10.1126/science.adv5441.title: The climate benefits of retiring a fully operational internal combustion engine vehicle
10.1126/science.adv5441.abstract: Internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles represent the single largest source of carbon dioxide emissions for most US households. Although battery electric vehicles (BEVs) considerably reduce use-phase emissions, the transition poses a fundamental life cycle optimization challenge: Is there a net climate benefit to retiring a functional ICE vehicle before its end of life? Retiring a functioning ICE vehicle incurs a fundamental trade-off between BEV manufacturing emissions and decreased vehicle operation emissions. In this study, we evaluated this trade-off across a comprehensive range of retirement scenarios and found that scrappage-and-replacement yields consistent emissions reductions across most contexts, including the retirement of new ICE vehicles. Although scrapping a functional asset remains economically prohibitive under current market conditions, these results demonstrate a major mitigation potential for policy interventions, such as enhanced scrappage subsidies, to address the emissions of an increasingly durable ICE fleet.

10.1126/science.aeh2982.title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
10.1126/science.aeh2982.abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

10.1126/science.aee7961.title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
10.1126/science.aee7961.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

10.1126/science.aeb0054.title: Nonviral delivery of chemically modified tRNA rescues nonsense mutations in cystic fibrosis
10.1126/science.aeb0054.abstract: Suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can rescue disease-causing nonsense mutations by promoting readthrough of premature termination codons (PTCs). Their clinical translation is limited by suboptimal activity and inefficient in vivo delivery. In this work, we combined site-specific chemical modification of sup-tRNAs with cargo-tailored pulmonary lipid nanoparticle (LNP) engineering to overcome these barriers. Incorporation of N 1 -methyladenosine in sup-tRNAs improved PTC readthrough, enhanced tRNA aminoacylation, prolonged functional persistence, and reduced innate immune activation. High-throughput ionizable lipid screening and formulation optimization identified a sup-tRNA-tailored LNP that efficiently delivered chemically modified sup-tRNAs to the lung. This approach restored cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) expression and function in bronchial epithelial cells, mouse models, and patient-derived organoids. Thus, LNP-delivered, chemically engineered sup-tRNAs represent a potential therapeutic platform for treating nonsense mutations.

10.1126/science.aed2974.title: Rising plant extinction rates on European mountain summits
10.1126/science.aed2974.abstract: Climate change increases plant species richness in alpine ecosystems. However, to what extent this diversity enrichment masks extinction dynamics of resident species remains elusive. In this study, we used floristic resurvey data from 896 permanent vegetation plots across 62 European mountain summits to show that local extinctions have increased over the past 21 years. Extinction rates rose with the magnitude of warming, and species were more likely to go extinct toward their low-elevation range margins and in communities undergoing stronger thermophilization. Moreover, local extinctions were significantly related to preceding abundance declines, which can serve as an early warning signal. These findings suggest that despite increasing plant species richness, plant assemblages above the treeline face an accelerating but so far neglected loss of their most characteristic species.

10.1126/science.adq0420.title: Room-temperature multiferroicity in all-van der Waals heterostructures
10.1126/science.adq0420.abstract: Multiferroics host simultaneous and coupled ferroic orders, allowing disparate external stimuli to induce abrupt transformations in their structures and properties. Creating multiferroicity in two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) platforms would add the elements of strong quantum confinement, enhanced quasiparticle excitations, and wide tunability to the capabilities of these systems. In this work, we constructed vdW heterostructures of ferromagnetic triiron gallium ditelluride (Fe 3 GaTe 2 ) and ferroelectric copper indium thiophosphate (CuInP 2 S 6 ) to integrate their respective orders. We observed strong interferroic coupling at room temperature by demonstrating ferroelectrically reconfigurable magnetic anisotropy of 2D Fe 3 GaTe 2 . The interferroic magnetoelectricity diminished with increasing Fe 3 GaTe 2 thickness, revealing the interfacial nature of heterostructure multiferroicity. Our discovery of all-vdW heterostructure multiferroicity opens the door to the artificial assembly of vdW layers for designer 2D multiferroics.

10.1126/science.ady5180.title: Thalamic NRXN1-mediated input to human cortical progenitors drives excitatory neurogenesis
10.1126/science.ady5180.abstract: The human cerebral cortex develops through coordinated signals from within the cortex and from other brain regions, including the thalamus. However, how thalamic neuronal projections influence early human cortical development remains less well-understood. In this study, we fused cortical and thalamic organoids to investigate how thalamic input shapes the maturation of human cortical cells. Using single-nuclei RNA-sequencing and cellular imaging, we found that thalamic input increases the production of cortical excitatory neurons. We identify neurexin-1 (NRXN1) as a mediator of physical contact between thalamic axons and cortical outer radial glia. Genetic knockout of thalamic NRXN1 reduced these contacts and attenuated the production of upper-layer excitatory neurons. These findings reveal a mechanism by which thalamic input regulates human cortical progenitors and shapes excitatory neuron production during development.

10.1126/science.adx1707.title: Levitated sensor for magnetometry in ambient environment
10.1126/science.adx1707.abstract: Levitated particle systems have gained attention as a rapidly advancing platform for precision sensing, offering low-loss, highly isolated environments by eliminating mechanical contact and associated noise. Current room-temperature levitation techniques are primarily sensitive to acceleration, and it remains challenging to integrate them with high-sensitivity magnetic sensing. In this work, we demonstrate a diamagnetically stabilized magnetically levitated magnet magnetometer, where the motion of the magnet is detected optically. We achieved a sensitivity of 32 femtoteslas per square root of Hertz, which is adequate for a wide range of applications in biology, chemistry, and fundamental physics, matching the performance of superconducting quantum interference devices and atomic magnetometers, while offering the advantage of operating at room temperature and under Earth’s magnetic field.

10.1126/science.aea4287.title: Lean adipocyte oxylipin signaling restrains breast cancer through ferroptosis
10.1126/science.aea4287.abstract: Obesity increases breast cancer risk and tumor aggressiveness, yet the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. In this work, we identify a tumor-suppressive lipid signaling pathway in which mammary adipocytes secrete the oxylipin 9S-hydroxyoctadecadienoic acid (9S-HODE). 9S-HODE induces ferroptosis in breast cancer cells by disrupting iron homeostasis. Adipocytes in obese mammary tissue produce less 9S-HODE, and tumors in obese mice exhibit reduced ferroptosis. Accordingly, ferroptosis inhibition accelerates tumor growth in lean mice, and restoring 9S-HODE suppresses tumor growth in obese mice. In humans, mammary 9S-HODE content is inversely correlated with body mass index, and 9S-HODE inhibits patient-derived breast cancer organoid growth. These findings identify the loss of adipocyte-derived 9S-HODE as a mechanism by which obesity promotes breast cancer and suggest that the restoration of ferroptosis-inducing lipid signaling may be a therapeutic strategy.

10.1126/science.adx6059.title: Tunnel field-effect transistors exhibiting performance beyond the Boltzmann thermionic limit
10.1126/science.adx6059.abstract: The International Roadmap for Devices and Systems (IRDS) has identified the tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) as the most promising next-generation logic device that enables sustainable downscaling in driving voltage and power consumption. Demonstrating an acceptable sub-Boltzmann-limit ON current (namely I 60 , the current level when a TFET switches to a subthreshold swing level of 60 millivolts per decade) and current-switching ratio has presented a formidable challenge. We report a TFET based on a bismuth/indium selenide (Bi/InSe) heterostructure that exhibits an I 60 of up to ~10 microamperes per micrometer and a current-switching ratio of >10 7 . We attribute such promising TFETs to precise material design, clean interfaces fabricated under vacuum, and band engineering based on subthreshold swing physics. Our results demonstrate a high-performance basic building block that meets the IRDS requirements for next-generation integrated circuits.

10.1126/science.adx7367.title: Calcium tunes snail mucus-based materials to multiple functions
10.1126/science.adx7367.abstract: Mucus is known as a viscous fluid; yet, snails manufacture various mucus-based materials with much higher cohesion and tailored to different and even antagonistic functions, including lubrication, adhesion, protection, and defense. To gain insight into this versatility, we use a multidisciplinary approach to investigate five different mucus-based materials produced by the snail Cepaea nemoralis . Our results demonstrate that snails use collagen VI as a main structural component and add amorphous calcium carbonate (ACC) during mucus secretion. ACC functions as an ion source in wet mucus types, most likely for cross-linking, or as a mineral precursor in dry mucus types. These findings shed light on the versatility of these viscoelastic materials, which are able to switch between very different properties on the basis of calcium and protein content.

10.1126/science.aea7605.title: Chemovaccination with a late-liver-stage antimalarial induces durable immunity against malaria
10.1126/science.aea7605.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum sporozoite vaccines, in which parasites are attenuated at the liver stage, provide high efficacy but require complex manufacture and intravenous administration of high sporozoite doses. We found that a single low-dose P. berghei sporozoite exposure (intravenous or mosquito bite) and treatment with a plasmepsin IX and X (PMIX/X) inhibitor, either WM382 or MK-7602, that produced “chemo-attenuated liver merozoites” (CALM) induced sterile immunity in mice for up to 21 months. Protection involved anti-circumsporozoite protein (CSP) antibodies and CD8 + T cells, including liver-resident memory subsets that recognized diverse antigens (SERA1, RPL6, GAP50, RNT, PHIST, S20, and RBP). WM382 also attenuated P. falciparum liver merozoites, and conservation of PMIX/X active sites supports pan- Plasmodium potential for preventing malaria. CALM vaccination merits clinical evaluation, including by natural mosquito exposure if long-acting injectable PMIX/X inhibitor formulations prove feasible.

10.1126/science.aec8866.title: Growth rate overrides the benefit of extended growing season from boreal to semiarid conifers
10.1126/science.aec8866.abstract: Climate warming lengthens the productive season in extratropical forests. Yet there is inconclusive evidence on whether this in turn elicits enhanced tree growth and forest carbon sequestration. In this study, we used cellular observations of conifer wood formation spanning boreal to semiarid forests to quantify the relative importance of cambial growth rate versus season length in driving annual cell production, the key process underlying woody growth. We found that rate is the primary driver of annual cell production. Furthermore, whereas the growing season lengthens with annual temperature, growth rate exhibited an optimum at ~6°C, beyond which increasingly dry conditions compromise wood production gains. The negative impact of warming on intra-annual growth dynamics can thus largely offset the benefit of longer growing season on future forest carbon storage.

10.1126/science.aej2018.title: The worst energy policy in the world
10.1126/science.aej2018.abstract: The Iran war could serve as a turning point in accelerating the global transition away from fossil fuels: Every additional day that oil and gas prices are high and future supplies are uncertain, wind and solar power-cheaper and more scalable than ever before-grow all the more appealing. But nearly half of the world’s countries have adopted emergency subsidies that research shows will make this transition slower, more expensive, and less equitable.

10.1126/science.aec5252.title: A tripartite genetic conflict system controls hybrid sterility in rice
10.1126/science.aec5252.abstract: Interspecific Asian-African hybrid rice could substantially boost yield but is limited by severe hybrid sterility. We identify RHS3 as a major quantitative trait locus controlling this trait. RHS3 encodes a tripartite toxin-antidote system composed of MAO, DUN, and JIA, in which MAO acts as a toxin that aborts gametes by disrupting mitochondrial function, whereas DUN and JIA function as antidotes that neutralize MAO toxicity, conferring a transmission advantage to the African allele. We demonstrate that detoxification relies on selective autophagy through formation of a tripartite JIA-DUN-MAO protein complex. We infer the de novo origin of RHS3 in the AA-genome rice lineage, illustrating a role for genetic conflict in speciation and suggesting strategies to harness heterosis between Asian and African rice.

10.1126/science.adt1992.title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
10.1126/science.adt1992.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.
authors: Qingkai Meng, Xiaokang Li, Jie Liu, Lingxiao Zhao, Chao Dong, Zengwei Zhu, Liang Li, Kamran Behnia

10.1126/science.ady8560.title: Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity
10.1126/science.ady8560.abstract: Lifestyle-related type 2 diabetes and associated obesity (diabesity) affect >2.5 billion people worldwide and impose nearly $3 trillion in annual health care costs. We developed an implantable, wirelessly powered electrocatalytic closed-loop health optimization (ECHO) device containing platinum-decorated gold nanoclusters embedded in graphite felt that enabled selective, electrically tunable oxidation of blood glucose to renally cleared gluconate. In type 2 diabetic mice, wireless, low-power activation (0.75 volts, 10 milliamperes) restored glucose homeostasis within 1 hour, shifted metabolism from glucose to lipid utilization, reduced body weight and triglycerides, and increased circulating free fatty acids and ketone bodies without detectable hypoglycemia or adverse physiological, inflammatory, or behavioral effects during 6 weeks of treatment. Coupling this ECHO device to a commercial continuous glucose monitoring system enabled autonomous, smartphone-controlled, drug-free closed-loop management of experimental diabesity.
authors: Debasis Maity, Preetam Guha Ray, Peter Buchmann, Ghislaine Charpin-El Hamri, Martin Fussenegger

10.1126/science.aea2181.title: BAK and BAX form a multiprotein complex to drive mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death
10.1126/science.aea2181.abstract: The apoptotic regulators BAX and BAK, once activated, form homo-oligomers to trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), activating the apoptosome and caspases. Activation of BAX-BAK without apoptosome activation triggers sustained efflux of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and caspase-independent cell death. However, the molecular basis of mtDNA efflux remains unclear. We purified a macromolecular complex comprising BAK, BAX, activator BH3-only molecules, voltage-dependent anion channels 1 and 2 (VDAC1 and VDAC2), and prohibitins that released mtDNA from mitoplasts. BAX-BAK activation resulted in VDAC closure, mitochondrial calcium influx, and mtDNA efflux. Loss of VDAC1, VDAC2, or prohibitins prevented BAX-BAK activation-induced mtDNA efflux and caspase-independent cell death without affecting MOMP or mitochondrial inner membrane herniation. These findings support differential regulation of cytochrome c and mtDNA efflux by distinct BAX-BAK complexes.
authors: Shaoyuan Yang, Hyungjin Kim, Guanghong Liao, Na Ta, Ho-Chou Tu, Shriram Ramani, Chih-Yu Chen, Zih-Yu Li, Nobuhiro Tanno, James J. Hsieh, Emily H. Cheng

10.1126/science.aea7156.title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
10.1126/science.aea7156.abstract: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.
authors: Ryan P. Englander, Mattia Brugiolo, Maëva Devoucoux, Te-Chia Wu, Mitch Kostich, Nathan K. Leclair, Isha Walawalkar, Hyeon Gu Kang, SungHee Park, Florentina Marches, Mark E. Peeples, Phylip Chen, Jacques Banchereau, Peter Yu, Andrew Salner, Romain Banchereau, Karolina Palucka, Olga Anczuków

10.1126/science.aed3379.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
10.1126/science.aed3379.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.
authors: Nicolás E. Young, Gifford H. Miller, Martha Raynolds, Helga Bueltmann, Scott J. Lehman, Jonathan H. Raberg, Kylie Seward, Simon L. Pendleton, John T. Andrews, Patrick J. Webber, Joerg M. Schaefer

10.1126/science.aed6459.title: Ultrarapid decision-making in an avian brain
10.1126/science.aed6459.abstract: Perceptual decision-making is well studied in mammals, but its operation in other vertebrates remains unclear. We show that carrion crows ( Corvus corone ) make deliberate decisions in a classic visual motion discrimination task with unprecedented speed, reporting choices in approximately 235 milliseconds on average, which is roughly twice as fast as has been observed in monkeys or humans and without sacrificing accuracy. Recordings from the pallial endbrain reveal that direction-selective neurons encode the upcoming choice as early as about 70 milliseconds after stimulus onset and about 170 milliseconds before the response, with ramping activity scaling with sensory evidence and converging at response onset. These findings highlight the extraordinary efficiency of avian decision-making circuitry, possibly shaped by evolutionary pressures for rapid visuomotor control.

10.1126/science.aed8319.title: Dynamic functionality-enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
10.1126/science.aed8319.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.
authors: Hao Zhang, Yuan Kang, Fan Feng, Ting Hu, Rongming Xu, Hang Yu, Kaiqiang He, Zhe Yang, Zhuyuan Wang, Cher Hon Lau, Ze-Xian Low, Qinfen Gu, Jefferson Zhe Liu, Huanting Wang, Xiwang Zhang

10.1126/science.aee6967.title: Imaging electron-hole asymmetry in the quantum melting of generalized Wigner crystals
10.1126/science.aee6967.abstract: Two-dimensional moiré materials provide a versatile platform to explore phase transitions in strongly correlated systems. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we imaged the density-driven melting of generalized Wigner crystals (GWCs) and Mott insulators (MIs) in electron-doped, near-60°-twisted molybdenum diselenide bilayers featuring a triangular moiré superlattice. We observed notable electron-hole asymmetry in GWC melting: Hole-doped GWCs yielded interaction-driven disordered states, whereas electron-doped GWCs melted into delocalized liquid-like states. This asymmetry arose from the broken particle-hole symmetry of the moiré superlattice, which produced electron and hole Fermi pockets with different momentum geometries upon GWC condensation. MI states melted without such asymmetry, consistent with the absence of a symmetry-breaking density modulation. This work provides direct visualization of the emergent phases that appear as GWCs undergo quantum melting transitions.
authors: Emma Berger, Michael Arumainayagam, Zhihuan Dong, Lucas Schneider, Tianle Wang, Greyson Nichols, Salman Kahn, Rwik Dutta, Gaoqiang Wang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Mit H. Naik, Michael P. Zaletel, Feng Wang, Michael F. Crommie

10.1126/science.aef0940.title: Visualizing symmetry-broken Chern insulators and their quantum melting
10.1126/science.aef0940.abstract: In the presence of a magnetic field, electronic states of moiré quantum materials develop a Hofstadter spectrum that provides a distinctive setting for studying the interplay between band topology and strong electron-electron interaction. Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we studied Hofstadter’s states in bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride and directly visualized the formation of interaction-driven symmetry breaking Chern insulators. Our measurements revealed the formation of phases that double, triple, or quadruple the moiré unit cell at fractional filling of the Hofstadter bands as well as states with complex intra-unit cell wave functions. We visualized two distinct quantum phenomena in different Chern states, including quantum melting driven by the appearance and proliferation of topological defects and a quantum transition co-occurring with phase competition and separation.
authors: Minhao He†, Yen-Chen Tsui†, Ran Peng, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Oskar Vafek, Ali Yazdani

10.1126/science.aef9745.title: Decoupled self-assembled monolayer and perovskite deposition for efficient flexible solar modules
10.1126/science.aef9745.abstract: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of flexible perovskite solar modules (PSMs) are less than those of their rigid devices because surface hydroxyls desorption on flexible substrates, which disrupts self-assembled monolayer (SAM) anchoring and perovskite crystallization. We developed a decoupled SAM-perovskite codeposition strategy that accelerates SAM anchoring by reducing the SAM-perovskite interaction and ameliorates perovskite crystallization. The certified PCE with phenethylammonium iodide as the passivation molecule was 20.2% on PSMs with device areas of 750 cm 2 . With 1,3-diaminopropane dihydroiodide as the passivator, the PCE of 22.0% for a device area of 14.55 cm 2 decreased by 8% after 1044 hours under maximum power point tracking at 85°C and 65% relative humidity. The devices pass all sequences of an international commercialization assessment standard for flexible portable PSMs.
authors: Yeyong Wu, Xikun Zhang, Tiankai Zhang, Guiying Xu, Yunxiu Shen, Chengxin Guo, Qing Miao, Junyuan Ding, Yue Yin, Qinrong Cheng, Wen Liu, Xiaoxiao Wu, Kaiqiang Chen, Wenwen Kou, Zhiyun Cao, Haiyang Chen, Weijie Chen, Yujin Chen, Feng Gao, Yaowen Li, Yongfang Li

10.1126/science.aeg1821.title: Natural product biosynthesis by guanidine prenyltransferases in plants and bacteria
10.1126/science.aeg1821.abstract: Guanidine exists almost exclusively as a resonance-stabilized cation, making its direct enzymatic functionalization challenging. We identified the cyanobacterial enzyme NosH, which catalyzes direct prenyl transfer to free guanidine. Structural and mechanistic analyses revealed guanidine activation by a two-aspartate clamp coupled to prenyl-donor binding through a distinct catalytic architecture. Guided by these features, we identified a large family of guanidine prenyltransferases across bacteria and plants. Plant enzymes produced guanidine alkaloids such as galegine in vitro and heterologous expression of a plant ortholog in Nicotiana benthamiana produced galegine in planta, providing a direct enzymatic link to plant-specialized metabolism.
authors: Dominik Kolling, Katharina Konzok, Daghan Taser, Tom Jentsch, Svenja Schwoerer, Henry Struwe, Arne Bültemeier, Jonas Freiberg, Claus-Peter Witte, Jakob Franke, Andriy Luzhetskyy, Andreas Kirschning, Sophia Rudorf, Jesko Koehnke

10.1126/science.aeh7930.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
10.1126/science.aeh7930.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.
authors: Harsha Nori, Mayank Daswani, Christopher Kelly, Scott Lundberg, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Marc Wilson, Xiaoxuan Liu, Viknesh Sounderajah, Jonathan M. Carlson, Matthew P. Lungren, Bay Gross, Peter Hames, Mustafa Suleyman, Dominic King, Eric Horvitz

10.1126/science.aek5696.title: Noncoding transcription controls the developmental dynamics of long-range gene regulation
10.1126/science.aek5696.abstract: The genomic regions regulating gene expression are often themselves transcribed into a variety of noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs). However, the regulatory roles of this noncoding transcription remain largely unknown. By using live imaging, we reveal that the sequential transcription of ncRNAs emanating from distinct regulatory elements underlies gene activation in Drosophila embryos. Single-allele covisualization uncovers that optimal gene activation is achieved by only moderate levels of enhancer activity. Disrupting enhancer-associated ncRNAs causes precocious gene activation, providing evidence that ncRNAs control the timing of gene expression in development. We further show that enhancer transcription can regulate long-range interactions within complex regulatory landscapes. We propose that ncRNAs locally modulate regulatory element activity in cis to shape genome organization and orchestrate the temporal control of gene expression in development.
authors: Philippe J. Batut and Michael S. Levine

10.1126/science.adt9825.title: Electronic bound states in the continuum in a two-dimensional metal
10.1126/science.adt9825.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are quantum states that remain localized despite lying within a continuum of extended, delocalized states. Whereas optical BICs have been realized in photonic systems, achieving electronic bound states embedded in a metallic background remains an ongoing challenge. In this study, we used scanning tunneling microscopy to identify two defect-induced electronic states that remain localized within the metallic continuum of Pd 5 AlI 2 , a two-dimensional van der Waals metal. Our calculations suggest that electron-hopping interference on the decorated checkerboard lattice of Pd 5 AlI 2 gives rise to a (quasi) flat band built from spatially localized eigenstates that are orthogonal to the dispersive continuum. Atomic defects within this frustrated lattice shift the associated flat-band localized states into the metallic continuum, forming robust, symmetry-protected BICs.
authors: Morgan Thinel, Xiong Huang, Daniel G. Chica, Simon Turkel, Sebastian E. Rossi, Christie S. Koay, Hong Li, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Bipasa Samanta, Madisen Holbrook, Aravind Devarakonda, Luca M. Nashabeh, Alexandru B. Georgescu, Xavier Roy, Xiaoyang Zhu, Abhay N. Pasupathy, Raquel Queiroz

10.1126/science.aeg6779.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
10.1126/science.aeg6779.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type-specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

10.1126/science.aen2722.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
10.1126/science.aen2722.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human-AI system, not the AI model alone.

authors: Michael Funk, and Leslie Ferrarelli, Di Jiang, Yevgeniya Nusinovich, Jelena Stajic, Marc S. Lavine, Bianca Lopez, Michael A. Funk, Priscilla N. Kelly, Phil Szuromi, L. Bryan Ray, Sacha Vignieri, Jesse Smith, and Leoma Bere

10.1126/science.aei3472.title: VIPR RNA-guided DNA recognition by noncontiguous geometric triplex formation
10.1126/science.aei3472.abstract: Viral interference programmable repeat (VIPR) systems use a noncontiguous code for RNA-guided transcriptional silencing. How the Vipr protein and a VIPR RNA (vrRNA) comprising alternating GGY and NN segments achieve precise DNA targeting is unknown. Here, we present 21 cryo-electron microscopy structures that help explain the mechanism of target engagement. Vipr protomers oligomerize along the vrRNA to form a right-handed helical filament, sequestering each GGY motif and positioning the adjacent NN bases for target base pairing. DNA binding, in which every third nucleotide is skipped, results in a gapped vrRNA-DNA hybrid helix that encircles the nontarget DNA strand to form a geometric triplex. These findings suggest that triplex-mediated target-strand handoff could enable noncontiguous and programmable RNA-guided DNA recognition in VIPR systems.

10.1126/science.adt9365.title: Unphosphorylated tyrosines mediate PD-1 inhibition of T cell signaling condensate formation
10.1126/science.adt9365.abstract: T cell receptor (TCR) engagement stimulates formation of a biomolecular condensate, including the scaffold protein linker of activated T cells (LAT). We investigated whether the immune-inhibitory receptor programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibits by impeding TCR-induced LAT condensation. In vitro reconstitutions revealed that the cytoplasmic domain of PD-1 directly inhibited LAT condensation. This inhibitory interaction required tyrosine residues in the two inhibitory motifs of PD-1. Contrary to current working models, tyrosine phosphorylation eliminated PD-1 inhibition. Replacing tyrosine with tryptophan reconstituted PD-1 inhibition in T cells, confirming that phosphorylation does not mediate this effect. These findings support the concept that hydrogen bond-donating aromatic residues within inhibitory motifs provide the primary mechanism that explains how inhibitory receptors disrupt signaling networks and block immune activation.

10.1126/science.aec7337.title: Endurance beyond 10 billion cycles in wurtzite ferroelectrics by confining nitrogen vacancies
10.1126/science.aec7337.abstract: Wurtzite ferroelectrics could provide a route to wafer-scale integrated ferroelectric memories but are limited by endurance, typically failing at ~10 8 cycles. We identified nitrogen-vacancy ( V N ) clustering and long-range percolative migration as the defect-mediated pathways that drive leakage-current growth and dielectric breakdown. We combined a spatially engineered aluminum scandium nitride/aluminum nitride (AlScN/AlN) superlattice with a dynamic recovery protocol to spatially and energetically confine V N evolution that stabilized defect topology under cyclic electrical stress and suppressed hard breakdown and ferroelectric degradation. We demonstrated endurance beyond 10 10 cycles in wurtzite ferroelectrics under a complete-switching criterion (remnant polarization ≥ 100 microcoulombs per square centimeter). These findings establish V N confinement as a scalable defect-topology framework that couples atomic-scale defect stability to reliable ultradense ferroelectric memories and provide guidance for next-generation nonvolatile memory technologies.

10.1126/science.aej5896.title: Targeting an atypical G protein-coupled receptor signaling pathway for cardiac fibrosis therapy
10.1126/science.aej5896.abstract: Cardiac fibrosis independently predicts adverse outcomes in heart failure (HF), yet no Food and Drug Administration-approved therapy directly targets fibrotic remodeling in the heart. To address this unmet clinical need, we used a multidimensional drug discovery pipeline centered on a human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-based platform. Through high-throughput screening, we identified CGS15943 (CGS) as the lead antifibrotic compound and validated its activity in human cardiac fibroblasts, three-dimensional engineered heart tissues, and animal models of HF. Mechanistic studies revealed an atypical adenosine receptor (AR)-dependent signaling pathway in which AR subtypes converge on Gβγ (the βγ subunits of heterotrimeric GTP-binding proteins) to activate phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)-AKT and yes-associated protein (YAP). CGS suppressed this signaling axis, thereby reducing fibrotic gene expression and fibroblast activation. These findings establish AR-driven Gβγ signaling as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac fibrosis.

10.1126/science.aec7230.title: Splenic regulation of systemic platelet activation state
10.1126/science.aec7230.abstract: Platelets are essential to prevent blood loss and to orchestrate inflammation. Thrombotic complications of vascular disease and hyperresponsive platelets are associated with adverse outcomes, yet physiological mechanisms counteracting systemic platelet activation are poorly defined. In mice, we found that the spleen filters activated platelets in thrombotic and inflammatory conditions, limiting pathology by maintaining platelet quiescence. Glycoprotein VI-dependent activation of platelets initiated by extracellular matrix components in the splenic red pulp was counterbalanced by G6b-B-immunoreceptor tyrosine-based inhibitory motif signaling triggered by perlecan in quiescent platelets, allowing them to recirculate. By contrast, threshold activation signals in preactivated platelets could override inhibition, leading to splenic capture through inside-out signaling and β1-integrin engagement. Thus, the spleen acts as a modulator of platelet responsiveness and thrombo-inflammatory risk.

10.1126/science.adz6415.title: How 8 years of social and individual learning interact to shape ecological competence in orangutans
10.1126/science.adz6415.abstract: Cultural learning permeates human skill and knowledge acquisition. To understand its importance for nonhuman apes, we analyzed just under 7000 records of behavioral bouts of social and individual learning across wild orangutans’ 8-year dependency period to assess their combined effects on ecological competence, which is crucial for independent survival. Social learning was five times more frequent than individual learning and influenced subsequent learning for hours. Immature orangutans varied substantially in their learning propensities, and those with heightened social and individual learning propensities developed the most expansive diet profiles at independence. Furthermore, social learning had a compensatory effect on diet profile development when individual learning was low. Our findings advance the science of cultural evolution by showing how multiyear social and individual learning interact to shape great apes’ broad ecological competence.

10.1126/science.aef5487.title: Prussian blue regulates ion dynamics in perovskite solar cells
10.1126/science.aef5487.abstract: Perovskite photovoltaics are limited by structural instabilities initiated during crystallization and amplified under operation. We report that a lattice-matched Prussian blue scaffold directs heterogeneous nucleation to produce highly oriented, strain-relaxed films. Its redox-active Fe-C≡N-Fe network mediates the conversion of Pb 0 and I 0 defects, and its rigid open framework suppresses A-site cation redistribution and the resulting electronic inhomogeneity under bias. This strategy yielded champion power conversion efficiencies of 26.1% (n-i-p) and 26.9% (p-i-n; 26.2% certified), scaling to 23.4% in 6-centimeter-by-6-centimeter minimodules and a certified 22.9% in 30-centimeter-by-30-centimeter submodules. Submodules with initial power conversion efficiencies ranging from 20.2 to 21.0% showed robust durability under accelerated aging and no discernible decline relative to a silicon reference over 5 months of outdoor testing.

10.1126/science.adx9928.title: Protecting tropical forests is more cost-effective for biodiversity and climate than restoration
10.1126/science.adx9928.abstract: Halting deforestation and promoting restoration are at the core of strategies to confront the biodiversity and climate crises in tropical forests. Avoiding forest disturbances is also critically important but has received far less attention, and there is a lack of clarity about the relative cost-effectiveness of these three interventions. We compare the biodiversity and carbon benefits and costs associated with each intervention, comparing observed and counterfactual outcomes based on in-depth field assessments and high-resolution remote sensing in the Brazilian Amazon deforestation frontier. Avoidance interventions delivered the greatest benefits and were more cost-effective than restoration, with results being robust to a range of benefit and cost assumptions. However, combined interventions delivered the greatest gains and were essential to reverse biodiversity and carbon losses.

10.1126/science.adx5917.title: Nuclear tests at Mt. Mantap have reactivated intraplate faults
10.1126/science.adx5917.abstract: Underground nuclear explosions typically produce short-lived seismic sequences that decay rapidly after testing ceases. By contrast, seismicity near the Punggye-ri nuclear test site at Mt. Mantap in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea has persisted and intensified for years after the final large-yield explosion in 2017, evolving from diffuse activity to spatially organized distribution along fault-controlled structures. Analysis of 17 years of continuous waveform data reveals a progressive increase in seismicity and delayed reactivation of shallow faults. Earthquakes cluster beneath asymmetric topography, indicating progressive stress redistribution within a critically stressed crustal volume. These observations challenge conventional expectations, showing that under specific geological conditions, underground nuclear testing can drive multiyear fault reactivation and extend posttest seismicity well beyond the immediate aftermath of an explosion.

10.1126/science.adu2107.title: Two-dimensional topological quantum chemistry and catalog of topological materials
10.1126/science.adu2107.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) topological materials host symmetry-protected, disorder-robust edge states central to quantum technologies. Yet they remain scarce compared with their 3D counterparts. We adapted the topological quantum chemistry formalism to layer groups and studied the band topology of 8872 entries from the computational materials databases C2DB and MC2D. We found 4073 topological or obstructed entries, including 905 topological insulators and 1003 obstructed atomic insulators, greatly expanding the library of such materials in two dimensions. Detailed electronic and topological properties of all materials have been compiled into a Topological 2D Materials Database (2D-TQCDB), and the edge states of selected new materials have been studied in detail. Our methodology has been implemented in publicly available programs, designed to study the topology of any nonmagnetic monolayer or multilayer material.

10.1126/science.adw7709.title: Neural evidence that dogs segment the speech they hear with a humanlike consonant bias
10.1126/science.adw7709.abstract: Across many human languages, consonants carry more lexical information than vowels. During speech segmentation, humans, unlike nonhuman primates, rely more on consonant than vowel patterns, despite vowels’ greater acoustic saliency. To investigate whether this consonant bias is specific to humans or could also emerge in other species exposed to human speech, we performed noninvasive electroencephalography in humans and dogs. Intertrial coherence measures of neural entrainment and event-related potentials revealed enhanced word-level tracking for consonant- compared with vowel-structured streams in both species. This suggests that dogs, similar to humans, exhibit consonant bias when segmenting the speech they hear. Linguistic regularity-based processing biases can thus also emerge in a nonspeaking species exposed to speech.

10.1126/science.adq7553.title: Ancient introgression drives wild boar expansion and phenotypic diversification of domestic pigs
10.1126/science.adq7553.abstract: Despite the ubiquity of wild boar populations across Eurasia, their origins, routes of dispersal, and phenotypic evolution remain uncertain. Here, using 745 genomes representing populations across Eurasia, we demonstrate that wild boar expanded from South Asia during the Middle Pleistocene. This expansion was preceded by a Pliocene introgression (~3 to 5 million years ago) in South Asia from an archaic Suinae lineage that introduced a ~43 megabase X-chromosomal haplotype into the ancestral wild boar population. This haplotype includes loci associated with increased body size and adaptation to cold climates. During domestication, this region was selected at least three times independently to develop modern large-bodied breeds. Our findings reveal a long-lasting evolutionary legacy of this ancient introgression, which provided genetic material that was later shaped by natural and artificial selection.

10.1126/science.ady6372.title: Multi-organelle signatures map cell-state diversity and metabolic adaptation in tissues
10.1126/science.ady6372.abstract: Cell-state diversity drives tissue adaptability, repair, and disease resilience, but capturing this complexity is a challenge. Current approaches rely on transcriptional profiling and overlook organelle structure, a key indicator of metabolism and stress. We developed spatial Organellomics (sOrganellomics), an imaging workflow that integrates automated segmentation with machine learning to classify and spatially map cell states from multi-organelle signatures. In liver and pancreas, these signatures distinguished broad cellular classes. In liver, sOrganellomics revealed that zonal position did not fully explain organelle-defined hepatocyte categories. Instead, hepatocytes formed intermixed communities within canonical zones, supporting a refined subzonal diversity model. Nutritional stress reshaped this organization. Intravital imaging linked fasting-induced organelle remodeling with altered mitochondrial membrane potential in vivo, supporting multi-organelle architecture as a structural readout of tissue adaptation.

10.1126/science.adz0521.title: Extreme loss suppression in an ultracold molecular gas with widely tunable dipolar interactions
10.1126/science.adz0521.abstract: Ultracold dipolar molecules hold great promise for the creation of exotic quantum states of matter, but the realization of long-lived molecular bulk samples with strong dipole-dipole interactions has remained challenging. In this work, we realized a collisionally stable gas of ultracold ground state molecules with a lifetime of several seconds. Utilizing double-microwave dressing, we achieved an extreme suppression of inelastic two- and three-body losses by factors of more than 10,000 and 1000, respectively. We found that losses remained suppressed across a wide range of dipole-dipole interactions, allowing the continuous tuning of the dipolar length from −21,000 to 12,000 a 0 , where a 0 is the Bohr radius. Combined with the recent realization of Bose-Einstein condensation of dipolar molecules, our findings open the door to the exploration of strongly dipolar quantum liquids.

10.1126/science.aeb5077.title: Modality-specific neurovascular coupling via layer-segregated arteriole networks
10.1126/science.aeb5077.abstract: The brain’s vascular system dynamically regulates energy supply through neurovascular coupling. In this study, we show that in mice, neurovascular coupling is modality-dependent: Distinct sensory inputs recruit specific arteriole types, producing differential laminar blood flow patterns. Using multiscale optical imaging, we compared neuronal and vascular responses to touch, nociception, motor-sensory feedback, and spontaneous activity. Shallow arteriole dilation emerges with increasing superficial-layer activity, whereas deep arterioles integrate signals broadly across input conditions. Arteriole type-specific dilation decouples the magnitude of local neuronal activity from capillary blood flow responses, with flow patterns shaped by vascular topology and recapitulated in silico. Together, these findings reveal how interactions between laminar circuit activity and vascular network architecture dynamically shape the spatial profile of blood flow delivery across the cortex.

10.1126/science.aeg4791.title: Senescence-directed nanotherapy ameliorates fibrosis and overcomes immune exclusion in cancer
10.1126/science.aeg4791.abstract: Fibrotic remodeling of tissues and tumors establishes immunosuppressive microenvironments that drive organ dysfunction and, in cancer, limit response to immunotherapy. Senescent-like cells are conserved drivers of fibrosis and therapeutic targets, yet their functional heterogeneity complicates therapeutic intervention. Here, we show that P-selectin is expressed by a subset of senescent-like cells in fibrotic tissues and tumors. Leveraging fucoidan-based nanoparticles that bind P-selectin, we developed senescence-modulating nanoparticles (SMNPs) to selectively target these disease-associated states. SMNPs exerted potent antifibrotic and immunomodulatory effects while improving the therapeutic index. Mechanistically, we identified a pathogenic, immunosuppressive macrophage population as a functional target in vivo. In fibrotic tumors, niche remodeling restored immune infiltration and sensitized tumors to immune checkpoint-based therapies. These findings establish SMNPs as a generalizable strategy to target pathogenic senescent cell subsets across fibrosis and cancer.

10.1126/science.aec6129.title: An expert-level generalist AI for abdominal CT diagnosis
10.1126/science.aec6129.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology aspires to deliver expert-level diagnosis across diverse clinical tasks, yet existing supervised strategies remain limited in scope. We developed RADAR, a generalist vision-language model trained on more than 400,000 contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) examinations and 15 million anatomy-wise image-text pairs, learning directly from clinical reports without manual annotation. Throughout internal and external evaluations across multiple centers and varied clinical scenarios, RADAR achieved high diagnostic performance and robust generalization for 18 anatomical structures and 146 imaging findings. In a reader study, RADAR assistance increased the diagnostic sensitivity of 26 radiologists by ~10%. RADAR offers a scalable, versatile, and interpretable solution for abdominal CT, demonstrating that generalist AI can match human experts in general and complicated radiology tasks.

10.1126/science.adp3564.title: Open framework-based Brønsted acid-Lewis base interfaces boost proton transfer in the fuel cells
10.1126/science.adp3564.abstract: Limited proton conductivity within the catalyst layer induces severe ohmic polarizations and constrains power output at high hydrogen-to-electricity efficiencies in proton exchange membrane fuel cells. We demonstrate that proton transfer can be boosted by constructing Brønsted acid-Lewis base interfaces through integrating organic open frameworks with Nafion. These confined interfaces mediate low-barrier relay pathways, disrupt hydrogen bonding to expedite water network reorganization, facilitate consecutive proton transfer, and enrich protons locally. Compared with Nafion, the complexes exhibit an order-of-magnitude increase in proton self-diffusion coefficient, a 6.5-fold rise in proton conductivity, and a 55% reduction in activation energy. When integrated with commercial platinum on carbon, they deliver a fourfold increase in rated power output relative to the baseline, outperforming representative state-of-the-art membrane electrode assemblies with advanced catalysts under similar conditions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
10.1038/s41467-026-78271-9.abstract: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0.title: Unmet care needs at the end-of-life among older adults with activity limitations
10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74719-0 Formal end-of-life care expansion in the US, Europe, and South Korea has not fully compensated for declining informal care, resulting in care gaps. Demographic transitions interact with development contexts to create distinct care landscapes.

10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7.title: NiCLIP: neuroimaging contrastive language-image pretraining model for predicting text from brain activation images
10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78451-7 Researchers developed NiCLIP, an AI model that decodes cognitive tasks, concepts, and domains from brain activation patterns. Trained on over 23,000 papers, NiCLIP excels at group-level decoding, outperforming traditional decoders.

10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets
10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 13 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78527-4 In this study, the authors develop a computational framework, Scellmate, that curates and analyzes large-scale microbial single-cell datasets from complex environments, and show that this helps to reveal microbial diversity and infer microbe-plasmid and microbe-phage associations in sewage.

10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
10.1038/s41467-026-78169-6.abstract: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.
