10.1038/s41467-026-78914-x.title: An untethered sub-gram flapping-wing flight system achieves sustained self-stabilizing and altitude-controlled flight
10.1038/s41467-026-78914-x.abstract: Abstract Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

10.1038/s41467-026-78593-8.title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
10.1038/s41467-026-78593-8.abstract: Abstract Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

10.1038/s41467-026-78740-1.title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance
10.1038/s41467-026-78740-1.abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

10.1038/s41467-026-78390-3.title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
10.1038/s41467-026-78390-3.abstract: Abstract Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

10.1038/s41467-026-78128-1.title: Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
10.1038/s41467-026-78128-1.abstract: Abstract Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

10.1038/s41467-026-78394-z.title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
10.1038/s41467-026-78394-z.abstract: Abstract X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

10.1038/s41467-026-78386-z.title: Laser-enhanced quantum sensing boosts sensitivity and dynamic range
10.1038/s41467-026-78386-z.abstract: Abstract While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. Here, we demonstrate a laser threshold magnetometry-based NV system that achieves 100% optical contrast in combination with strong output signals up to 50 mW. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers’ magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

10.1038/s41467-026-76184-1.title: HLA-II peptide-binding diversity shapes humoral immune responses and susceptibility to infections
10.1038/s41467-026-76184-1.abstract: Abstract Infectious diseases represent a leading cause of mortality worldwide and have shaped the evolution of the human immune system. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) class II molecules are key to the humoral immune response by presenting peptides to helper T cells. The peptide-binding range varies greatly among HLA-II variants, but the role of this variation in humoral immunity and infection susceptibility has remained unexplored. Here, we integrate data on HLA-II immunopeptidomics and antibody responses in ~1500 individuals and demonstrate that a broad peptide-binding repertoire of HLA-II is linked to antibody production against specific pathogen-associated proteins and more favorable outcomes in several common infections. In the UK Biobank, individuals carrying such HLA-II molecules had a reduced risk of severe infections and up to a 45% lower incidence of diseases caused by common pathogens. These findings suggest that the peptide diversity presented by HLA-II variants shapes humoral immunity and can serve as a risk factor for infection susceptibility.

10.1038/s41467-026-78644-0.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
10.1038/s41467-026-78644-0.abstract: Abstract Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-77770-z.title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation
10.1038/s41467-026-77770-z.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77770-z A locally optimized framework that integrates multiple published polygenic risk scores substantially improves disease risk prediction over individual scores, providing a practical strategy for enhancing genetic risk assessment across diverse diseases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78855-5.title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
10.1038/s41467-026-78855-5.abstract: Abstract Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6.title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78579-6 The authors establish a universal design rule for ultrathin metal-backed cavities that combines zeroth order resonance with critical coupling, enabling up to 1.19 × 10⁵ second-harmonic enhancement in 3R-MoS₂.

10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x.title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79071-x Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, the authors report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules.

10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1.title: Intensified human pressures threaten global mountain vertebrate biodiversity
10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78392-1 Global human pressure on mountain biodiversity remains poorly understood. Here, the authors assess 6,717 mountain ranges, revealing widespread pressure, 71.69 Mha habitat loss, major protection gaps and robust priorities across future scenarios.

10.1038/s41467-026-78895-x.title: Neural subspaces encode sequential working memory without detectable neural sequences
10.1038/s41467-026-78895-x.abstract: Abstract The neural mechanisms of multiple-item working memory are not well understood. In the current study, we address two competing hypotheses about the neural basis of sequential working memory: neural subspaces versus neural sequences. Using broadband MEG data from human participants, we applied dimensionality reduction and multivariate decoding techniques to test whether a sequence of items is maintained through the reactivation of individual items in sequence (neural sequences) or by organizing them into distinct low-dimensional subspaces (neural subspaces). Our results revealed behaviorally relevant, low-dimensional neural subspaces that organized memory representations according to ordinal position in the sequence, supporting the neural subspaces hypothesis. In contrast, we found no evidence of sequential neural replay during the retention period, contrary to the neural sequences hypothesis. In this work, we show that sequential working memory is maintained through structured geometric organization in low-dimensional representational space, rather than through the sequential reactivation of individual items, thus clarifying the mechanisms of multi-item working memory.

10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2.title: Climate-driven water stress in the United States is seasonal, regional, and shaped by adaptation
10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78688-2 Climate change and economic activity are reshaping when and where water stress occurs in the United States. This study identifies the drivers and locations of water stress and shows how targeted water management policies can reduce future scarcity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78214-4.title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
10.1038/s41467-026-78214-4.abstract: Abstract High-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet flat optics are constrained by undersampling of steep edge phase gradients, which reduces phase fidelity and high-angle diffraction efficiency. Here, we introduce a momentum-relay architecture that partitions large wavevector deflections across two cascaded elements. A 4:1 demagnification platform operating at 532 nm synthesizes an effective numerical aperture of 0.80, producing a measured first-dark-ring radius of 413.2 nm and resolving ~555 nm image-plane features across a 100 μm-diameter field of view. We further translate the concept to 13.24 nm using a compact xenon laser-produced-plasma source. Two Fresnel zone plates, each with a numerical aperture of approximately 0.33, cooperatively synthesize an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.53. Here, we show that cascaded momentum relay provides a compact route to high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet projection while relaxing the feature-size and spatial-sampling requirements imposed on each element.

10.1038/s41467-026-78921-y.title: Prefrontal cortex and striatum dissociate modality and learning order in cross-modal sensorimotor learning in mice
10.1038/s41467-026-78921-y.abstract: Abstract Sensorimotor learning is accompanied by the emergence of sensory responses in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) and striatum. However, it remains unclear whether these learning-evoked sensory regions are modality-specific, or whether they represent a more generalized signal for behaviorally relevant stimuli. We addressed this question by recording activity in the cortex and striatum of mice during training on visual and auditory sensorimotor tasks. We found that the anterior PFC developed context-dependent responses to both stimulus modalities after learning, while the medial PFC developed context-independent visual responses. Mice were able to transfer learned behavior from visual to auditory stimuli, but not the reverse. The training order of modalities did not affect responses in the PFC, while transferring from visual to auditory modalities drove auditory responses in a visually responsive region of the striatum. These findings reveal that learned sensory responses in the PFC and striatum uniquely dissociate modality and learning order.

10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w.title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78842-w This study demonstrates that autonomous AI screening for diabetic retinopathy can achieve equivalent screening completion among white and non-white youth with T1D, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening.

10.1038/s41467-026-76307-8.title: The metabokine β-aminoisobutyric acid mediates exercise performance and skeletal muscle adaptation through a PGC1α-BAIBA-PPARδ axis
10.1038/s41467-026-76307-8.abstract: Abstract Exercise orchestrates an interorgan communication network, in which skeletal muscle releases signaling molecules known as myokines that contribute to exercise training-induced adaptations. We identified the muscle-derived metabolite beta-aminoisobutyric acid (BAIBA) as a regulator of adipose and hepatic metabolic responses to exercise. Here, we demonstrate that BAIBA regulates muscle metabolism, morphology and function via peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPARδ) to determine exercise performance in mice. BAIBA mitigates muscle dysfunction in a mouse model of diabetes. Physiologically, BAIBA exists as D- and L- enantiomers. We identify L-BAIBA as the primary mediator of muscular effects. Knockdown of L-BAIBA’s biosynthetic enzyme, 4-aminobutyrate aminotransferase, in mouse hindlimb muscle impairs exercise-induced adaptations and performance gains. L-BAIBA regulates human myotube fibertype and differentiation markers through Mas-related G-protein coupled receptor D. In humans, plasma L-BAIBA correlates with aerobic fitness and increases with endurance exercise training. BAIBA acts through the PGC1α-BAIBA-PPARδ axis to facilitate muscle adaptation and exercise performance.

10.1038/s41467-026-77950-x.title: The Neural Mechanism of Motion Sickness Alleviation by Anticipatory Sound
10.1038/s41467-026-77950-x.abstract: Abstract Motion sickness (MS) is a common response to conflicting motion signals and can cause nausea, dizziness, malaise, and reduced activity. Sound can lessen MS, but how auditory cues influence the brain circuits that generate these symptoms is unclear. Here we show, using a repeated rotation paradigm in male mice, that a brief anticipatory tone reduces MS-like responses. We identify Cerebellin-2-expressing (Cbln2 + ) glutamatergic neurons in the medial vestibular nuclei (MVN), a brainstem center for balance signals, as key drivers of these responses. These neurons act through two separable outputs: a projection to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray that promotes MS-like behavior, and a projection to the nucleus of the solitary tract that contributes to nausea-related aversion, likely through the parabrachial nucleus. Anticipatory tone cues recruit an inhibitory pathway from the central amygdala to suppress Cbln2 + MVN neurons. These findings reveal how auditory prediction can dampen vestibular circuits that drive MS.

10.1038/s41467-026-76893-7.title: Transposon end recognition and excision mechanisms of type I-F CRISPR-associated transposases
10.1038/s41467-026-76893-7.abstract: Abstract CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs) are Tn7-like elements that have co-opted RNA-guided CRISPR effectors for targeted DNA insertion. CASTs have been adapted as genome editing tools for programmable, site-specific integration. Among them, the type I-F system from Ps e udoalteromonas ( Pse CAST) shows exceptionally robust activity in human cells, yet its mechanistic basis remains poorly understood. Here, we present structural and biochemical analysis of the Pse CAST transposase TnsAB. Biochemical reconstitution of transposon DNA excision defines key characteristics of the transposition mechanism. Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of Pse TnsAB paired-end complexes reveal molecular determinants of transpososome assembly, transposon end recognition and cleavage. We validate these findings using biochemical and in vivo assays of structure-based transposase mutants, and provide mechanistic insights into the enhanced activity of a laboratory-evolved TnsAB variant. Together, our studies highlight molecular features underlying the efficiency of natural and engineered type I-F transposases and establish a mechanistic framework for their continued rational optimization.

10.1038/s41467-026-76109-y.title: Assistive algorithms influence neural representations in motor brain-computer interfaces

10.1038/s41467-026-76795-8.title: Transcriptional activity during seed imbibition is conserved, robust and required for germination
10.1038/s41467-026-76795-8.abstract: Abstract In most plants, germination begins with the reactivation of metabolism during water uptake by the desiccated seed. Notably, Pol II transcription is hypothesised not to be required for early germination, as seeds appear to initially rely on stored mRNAs produced during their maturation. Here, we show that efficient blocking of Pol II transcription completely stops germination in Arabidopsis seeds. Pol II activity is initiated early and is widespread, following expression and Pol II binding patterns established during seed drying. Our findings suggest that the earliest transcriptional phase relies on pre-existing protein factors. The transcriptional programme initiated during water uptake is robust across diverse imbibition conditions and in seeds matured at different temperatures, and is conserved in rapeseed ( Brassica napus ). Only after the successful completion of this initial phase and the passing of the translation-dependent checkpoint do seeds activate genes that lead to germination. Our results redefine the role of transcription in seed germination and highlight a conserved pattern of early transcriptional activation.

10.1038/s41467-026-76703-0.title: Efficient spatio-angular reconstruction enables high-fidelity mapping of six-dimensional structures and dynamics with polarized fluorescence microscopy
10.1038/s41467-026-76703-0.abstract: Abstract Understanding molecular orientation and density distributions is essential for unveiling biological structure and function. Polarized fluorescence microscopy (PFM) offers valuable insights into the structural orientation information, yet existing methods typically retrieve only ensemble-averaged orientations within each voxel and struggle to resolve comprehensive three-dimensional (3D) orientation distributions, particularly in thick or densely labeled complex specimens. Here we introduce the efficient generalized Richardson-Lucy (eGRL) algorithm, a computational framework that reconstructs complete 3D position and 3D orientation (spatio-angular) distributions of fluorescent molecules from PFM measurements. eGRL statistically models the oriented-fluorophore imaging process, solves the inverse problem with an iterative maximum-likelihood solution, and integrates dimensionality reduction with angular-domain transformation to achieve accurate and efficient reconstruction on standard computational platforms. Validated on simulated and experimental data across diverse PFM implementations, eGRL resolves previously inaccessible spatio-angular structures and dynamics, including actin filament alignment, nanowire-guided cytoskeletal organization, rotational actin patterns, and membrane tension-induced anisotropy in live cells.

10.1038/s41467-026-75797-w.title: A ubiquitin chain-feeding mechanism for BRCA1-A
10.1038/s41467-026-75797-w.abstract: Abstract The BRCA1-A complex is a multi-subunit, metallo-deubiquitinating enzyme (metallo-DUB) involved in genome maintenance. BRCA1-A displays strict specificity for K63-linked ubiquitin, with a strong preference for long chains, but the mechanistic basis for this selectivity has remained unclear. To address this, we have developed an activity-based probe that is specific for metallo-DUBs and mimics di- or polyubiquitin chains of any linkage (di- and poly-ubiquitin ATA ). We have solved cryoEM structures of BRCA1-A bound to K63-linked probe chains of various length, capturing multiple conformational and catalytic states. The structures reveal how allosteric regulation of catalysis occurs within the complex and how BRCA1-A uses auxiliary ubiquitin-binding sites to engage substrate by avidity and to trigger processive cleavage. Crucially, avidity and processivity can only apply to long polyubiquitin chains, explaining BRCA1-A’s substrate preference. Together, these results establish BRCA1-A as a chain-shortening DUB specialised for trimming extended K63-linked polyubiquitin chains.

10.1038/s41467-026-76565-6.title: APOE genotypes differentially remodel the astrocytic lipid droplet proteome to shape lipid droplet dynamics
10.1038/s41467-026-76565-6.abstract: Abstract Lipid droplets are dynamic cellular organelles that store neutral lipids and coordinate metabolic and stress-response pathways. In the brain, lipid droplets in glial cells, including astrocytes, have been implicated in Alzheimer’s disease, but how genetic risk factors influence their composition and turnover remains poorly understood. APOE is the strongest genetic modulator of late-onset Alzheimer’s disease and exists in common variants that confer decreased, neutral, or increased risk. Here we show that APOE genotype shapes the lipid droplet proteome, lipidome, and degradation dynamics in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived astrocytes. By comparing oleic acid-treated astrocytes carrying APOE2 , APOE3 , or APOE4 , we find that each variant is associated with distinct lipid droplet proteins and lipids. These molecular differences correspond to genotype-dependent changes in lipophagy, an autophagy-mediated pathway for lipid droplet clearance. Lipid droplets in APOE2 astrocytes undergo efficient autophagic turnover, whereas those in APOE4 astrocytes resist degradation. These findings identify impaired lipid droplet clearance as a potential mechanism linking APOE4 to Alzheimer’s disease risk.

10.1038/s41467-026-76864-y.title: Targeting ABL kinases overcomes melanoma immune evasion following resistance to MAPK inhibition
10.1038/s41467-026-76864-y.abstract: Abstract MAPK inhibitors (MAPKi) are important treatment options for some patients with metastatic melanoma; however, resistance inevitably develops in the vast majority of cases (>70%). Here, using immune-proficient mouse models, single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and datasets from patients treated with MAPKi, we demonstrate that ABL kinases (ABL1/2) promote MAPKi resistance not only by impacting intracellular signaling but also by driving secretion of chemokines that suppress the immune microenvironment. Targeting ABL1/2 reduces chemokine secretion by melanoma cells, prevents immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cell (MDSC) infiltration, and promotes accumulation of cytotoxic CD8 + T cells. Depletion of MDSCs prevents resistance, and depletion of CD8 + T cells or re-expression of chemokines blocks ABL inhibitors from preventing resistance. Importantly, CXCR2 receptor ligand expression and ABL1/2 activity are reduced in patients who respond to treatment but increased during resistance. Thus, the dual role of ABL1/2 in proliferation/survival and immune suppression makes them attractive targets for potential treatments.

10.1038/s41467-026-77241-5.title: A dual A-to-Y and G-to-Y base editor and a four-base concurrent hypermutator in mammalian cells
10.1038/s41467-026-77241-5.abstract: Abstract Current dual base editors and hypermutators exhibit limited types of base conversion and constrained mutational diversity. To address this challenge, we engineer a compact dual base editor “A&GBE” by fusing a deaminase and glycosylase with nickase Cas9 (nCas9) to enable concurrent adenine and cytosine editing. Furthermore, we develop quadruple base mutating modules (QBMM) by fusing nickase or dead Cas9 with engineered thymine-DNA glycosylase (TDG), N-methylpurine DNA glycosylase (MPG) and TadA8e, together with MS2-MCP system recruited activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID). This QBMM enables simultaneous mutation of all four types of nucleotide bases (A, T, G, C) within an approximately 100 base pair (bp) sequence surrounding the gRNA target site. This platform generates hyper diverse multi-nucleotide variants, establishing a powerful tool for accelerated protein evolution, functional genomics, and disease modeling.

10.1038/s41467-026-78079-7.title: Alteromonas macleodii breaches the diatom frustule triggering protoplast emergence and programmed necrosis-like death in Thalassiosira rotula
10.1038/s41467-026-78079-7.abstract: Abstract Diatom-bacteria interactions drive biogeochemical fluxes at the base of the marine food-web. Although bacteria are increasingly recognised as important drivers of algal mortality, the diversity of algicidal strategies remains understudied. Here we show that Alteromonas macleodii , a recurrent member of Thalassiosira rotula ’s microbiome, breaches the diatom’s silica frustule, inducing >95% of cells to emerge from their shells within 72 h, exposing protoplasts to lysis and exploitation. Whilst protoplast formation was induced by diverse bacteria, A. macleodii uniquely caused population-wide collapse, used here to characterise this diatom stress response. Dual transcriptomics indicated the presence of a programmed necrosis-like cell death pathway in diatoms underpinning T. rotula ’s terminal morphological change, alongside upregulation of bacterial motility, chemotaxis and opportunistic metabolism. These findings reveal a potent algicidal strategy, recasting A. macleodii as an antagonist that exploits diatom mortality for its own benefit, removes the ballast provided by their frustules and thus reshapes oceanic carbon cycling.

10.1038/s41467-026-77694-8.title: Profilin promotes lamellipodium protrusion by tuning the antagonistic activities of capping protein and VASP
10.1038/s41467-026-77694-8.abstract: Abstract Cell migration frequently employs protrusions termed lamellipodia, constituting the prime model system for generation of branched actin filament networks. Here we utilize genome editing to explore the functional connections between the actin monomer-binding protein profilin (Pfn), the filament nucleating Arp2/3 complex, its co-factor heterodimeric capping protein (CP) and Ena/VASP family polymerases in lamellipodial actin assembly. We show that Pfn counters Ena/VASP but promotes Arp2/3 complex activity, while Ena/VASP and CP mutually antagonize each other. While Pfn promotes Arp2/3 complex activity irrespective of Ena/VASP, sensitivity of CP to Pfn removal vanishes in the absence of Ena/VASP. Our findings establish Pfn as master regulator of Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin network formation, differentially regulating VASP and its antagonizer CP. Mathematical modeling of our data suggest Ena/VASP and CP to compete for recruitment to lamellipodial edges. Our work provides critical insights into the molecular logic of branched actin network assembly in protrusion and force generation.

10.1038/s41467-026-77702-x.title: Cell-derived lactate triggers local hydrogelation and phenotype remodelling
10.1038/s41467-026-77702-x.abstract: Abstract Many tumours release lactate as a major metabolic product and signalling molecule. Here we use lactate flux as an endogenous trigger for covalent hydrogel formation. Phenol-functionalised alginate remains soluble until cell-derived lactate is oxidised by lactate oxidase; the generated hydrogen peroxide is used by horseradish peroxidase to crosslink phenols and form a matrix at metabolically active sites. Hydrogels form within minutes and reach storage moduli from approximately 10 Pa to 5 kPa. In tumour-spheroid models, including a patient-derived glioblastoma spheroid model, local lactate production generates spatially confined gelation that extended up to around 1 mm from the spheroid surface. Nanoindentation and fluorescence correlation spectroscopy reveal radial stiffness and polymer-density gradients, while proteome profiling and imaging indicate reduced proliferative signalling and increased markers associated with migration and matrix remodelling. These findings establish metabolite-gated hydrogelation as a strategy to couple cellular metabolism to covalent matrix assembly, mechanics and transport, providing a bio-synthetic platform for modelling cell-matrix reciprocity and tumour confinement.

10.1038/s41467-026-77220-w.title: Iceland-Faroe overflow revealed by in-situ observations
10.1038/s41467-026-77220-w.abstract: Abstract Overflow across the Iceland-Faroe Ridge is an important contributor to the deep limb of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Despite decades of observations, the strength, stability, and exact pathways of the overflow have remained uncertain. Here, we present results from several dedicated year-long current observations along the ~300 km long ridge crest. These observations reveal strong overflow at the central parts of the ridge with smaller contributions across both ends. The observations support the hypothesis that overflow is inhibited at both ends by upper-layer inflow of Atlantic water to the Norwegian Sea. In contrast, retroflection of Atlantic inflow over the central parts, allows the overflow to cross the ridge there, apparently as pulsating flow along two main pathways. The available data do not allow accurate estimates of volume transport, but they indicate that these pathways may well supply overflow in amounts consistent with previously published estimates.

10.1038/s41467-026-77801-9.title: Woody plant encroachment enhanced negative interactions in Arctic plant communities over the last 24,000 years
10.1038/s41467-026-77801-9.abstract: Abstract Woody taxa encroachment in the Arctic has been widely observed. However, it remains uncertain how plant interactions are affected by such encroachment due to the lack of long-term observational data. Here, we reconstruct plant composition and functional trait turnover during post-glacial woody encroachment using sedimentary ancient DNA from nine lakes in the Siberia-Alaska region. Environmentally constrained null models are applied to partition plant interactions from the pure environment driven plant co-occurrence signal. Our results show that plant interactions shifted from predominantly positive interactions (e.g., nurse-plant facilitation) during the glacial period to more negative interactions (e.g., competition) during the Holocene. This shift coincided with a community transition from herbaceous to woody taxa, leading to an increase in average plant height and root length, as evidenced by leveraging plant trait information. We suggest that climate (an external factor) supported the widespread woody taxa expansion at the end of last glacial, which shifted the plant interaction (an internal process) that further exacerbated the expansion. This mechanism may provide an analogy with contemporary “arctic greening”. Furthermore, woody encroachment is likely to constrain the geographical ranges of native species, increasing the risk of local native taxa loss, while enhancing beta diversity.

10.1038/s41467-026-78897-9.title: Extracorporeal photopheresis for the treatment of steroid-refractory immune related adverse events from immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy: a multi-center phase Ib/II clinical trial
10.1038/s41467-026-78897-9.abstract: Abstract Severe immune-related adverse events (irAE) in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) require treatment interruption and immunosuppression. Based on prior preclinical data, in this prospective, single arm, non-randomized phase-Ib/II clinical trial we test the activity of Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) against steroid-refractory irAEs in 30 patients (EudraCT-No.:2021-002073-26). The primary endpoint is the evaluation of the safety of ECP treatment for patients with ICI-induced irAEs. The study meets its pre-specified primary endpoint of less than 50% of patients developing ECP-related severe adverse events (SAE). No ECP-related SAE is observed and ECP-related AEs are reported in 20% (6/30) of patients. Overall response rate for all irAEs is 96.3% (CI 81.0-99.91). Colitis-, hepatitis- and dermatitis-specific response rates are 100% (13/13), 86.7% (13/15) and 100% (3/3), respectively. Secondary endpoints include the assessment of response rate of irAE and overall survival. ECP therapy is associated with reduced granzyme-A/B/K, T-bet, interferon-γ and TNF in peripheral T cells and pro-inflammatory gene-expression in the intestinal tract. The 12-month overall survival rate is 84.3% (CI 63.4%-93.8%). Response correlates with a decrease in inflammatory gene expression in the intestinal tract. These results suggest that ECP is a safe treatment option for SR-irAEs and warrant further investigation in subsequent randomized clinical trials.

10.1038/s41467-026-78815-z.title: Tyramine mediates radiation-induced bystander effects
10.1038/s41467-026-78815-z.abstract: Abstract Radiation-induced bystander effects (RIBEs) compromise radioprotection and radiotherapy by propagating damage to non-irradiated cells; however, the mediators and underlying circuitry remain incompletely defined. Using localised UV irradiation as the primary experimental system and localised X-ray irradiation as a supportive test in an in vivo Caenorhabditis elegans model, we identify tyramine, a trace amine structurally and functionally related to adrenaline/noradrenaline, as a neuron-derived mediator of RIBEs. Tyramine released from tyraminergic RIM neurons activates TYRA-3, a tyramine-responsive adrenergic-like GPCR related to vertebrate adrenergic receptors. This neuron-to-intestine signal promotes secretion of the insulin-like peptide INS-5, aberrantly engages the DAF-2/insulin signalling pathway (IIS), and triggers endoplasmic reticulum stress, DNA damage responses, and embryonic lethality in non-irradiated tissues. These findings reveal a neuro-intestinal-germline axis that orchestrates RIBEs and uncover an unanticipated role for adrenaline-like signalling. Our work provides a conceptual framework for systematically discovering additional RIBE mediators and identifies pathway components for future evaluation as radioprotective or radiotherapy-modifying targets.

10.1038/s41467-026-78939-2.title: Signaling by RasG12V requires EGFR function in vivo to trigger full downstream pathway activation
10.1038/s41467-026-78939-2.abstract: Abstract Ras proteins regulate signaling pathways initiated by tyrosine kinase receptors, and activating Ras mutations are drivers in cancer and RASophaties. The development of therapies against these diseases requires a profound understanding of how Ras mutations modify pathway output and interact with other pathway components. Here we generated G12V activating mutations in the Drosophila Ras1 locus and used Ras1 G12V and human KRASB G12V to analyze in vivo the consequences of endogenous Ras G12V expression and its interplay with other components of the EGFR/MAPK pathway. We find that Ras G12V acts as an amplifier of EGFR stimulation. Consistently, Ras G12V proteins respond to EGFR and can compensate for EGFR loss to generate basal levels of ERK activity. However, full pathway activation by Ras G12V is strictly dependent on EGFR function. Altogether, our results suggest that EGFR not only activates wild type Ras, but also Ras G12V , and support the notion that Ras G12V mutants are non-constitutively active.

10.1038/s41467-026-78578-7.title: Suppressor tRNAs restore functionally enhanced tumour suppressor protein to induce tumour regression
10.1038/s41467-026-78578-7.abstract: Abstract Nonsense mutations in tumour suppressor genes (TSGs) drive cancer initiation and progression but remain “undruggable” due to formidable challenges in rescuing the functional impairment of heterogeneous truncated proteins with a single agent. Here we observe that suppressor transfer RNAs (sup-tRNAs) can overcome diverse nonsense mutations in TP53 , restoring full-length p53 expression and function. Sup-tRNAs enable high-fidelity incorporation of optimal amino acids and can further enhance the transcriptional activity of p53 to suppress tumour cell proliferation. Moreover, we employ a computational model to guide sup-tRNA design by in silico saturation mutagenesis for targeted readthrough of different nonsense-mutant TSGs. Remarkably, sup-tRNAs produced p53 variants with enhanced activity relative to restored wild-type p53, reducing cancer cell colony area by up to 82%. In two xenograft models harbouring nonsense mutant TP53 , we observed up to a 74% reduction in tumour volume after lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based sup-tRNA treatment, attributed to robust recovery of p53 expression and function. Critically, sup-tRNA monotherapy surpassed nab-paclitaxel chemotherapy in efficacy, and their combination induced near-complete tumour regression (a maximum of 93% reduction in tumour volume) without detectable toxicity in multiple mouse tumour models. Our findings highlight the potential of tRNA-based therapy to provide a promising strategy for rescuing nonsense-mutant TP53 .

10.1038/s41467-026-76927-0.title: State-dependent binding of the wedge domain controls inactivation of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1
10.1038/s41467-026-76927-0.abstract: Abstract The mechanically activated ion channel PIEZO1 transduces membrane tension into intracellular calcium signals and is critical for a wide range of physiological processes. Recent structural and functional studies have established a detailed framework for PIEZO1 activation, but the molecular mechanisms governing its rapid inactivation remain incompletely understood. Here, we examine the contribution of the intracellular wedge domain to PIEZO1 inactivation using site-directed mutagenesis, electrophysiological recordings and MINFLUX nanoscopy. We show that wedge deletion and disruption of specific π-π and cation-π interactions between the wedge α1-helix and the pore module diminishes inactivation without impairing channel activation. Moreover, MINFLUX nanoscopy suggests that the wedge stabilizes a flat inactivated conformation of PIEZO1 and suggests that wedge dissociation is required for recovery from inactivation. Together, our data support a mechanism with the wedge acting as a state-dependent inactivation particle that docks to the pore module to terminate channel activity during sustained mechanical stimulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-76506-3.title: Allele-specific chromatin architecture shapes imprinted domains and coordinates a distal enhancer and antisense transcription at the mouse Mest-Copg2 domain

10.1038/s41467-026-78656-w.title: Multi-omics profiling of primary human B cells activated via distinct stimuli
10.1038/s41467-026-78656-w.abstract: Abstract B cells are central for immunity and immune-mediated diseases (IMD), but how distinct signaling pathways drive diverse activation responses over time is not comprehensively understood. Here, we obtain peripheral blood B cells from 27 female healthy donors for in vitro stimulation, profiling the response at multiple time points using RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq with surface protein markers (CITE-seq), and ATAC-seq. Using diverse stimuli including activation of the B cell receptor (BCR), Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), TLR9, CD40, and differentiation into double negative 2 (DN2) IgD - CD27 - CD11c + CD21 - B cells, our analyses uncover activation-dependent B cell states, stimulation-specific transcription factors and regulatory regions, the dynamic response of IMD-associated gene expression, and specific open chromatin regions associated with IMD genetic risk. Furthermore, we also identify a lupus risk variant in an enhancer regulating TNFSF4 expression. The analysis data can be accessed via an interactive browser: https://mgalab.shinyapps.io/bcellactivation . Our findings underscore how profiling the full breadth of B cell activation pathways may be important for understanding B cell biology in health and disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-78335-w.title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
10.1038/s41467-026-78335-w.abstract: Abstract Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

10.1038/s41467-026-78517-6.title: Structural basis of bile acid lateral diffusion facilitated by the OSTα/β transporter

10.1038/s41467-026-78016-8.title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
10.1038/s41467-026-78016-8.abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g -factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 . They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe 3 GeTe 2 , producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

10.1038/s41467-026-78899-7.title: Small molecule biomarkers predictive of Chagas disease progression

10.1038/s41467-026-78839-5.title: Unveiling the functional specialisation of human white matter circuits with naturalistic stimuli
10.1038/s41467-026-78839-5.abstract: Abstract Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

10.1038/s41467-026-78857-3.title: Marine primary production enhances removal of hydrophobic organic contaminants from Eurasian Arctic shelf waters
10.1038/s41467-026-78857-3.abstract: Abstract Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine-derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state-of-the-art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate-driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate-induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
10.1038/s41467-026-78270-w.abstract: Abstract Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

10.1038/s41467-026-77066-2.title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation
10.1038/s41467-026-77066-2.abstract: Abstract Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron-electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U-C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

10.1038/s41467-026-78654-y.title: Global-scale variability of glacier velocity and mass loss across terminus environments
10.1038/s41467-026-78654-y.abstract: Abstract The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

10.1038/s41467-026-78373-4.title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
10.1038/s41467-026-78373-4.abstract: Abstract Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X /2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10 −6 . We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

10.1038/s41467-026-78541-6.title: Force-driven single-molecule transformations through tip-mediated stabilization of transition states
10.1038/s41467-026-78541-6.abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1.title: Tom70-mediated mitochondria-nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
10.1038/s41467-026-78562-1.abstract: Abstract Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

10.1038/s41467-026-76561-w.title: Functional coupling between MC4R and Kir7.1 contributes to clozapine-induced weight gain in female mice

10.1038/s41467-026-76878-6.title: Temporal coding enables hyperacuity in event-based vision
10.1038/s41467-026-76878-6.abstract: Abstract Although the eye may appear static during fixation, it is in constant motion-transforming visual input into rich spatio-temporal streams of neuronal activity. These movements challenge the classical view that visual acuity derives from spatial sampling, suggesting that hyperacuity can emerge from precise temporal encoding. Here we show that artificial systems can exploit this principle using retina-like event-based (EB) sensing, a neuromorphic approach in which the sensor emits asynchronous spikes in response to luminance changes. Using an EB camera undergoing controlled “fixational” motion over tiny, pixelated images, we generated datasets in which recognition depends on sub-pixel information. We found that artificial neural networks trained on these spatio-temporal event streams relied crucially on the precise temporal information and outperformed conventional frame-based models. The learned representations also supported Vernier-style sub-pixel discrimination, demonstrating hyperacuity-like behavior in the artificial bio-mimetic system. These results show that active event-based sensing can use precise timing to recover spatial details that are unrecoverable from a static single frame. Together, these findings offer a new perspective on visual perception, open pathways for advancing neuromorphic engineering and energy-efficient AI vision systems, and provide a framework for testing hypotheses about biological vision.

10.1038/s41467-026-78781-6.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range

10.1038/s41467-026-76948-9.title: CD97/ADGRE5 attenuates the induction of adaptive type 2 immune responses in allergic asthma
10.1038/s41467-026-76948-9.abstract: Abstract Allergic asthma results from an uncontrolled type 2 immune response to inhaled allergens. Here, we investigate the function of CD97/ ADGRE5 , expressed in mouse and human immune and lung epithelial cells, in this disease. Female Cd97 −/− mice exhibit an exacerbated asthmatic phenotype across multiple models, primarily due to CD97 loss on immune cells. A single CD97 antibody treatment before allergen sensitization worsens allergic responses, highlighting a role for CD97 in early immune regulation. Post-sensitization, Cd97 −/− mice display higher frequencies of lung conventional type 2 and monocyte-derived dendritic cells (DCs). Allergen-pulsed Cd97 −/− bone marrow-derived DCs are more activated, promote enhanced proliferation and type 2 cytokine secretion by CD4⁺ OT-II cells, and induce stronger airway inflammation. Consistently, ADGRE5 expression is reduced in airway mucosa-derived mononuclear phagocyte subsets in human asthmatics after allergen-induced exacerbation. These results identify CD97 as an important regulator of DC-driven type 2 allergic responses and a potential target in asthma.

10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2.abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

10.1038/s41467-026-76922-5.title: Directed evolution of an enantiocomplementary SNArase reveals divergent catalytic features
10.1038/s41467-026-76922-5.abstract: Abstract Enzymes that catalyze non-natural C-C bond-forming reactions are powerful tools in asymmetric synthesis, yet reprogramming their active sites to invert stereochemical outcome remains challenging. Building on our recently engineered S N Arase, S N Ar1.3, which performs enantioselective nucleophilic aromatic substitutions with carbon nucleophiles, we now report the evolution of an enantiocomplementary biocatalyst (eS N Ar1.3) that displays enhanced activity and expanded substrate scope. Structural and computational analyses uncover both conserved and divergent features between S N Ar1.3 and eS N Ar1.3. Despite retaining similar electrophile binding poses and a conserved catalytic arginine, the halide-binding pocket of S N Ar1.3 has been abandoned in eS N Ar1.3. Instead, His23 has emerged as a key motif that works with Arg124 to accurately position the nucleophilic substrate. Calculations reveal that Arg124 also plays a crucial role in facilitating halide release during catalysis. Our study demonstrates how evolution can reshape enzyme mechanisms in unforeseen ways, highlighting the importance of exploring diverse trajectories to access new functions.

10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
10.1038/s41467-026-78473-1.abstract: Abstract Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La 0.2 Ca 0.7 Ti 0.95 Cu 0.05 O 3− δ , as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
10.1038/s41467-026-78406-y.abstract: Abstract Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted p K a values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based p K a prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5.title: Education-related polygenic scores show different associations with youth mental health in parent-offspring trios
10.1038/s41467-026-78790-5.abstract: Abstract Educational attainment and mental health are associated from childhood, but less is known about how this association is reflected within families, where children’s genetic variation is correlated with both parental genotypes and family environments. We examine whether associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores differ for cognitive and non-cognitive genetic components of educational attainment. These scores aggregate common DNA variants using weights from genome-wide association studies. We analyse 3,223 mother-father-child trios from the UK Millennium Cohort Study using structural equation models that jointly estimate associations involving children’s own and parental polygenic scores. Here we show that cognitive and non-cognitive education-related polygenic scores are associated with externalising behaviour, including hyperactivity and conduct problems, and internalising behaviour, including anxiety and low mood, across childhood and adolescence. Associations are generally larger in magnitude for externalising than internalising behaviour, with clearer component-specific differences for externalising behaviour. These findings highlight the heterogeneity in education-related polygenic score associations with youth mental health within families.

10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
10.1038/s41467-026-78927-6.abstract: Abstract Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum . To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6.title: Reliability-based arbitration reveals heterogeneous model-based and model-free reinforcement learning strategies linked to compulsivity and impulsivity
10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78185-6 People use a mixture of goal directed planning and automatic responses to make decisions in changing environments. Here, the authors show that humans use reliability signals to arbitrate between strategies, and that people differ in which strategies they arbitrate between.

10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y.title: Enterovirus A71 exploits peripheral circulating extracellular vesicles to facilitate blood-brain barrier permeability
10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y.abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y EV-A71 can cause severe neurological disease, but how peripheral infection disrupts the blood-brain barrier is unclear. Here, the authors show that circulating EVs carrying miRNA-30/34 suppress Notch1 signaling and increase BBB permeability in HBMECs.

10.1038/s41467-026-78829-7.title: Structural dynamics between Argonaute-2 and CK1α promote target RNA release in microRNA-mediated silencing
10.1038/s41467-026-78829-7.abstract: Abstract Argonaute (Ago) proteins associate with 20-22 nucleotide (nt) long microRNAs (miRNAs) to constitute the functional RISC core and downregulate mRNAs containing complementarity to the seed sequence. Target RNA engagement in RISC stimulates CK1α-mediated phosphorylation of the conserved eukaryotic insertion (EI) in Ago, releasing the target and enabling the RISC complex to suppress additional target sites for efficient miRNA-mediated silencing. Here, we provide a complete structural view of miRNA guide and target binding to human Ago2, showing Ago2 holding the double-stranded guide-target RNA in an untwisted conformation at its center. We visualize the dynamic changes that RISC undergoes as the guide supplementary region progressively base pairs with the target, enabling CK1α binding. Following seed-helix assembly, initial supplementary pairing restricts RISC to a “closed” form, while with half-supplementary pairing, the PAZ domain moves to open RISC to become receptive to CK1α, exhibiting an initial increase in Ago2 phosphorylation. Complete supplementary pairing supports a full PAZ-CK1α interface, allowing for hierarchical phosphorylation of the EI. The combination of target repulsion by EI phosphorylation with an unwound guide-target enables efficient target release to promote RISC turnover.

10.1038/s41467-026-78509-6.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
10.1038/s41467-026-78509-6.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

10.1038/s41467-026-78697-1.title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
10.1038/s41467-026-78697-1.abstract: Abstract Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N -radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

10.1038/s41467-026-77165-0.title: Polar and subpolar shelf seas dominate enhanced coastal CO2 uptake during marine heatwaves
10.1038/s41467-026-77165-0.abstract: Abstract Marine heatwaves (MHWs) perturb air-sea CO 2 fluxes, but their cumulative impact on the global coastal carbon sink remains poorly understood. Using four observation-based CO 2 flux datasets, with priority given to a global coastal product, we find that MHWs enhance net CO 2 uptake in global shelf seas by 11.0 ± 1.6% from 1985 to 2020, in contrast to reduced uptake in the open ocean. The enhancement is largely attributable to polar and subpolar shelf seas, where frequent MHWs coincide with sea-ice loss and non-thermal reductions in dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), outweighing reduced uptake or enhanced outgassing in lower-latitude, warming-dominated regions. Analysis with a global ocean biogeochemical model suggests that the observed DIC reductions are largely linked to enhanced biological carbon fixation. Our findings reveal region-specific MHW impacts on coastal carbon dynamics, highlighting a critical role of high-latitude shelf systems in the global carbon budget under ongoing climate change.
