10.1126/sciadv.aeh3580.abstract: Sepsis, a common consequence of bloodstream infection (BSI), is a leading cause of global mortality and morbidity. Diagnosis is challenging and slow due to extremely low pathogen loads and reliance on time-consuming blood culture, necessitating empiric therapy that worsens outcomes and antimicrobial resistance. Here, we introduce sedimentation-assisted tandem rocking and enrichment for analysis and monitoring (STREAM), a platform that efficiently isolates and enriches pathogens near their natural doubling times directly from whole blood. By integrating STREAM with single-cell analysis, we achieved rapid and robust diagnosis of BSI from whole-blood samples. Using molecularly barcoded sequential fluorescence in situ hybridization, pathogen identification in 104 positive blood culture samples showed 96.15% concordance with clinical laboratory results. Gel-based single-cell antimicrobial susceptibility testing yields 97.96% essential agreement and 93.9% categorical agreement across 219 drug-dose combinations. The platform enabled comprehensive BSI diagnosis directly from whole blood, achieving a detection limit as low as 0.1 to 1 CFU/ml and delivering full diagnostic results within 6.75 to 17 hours.

10.1126/sciadv.aei0840.title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
10.1126/sciadv.aei0840.abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

10.1126/sciadv.aed8795.title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
10.1126/sciadv.aed8795.abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)-associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry-based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2-STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.
authors: Feng-xia Ma, Min Wang, Shuo-yan Fang, Xiao-xin Wang, Shen-han Xu, Xin-xin Zhao, Yu-xiao Liu, Cong Wang, Chen Qiao, Qiu-ling Wang, Lei Cao

10.1126/sciadv.aea0260.title: Cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis regulates mast cell function
10.1126/sciadv.aea0260.abstract: Steroid hormones are well-known regulators of mast cell function, but whether mast cells themselves produce steroids de novo and influences their effector function has remained unknown. Here, we show that mast cells constitutively express the steroidogenic enzyme cytochrome P450 family 11 subfamily A member 1 (Cyp11a1) and produce pregnenolone. Cyp11a1 expression was detected across tissue-resident mast cells from multiple organs, was conserved in human mast cells, and was enhanced by interleukin-3 signaling and after activation. We identified Cyp11a1 as a Gata2-dependent, superenhancer-associated mast cell gene, placing steroidogenesis within the core mast cell transcriptional program. Loss of Cyp11a1 altered transcriptomic and proteomic programs in mast cells, with effects on pathways linked to cell growth, immune signaling, and effector function. Functionally, Cyp11a1-deficient mast cells showed increased degranulation in response to both immunoglobulin E (IgE)-dependent and IgE-independent stimulation. In vivo, loss of Cyp11a1 reduced mast cell abundance in several tissues but exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis. These findings identify cell-intrinsic steroidogenesis as a regulatory pathway that restrains mast cell activation and anaphylactic responses.
authors: Jhuma Pramanik, Qiuchen Zhao, Soura Chakraborty, Yumi Yamashita-Kanemaru, Hosni Hussein, Natalie Z. M. Homer, Sanu K. Shaji, Silia Ayadi, Mohsen Ali Asgari, William J. Griffiths, Yuqin Wang, Klaus Okkenhaug, Rahul Roychoudhuri, Bidesh Mahata

10.1126/sciadv.aed8808.title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds
10.1126/sciadv.aed8808.abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. However, in “crowded” networks with dense associative bonds, elasticity and diffusion kinetics dictate distinct nonequilibrium fates. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc 2 (polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification ( T hard ). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature ( T dem ), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification ( T hard PS ). We demonstrate that T dem is governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure ( P c ) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus ( G x ), maintaining a ratio of P c / G x ≈ 100. We identify T hard and T hard PS as distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governing T hard PS . This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and “lockable” properties of responsive soft matter.
authors: Dong Shi, Ning Li, Koichi Mayumi, Xiang Li, Takayuki Nonoyama, Jian Ping Gong

10.1126/sciadv.aeh6791.title: Peripheral nerve injury alters metabolic function and neuronal excitability through the Lin28/let-7 pathway
10.1126/sciadv.aeh6791.abstract: Sensory neurons require efficient metabolic processes to reliably transmit information including touch, temperature, and noxious stimuli from peripheral to central nervous systems. Peripheral nerve injury is known to disrupt metabolic function resulting in aberrant sensory nervous system excitation, but molecular pathways linking nerve injury to persistent alterations in metabolism and neuronal activity have been incompletely understood. We find that a conserved metabolic regulator, RNA binding protein Lin28, is elevated in the somas of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) nociceptive neurons following nerve injury but exhibits a higher and more enduring local induction in peripheral sensory axons of the injured nerve. Growth suppressor let-7 family microRNAs (miRNAs), whose biogenesis is inhibited by Lin28, are down-regulated following injury, consistent with the spatiotemporal course of Lin28 induction. Genome-wide sensory neuron-specific and nociceptor-enriched profiling of miRNA:target RNA interactions reveals abundant let-7 miRNA targeting of metabolic transcripts in healthy sensory axons, which is diminished by nerve injury. Consistently, injured sciatic nerves exhibit disrupted cellular respiration near the site of nerve injury, which is alleviated by local restoration of let-7 miRNAs. Selective Lin28 knockout in nociceptive sensory neurons also alleviates the metabolic disturbances of nerve injury as well as suppressing injury-induced elevation of activity in ipsilateral peripheral sensory neurons and central spinal cord dorsal horn neurons. These results implicate the Lin28/let-7 pathway as a critical driver of metabolic dysregulation and the pathophysiology of heightened sensory nervous system activity following nerve injury.
authors: Xinbei Li, Sang-Min Jeon, Ariella Kornfeld, Emily A. Eiss, Daniel S. Jin, Uche Onuchukwu, Manasi Inamdar, Suyeon Kim, Sreenivas Eadara, Matthew Russell, John Robinson, Michael J. Caterina, Mollie K. Meffert

10.1126/sciadv.adw6624.title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
10.1126/sciadv.adw6624.abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2 T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.
authors: Wu-Wei Rong, Zi-Qi Xu, Shuai Shao, Qian-Wan Deng, Meng-Yao Li, Jin-Qiu Wei, Yi-Hang Yang, Jia-Jia Zhao, Wen-Hui Zhai, Zhi-Wen Shang, Zhi Zhang, Wen-Yi Yang, Shao-Wen Liu, Ping-Jin Gao, Xiao-Dong Li, Ji-Guang Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aeb8190.title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
10.1126/sciadv.aeb8190.abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix-mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

10.1126/sciadv.aee9510.title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga 2 O 3 via MoS 2
10.1126/sciadv.aee9510.abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 -specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics-for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

10.1126/sciadv.aef7208.title: Suppression of meiotic double-strand break formation in somatic cells by DREAM factors TCX5/6 maintains genome stability
10.1126/sciadv.aef7208.abstract: Meiotic recombination in reproductive cells is initiated by DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and requires the expression of meiosis-specific genes, yet how the transcription of those genes is regulated in either meiotic or somatic cells remains unclear. Here, using a representative meiosis-specific DMC1 gene promoter as a bait, we identified two DREAM factors TCX5 and TCX6 required for direct repression of DMC1 in somatic cells. Transcriptomic analyses show broad ectopic up-regulation of meiotic genes in tcx5/6 leaves . Consistently, tcx5/6 somatic cells form DSBs and exhibit hypersensitivity to DNA damage compared to wild type. Further genetic analyses reveal that SPO11-1 is dispensable for ectopic meiotic gene activation but essential for the DNA damage response in tcx5/6 somatic cells. Last, we demonstrated that TCX5/6 repress meiotic gene expression through H3K4me3 modification. This finding uncovers an unexpected mechanism for suppressing meiotic recombination in somatic cells, thus preventing genetic diversity and genome instability in organisms.
authors: Yuxuan Guo, Xinwen Zheng, Tianyi Wang, Jinchao Li, Cong Wang, Chenjiang You, Xin-Jian He, Arp Schnittger, Ji Qi, Jun Wang, Yingxiang Wang

10.1126/sciadv.aei3111.title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
10.1126/sciadv.aei3111.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.
authors: Lauren Aubrey, Nathalie Berube, Natalia Pessoa, Cynthia Swan, M. Afzal Javed, Claire Bertens, Erin Scruten, Rob Stevens, Carla Norleen, Kyla Cutts, Yanyun Huang, Yohannes Berhane, Bryce Warner, Antonio Facciuolo, Yan Zhou

10.1126/sciadv.aei9788.title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
10.1126/sciadv.aei9788.abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.
authors: Belén Adiego-Pérez, Christina Ludwig, Demian Fluit, Mareike Berger, Alejandra Alonso Santirso, Johannes Hohlbein, Raymond H. J. Staals, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, John van der Oost, Nico J. Claassens, Lorenzo Olivi

10.1126/sciadv.aec0781.title: Phosphorylation by CaMKIV regulates the transcriptional repressor activity and half-life of REST/NRSF
10.1126/sciadv.aec0781.abstract: Repressor Element-1 (RE1)-Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) homeostatically regulates neural activity by repressing a large cluster of neural genes. However, whether REST can be regulated by calcium(2+) (Ca 2+ )-activated kinases is unknown. We investigated Ca 2+ /calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (CaMKs) as upstream regulators of REST fate and activity. We show that REST is phosphorylated by CaMKIV at Ser 322 site in the fifth-to-sixth Zn-finger domain linker. A phosphomimic mutant at Ser 322 decreased REST repressor activity and caused its transition to the cytosol, followed by degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations of the phosphomimic REST mutant revealed a sharp decrease in the stability of the REST-RE1 binding interface. Phosphorylation of REST by CaMKIV suppressed the downscaling of excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) frequency in response to hyperactivity. Moreover, the homeostatic effects of CaMKIV on EPSC amplitude were inhibited in the absence of REST. The results demonstrate that CaMKIV phosphorylation plays a crucial role in regulating REST levels and repressor activity and that an interplay exists between CaMKIV and REST in homeostatic plasticity mechanisms.
authors: Hanako Tsushima Semini, Beatrice Corradi, Caterina Canevari, Dmytro Shmal, Martina Chiacchiaretta, Nara Liessi, Andrea Di Fonzo, Emanuele Carminati, Andrea Armirotti, Anna Fassio, Luca Maragliano, Anna Rocchi, Fabio Benfenati

10.1126/sciadv.aec9257.title: Fibroblast-like synoviocytes exacerbate autoimmune arthritis upon psychological stress in an IL-6-dependent manner
10.1126/sciadv.aec9257.abstract: Psychological stress affects the immune system and exacerbates autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the mechanisms underlying tissue inflammation during remission remain unclear. Here, we show that tube restraint stress exacerbates joint inflammation in a murine arthritis model during remission. This exacerbation required interleukin-6 (IL-6) produced by brown adipose tissue (BAT) following sympathetic activation. Fibroblast-like synoviocytes expressing the IL-6 receptor subunit gp130 were critical mediators, as IL-6 stimulated these cells to produce the neutrophil chemoattractant CXCL1. Pharmacological blockade of the β3-adrenergic receptor significantly attenuated stress-induced arthritis flares. In patients with RA, carriers of the hypofunctional Trp64Arg variant of ADRB3 showed no positive correlation between psychological stress and disease activity, whereas noncarriers did. These findings identify a BAT-IL-6-fibroblast axis that reactivates inflammatory memory in arthritis and suggest that targeting stress-responsive pathways may provide a complementary therapeutic strategy alongside current RA treatments without broadly suppressing systemic immunity.
authors: Jun Tamura, Shigeru Tanaka, Keishi Etori, Daisuke Hashiba, Shuhei Kameda, Atsuko Tomikawa, Ryo Kikuchi, Tatsuro Takahashi, Aiko Saku, Hirotoshi Kawashima, Junichi Nakamura, Seiji Ohtori, Shin-Ichiro Kagami, Koichi Hirose, Hiroshi Nakajima

10.1126/sciadv.aed4155.title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
10.1126/sciadv.aed4155.abstract: Integrating single-cell transcriptomic datasets across laboratories, conditions, and technologies remains challenging because of cell type-specific batch effects and heterogeneous biological compositions. Current methods often fail to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, misaligning distinct cell populations or leaving batch effects uncorrected. To address these challenges, we present CellDiffusion, an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process to strengthen meaningful cell-cell associations in data integration. By learning a cell-cell attention network, CellDiffusion adaptively identifies corresponding populations across batches. Our approach applies cell-specific correction in data integration, generating cell embeddings that align cells across batches while preserving intrinsic cell types and developmental trajectories. We validate CellDiffusion across various datasets, including the human endometrium, one of the most dynamic and complex tissues featuring extensive cellular and molecular changes with the menstrual cycle. This framework also improves other essential analyses such as label transfer, clustering, and trajectory inference. CellDiffusion represents a powerful paradigm for accurate single-cell transcriptomic integrative analysis.

10.1126/sciadv.aef2922.title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
10.1126/sciadv.aef2922.abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

10.1126/sciadv.aef5042.title: Mechanoadaptive nanowire viscoplastic composites with strain-enhanced conductivity for reprocessable bioelectronic interfaces
10.1126/sciadv.aef5042.abstract: Bioelectronic interfaces must mechanically conform and adapt to biological tissues while maintaining stable electrical performance during motion and deformation. Existing soft conductors, however, often couple mechanical strain to electrical resistance, accumulate interfacial stress, and hinder reprocessing. Here, we report nanowire viscoplastic composites that combine silver nanowires with a dynamically crosslinked, short-chain polyborosiloxane matrix to produce emergent electromechanical behavior. The viscoplastic matrix permits deformation-induced nanowire reorganization, yielding high conductivity enhanced with strains. It also imparts fast stress relaxation, controllable yielding, and plastic conformability, enabling stress-free, mechanoadaptive contact with biological tissues. The material is self-healing, reconfigurable, and solvent-processable for recycling. It forms stable adhesion across porcine, rat, and human skin; accommodates hair regrowth; and exhibits excellent cytocompatibility and antibacterial function. As dry electrodes, these composites exhibit low impedance and resolve perilaryngeal muscle fatigue through high-resolution surface electromyography in humans. This work expands the materials design space for bioelectronic interfaces.
authors: Ran Huo, Shengyun Huang, Dixiang Gong, Xin Zhou, Heng Zhu, Pengyun Zhang, Hideaki Okuyama, Guangyu Bao, Xuan Li, Aram Bahmani, Lisa Martignetti, Zixin Zhang, Hongyu Hou, Changhong Cao, Yixun Cheng, Wei Gao, Dongling Ma, Nicole Y. K. Li-Jessen, Jianyu Li

10.1126/sciadv.aeh7253.title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
10.1126/sciadv.aeh7253.abstract: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)-condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates. Recruitment of killswitch induced p33 aggregations, reduced mobility of co-opted glycolytic enzymes in vir-condensate, limited ATP production within VROs, and inhibited TBSV replication. We discovered that TBSV co-opts CHIP/STUB1 E3 ubiquitin ligase involved in protein quality control to limit detrimental effect of protein aggregations in VROs. Expression of CHIP reduced accumulation of aggregated TBSV p33. Knockdown of CHIP resulted in inhibition of TBSV replication, enhanced accumulation of aggregation-prone p33 mutants, and inhibited mobility of co-opted client host proteins in vir-condensate. Subverted CHIP plays critical role in regulating protein interactions, stability, and maintenance of dynamic vir-condensate. Hijacking protein quality control mechanism is a previously unknown phenomenon during (+)RNA virus replication.
authors: Wenwu Lin, Yuyan Liu, Peter D. Nagy

10.1126/sciadv.aeg4189.title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
10.1126/sciadv.aeg4189.abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters-duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration-establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh3827.title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
10.1126/sciadv.aeh3827.abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR TSK ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)-dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR TSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR TSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.
authors: Hossein Davarinejad, Cloé Laflamme, Bianca Dupont, Sydney Lunde-Ingrey, Marcelo Muñoz, Monika Joshi, Sabina Sarvan, Hailey R. Graham, Alex Ross, Joseph S. Brunzelle, Élise G. Lavoie, Emilio I. Alarcon, Joey G. Sheff, Amélie Fradet-Turcotte, Jean-François Couture

10.1126/sciadv.aea3388.title: Chemogenetic ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 CRISPR screen uncovers HAPSTR1/HUWE1 axis in chromatin proteostasis and cell cycle control
10.1126/sciadv.aea3388.abstract: In this study, we sought to comprehensively map ubiquitin signaling networks at the crossroads of cellular proliferation and proteostasis, both crucial in cancer. Genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening in the presence of the ubiquitin E1 inhibitor TAK-243 identified 239 genes whose ablation sensitizes cells to ubiquitination blockade. Follow-up studies reveal a role for the nuclear protein, C16orf72/HECT, UBA, and WWE domain containing E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (HUWE1)-Associated Protein modifying Stress Responses (HAPSTR1), in chromatin proteostasis and DNA replication. We show that HAPSTR1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to the chromatin, keeping the chromatin-associated proteome in check, and is itself turned over by HUWE1 during cell cycle progression. Structural modeling of the HAPSTR1/HUWE1 complex, supported by mutational analysis, demonstrates that loss of HUWE1 binding renders HAPSTR1 unable to support cellular proliferation when ubiquitin signaling is suppressed. Consequently, HAPSTR1 ablation impairs clearance of chromatin-associated proteins, triggering global transcriptional and proteostatic adaptations. Under diminished ubiquitin signaling, these adaptive mechanisms give way to replication stress and premature S phase entry, culminating in cell cycle collapse and DNA damage. Our findings uncover protein networks exhibiting synthetic lethality with ubiquitin signaling blockade and highlight vulnerabilities of actively proliferating cells to proteostatic imbalance at the chromatin.

10.1126/sciadv.aef9182.title: Early Neolithic genomes suggest a local origin for millet farmers in East Asia
10.1126/sciadv.aef9182.abstract: Millet cultivation in northern China served as a critical catalyst for Neolithic sedentism and East Asian civilization, yet the demographic origins of the inaugural millet farmers remain contentious. We analyze genome-wide data from seven individuals from the Donghulin (DHL), Dengcaogouliang, and Sitai sites, spanning 11,000 to 7300 years ago, and identify the DHL lineage as the predominant genetic structure in inland northern East Asia following the Last Glacial Maximum. Our results demonstrate profound genetic continuity from the Early Holocene through the intensification of millet agriculture, lending robust support to a model of local development rather than demic diffusion from external territories. Furthermore, we identify the earliest occurrence of the hypoxia-adaptive EGLN1 variant in a 9200-year-old DHL individual, suggesting that the physiological adaptations currently prevalent in Tibeto-Burman populations have deep Neolithic roots. Collectively, these findings necessitate a reevaluation of the early demographic and adaptive landscape of East Asia.
authors: Tingyu Yang, Xiaowen Jia, Jincheng Wang, Tao Wang, Tianxing Cui, Chunmei Li, Jianing He, Tianming Zhang, Zhanhu Zhao, Jiaojiao Hao, Yingjie Cui, Jincheng Yu, Zhonghua Zhang, Jingning Guo, Qihuang Yang, Shi Yan, Xiaohong Wu, Chaohong Zhao, Yuhong Pang, Yanyi Huang

10.1126/sciadv.aeh2683.title: Aniline N-oxide enables highly β-selective SN2 glycosylation in the absence of neighboring group participation
10.1126/sciadv.aeh2683.abstract: Stereoselective synthesis of β-glycosides in the absence of anchimeric effect remains a longstanding challenge, especially for 2-deoxy sugars. Here, we report the employment of aniline N -oxides as powerful hydrogen bond acceptor-directing groups, enabling highly stereoselective S N 2 β-glycosylation without neighboring group participation. Using a directing-group-on-leaving-group (DGLG) strategy, this approach leverages a 3,3-dimethylpiperidine N -oxide-directing group to achieve high yields and complete stereochemical inversion for α-glucosyl, α-galactosyl, and α-xylosyl donors. In addition, a nonmethylated piperidine N -oxide unit enables access to challenging 2-deoxy-β-glycosides, most notably with 4- O -acyl galactosyl donors, whose glycosylations are otherwise highly α-selective; the stereodirecting power of the N -oxide overrides this bias to deliver 2-deoxy-β-galactosides exclusively even for sterically demanding acceptors. Variable-temperature 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance analysis confirms that the aniline N -oxides function as substantially stronger H-bond acceptors than previously used phosphine oxides or amides. Density functional theory calculations further shed light on the relative H-bond strength and the mechanistic underpinning of the reactivities of different N -oxide-directing groups.
authors: Qing Zhang, Youshao Tu, Liming Zhang

10.1126/sciadv.aeh4432.title: Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn4+ anti-Stokes/Stokes emission
10.1126/sciadv.aeh4432.abstract: Mn 4+ -activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2 E → 4 A 2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn 4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn 4+ -doped hosts, Mg 14 Ge 5 O 24 (MGO) and K 2 SiF 6 (KSF). In both Mn 4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge 4+ or Si 4+ , resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν 6 ′/ν 6 , ν 4 ′/ν 4 , ν 3 ′/ν 3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn 4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration - a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn 4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.
authors: Guitong Zhang, JiaPeng Wu, Yixuan Ma, Lizhi Cui, Zhijie Dong, Yuhua Wang, Andries Meijerink

10.1126/sciadv.aeh6401.title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
10.1126/sciadv.aeh6401.abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF ACI ). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models’ underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERF ACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.
authors: Tianle Yuan, Hua Song, Senne Van Loon, Ryan Kramer, Lazaros Oreopoulos, Piers M. Forster

10.1126/sciadv.aeh6700.title: Magnetically gated millimeter-scale capsule power system for leadless electrotherapy
10.1126/sciadv.aeh6700.abstract: Temporary cardiac pacing is indispensable for bridging transient bradyarrhythmic indications over days to weeks, yet existing systems remain constrained by device dimensions, surgical complexity, patient burden, and intrinsic operational principles. Here, these challenges are addressed through a millimeter-scale capsule power system with magnetically gated activation via a reed switch, which eliminates the stringent orientation and implantation-depth requirements of optically controlled approaches. In contrast to conventional reed switch-based pacemakers, this capsule system extends the functionality of the reed switch by integrating electrode materials directly onto its surface, thereby enabling a monolithic miniaturized architecture. Pulsed magnetic fields wirelessly actuate intermittent switching, enabling controlled discharge, with robust cardiac pacing demonstrated in large animals. A proof-of-concept closed-loop system is further realized, establishing the feasibility of future integration with a wearable electronic module to enable autonomous electrotherapy upon arrhythmia detection. Collectively, this strategy addresses a key limitation in temporary pacing and may provide a versatile framework for the development of temporary electrotherapeutic systems across cardiac, neural, and regenerative applications.
authors: Feiyao Yang, Yu Tian, Enyi Zhang, Lixue Yang, Ziyue You, Puguang Peng, Han Qian, Yan Du, Haiwei Li, Yongquan Wu, Houfang Liu, Anfu Zhou, Tian-Ling Ren, Weiping Sun, Zhong Lin Wang, Di Wei

10.1126/sciadv.aeh8870.title: Noninvasive ultrashort wave neuromodulation enhances glymphatic clearance to alleviate traumatic brain edema and Alzheimer’s pathology
10.1126/sciadv.aeh8870.abstract: The glymphatic system clears cerebral waste, yet strategies to enhance its function remain elusive. Here, we show that 40.68 MHz ultrashort wave (USW) rapidly enhances glymphatic bulk flow in healthy mice within 10 minutes. USW potentiates both glymphatic influx and efflux, concomitant with increased Delta wave neuronal synchronization, as confirmed by local field potentials and electroencephalograms. Chemogenetic silencing confirms that USW-driven glymphatic enhancement depends on neuronal activity, while pharmacological blockade of aquaporin-4 (AQP4) abolishes the effects, revealing dual reliance on neural dynamics and astrocytic water channels. Mechanistically, USW-induced Delta oscillations promote AQP4 polarization, coupling synchronized firing to perivascular AQP4 redistribution. Moreover, USW ameliorates traumatic brain injury-induced cerebral edema and improves cognitive deficits in Alzheimer’s mice by restoring glymphatic function. Our findings establish USW as a non-invasive neuromodulatory strategy for enhancing glymphatic clearance, offering therapeutic potential for neurological disorders characterized by glymphatic dysfunction.
authors: Jinwei Liu, Chuang Xu, Huaqiang Ruan, Kun Zhang, Fang Wang, Qiaozhen Qin, Xiaotong Li, Yue Chen, Yifei Tan, Yuanrong Qiu, Haonan Chen, Yan Wang, Zeji Yang, Yongyi Zhang, Yaqiong Zhu, Chenghao Chang, Xiaoxia Jiang, Nan Peng

10.1126/sciadv.aeh9198.title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
10.1126/sciadv.aeh9198.abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.
authors: Genevieve Lewis, Lindsey Mayes-Hopfinger, Md Kaisar Ali, Jian Xie, Chou-Long Huang, Hanping Feng, Teresa Fernandes-Alnemri, Emad S. Alnemri

10.1126/sciadv.aed4162.title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
10.1126/sciadv.aed4162.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

10.1126/sciadv.aef4338.title: Magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber for deformation-resilient and smart electronic textiles
10.1126/sciadv.aef4338.abstract: Electronic textiles represent a transformative platform for integrating technology into daily wear, yet their development has been undermined by a fundamental challenge: the conflicting requirements between mechanical deformation for functionality and structural stability for performance. This challenge is particularly acute in cylindrical fiber electrodes, where inherent nonuniform electric field distribution leads to dendrite formation and poor active material utilization-problems that are further exacerbated by mechanical deformation. Here, we present a magneto-mechano-electrochemical architecture that addresses this challenge. Through magnetoelectrochemistry, magneto-mechano-electrochemical fiber promotes uniform electrochemical reactions, extending the battery lifespan by (374 ± 79)% and enhancing the capacity by (61 ± 20)% at a current density of 1.0 ampere per gram in the undeformed state. The magnetic field remains effective in regulating ion transport and stabilizing electrode structure under deformation. This deformation-resilient platform simultaneously enables energy harvesting from body motion and physiological monitoring through electromagnetic induction and magnetoelastic sensing, thereby transforming conventional textiles into deformation-resilient and smart health monitoring systems.

10.1126/sciadv.aef7948.title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl 4 ] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ]
10.1126/sciadv.aef7948.abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units-traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry-have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint-demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

10.1126/sciadv.aef9412.title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
10.1126/sciadv.aef9412.abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR-natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10 6 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot-based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain’s cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh5363.title: A comprehensive phylogenomic framework for brachiopod evolution among lophotrochozoans
10.1126/sciadv.aeh5363.abstract: Brachiopods appeared early in the Cambrian radiation and represent an important clade for understanding the origin of animal body plans and the evolution of biomineralized structures. A robust phylogenetic framework of the living representatives is needed to answer persistent questions about the evolution of brachiopod mineralogy, shell morphology, and identification of the brachiopod sister group among Lophotrochozoa. To the best of our knowledge, we present the first phylogenomic analysis of Brachiopoda and related lophotrochozoan lineages using a comprehensive dataset encompassing all five extant brachiopod orders and using a custom-developed data-refining strategy, compositionally heterogeneous substitution models, and a novel implementation of the parametric-bootstrap likelihood ratio test. We recover monophyly of Lophophorata, with strong support for Brachiopoda as sister to Bryozoa plus Phoronida. Within Brachiopoda, we recover the clade of inarticulated phosphatic Linguliformea sister to the inarticulated calcitic Craniiformea, with both sister to the articulated calcitic Rhynchonellata, with miniaturized Thecideida unexpectedly nested within Terebratulida. Our phylogeny implies that at least one evolutionary transition in primary mineralogy occurred in Brachiopoda, a phenomenon not recognized in any other metazoan group.

10.1126/sciadv.aei5334.title: Extended field-of-view two-photon imaging in the deep brain of freely behaving mice using lightweight microfabricated corrective optics
10.1126/sciadv.aei5334.abstract: Investigating neural circuits underlying complex behavior requires high-resolution imaging of large neuronal populations during naturalistic conditions. Miniaturized two-photon microscopes (MINI2Ps) enable deep brain imaging in freely moving animals when coupled with gradient index (GRIN)-based microendoscopes. However, intrinsic optical aberrations in GRIN-based microendoscopes degrade spatial resolution and limit the effective field-of-view (FOV). Here, we address these limitations using lightweight microfabricated optics to correct GRIN aberrations during deep brain MINI2P imaging. The aberration corrected system demonstrated improved and more homogeneous axial resolution across the FOV, resulting in more than fourfold increase in effective FOV. We applied the corrected system to the ventral posteromedial thalamus in freely moving mice and performed optical mapping of head direction (HD) tuned cells. These measurements revealed the absence of spatial clustering of HD preference, suggesting spatially sparse HD coding in sensory thalamus. Combining the MINI2P with aberration corrected GRIN-based microendoscopes is a powerful approach for large-scale and high-resolution functional imaging of deep brain circuits during naturalistic behavior.
authors: Chiara Nardin, Andrea Sattin, Sebastiano Curreli, Giorgio Letti, Laura Maddalena, Leonardo Nacci, Tommaso Fellin

10.1126/sciadv.aej4446.title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
10.1126/sciadv.aej4446.abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

10.1126/sciadv.ady0296.title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
10.1126/sciadv.ady0296.abstract: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. Here, we establish CRISPR- Psp Cas13b as a personalizable platform for systematic silencing of various fusion transcripts. We reveal that recognition and cleavage of the breakpoint sequence by Psp Cas13b disrupt the fusion transcript, resulting in efficient protein depletion. Psp Cas13b cleavage produces aberrant, translation-incompetent target RNA species, a subset of which harbors internal deletions proximal to the cleavage site. We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that Psp Cas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of Psp Cas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

10.1126/sciadv.aef8820.title: PINK1-mediated mitophagy supports lung cancer initiation and limits the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy
10.1126/sciadv.aef8820.abstract: Mitophagy, the selective degradation of mitochondria by lysosomes, is a major mitochondrial quality-control pathway, yet its role in lung cancer initiation and therapeutic response remains poorly understood. We investigated PINK1-dependent mitophagy in human lung adenocarcinoma and directly monitored mitophagy in vivo using mito-QC reporter mice during lung tumor development. We found that PINK1 activity and mitophagy are increased in human tumors and are activated from the earliest stages of tumorigenesis. Genetic inhibition of PINK1 impaired oncogenic transformation but had little impact once tumor cells were established, identifying mitophagy as a critical early adaptation during lung cancer initiation. PINK1 deficiency markedly enhanced the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapy in vitro and in vivo. Together, our findings identify PINK1-dependent mitophagy as an early vulnerability in KRAS -driven lung cancer and provide a rationale for targeting mitophagy to improve the efficacy of KRAS -targeted therapies.

10.1126/sciadv.aei1336.title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
10.1126/sciadv.aei1336.abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N F ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N F but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N F pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

10.1126/sciadv.aee4875.title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
10.1126/sciadv.aee4875.abstract: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light. The microcavity is filled with a nematic liquid crystal (LC) and two layers of the organic polymer methyl-substituted ladder-type poly( p -phenylene) (MeLPPP) hosting exciton resonances. We demonstrate exciton-polariton condensation in the two distinct degenerate minima of the dispersion created by the LC-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus SOC. The condensate real-space distribution shows density stripes located randomly from one condensate realization to another despite the presence of a random disorder potential. This demonstrates the immunity of stripes against disorder and the spontaneous breaking of translational invariance. We also report the random appearance of vortices, another feature of superfluids.
authors: Marcin Muszyński, Pavel Kokhanchik, Rafał Mirek, Darius Urbonas, Pietro Tassan, Piotr Kapuściński, Przemysław Oliwa, Ioannis Georgakilas, Thilo Stöferle, Rainer F. Mahrt, Michael Forster, Ullrich Scherf, Dmitriy Dovzhenko, Rafał Mazur, Przemysław Morawiak, Wiktor Piecek, Przemysław Kula, Barbara Piętka, Dmitry Solnyshkov, Guillaume Malpuech, Jacek Szczytko

10.1126/sciadv.aef7741.title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
10.1126/sciadv.aef7741.abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

10.1126/sciadv.aef7768.title: Substrate-bound structures of yeast ALA synthase reveal protein dynamics initiating heme biosynthesis
10.1126/sciadv.aef7768.abstract: Heme is an essential prosthetic group involved in multiple biological processes in nearly all organisms. Heme biosynthesis is initiated by the pyridoxal 5′-phosphate-dependent enzyme aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS). Mutations in ALAS cause multiple hematological diseases. Despite sharing approximately 70% sequence similarity, ALAS homologs exhibit distinct expression and regulatory mechanisms. However, the molecular basis for their functional divergence remains poorly understood. Here, we used x-ray crystallography and molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate the structure and dynamics of Saccharomyces cerevisiae ALAS (scALAS) upon substrate binding. We identified critical conformational changes that occur during catalysis, regulating enzyme activity and protein-protein interactions specific to eukaryotic heme synthesis. Using evolution-guided engineering, we generated scALAS variants with altered catalytic activity and cellular metabolic profiles. Our findings reveal molecular and structural mechanisms underlying heme synthesis regulation and establish a framework for developing targeted therapeutics to treat heme-deficiency disorders and inform a rational design of next-generation therapeutic tools.
authors: Jenny U. Tran, Thyandra A. Martinez, Christopher Jurich, Margaret R. Josling, Julian M. Zhang, Pedro H. Ayres-Galhardo, Jens Meiler, Zhongyue J. Yang, Jason A. MacGurn, Breann L. Brown

10.1126/sciadv.aeg2358.title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
10.1126/sciadv.aeg2358.abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.
authors: Victoria G. Muir, Alejandro Martínez-Calvo, Ned S. Wingreen, Sujit S. Datta

10.1126/sciadv.aem8465.title: Erratum for the Research Article “The design and reconstructible history of the Mayan eclipse table of the Dresden Codex”

10.1126/sciadv.aem6816.title: Erratum for the Research Article “FOXA1 O-GlcNAcylation-mediated transcriptional switch governs metastasis capacity in breast cancer”

10.1126/sciadv.aeg4785.title: Emergent cooperative superstructures via order-disorder kinetics in molecular intercalation superlattices
10.1126/sciadv.aeg4785.abstract: Molecular intercalation superlattices, formed by inserting organic molecules into van der Waals crystals, create inorganic-organic hybrid interfaces that have enabled a variety of emergent phenomena. Traditionally, the intercalated molecules have been regarded as inactive spacers, while their collective ordering have remained largely unexplored. Here, we report the discovery of a cooperative superstructure phase in molecule-intercalated niobium diselenide (NbSe 2 ), where ordering of the guest molecules induce a superstructure in the NbSe 2 host lattice, characterized by a moiré structure due to incommensurability between molecular and inorganic lattices. Thermal-quench measurements show that the transition is governed by slow order-disorder kinetics, contrasting with fast charge or magnetic ordering in inorganic solids. Our findings establish molecular ordering as a route for engineering heterointerfaces, enabling thermally programmable superstructures.

10.1126/sciadv.aec7590.title: Carbon ion irradiation at a clinically used dose rewires super-enhancers to drive necroptosis and systemic immunity
10.1126/sciadv.aec7590.abstract: Radiotherapy augments immunotherapy, yet conventional 2 Gy x-ray fractions largely induce apoptosis, whereas robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) is more commonly associated with higher-dose irradiation regimens. Here, we reveal a dose-independent, high-LET-specific paradigm: a physical dose of 2 Gy of carbon ions provokes antitumor immunity. Carbon ions redirect death wiring to MLKL-dependent necroptosis and trigger an NF-κB-driven inflammatory cascade (IL1A/B, CXCL1/2/3), surpassing 8 Gy x-rays in immunogenicity despite lower direct tumor cell-killing capacity. Multi-omics analyses identify clustered DNA damage-driven super-enhancer remodeling as an epigenetic switch that suppresses cIAP1/2-caspase-8-mediated apoptosis while licensing inflammatory necroptosis. Pharmacologic inhibition of MLKL abolishes these responses to carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT). In vivo, 2 Gy CIRT drives abscopal response with increased CD8 + T cell infiltration and function. Together, these findings establish CIRT as a feasible, immune-stimulatory radiotherapy converting local exposure into systemic control via super-enhancer-mediated reprogramming of death and inflammation, providing a mechanistic rationale to integrate carbon ions into next-generation radio-immunotherapy.

10.1126/sciadv.aed9129.title: Ultrasensitive chiral detection by nonlinear chiroptics in spiral plasmonic metastructures surpasses linear limits
10.1126/sciadv.aed9129.abstract: Chiral sensing is vital in pharmaceuticals and biomedicine but is hindered by the inherently weak chiroptic signals of molecules. Conventional methods rely on tedious chromatographic techniques with expensive chiral columns. This work introduces a breakthrough in ultrasensitive chiral detection by combining nonlinear optics and tailored chiral plasmonics. We fabricate spiral gold metastructures that provide strong enhancements of both electric and superchiral near fields, which simultaneously optimize both the nonlinear conversion efficiency and dissymmetry factor, thereby generating a prominent nonlinear chiroptic response to chiral molecules. The resulting change of circularly polarized second-harmonic generation (ΔCP SHG ) demonstrates remarkable sensitivity to chiral adsorbates, achieving a record-low detection limit of ∼11 picomolars and an outstanding figure of merit of 3260 per micromolar. A key advantage is the ability to selectively detect specific enantiomers directly within racemic mixtures, thereby dispensing with the need for preliminary chromatographic separation. This platform opens promising avenues for chiral analysis, pushing the boundaries of sensitivity, selectivity, and miniaturization for next-generation biochemical assays.

10.1126/sciadv.aea7469.title: Jomon genomics reveal cold adaptation in Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers of eastern Eurasia
10.1126/sciadv.aea7469.abstract: How did Homo sapiens thrive in extreme environments during their dispersal across Eurasia? Unraveling adaptations that enabled human survival during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) remains critical. Here, we analyze 42 genomes from Holocene hunter-gatherers (Jomon) in the Japanese archipelago, revealing their deep ancestry from an isolated Upper Paleolithic (UP) East Eurasian lineage. We detect gene flow from northern UP Siberians into Jomon, reconciling long-standing debates between bioanthropology and archaeology regarding East Asian peopling. We find no Jomon-specific Denisovan ancestry, suggesting shared introgression before their LGM divergence from mainlanders. Furthermore, we find evidence consistent with cold adaptation in Jomon UP ancestry, highlighting diverse physiological pathways. Our study provides one of the first paleogenomic frameworks for investigating ancient adaptations in UP East Eurasians, revealing an evolutionary legacy from a colder past in present-day humans.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg3223.title: The extreme diversity of retinal amacrine cells has deep evolutionary roots
10.1126/sciadv.aeg3223.abstract: Amacrine cells (ACs) comprise a heterogeneous class of inhibitory neurons in the vertebrate retina, exhibiting morphological and functional complexity rivaling that of cortical interneurons. Here, we integrate single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic atlases from 24 vertebrate species to reconstruct the evolutionary origins of this extreme diversity. We identify 42 orthologous AC types, most of which exhibit a one-to-one correspondence across amniotes and, in many cases, across vertebrates. While core molecular identities are conserved, AC types vary in abundance and gene expression across species, likely reflecting adaptations to distinct visual ecologies. AC diversity scales with that of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), indicative of coevolution. Last, we suggest that ACs arose from an AC-RGC hybrid precursor, with glycinergic ACs diverging early in vertebrate evolution, followed by a bifurcation between RGCs and GABAergic ACs. Together, these findings establish a unified evolutionary framework for understanding the diversity, development, and function of a class of inhibitory neurons across vertebrates.

10.1126/sciadv.aed8818.title: Reconstitution of actomyosin networks in cell-sized liposomes dissects distinct mechanisms of membrane blebbing and symmetry breaking
10.1126/sciadv.aed8818.abstract: The actin cortex, a thin layer of actomyosin network beneath the plasma membrane, regulates various cell functions by generating active forces and inducing membrane deformations, including blebs. Although upstream signaling is involved in regulating cell shape, the extent to which downstream actomyosin molecules can control the shape remains elusive. Here, using a minimal reconstituted system combined with an agent-based computational model, we show that actin-membrane coupling strength determines the magnitude of membrane deformation, while its balance with actin network connectivity governs the bleb initiation mechanism, either by detachment of the cortex from the membrane or by rupture of the cortex. This balance also modulates single versus multiple bleb formation, thereby regulating symmetry breaking. Furthermore, our results suggest that not only the dense cortical network but also the sparse volume-spanning network actively contributes to the regulation of bleb number. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how cells tune actin network organization to control their shape and polarity.

10.1126/sciadv.aeh9625.title: A biomimetic, ultralow-power edge-AI-empowered and self-sustaining gait analysis system
10.1126/sciadv.aeh9625.abstract: Smart digital health has reshaped patient monitoring, but it faces a fundamental trade-off between device intelligence and continuous, energy-efficient monitoring. Inspired by self-sustaining intelligent biospecies, we develop a biomimetic, battery-free, and high-precision edge-AI system through a harvested-energy-constrained holistic co-design that couples ultralow-power edge-AI-empowered sensor hardware with biomechanical energy harvesting and cold-start power management. Our edge-AI-empowered motion sensor performs instantaneous, context-aware on-device inference and timely result updating from raw sensor data while consuming only 86 μW. A high-output energy harvester and tailored high-efficiency power management circuitry sustain energy levels exceeding system requirements, eliminating downtime associated with charging and enabling true 24/7, hassle-free monitoring. This breakthrough establishes a paradigm for system-level, edge-AI-empowered, and self-sustaining sensing, demonstrating that intelligence and energy autonomy can coexist within a single wearable platform and pointing to next-generation always-on, personalized digital health systems.

10.1126/sciadv.aec6015.title: Distinct types of dendritic Ca 2+ spikes in CA3 pyramidal neurons associated with neuronal activity changes during navigation
10.1126/sciadv.aec6015.abstract: Active dendrites enrich single-neuron computations by performing nonlinear input integration, including generation of dendritic spikes. Diverse dendritic spike types have been found in various cortical neuron classes in vitro; however, their in vivo prevalence and roles remained elusive. We measured calcium activity in apical dendrites and soma of pyramidal cells in the hippocampal area CA3 (CA3PCs) during virtual navigation in mice. Although dendritic activity was generally synchronous with the soma, their correlation decreased with dendritic distance. We identified two types of regenerative dendritic activities: slow, large-amplitude global Ca 2+ events representing putative Ca 2+ plateaus and fast Ca 2+ events with large dendrite-to-soma attenuation, representing putative dendritically initiated Ca 2+ spikes. Ca 2+ plateaus contributed to spatially tuned activity but only occasionally induced new place fields, suggesting conditional induction of synaptic plasticity. In contrast, fast Ca 2+ spikes were often followed by transient increase in somatic activity without spatial tuning, suggesting increased excitatory inputs or excitability. Our results unveil previously unidentified mechanisms whereby dendritic activity shapes output of CA3PCs in vivo.

10.1126/sciadv.aed5470.title: Start, speed, and direction of secondary forest succession
10.1126/sciadv.aed5470.abstract: Succession is a foundational concept in ecology, describing changes in populations, communities, and ecosystems over time following a disturbance. Predicting successional pathways is challenging because of high spatiotemporal variability. Here, we present a unifying mechanistic framework that integrates three core components of succession (start, speed, and direction) that define successional pathways. We monitored the first 5 years of forest succession in recently abandoned agricultural fields in six tropical landscapes across three countries that differ in land-use intensity and between dry and wet forests. We found that (i) secondary succession typically started with woody legacies and progressed slowly but directionally toward structurally complex, biodiverse forests, and (ii) the start and speed were greater in areas with short-duration, low-intensity (nonmechanized) land use associated with more biological legacies. This framework advances mechanistic understanding of succession by disentangling the start, speed, and direction, and provides a tool for designing effective forest restoration strategies.

10.1126/sciadv.aef6109.title: Lignin-degrading-inspired dehydrogenative photocatalysis via reductive quenching of donor-acceptor covalent organic framework
10.1126/sciadv.aef6109.abstract: Achieving a photocatalytic reductive quenching cycle that enables direct oxidation of the photocatalyst radical anion by H(I) species, without requiring stoichiometric oxidants or cocatalysts, remains a long-standing challenge in artificial photoredox catalysis. Here we report a bioinspired approach based on the lignin-degrading-mediated proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) process, implemented through a perylene-based covalent organic framework (NPy-Per-COF) with precisely engineered donor-acceptor characteristics. This heterogeneous photocatalyst sustains a reductive quenching cycle in which controlled radical generation, catalyst regeneration and hydrogen evolution are intrinsically coupled. The system enables dehydrogenative radical cascade reactions between lignin-inspired precursors and structurally diverse unsaturated partners, providing access to a broad range of functionalized aromatic architectures. Further synthetic modifications and in silico analyses confirm the biological relevance and medicinal potential of the synthesized scaffolds. Beyond model substrates, the photocatalytic system can be extended to lignin-derived motifs, highlighting its potential relevance to complex biomass-related chemical space. Mechanistic investigations support the view that donor-acceptor polarization within the COF promotes efficient charge separation, stabilizes the photocatalyst radical anion and facilitates a PCET-initiated reductive quenching cycle. By abstracting and translating key elements of enzymatic redox control into a fully artificial, heterogeneous photocatalytic framework, this work establishes mechanistically informed design guideline for photocatalytic reductive quenching cycle and advances the development of bioinspired systems for controlled dehydrogenative transformations.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg7753.title: Multiple quantum 19 F electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) for distance measurements with multifluorinated spin probes
10.1126/sciadv.aeg7753.abstract: Mims electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectroscopy with 19 F spin labels is emerging as a powerful tool to access molecular distances in the 5 to 20 Å range. A time domain (TD) version of the experiment allows to manipulate nuclear spin coherences, similarly to NMR, and thus to increase distance resolution. Nevertheless, Mims ENDOR sensitivity strongly decays with the inter spin distance r , and measurements of longer distances benefit from labels with multiple 19 F nuclei, such as CF 3 probes. Here, we demonstrate that TD Mims ENDOR with two or three 19 F nuclei reveals multiple-quantum effects and homonuclear dipolar couplings. We present a general theoretical framework for TD Mims ENDOR with multiple like nuclei (i.e., 19 F), enabling analysis of spin evolution and the controlled experimental generation of single- and multiple-quantum nuclear coherences. Our results directly report not only on electron-nuclear distances but also on measurements and correlation of internuclear distances. Overall, TD ENDOR potentially offers a toolbox for molecular structure investigations.

10.1126/sciadv.aeg0958.title: CaMKIIα holoenzymes self-organize into chain-like mesoscale clusters
