10.1002/adma.74476.title: Cryogenic Thermoelectric Enhancement by Nonparabolic Band-Edge Transport in Bi2Te3
10.1002/adma.74476.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective scattering of electrons near the Fermi level is the kinetic origin of the thermoelectric effect. Pronounced band nonparabolicity near the band edge is expected to promote the decoupling of a high Seebeck coefficient from high electrical conductivity; however, accessing this band-edge transport regime at low temperatures remains challenging, as defect-dominated scattering often masks the intrinsic band-structure effects. Here, we experimentally show that single-crystalline Bi 2 Te 3 can access a reduced-scattering band-edge transport regime in which the transport distribution becomes strongly energy dependent, enabling simultaneously a sizable thermopower and a high carrier mobility at cryogenic temperatures. This approach yields a record thermoelectric power factor of three times as high as that of conventional parabolic band-dominated Bi 2 Te 3 . Quantum oscillation measurements reveal multiband transport components consistent with the band-structure complexity of Bi 2 Te 3 , and magneto-thermal conductivity measurements indicate a reduced Lorenz factor and suppressed electronic thermal conductivity in the same regime. The resultant over 600% thermoelectric enhancement in conventional Bi 2 Te 3 demonstrates a practical strategy of advancement by engineering band-edge transport in strong spin-orbit coupled materials.
authors: Xuemei Wang, Shuxian Zhang, Zhiwei Chen, Xinyue Zhang, Minghao Xue, Han Zhao, Wen Li, Zhijian Yin, Jun Luo, Yanzhong Pei

10.1002/adma.74657.title: Ultrathin 2D Multivariate Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework Nanosheets for Fluorescent DNA Sensing
10.1002/adma.74657.abstract: ABSTRACT The multivariate strategy is generally incompatible with densely packed structures, as this approach typically requires porous frameworks to manage the steric demands of incorporated functional groups. Without sufficient free volume, the frameworks are prone to structural transformations driven by steric hindrance. Here, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome by exploiting an interaction hierarchy in hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (HOFs), where strong directional charge-assisted hydrogen bonds define the framework while weaker interactions accommodate steric perturbations. This enables the extension of the multivariate strategy to densely packed systems, yielding multivariate HOFs with well-defined structures and tailored functionalities. Specifically, a carboxylate-amidinium-based layered HOF (HOF-FAFU-4) was synthesized as a prototype platform. It enables the integration of diverse building blocks and precise tuning of the spatial arrangement of functional groups. Benefiting from their layered structure, these materials can be further exfoliated into ultrathin 2D nanosheets, thereby enhancing the accessibility of functional sites. These ultrathin 2D nanosheets serve as fluorescent sensing platforms for DNA detection, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 8.1 pM and demonstrating broad generality for multiple DNA analytes. This work not only broadens the scope of the multivariate strategy but also expands the structural diversity and applicability of HOFs.
authors: Xiao-Ping Zhan, Qi Yin, Jin-Ying Qin, Hong-Xin Su, Duan-Ping Hu, Lin-Yi Li, Zhi-Feng Cai, Fa-Qiang Tang, Tian-Fu Liu, Zu-Jin Lin

10.1002/adma.74582.title: Synergistic Interface Stabilization and Dynamic Defect Passivation for High-Performance Ultraviolet-Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.74582.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite major efficiency breakthroughs in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), their stability under ultraviolet (UV)-induced degradation remains challenging because photoinduced defect accumulation in the perovskite and deterioration of the buried ITO/SAM/perovskite interface occur simultaneously under illumination. We develop a bulk/interface synergistic stabilization strategy by combining dynamic perovskite defect regulation with buried-interface reinforcement. The photoisomerizable molecule 1,3,3-trimethylindolino-6'-bromobenzopyrylospiran (TIBBP) serves as a dynamic passivator. It responds to light and reversibly transitions from a closed form to an open form, enabling a continuous functional pathway from film formation to device operation. The closed form regulates crystallization and initial defects, while the UV-induced open form generates multiple active sites for passivating newly formed defects. To strengthen the buried hole-transport interface, [4-(3,6-difluoro-9H-carbazol-9-yl)phenyl]phosphonic acid (F-PhPACZ) is designed as a UV-durable SAM. The conjugated backbone improves SAM chemical stability and ITO anchoring under UV stress, while fluorine-related interactions contribute to buried-interface passivation and improved perovskite growth. By simultaneously suppressing perovskite defect evolution and buried-interface degradation, the inverted PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency of 27.18% (certified 26.65%) and markedly improved stability under UV irradiation, air exposure, and thermal aging. This work provides a device-failure-pathway-oriented strategy for efficient and stable inverted perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Yuning Zhang, Bo Yu, Tong Tang, Xiaochun Wei, Qingbin Cai, Huangzhong Yu

10.1002/adma.202507040.title: Lignin Mimicking Protein Methylation Augments the Efficacy of FOLFOX Chemotherapy by Anchoring Thymidylate Synthase
10.1002/adma.202507040.abstract: ABSTRACT FOLFOX has served as the standard chemotherapy regimen for advanced stages, specifically in the treatment of pancreatic, colorectal, and bladder cancers. However, the issues of excessive toxicity and prolonged treatment cycles persist. To address this limitation, we developed a novel methylated amino acid-modified lignin inspired by biological methylation, creating a pH-responsive charge-reversal drug delivery system for FOLFOX chemotherapy. This system stabilizes thymidylate synthase (TS) and combines with deoxyuridine monophosphate (dUMP) to demonstrate significantly improved therapeutic outcomes of FOLFOX against colorectal cancer (CRC). The FOLFOX-loaded nanodrug showed targeted antitumor activity against CRC and induced tumor cell death through multiple mechanisms, including apoptosis, necrosis, cell cycle regulation, DNA damage, and reactive oxygen species generation. Furthermore, the nano-formulation activated immune responses to enhance chemotherapeutic potency and effectively reducing renal toxicity associated with chemotherapy drugs. These findings suggest that protein methylation-mimicked lignin could be a valuable addition to current first-line chemotherapy options and holds promise for enhancing chemotherapy against solid tumors.
authors: Shiyao Song, Yan-Lai Tang, Xiaoting Liu, Jiayi Zheng, Chong Wu, Tang Li, Junhong Ye, Dianmin Xia, Yong Mei, Jingxuan Ma, Libin Huang, Xuequn Luo, Liheng Chen, Yanlin Qin, Weiling He

10.1002/adma.74636.title: A Wearable Electrochemical Patch for Sustained Local Oxygen Therapy of Chronic Wounds
10.1002/adma.74636.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable bioelectronics are dominated by low-power sensing, whereas effective therapy requires sustained molecular fluxes that conventional soft devices rarely support. A central challenge is simultaneously maintaining solid-solid charge transport, hydration-dependent ionic conduction, and biofluid resistance within a lightweight, fixture-free architecture. Here, we report a vapor-fed electrochemical materials architecture for skin-conformal oxygen delivery. The system integrates a mechanically interlocking 3D current collector/catalyst interface to stabilize electronic transport, femtosecond-laser-defined microchannels to reconstruct vapor-phase mass transport within an all-solid-state membrane electrode assembly, and a phase-selective porous barrier blocking exudate intrusion while preserving gas diffusion. This hierarchical design enables an ultralight (<4 g) patch to operate at high current densities (>100 mA cm −2 ), sustaining continuous operation for 735 h to deliver 16.8 L of high-purity (>99%) O 2 . The architecture remains stable for >500 h in simulated exudates and supports efficient transdermal oxygen transport across porcine skin. In a rat pressure-ulcer model, short-course treatment accelerates early wound closure 1.7-fold at day 3, enhancing M2 macrophage polarization and vascular normalization. These results establish a materials framework for translating wearable bioelectronics from passive information interfaces to active molecular-delivery systems.
authors: Jichen Zhao, Xuewei Kan, Xin Tang, Xin Huang, Shuo Li, Shiyu Ji, Yimin Li, Xuyan Zhao, Yi Tan, Ting Si, Guiqiang Li, Chunyu Zhao, Jun Tang, Yu Zhang, Yuen Wu

10.1002/adma.74499.title: A Low-Cost, Scalable, and Integrated Hydrogen Electrode Toward Industrial-Grade Hydrogen Batteries
10.1002/adma.74499.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous hydrogen batteries are promising candidates for large-scale energy storage because of their high reliability and long lifespan. However, their practical application remains hindered by hydrogen electrodes that suffer from insufficient catalytic activity, high cost, and limited scalability. Here, we develop an integrated hydrogen electrode (iHE) by rationally integrating a catalyst with a meter-scale, ultrathin hydrogen diffusion layer. A Ni-based catalyst is incorporated as a representative into the hydrogen diffusion layer composed of an ultrathin, porous, and hydrophobic nickel-plated membrane, yielding an electrode cost of only $3.6 m −2 , approximately 5% that of a conventional hydrogen electrode based on Pt catalyst supported on a commercial gas diffusion layer (Pt@GDL). The iHE exhibits a low polarization of 26 mV at 5 mA cm −2 and stable operation over 1600 h. The Ni-H 2 (iHE) battery delivers a long cycle life of 3300 h with ~98% capacity retention and a negligible Coulombic efficiency decay rate of 0.033% h −1 . Furthermore, the Ni-H 2 (iHE) full cell achieves an energy cost of only one-sixth that of the Ni-H 2 (Pt@GDL) counterpart, together with an energy density of 179.5 Wh kg −1 . These results highlight the advantages of the iHE in activity, stability, scalability, and cost, demonstrating its potential for grid-scale energy storage.
authors: Shunxin Tan, Peiyan Tong, Xuzhi Zhang, Hongxu Liu, Yameng Fan, Shuyang Wei, Guili Zhao, Yidi Wang, Ziwei Zhang, Zhenshan Lv, Zuodong Zhang, Ruihao Luo, Jingwen Xu, Nan Zhang, Yangping Sheng, Rong Xu, Taoli Jiang, Wei Chen

10.1002/adma.74571.title: Bioinspired Hydrogen-Bond Traps Enabling Ultrasensitive Temperature Sensing
10.1002/adma.74571.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of flexible temperature sensors is hindered by the intrinsically low thermal sensitivity of soft ionic conductors, which arises from averaged energy landscapes and competing transport mechanisms. Inspired by the gating mechanism of biological transient receptor potential (TRP) ion channels, we propose a hydrogen-bond trap regulation strategy. By constructing localized hydrogen-bond traps with heterogeneous energy distributions within a deep eutectic solvent (DES) gel network, continuous ion transport is transformed into a confined, thermally activated hopping process. This approach yields an ultrahigh temperature coefficient of resistance (TCR) of 178% °C −1 and a high B value of 7880 K. A miniature flexible probe (Ø1.0 mm × 1.0 mm) demonstrates practical potential in organ temperature monitoring and wireless respiratory tracking. The tailored hydrogen-bond traps also effectively suppress multimodal crosstalk, enabling the fabrication of a decoupled trimodal sensing system that independently resolves proximity, pressure, and temperature signals for human-robot interaction. This work establishes a versatile materials strategy for achieving thermal perception in soft electronics and provides a general platform for tuning ion transport in polymer networks.
authors: Zhimin Lu, Yuhang Song, Changming Wu, Liping Xu, Yunting Wang, Duixin Ma, Na Li, Yifei Chen, Wei Li, Bing Shen, Tianwen Bai, Shuang Zheng, Yang Xu, Jia Huang

10.1002/adma.74562.title: Autocatalytic Eutectic Gel Electrolyte for Quasi-Solid State Zn-Ion Cells
10.1002/adma.74562.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrated eutectic electrolytes offer immense application potential for zinc-ion batteries. However, the high reactivity between the electrodes and hydrated eutectic electrolytes causes dendrite growth and cathode dissolution owing to the unstable and adverse interface layer formation. Although gelation of the eutectic electrolyte can mitigate the reactivity, the traditional polymerization initiation strategy still leads to severe residual monomers and initiators. These highly chemically and electrochemically reactive residual monomers/initiators can further react with the electrodes, deteriorating the electrode interface and ultimately leading to battery performance degradation. Herein, we designed an initiator-free acrylamide eutectogel electrolyte featuring autocatalysis, wherein polymerization is spontaneously driven by its own components, which reduces residual monomer and in situ converts residual acrylamide into a nitrogen-containing protective interphase during cycling, thereby suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction, harmful chlorinated by-products, and cathode dissolution. As a result, the Zn||NaV 3 O 8 ·1.5H 2 O cells deliver a capacity of 172.7 mAh g −1 with 98.5% retention over 2450 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 , and can also cycle stably at −20°C and 65°C. This autocatalytic polymerization strategy holds great promise for other polymer monomers and Lewis acid salts, and may offer a scalable approach to developing long-life quasi-solid zinc batteries.
authors: Mengyu Zhu, Dan Chan, Huibo Wang, Jin Yang, Wenlong Zhao, Huicai Wang, Chunxin Li, Shuang Li, Wenjing Cheng, Yanyan Zhang, Oleksandr I. Malyi, Yuxin Tang

10.1002/adma.74633.title: Analog Tensor Processing With Carbon Nanotube In-Memory Matrix Multiplications for Edge Computer Vision Acceleration
10.1002/adma.74633.abstract: ABSTRACT Computer vision requires intense tensor operations, primarily matrix multiplications, imposing substantial computation demands. Using hardware such as GPU and ASICs for acceleration offers a viable solution. Their application at edge, however, can be constrained by complexity in the computing architecture and incompatibility with analog systems. Here, we prototype an analog tensor core based on carbon nanotube charge-trapping nonvolatile memory for edge computer vision acceleration. The memory, exhibiting ∼100 linear, symmetric analog weights with fast programming (500 ns) and data processing (1 Mbit/s), enables in-memory matrix multiplications, facilitating compact tensor core design and operation of vectors and scalars in visual tasks. As demonstrations, the analog tensor core proves three-dimensional (3D) spatial transformation with an error of <2.81% and edge detection with a signal-to-noise ratio of >22 dB, underpinning its potential for accelerating computer vision tasks in, for example, autonomous driving, VR/AR, robot navigation, and industrial automation. Proof-of-concept simulation achieves viewfield distortion correction and edge detection of street view fisheye captures by parallel single-layer tensor processing using our analog tensor core in large scales.
authors: Jingfang Pei, Lekai Song, Songwei Liu, Yingyi Wen, Yaoqiang Zhou, Yang Liu, Pengyu Liu, Wenyu Cui, Xin Lu, Teng Ma, Zegao Wang, Guohua Hu

10.1002/adma.74560.title: Engineering Pluripotent Stem Cells-Derived Inner Ear Organoids With Enhanced Maturation and Reproducibility by Micro-Topographical Cues
10.1002/adma.74560.abstract: ABSTRACT Inner ear organoids (IEOs) derived from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) provide a promising platform for modeling neurosensory disorders and hearing loss; however, conventional systems often exhibit substantial structural variability, incomplete maturation, and limited reproducibility due to insufficient control of early organoid morphogenesis. Here, we demonstrate that micro-topographical cues applied during initial IEO formation enhance the development and functional maturation of PSC-derived IEOs. This microengineering strategy introduces temporally defined microscale geometric confinement to regulate early cell-cell and cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) interactions, thereby promoting epithelial organization and developmental fidelity. Microengineered IEOs (M-IEOs) exhibit improved reproducibility and neurosensory maturation, including increased hair cell-like populations, stereocilia-like structures and kinocilium-like features exhibiting a characteristic (9 × 2) + 2 microtubule organization. Functionally, M-IEOs exhibit enhanced electrophysiological responsiveness, supported by complementary transcriptomic and in situ analyses indicating activation of inner ear lineage maturation pathways. Furthermore, we demonstrate the versatility of M-IEOs by integrating them with a microfluidic vascular system to model vascular-epithelial interactions and inflammatory responses, highlighting its potential for disease modeling and pharmacological screening. Together, these findings establish transient micro-topographical guidance as an instructive regulator of inner ear organoid development and provide a robust, vascular-compatible platform for neurosensory research, disease modeling, and translational screening applications.
authors: Harshita Sharma, Jungeun Lim, Woochan Kim, Yeon Ju Kim, Dream Kim, Shinyull Lee, Chaeyeon Park, Stephen Rhee, Shruthy Kuttapan, Jungho Ha, Sang Wook Park, Kyunghoon Kim, Noo Li Jeon, Sunho Park, Yun-Hoon Choung, Jangho Kim

10.1002/adma.74569.title: Tailoring Symmetry Breaking in Engineered van der Waals Superlattices
10.1002/adma.74569.abstract: ABSTRACT Superlattice engineering in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures (e.g., by moiré engineering) provides a powerful platform for designing electronic bands and realizing correlated and topological quantum phenomena. Here, we pioneer a scheme to tailor superpotentials based on intrinsic substrate electronic orders. We show that this establishes a robust, self-aligned, and highly versatile route to band-structure control, as we demonstrate in graphene by engineering two distinct, nearly commensurate superlattices using the charge density waves (CDWs) of 1T-NbSe 2 . In these superlattices, the graphene's Dirac cones are folded either to the -point or to the K-points of the mini-Brillouin zone (mBZ). Using scanning tunneling microscopy, we observe that the -folded system preserves symmetry, while the K-folded system exhibits symmetry breaking. Combining density functional theory with an interlayer interaction model, we reveal that this difference is not electronically driven but originates from a structural instability. Our work establishes superlattice engineering for designer quantum states and unveils a structural mechanism for controlled emergent symmetry breaking.
authors: Keda Jin, Lennart Klebl, Zachary A. H. Goodwin, Junting Zhao, Felix Lüpke, Dante M. Kennes, Jose Martinez-Castro, Markus Ternes

10.1002/adma.74692.title: Electron Lever-Assisted d-Band Center Engineering in Intermetallic Alloy Nanozymes for Efficient Marine Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion Inhibition
10.1002/adma.74692.abstract: ABSTRACT Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) remains a persistent global challenge, with traditional inhibition strategies often constrained by limited efficiency, poor durability, and ecological toxicity. Herein, we propose a rational design that utilizes a heteroatom as an electronic lever to circumvent these constraints. By integrating heteroatom Ag into an FePt matrix, the d-band center of the Pt active sites is upshifted, optimizing the adsorption energy of substrates and ensuring superior catalytic performance even in H 2 O 2 -limited marine environments. The resulting FePtAg ( L -FPA) nanozymes exhibited enhanced triple-enzyme activities (haloperoxidase, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase, and peroxidase), triggering a localized burst of reactive chlorine and oxygen species. This synergistic action effectively disintegrated the extracellular polymeric substance barrier and induced metabolic disruption, achieving an exceptional 99.9% biofilm inhibition rate and 99.3% MIC inhibition efficiency against Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Furthermore, the intermetallic structure promoted by heteroatom Ag provided outstanding durability of nanozymes, with their antibiofilm efficiency decreasing by only 3% for over 120 days. This work not only elucidates the intrinsic correlation between electronic modulation and inhibition efficiency in MIC inhibitors but also offers a rational framework for designing nanozymes tailored to challenging and hostile environments.
authors: Linlin Yang, Bin Yu, Yizhe Dong, Yugui Ding, Xiangying Meng, Yongqiang Fan, Tingyue Gu, Fuhui Wang, Dake Xu

10.1002/adma.75357.title: Pulsed Oxidative-Reductive Electrolysis Over Dual Cu and Co Single-Atom Sites for Urea Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adma.75357.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical C─N coupling of CO 2 with nitrogen species offers a sustainable route to urea and related chemicals but is constrained under steady-state electrolysis by mismatched reaction kinetics. Here, pulsed oxidative-reductive electrolysis temporally coordinates CO 2 reduction and NH 3 oxidation, regulating the generation and coexistence of carbon- and nitrogen-derived intermediates. Co/CuNC, containing atomically dispersed Co and Cu sites within a nitrogen-doped carbon (NC), achieves a total C─N faradaic efficiency of 42 ± 4%, dominated by urea (20 ± 2%) and ethyl urea (16 ± 2%), with respective yield rates (YR) of 295 ± 25 and 50 ± 5 mmol h −1 g cat −1 . In situ synchrotron x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals potential-dependent changes in Cu and Co oxidation states and coordination environments, while in situ infrared spectroscopy identifies pulse-regulated *CO and *NH x intermediates and suggests concurrent electrochemical and Wöhler-type pathways. Density functional theory calculations reveal complementary site functions: Cu favors *NH 2 formation, whereas Co more strongly stabilizes *NH x and *CO intermediates, with *CO also accessible at Cu sites. These findings establish temporal coordination of reactant activation, intermediate populations, and active-site states as a mode-enabled strategy for accessing higher-order C─N products.
authors: Putri Ramadhany, Peiqi Qiu, Thành Trần-Phú, Denny Gunawan, Bernt Johannessen, Rosalie K. Hocking, Yan Jiao, Rose Amal, Rahman Daiyan

10.1002/adma.75346.title: Demagnetization-Driven Nanoscale Chirality-Selective Phonon Transport
10.1002/adma.75346.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral-lattice degrees of freedom can offer novel chirality-selective functionalities for thermotronic applications. Chiral phonons, which carry both heat and angular momentum, can arise from broken chiral degeneracy in phonon bands or from angular momentum transfer from photons or spins. Here, we demonstrate a nanoscale chirality-selective phonon transport based on a simple heterostructure of ferromagnetic [Co/Pt] multilayers and insulating chiral α-SiO 2 . Using magneto-optic thermometry, we show that the effective thermal conductivity of α-SiO 2 depends systematically on both the magnetization direction of [Co/Pt] and the structural handedness of α-SiO 2 . This behavior is supported by first-principles-based molecular dynamics simulations, which reveal chirality-dependent phonon transport across the ferromagnet/chiral-material interface. The magnetization-dependent thermal on/off ratio reaches 1.07 at room temperature and increases to approximately 1.2 at 50 K, reflecting reduced Umklapp phonon-phonon scattering. These results establish a ferromagnet/chiral-material platform for controlling nanoscale heat flow through chiral phonons.
authors: In Hyeok Choi, Daeheon Kim, Yeon Jong Jin, Seungmo Yang, Tae-Seong Ju, Changsoo Kim, Chanyong Hwang, Dongbin Shin, Jong Seok Lee

10.1002/adma.75324.title: Iron-Induced Interfacial Electronic Asymmetry Steers Pathway Divergence in Cobalt-Centered Fenton-Like Catalysis
10.1002/adma.75324.abstract: ABSTRACT Deep mineralization and matrix tolerance are difficult to reconcile in advanced oxidation processes because radical and nonradical pathways are often coupled in a composition-defined paradigm. Although multimetal materials can catalyze both pathways, the parallel reactions typically occur at different active sites, and their relative contributions are often governed by catalyst composition and active-site distribution, making deliberate regulation of pathway competition difficult. Here, we propose a multimetal catalyst with an electronically asymmetric Fe─O─Co interface to enable pathway divergence within a Co-centered catalytic environment. Fe introduction into CoNi layered hydroxides leads to electron density redistribution at neighboring Co sites and shifts PMS activation from a high-valent Co IV ═O-biased route toward a sulfate-radical-enriched regime while retaining complementary nonradical oxidation. The optimized catalyst achieved 1.43-fold greater TOC removal and a 1.47-fold higher PMS utilization efficiency (PUE) for norfloxacin (NOR) degradation than the Fe-free control, with robust decontamination performance against common background matrix interference and sustained activity over 96 h of high-flux continuous-flow operation. This work establishes interfacial Fe regulation as a pathway-engineering strategy for steering oxidant-activation selectivity through heterometal-induced electronic asymmetry, providing a route to reconcile mineralization depth with matrix tolerance in Fenton-like water treatment.
authors: Yun-Ze Qiu, Chun-Miao Zhang, Qing Li, Jing-Jing Feng, Wen-Qing Fei, Meng-Ting He, Qi-He Si, Wen-Jing Yang, Wen-Wei Li, Xue-Fei Sun

10.1002/adma.75143.title: Graphene Materials With Anomalous Infrared Emissivity Yet Superb Chemical Stability
10.1002/adma.75143.abstract: ABSTRACT Low infrared emissivity materials (i.e., metallic materials) are of significance for thermal radiation regulation. However, the easy-corrosion susceptibility and poor chemical stability are common bottleneck issues that affect their applications. We report a versatile electronic structure modulation strategy for low infrared (IR) emissivity graphene by engineering the surface chemistry of precursor graphene oxide and the followed reduction/doping process. The fabrication protocols minimize the irreparable disruption of the intrinsic graphitic structure and enable controllable assembly of nanosheets by suppressing formation of carboxyl groups. More significantly, the convenient reduction and halogen doping effects synergistically minimize electron scattering and enhance interfacial charge transport. The low-defective graphitic structure and the ordered multiscale architecture, as well as halogen doping effect, afford exceptional carrier mobility (∼27.1 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), carrier density (5.73 × 10 20 cm −3 ), and electrical conductivity comparable to highly oriented pyrolytic graphite. Surprisingly, the anomalous metallic response gives the lowest IR emissivity (0.15, 8-14 µm) for carbon materials, comparable to MXene and traditional metallic materials. The large-scale processability and outstanding long-term stability under chemical conditions offer new insights for the potential infrared applications of graphene materials.

10.1002/adma.75316.title: Fano-Engineered Au@Se Core-Shell Colloidal Pigments for Dual-Mode Structural Color
10.1002/adma.75316.abstract: ABSTRACT Colloidal structural colorants are attractive because they are substrate-free and solution-processable, but single-component plasmonic or dielectric colloids usually exhibit broad visible resonances that limit chroma. Here we report Au@Se core-shell colloidal pigments in which a plasmonic Au core is embedded within a visible-range Mie-resonant Se shell. The key signature is not the gradual red shift expected from passive dielectric loading, but an asymmetric hybrid feature with compressed linewidth, consistent with Fano-like interference between the broad electric-dipole response of the Se shell and the narrower Au-core electric-dipole response. The hybrid mode yields Q factors up to ≈15 in freely dispersed colloidal pigments, producing narrow transmission windows and spectrally separated reflection bands from the same liquid dispersion. By independently tuning the Au core diameter and Se shell thickness in a benchtop synthesis, we achieve broad visible color tuning in transmission and reflection and enlarge the accessible international commission on illumination chromaticity (CIE) area relative to single-component Au or Se colloids. The particles are formulated into ultraviolet (UV)-curable resins and writing inks for 254-ppi color filters, freeform paper deposition, and polarization-selective readout. This work establishes a colloidal design rule in which the shell acts as an active visible resonator rather than a passive refractive-index coating.
authors: YongDeok Cho, Yuwon Jeon, Min Kwon, Seungwoo Lee

10.1002/adma.75380.title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
10.1002/adma.75380.abstract: ABSTRACT The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI-driven techniques, and other high-tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross-contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal-ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1-Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene-containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1-Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape-changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1-Ru1 can be recycled via a one-pot, cross-contamination-free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high-tech applications.
authors: Dachuan Zhang, Chenrui Yuan, Jingning Cao, Shuofeng Liang, Zhulu Xie, Wenyong Jiang, Jie Yan, Si Wu

10.1002/adma.75342.title: Harnessing the Bacterial Membrane-Derived Oral Vaccine to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity and Metabolic Control of T Cells
10.1002/adma.75342.abstract: ABSTRACT The fluctuating gastrointestinal milieu and its restrictive epithelial barrier represent critical challenges for the design of oral cancer vaccines. Nevertheless, leveraging the gut microbiome as an interventional strategy has recently gained traction, especially in patients on immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, microbial-derived double-layered membrane vesicles are developed as adjuvants and cell-free carriers, fused with cell-penetrating peptide-modified antigens, and encapsulated in an alginate/chitosan-microsystem to engineer oral vaccines. This design strategically harnesses the crosstalk between the gut microbiome and gut-associated lymphoid tissues, driving dendritic cell maturation, plasma cell activation, and production of immune-stimulatory cytokines within the mesenteric lymph nodes and lamina propria. In mouse prophylactic and therapeutic tumor models, the select Bifidobacterium bifidum -derived oral vaccine combined with anti-PD1 treatment enhances cytotoxic antitumor responses, along with Th1-, Th17-immunity, leading to potent tumor suppression, prolonged survival, and long-term protection against tumor rechallenge. Mechanistically, the vaccine promotes interferon-γ-producing T cells and antitumor efficacy with ICI therapy via the improved microbiota diversity and signaling metabolites, with an indole-3-acetic-acid (3IAA) enriched diet profoundly shaping T-cell recruitment and differentiation. Our findings uncover a tryptophan metabolite-driven immune axis that amplifies the specific antitumor immune response, redefining oral vaccines as a powerful tool for cancer immunotherapy.
authors: Wenfei Chen, Fan Yang, Beibei Wu, Gelin Xiang, Xiaoya Lu, Jingyao Ma, Yining Xu, Li Mo, Xun Sun, Jinhan He

10.1002/adma.75197.title: Enhanced Bulk Photovoltaics in Polar 2D Hybrid Perovskite via Pressure-Strengthened Organic-Inorganic Interactions
10.1002/adma.75197.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in polar two-dimensional (2D) organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites (OIHPs) is currently impeded by an insufficient understanding of the microscopic mechanisms linking organic-inorganic interactions to photovoltaic output. Here, we utilize pressure as an effective thermodynamic probe to decouple these interactions in BDA(EA) 2 Pb 3 Br 10 (BDA is 1,4-butanediammonium, EA is ethylammonium), achieving the first pressure-engineered synergistic enhancement of short-circuit current ( I SC ) and open-circuit voltage ( V OC ). Comprehensive in situ characterizations reveal that pressure-strengthened N─H···Br hydrogen bonding induces cooperative organic cation ordering and inorganic octahedral distortion. This structural synergy amplifies spontaneous polarization, resulting in a 530-fold increase in BPVE efficiency to 0.18% at 1.5 GPa, a value surpassing all previously reported OIHPs. Moreover, the enhanced organic-inorganic interaction stabilizes the ferroelectric state, elevating the Curie temperature to 433 K. These results elucidate the microscopic mechanism underlying BPVE enhancement in 2D OIHP ferroelectrics and establish pressure modulation as an effective strategy for mechanistic studies and photovoltaic optimization.

10.1002/adma.75223.title: In Situ Ordered Glassification of Gels for Exceptional Stiffness and Toughness
10.1002/adma.75223.abstract: ABSTRACT Glassy gels are indispensable for applications ranging from structural composites to bioelectronics, yet their design is plagued by an intrinsic paradox where the rigid molecular constraints that endow high stiffness simultaneously restrict polymer chain dynamics, precluding the energy dissipation mechanisms essential for toughness. Here, we circumvent this fundamental trade-off through an in situ molecular constraint-induced ordered glassification strategy. By restricting localized conformations within a confined hydration environment, we drive the spontaneous assembly of long-range ordered, load-bearing nanodomains within a soft gel matrix. These domains function as rigid sacrificial units during initial deformation. Critically, they undergo a progressive, strain-activated dissociation that redistributes local stress and dissipates mechanical energy at the bulk scale. Unlike conventional post-treated gels, our material undergoes a rubbery-to-glassy transition in situ without external intervention, yielding a 3500-fold modulus enhancement and a toughness of 289 MJ m −3 , exceeding many reported high-modulus hydrogels and ionic gels. Furthermore, this molecular design imparts multimodal functionality, including strong yet water-removable adhesion (∼17 MPa to glass), superior impact resistance, and water-responsive shape programmability. This ordered glassification paradigm establishes a versatile molecular engineering route to create load-bearing gels that synergistically integrate stiffness, toughness, and adaptive intelligence, redefining the performance envelope of hydrated soft matter.

10.1002/adma.75184.title: Active Soft Hydrogels Reveal Cumulative Molecular Force Dosing in Stem Cell Fate Programming
10.1002/adma.75184.abstract: ABSTRACT Decoupling molecular-scale mechanical signaling from bulk substrate stiffness remains a fundamental challenge in biomaterial design. Here, we develop a soft-yet-active hyaluronic acid hydrogel (∼3 kPa) grafted with near-infrared-driven CD-PNIPAM-RGD molecular actuators to apply programmable, piconewton-scale forces directly to integrins without altering the bulk modulus. By isolating force history as an independent variable, we reveal that human mesenchymal stem cells act as cumulative mechanical integrators. A cumulative force dose of just 7 h (1-h daily pulses) drives irreversible osteogenic commitment on this classically non-permissive substrate. Mechanistically, each pulse bypasses canonical tension-based signaling. Despite negligible cytoplasmic traction, localized molecular pulling drives G-actin nuclear import, intranuclear F-actin polymerization, and rapid YAP activation. By recasting mechanotransduction from a continuous analog response into a discrete, cumulative integration of mechanical inputs, this work establishes active force dosing as a quantitative design principle for next-generation soft biomaterials.

10.1002/adma.75103.title: Giant Nonequilibrium Valley Control via Spin-Selective Hot-Carrier Transfer in an Antiferromagnetic van der Waals Stack
10.1002/adma.75103.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-selective hot-carrier transfer at interfaces between two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors and magnets offers a nonequilibrium route to manipulate spin and valley degrees of freedom. In van der Waals heterostructures, such transfer can be enabled by type-III band alignment together with magnetic-field-induced spin polarization of the bands in adjacent magnetic layers. Yet, continuous and robust valley control with high magnetic-field susceptibility remains challenging, particularly beyond binary switching in out-of-plane easy-axis magnets. Here we fabricate a CrSBr/WSe 2 /CrSBr heterostructure, where two semiconductor-magnet interfaces promote efficient hot-carrier transfer. Utilizing valley-resolved magneto-photoluminescence spectroscopy, we reveal a pronounced field-sign-asymmetric response and a magnetic-state-dependent evolution of emergent spectral features that track the spin configuration of multilayer CrSBr via spin-selective hot-carrier transfer. This mechanism enables giant, continuous tuning, and magnetic-state-dependent reversal of the degree of circular polarization (DoCP), reaching ∼ 40% for excitons and ∼ 80% for trion emission. Our results establish spin-polarized interlayer hot-carrier transfer as an efficient knob for engineering valley polarization and coherence in TMDs, and highlight antiferromagnet-based stacks as a versatile platform for magnetically programmable quantum optoelectronic functionalities.

10.1002/adma.74151.title: Stimuli-Responsive Hierarchical Structuring Controls Survival and Programs Hydrogelation of Supramolecular Metallofibers
authors: Merlin R. Stühler, László Mérai, Kai Ludwig, Rainer Haag, Quinn A. Besford, Alex J. Plajer

10.1002/adma.75385.title: Turning Nd-Fe-B Swarf Into High-Value Bulk Feedstocks via Sustainable Hydrogen Plasma: From Rare-Earth Oxides to Metals and Hydrides
10.1002/adma.75385.abstract: ABSTRACT Rare-earth permanent magnets (REPMs) are crucial for electric vehicles, wind turbines, and other high-efficiency electric motor systems. However, their production is energy-intensive, and global recycling rates are below 0.2%. Machining swarf is the main industrial waste from REPMs production. Despite its high rare-earth elements (REEs) content (∼20 wt.%), it has received limited attention for sustainable recycling. We introduce hydrogen plasma reduction (HPR) as a new environmentally friendly method to recover REEs from REPM swarf. By tuning the hydrogen content and treatment time, we achieve phase separation into metallic Fe and a Nd 2 O 3 -rich rare-earth fraction, providing a concentrated intermediate for subsequent REPM production. The process also enables direct rare-earth hydride formation, confirming the plasma-assisted partial rare-earth metallization in the molten state. This procedure turns REPM swarf into separated, high-value, high-purity feedstock in a single, acid-free step. Against the ∼70 kg CO 2 -eq kg −1 footprint of conventional REPM production, this recycling route offers a pathway toward substantially lower-emission magnet production while reducing reliance on primary REE supply.
authors: Naritai Chimed, Oliver Diehl, Ömer K. Büyükuslu, J. Manoj Prabhakar, Dennis Klapproth, Patricia Jovičević-Klug, Jürgen Gassmann, Dierk Raabe, Tim M. Schwarz, Matic Jovičević-Klug

10.1002/adma.75302.title: A Universal Spin-Polarization-Engineered Antibonding-Orbital Modulation Paradigm for Accelerating Reaction Kinetics in Ultrahigh-Rate Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75302.abstract: ABSTRACT Conversion-type anode materials hold great promise for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), yet their practical rate performance is fundamentally constrained by sluggish reaction kinetics beyond mass-transport limitations. Despite notable advances in accelerating ion/electron transport, intrinsically reducing the large reaction kinetic barrier and activation energy associated with robust metal-chalcogen (M─S) bonds remains a long-standing challenge. In this study, we propose a universal spin-polarization-engineered (SPE) antibonding-orbital modulation paradigm to fundamentally regulate M─S bond strength and enable ultrahigh-rate sodium storage. As a proof of concept, magnetic manganese heteroatom doping into heterojunctions enhances the saturation magnetization by ∼210%, inducing a spin-state transition from low-spin to high-spin configurations, which increases the electron occupation of antibonding orbitals formed between metal e g orbitals and chalcogen p orbitals, and thereby regulates M─S bond strength. Benefiting from this spin-engineered electronic reconstruction, Mn-FeS 2 /CoS 2 anode delivers an ultrahigh-rate capability of 300 mA h g −1 at 120 A g −1 , together with exceptional long-term durability (∼100% retention over 13 000 cycles at 100 A g −1 ), ranking among the best record. The generality of this strategy is further validated by extending SPE modulation to other magnetic dopants. Moreover, the industrial-level pouch cell is assembled to demonstrate the practical potential of this strategy.
authors: Yong Zhao, Junlan Fang, Shuyang Qiu, Xiang Li, Yijie Zhang, Chuang Bao, Runyi Zhou, Xiaodong Li, Jianhua Yan, Zheng Bo, Jun Lu, Huachao Yang

10.1002/adma.75321.title: Nonlinear Electro-Optic Visible Photonic Circuits for Solid-State Quantum Defects
10.1002/adma.75321.abstract: ABSTRACT Integrated visible photonic engines for solid-state quantum defects provide a foundation for scalable quantum networks. While miniaturization is advancing, active manipulation remains limited by the difficulty of achieving simultaneous milliwatt-scale visible light generation and high-contrast modulation. Despite extensive efforts, the concurrent chip-scale realization of nonlinear frequency conversion and fast temporal gating for high-fidelity quantum control has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate a monolithic thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) platform integrating periodically poled frequency conversion with GHz-bandwidth electro-optic (EO) switching. The device delivers off-chip green-light power exceeding 1 mW with an extinction ratio (ER) of 42.2 dB, enabling coherent spin control and time-resolved lifetime measurements of individual nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond through nanosecond gating. System performance is validated through pulsed optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR), Rabi oscillations, and Ramsey interference, supported by time-tagged photon counting with nanosecond resolution. By unifying sufficient nonlinear light generation with high-speed active manipulation, this platform establishes a scalable framework for the realization of high-rate quantum communication nodes.
authors: Yongchan Park, Yong Soo Lee, Hansol Kim, Jaepil Park, Junhyung Lee, Hyeyoon Jeon, Jinil Lee, Yong-Gwon Kim, Yeeun Choi, Min-Kyo Seo, Dae-Hwan Ahn, Hojoong Jung, Soo Jin Kim, Dongyeon Daniel Kang, Hyounghan Kwon

10.1002/adma.75392.title: Synchronized Ablation of Multifocal Tumors Enabled by Multi-Channel Lanthanide Nanocomposites
10.1002/adma.75392.abstract: ABSTRACT The multifocal nature of orthotopic breast tumors makes it difficult to treat due to individual tumor differences, requiring multiple therapeutic interventions. Here, a customized therapeutic strategy is presented for multiple tumors by using the same prescription based on a multi-channel lanthanide nanocomposite and orthogonally controlled drug release. The upconversion luminescence of the nanocomposite at different wavelengths can monitor pH-responsive mitoxantrone (MXT) release, reduced glutathione-responsive near-infrared (NIR) absorbance change, and eigen temperature, respectively, allowing modulation of photothermal treatment and temperature-responsive paclitaxel release through customized whole-body irradiation to achieve synchronized ablation of different individual tumors. Small animal experiments confirm multifocal breast tumors can be treated through this customized therapeutic strategy with both high efficiency and low overtherapy risk.
authors: Fang Li, Zheng Wei, Francesco G. Mutti, Hong Zhang, Felix F. Loeffler, Yuxin Liu, Xingjun Zhu

10.1002/adma.75381.title: Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics: From Anatomical Access to Disease-Focused Applications
10.1002/adma.75381.abstract: ABSTRACT Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have expanded from clinically validated prophylactic vaccines toward protein replacement and supplementation. Yet mRNA delivery remains centered on intramuscular vaccination and intravenous administration, largely optimized for systemic adaptive immunity or circulation-mediated biodistribution. Many localized diseases, however, are confined to tissues or compartments accessible by topical, transdermal, inhaled, oral, catheter-based, ocular, or intra-articular administration without initial reliance on circulation. For these diseases, the therapeutic objective is likewise local: therapeutically relevant mRNA expression occurs within the affected tissue, and efficacy derives predominantly from the local biological activity of the encoded protein rather than from downstream systemic effects initiated by local expression. This therapeutic paradigm is defined here as Anatomically Accessible Local mRNA Therapeutics (ALmT). The review first distinguishes ALmT from intravenous mRNA delivery and intramuscular mRNA vaccination, then organizes site-specific barriers and engineering strategies across major anatomical sites. It further examines disease-focused ALmT applications, highlighting protein restoration, cytokine or growth-factor supplementation, local antibody-fragment production, regenerative modulation, and tissue repair. Finally, it discusses general design principles, quantitative PK/PD evaluation, repeat-dose safety, and clinical translation. Overall, the ALmT framework may facilitate the design, quantitative evaluation, and clinical translation of mRNA therapies for localized diseases.
authors: Yashi Wang, Ruoyi Gan, Wei Chen

10.1002/adma.75368.title: Beyond Facet Engineering: Dislocation-Mediated Nucleation Enables Stable Lithium Deposition on Practical Polycrystalline Cu Collectors
10.1002/adma.75368.abstract: ABSTRACT Uniform Li deposition on practical Cu current collectors remains challenging in lithium metal batteries. Despite extensive efforts in facet engineering, achieving homogeneous Li deposition on practical polycrystalline Cu collectors remains elusive, highlighting an incomplete understanding of the structural factors governing Li deposition. Herein, a defect-mediated interfacial engineering strategy is developed by simultaneously introducing a high density of geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) and enriched <110>/<111> textures on commercial electrodeposited Cu foils. Theoretical calculations and experiments reveal that densely distributed dislocations provide thermodynamically favorable Li adsorption sites and abundant preferential heterogeneous nucleation sites, while the enriched <110>/<111> textures promote Li surface diffusion and lateral growth. This combined effect promotes uniform and compact initial Li deposition, guiding path-dependent deposition evolution and suppressing interfacial heterogeneity. The control experiments further support a key contribution of dislocation defects, while variations in surface chemistry or morphology alone cannot account for the observed performance differences. The optimized Cu foil sustains over 1200 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.52% ± 0.20% over the final 200 cycles ( n = 4) in Li||Cu cells and improves N/P = 0 Cu||NCM811 full-cell cycling. This work establishes dislocation-mediated nucleation and orientation-regulated growth as a design principle for practical Cu current collectors.
authors: Xinglong Liang, Yutong Nong, Pengfei Li, Xiaowei Wang, Jitao Nie, Cheng Peng, Weijie Ji, Jingyi Zhang, Shilin Su, Yitao Zhang, Xiaoyuan Bai, Chenxi Wang, Mengran Wang, Wanjing Yu, Xiaoming Yuan, Jiafeng Zhang, Ji Liang

10.1002/adma.75371.title: All-In-One Integration of Inherently Flame-Retardant, UV-Resistant, and Antibacterial Polymer by a Biguanide Unit
10.1002/adma.75371.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing fire accidents, excessive UV exposure, and health threats posed by bacterial infections urgently require advanced polymer materials integrating multiple safety protections. In this study, we propose an ultra-efficient strategy to achieve the all-in-one integration of inherently flame-retardant, UV-resistant, and antibacterial polymer materials through a single biguanide unit. The key lies in the unique triple protection mechanism exerted by the biguanide unit: high-temperature char-formation for flame retardance, n →π* transition absorption for UV-resistance, and disruption of the negatively charged bacterial surface for antibacteria. As a result, the biguanide-containing polymer material achieves the best UL-94 V-0 flame-retardant rating with excellent self-extinguishing properties, ≥99.3% ultra-high shielding rate for UV light, and ≥99.0% remarkable antibacterial rate. Importantly, the biguanide unit is chemically bonded to the polymer main chain, which not only avoids the health risks and performance degradation caused by the additive migration, but also exhibits outstanding heat resistance, thermal stability, and easy processability. This work simultaneously achieves triple functional integration of polymer materials through a single biguanide unit, realizing previously unattainable multiple safety protections against dangerous fires, harmful UV, and widely-existed bacteria.
authors: Yan Guo, Xi-Yuan Feng, Lei Zhang, Xiu-Li Wang, Lin Chen, Yu-Zhong Wang

10.1002/adma.75388.title: Ordered Crystallographic Orientation of Dion-Jacobson 2D Perovskites for Ultrastable Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75388.abstract: ABSTRACT Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites show great potential in stability but do not meet theoretical expectations for photovoltaics due to the random crystallographic orientation in films. We herein report ordered crystallographic orientation of the DJ 2D perovskite, achieved by modifying the intermediate-phase film with a Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) phase 2D perovskite based on the two-step processing method. The introduction of the RP 2D perovskite lowers the energy barrier for the transition from the intermediate phase to the 2D perovskite phase with the ordered alignment, and this strategy is applicable to various organic diammoniums-based DJ 2D perovskites. Solar cells with oriented DJ 2D perovskite films achieve an efficiency of 21.1% (19.05% for 1 cm 2 devices) and exhibit outstanding stability by retaining 98.1% of initial efficiency after 2000 h of maximum power point tracking at 65°C under continuous 1-sun illumination (ISOS-L-2 protocol) and 98.7% after 2500 h testing at a relative humidity of 85%.
authors: Xiaotao Liu, Jiangshan Qu, Hao Tian, Zhanjun Zhu, Xin Guo, Can Li

10.1002/adma.75400.title: Magnetic-Field-Annealing-Induced Short-Range Order in High-Entropy Alloys for Enhanced Electromagnetic Response
10.1002/adma.75400.abstract: ABSTRACT The growing demand for microwave absorbers in 5G/6G technologies motivates processing routes that balance matching thickness, attenuation, and temperature response. Here, magnetic field annealing (MFA) is investigated in rGO-supported FeCoNi, FeCoNiCr, and FeCoNiCrCu compositionally complex alloys at 0, 0.5, and 0.95 T. Among the investigated FeCoNiCr samples, the 0.5 T sample exhibits a favorable combination of dielectric and magnetic responses. Reflection loss yields a minimum of −72.30 dB at 1.59 mm, and a maximum effective absorption bandwidth of 4.40 GHz. At 85°C, the maximum bandwidth is 4.08 GHz, corresponding to 92.7% retention of temperature-specific maxima. Local microscopy, field-associated atomistic modeling, and fixed-composition electronic-structure calculations support an interpretation of the electromagnetic response in terms of Co-centered chemical correlations. Finally, flexible antennas and strain sensors based on this composite demonstrate stable wearable responses, validating this SRO strategy from atomic design to device integration.
authors: Lu-Yang Li, Zhuang Ma, Ji-Xing Bai, Wen-Qiang Cao, Li-Hong Gao, Qi Cao, Miao Jiang, Mao-Sheng Cao

10.1002/adma.75369.title: Nonreciprocal Bending in Ferroelectric Membranes Driven by Flexoelectricity
10.1002/adma.75369.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonreciprocity reflects the asymmetric propagation or motion of an object in two opposite directions and can achieve directional transport in physics. However, nonreciprocity in natural quasi-static mechanical systems, including nonreciprocal bending, has rarely been explored. Here we demonstrate nonreciprocal bending in a freestanding ferroelectric single-crystalline PbTiO 3 membrane using suspended-membrane nanoindentation. The mechanical bending of the ferroelectric membrane is strongly asymmetric in the two opposite bending directions with a difference in effective elastic modulus of up to 33%. The elastic recovery of bending deformation also becomes polarity-dependent. Such unconventional nonreciprocal bending originates from the asymmetric ferroelectric domain switching driven by the crucial flexoelectricity, as revealed by phase-field simulations. This work enriches the nonreciprocal functionalities of ferroelectrics and presents a route for exploring more nonreciprocal effects by flexoelectric engineering.
authors: Yingzhuo Lun, Lu Han, Qi Ren, Xinrui Yang, Leyan Nian, Songhua Cai, Zewei Hou, Xueyun Wang, Yuefeng Nie, Jiawang Hong

10.1002/adma.75413.title: Pathway Engineering Enables Durable Iridium-Free Acidic Water Oxidation
10.1002/adma.75413.abstract: ABSTRACT The pursuit of noble metal-free alternatives to iridium for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is critically impeded by a pervasive activity-stability trade-off, wherein non-precious metals undergo rapid oxidative dissolution under operating potentials. Here, we report a lutetium-stabilized cobalt oxide catalyst (Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 ) designed through site-specific electronic modulation, achieving a synergistic enhancement of both activity and stability in acidic OER for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical simulations reveal that Lu incorporation introduces robust Lu-O bonds and induces charge redistribution that strengthens Co-O covalency and suppresses Co 2+ dissolution, which is critical for improved OER durability, and simultaneously optimizes the Co-Co distance to favor direct O-O radical coupling with a reduced energy barrier. Leveraging these structural advantages, a practical PEMWE employing Lu 0.08 Co 2.92 O 4 delivers an industrially relevant current density of 1000 mA cm −2 at 1.837 V. Separately, it maintains stable operation for over 900 h under a stepwise current density from 200 to 500 mA cm −2 , highlighting its potential for sustainable hydrogen production.
authors: Feng Cao, Taiyan Zhang, Kang Hua, Wenchao Wang, Yifei Liu, Ruizhao Wang, Haonan Li, Keun Hwa Chae, Young Mi Lee, Min-Cherl Jung, Xiaoke Li, Wenjiang Ding, Lina Chong

10.1002/adma.75412.title: An Ultrarobust Dual-Modal Neural Fiber With In-Sensor Computing
10.1002/adma.75412.abstract: ABSTRACT Touch behavior constitutes the most direct physical manifestation of human intentions, meaning that intention decoding requires human-machine interfaces to simultaneously sense touch position and pressure. Conventional systems, however, rely on physically stacked discrete sensors and von Neumann architectures, causing data redundancy and impaired wearability. Here, we present an in-sensor-computing dual-modal neural fiber (ID neural fiber) that overcomes this fundamental limitation. The ID neural fiber achieves an unprecedented position resolution of < 5 mm and a pressure detection limit of 0.6 N, combined with exceptional robustness-sustaining 300 times load-bearing capacity and exhibiting < 8% performance fluctuation under bending. Coupled with flexibility, waterproofing, and reconfigurability, the ID neural fiber can be seamlessly integrated into textiles for reliable operation in harsh environments, including underwater robotic control. Crucially, the ID neural fiber enables in-sensor computing that dramatically increases the information density and allows synchronized feature fusion through programmable logic gates, enabling efficient real-time intention recognition. To capture touch habits, an intelligent system with the ID neural fiber achieves a remarkable identification accuracy of 98.21%. This work establishes a new material-architecture paradigm that unifies ultrarobustness, dual-modality, and in-sensor computing, setting the stage for next-generation wearable human-machine interfaces with both comfort and intelligence.
authors: Huasen Wang, Lei Liu, Shifan Yu, Zijian Huang, Yanhao Luo, Hongyu Chen, Yuchen Lin, Yu Hu, Wansheng Lin, Yue Yu, Gantang Su, Zhong Chen, Qingliang Liao, Chaoxing Wu, Yuanjin Zheng, Xinqin Liao

10.1002/adma.74642.title: TESCLA: A Fully Soft Electromagnetic Linear Actuator With Continuous Bending Enabled by Liquid-Metal Solenoids
10.1002/adma.74642.abstract: ABSTRACT Linear actuators are widely employed in robots and wearable devices due to their capability of directly generating linear motion. Although soft actuators and flexible linear actuators have been developed to enable effective operation in various configurations, they are still constrained by a limited actuation range and a discrete bending, which restricts their achievable workspace and curvatures. Here, we propose a tubular electromagnetic soft conformal linear actuator (TESCLA) exerting thrust force over a large actuation stroke with continuous bending. The actuator operates under both a straight configuration and a conformal deformation to the surrounding environment, leveraging the softness of liquid-metal solenoids (soft stator) and compliant magnetic composites (soft mover). The synchronous actuation strategy allows the actuator to produce controllable bidirectional electromagnetic thrust by applying an electric current to the soft stator. In addition, the step position is estimated by measuring inductance variance of the soft solenoids resulting from the displacement of the soft mover. The design of the actuator components is evaluated through numerical simulations to determine an effective configuration, considering performance characteristics such as thrust force, minimum step size, and sensing resolution. By utilizing the functionalities of the proposed actuator, biomimetic robotic applications and a wearable haptic device were demonstrated.

10.1002/adma.74942.title: Discovery of Multicomponent Invar Materials With Low Thermal Expansion, High Curie Temperature, and Superior Phase Stability Assisted by Active Learning
10.1002/adma.74942.abstract: ABSTRACT Zero thermal expansion (ZTE) materials provide exceptional dimensional stability under temperature fluctuations, making them indispensable for high-precision instrumentation and extreme environments. However, their natural scarcity, combined with the vast compositional space in multicomponent systems, renders traditional trial-and-error approaches both time-consuming and cost-prohibitive, posing an emergent challenge for modern high-tech applications. Here, we establish a task-specific active-learning framework with empirical fine-tuning to accelerate ZTE materials' design. By mining sparse experimental datasets, we identified a high-potential compositional region and uncovered several novel low-expansion alloys. Among them, Cr 1.4 Co 8.9 Ni 30.5 Fe 59 exhibits a low coefficient of thermal expansion of , and a high Curie temperature reaching 580 . Real-time in situ neutron and synchrotron x-ray diffraction confirm its single-phase face-centered cubic structure, excellent ductility, and robust phase stability against thermal and mechanical stimuli. Crucially, machine learning analysis pinpointed six key descriptors highly correlated with low-expansion performance, providing data-driven insights into the magnetovolume origins of this behavior. This work not only yields a high-performance dimensionally stable alloy, but also demonstrates how integrating physical insights with data-driven design can accelerate advanced materials development.

10.1002/adma.75378.title: A Critical Call for Mechanistic Investigations of Metal-Bacteria Interactions
10.1002/adma.75378.abstract: ABSTRACT The antibacterial properties of metals have been recognized for millennia. It is thus well established that this antibacterial response has tremendous importance for bioengineering applications, driving ever-increasing resources for research efforts, especially over the last few decades. What is less appreciated across the thousands of scientific investigations that appear in the literature, however, is the reproducibility crisis stemming from various challenging aspects of this research. In this perspective, we highlight this reproducibility problem, discuss its sources, and suggest solutions towards focused, mechanistic, interdisciplinary investigations. To make these recommendations operational, we provide a source-specific experimental roadmap, identify priority mechanistic questions with concrete investigation pathways, and highlight representative studies that combine causal perturbations, orthogonal measurements, and cross-laboratory validation.
authors: J. Rackwitz, A. Bandyopadhyay, S. Belkin, S. Bose, N. Eliaz, J. L. Gilbert, T. C. Lowe, F. Mücklich, R. J. Turner, C. C. Tasan

10.1002/adma.75351.title: Layered Spin-Crossover Metal-Organic Frameworks for Light-Induced Control of Two-Dimensional Quantum Materials
10.1002/adma.75351.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored for gas separation, catalysis, or energy storage, yet their integration with other electronically functional materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we integrate the layered Hofmann-type spin-crossover (SCO) MOF {Fe II (pyS 2 Et) 2 [Pt II (CN) 4 ]} into electrical nanodevices to control the properties of two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials. Our molecular approach exploits the stimuli-responsive nature of SCO-layered materials as switchable building blocks. We demonstrate selective modulation of the electronic transport in van der Waals heterostructures interfacing SCO with 2D quantum materials (few-layer graphene, magnetic CrSBr, superconducting NbSe 2 ) through the strain induced via thermal and light-induced spin transitions. In graphene, the conductivity is selectively switched by light. In spin-valves based on CrSBr bilayers, the MOF triggers magnetic hysteresis (absent in pristine CrSBr) and enables tunable non-volatile zero-field memory. In NbSe 2 , light modulates the superconducting critical current and transition temperature. These results establish layered stimuli-responsive SCO MOFs as active molecular control elements for 2D quantum materials, providing a route to strain-mediated control of electronic, magnetic, and superconducting functionalities, and extending MOF-based architectures beyond traditional porous-matter applications toward multifunctional electronics and spintronics.
authors: Carla Boix-Constant, Alejandro Orellana-Silla, José Antonio Real, Samuel Mañas-Valero, Eugenio Coronado

10.1002/adma.75384.title: Directional Confinement Governed Ion Transport for Efficient Actuation
10.1002/adma.75384.abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport kinetics in electrolytes are a key determinant of ionic actuator performance. Conventional random porous electrolytes are constrained by porosity and tortuosity, leading to an intrinsic limitation in ion mobility within the Bruggeman framework. Here, structural anisotropy is introduced to establish a unified framework that analyzes ion transport from random diffusion to directionally confined regimes. To validate this concept, anisotropic electrolytes with oriented channels are fabricated via directional freeze-drying. These structures exhibit pronounced directional dependence, with through-plane ion mobility twice higher than that of the disordered counterparts, leading to significantly enhanced ionic actuator performance and mitigating the inherent trade-off between strain and blocking force. Moreover, the directional confinement effect is observed across multiple polymer systems, highlighting the critical role of structural anisotropy in regulating ion transport and offering a framework for enhancing electrolyte performance through microstructural design. This strategy enables environmentally robust and stable operation of soft electrochemical actuators for grippers and biomimetic robotics.
authors: Yufei Zhang, Qiuchun Lu, Adit Gupta, Sen Wang, Xueyang Wang, Jian Yu, Xuanyi Hu, Daniel Mandler, Pooi See Lee

10.1002/adma.75387.title: Dual Twisted Interfaces Enable Tunable Second Harmonic Generation in Chemical Vapor Deposition Grown Trilayer MoS2
10.1002/adma.75387.abstract: ABSTRACT Twisted bilayer transition metal dichalcogenides, governed by a single twisted interface, offer a versatile platform for manipulating interlayer coupling and emergent optical behavior. However, despite extensive studies on single twisted interface systems, how multi-interface twisted stacking influences nonlinear optical behavior remains unclear. Here, we address this gap by systematically investigating the nonlinear optical performance of chemical vapor deposition (CVD) grown twisted trilayer MoS 2 (TT-MoS 2 ) with multi-interface twisted stacking. We fabricate all nine distinct trilayer MoS 2 configurations by CVD. Raman and photoluminescence show that twisted interfaces modulate interlayer coupling, giving rise to stacking-dependent phonon and excitonic responses. Atomic-resolution scanning, transmission electron microscopy, and selected area electron diffraction confirm dual twisted interfaces and a supermoiré lattice. Guided by these structural insights, we examine the second harmonic generation (SHG) response across all nine trilayer configurations. Extending the coherent SH field superposition model to a trilayer system with two independent twisted interfaces, we develop a framework that describes how the dual interfaces govern the SHG intensity and polarization orientation across stacking configurations. Our findings establish TT-MoS 2 as a versatile nonlinear platform and open new avenues for understanding and exploiting multi-interface twisted coupling to engineer nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals materials.
authors: Mengxuan Guo, Luyun Xuan, Mingwen Zhang, Han Zhang, Ziyue Chen, Lu Zheng, Weiwei Li, Mai Zhang, Tong He, Ruihuan Duan, Wu Zhao, Xuetao Gan, Zheng Liu, Manzhang Xu, Wei Huang, Xuewen Wang

10.1002/adma.75409.title: Solvation-Equilibrium Locking Enables Ultrawide-Temperature Operation of High-Voltage Lithium-Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75409.abstract: ABSTRACT High-energy lithium metal batteries are promising for space, polar, deep-sea, and other extreme environments, but their operation is constrained by temperature-sensitive ion transport, Li + solvation, and interfacial chemistry. A solvation-equilibrium-locked electrolyte (SELE) is reported by combining dimethyl sulfite (DMS), a low-freezing weakly solvating solvent, with Pyr 13 DFOB (1-methyl-1-propylpyrrolidinium difluoro(oxalato)borate) as an ionic-liquid co-solvent. Cooperative ion-dipole and weak C-H⋯O interactions between DMS and Pyr 13 + regulate the free-solvent reservoir, while TFSI − (bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide) and DFOB − enrich the primary Li + coordination shell. Variable-temperature 7 Li NMR, Raman, and molecular dynamics simulations show that solvent-separated ion pairs, contact ion pairs, and aggregates remain nearly invariant from −60°C to 60°C, unlike the strongly temperature-responsive Pyr 13 DFOB-free electrolyte. This locked anion-rich solvation structure reduces solvent coordination around Li + , mitigates solvent-derived interfacial decomposition and gas evolution, and promotes LiF- and borate-rich interphases on Li metal and NMC811. Consequently, Li||NMC811 cells deliver discharge capacity at −85°C and operate up to 120°C, while pouch cells remain functional after cooling to −122.9°C. A 6.6 Ah Li||Ni90 pouch cell further achieves 565 Wh kg −1 under lean-electrolyte conditions, establishing solvation-equilibrium locking as a molecular design principle for lithium metal batteries operating over a broad temperature range.
authors: Qingyu Dong, Nan Chen, Yang Li, Li Li, Xingjiang Liu, Feng Wu, Renjie Chen

10.1002/adma.75396.title: Voltage Hysteresis Induced by Fragile Quasi-Flat Bands in Oxygen-Redox Cathodes
10.1002/adma.75396.abstract: ABSTRACT Cathodes exploiting oxygen redox chemistry underpin the realization of lithium battery systems with specific energies beyond 600 Wh kg −1 . However, voltage hysteresis exceeding 1 V, especially during the first cycle, remains a long-standing and unresolved challenge, severely limiting energy efficiency and practical deployment. Here, we propose a quasi-flat-band framework in which oxygen 2p states near the Fermi level are intrinsically sensitive to perturbations. Even weak perturbations, such as minor lattice distortions during delithiation or thermal vibrations at room temperature, can disproportionately amplify band dispersion and induce hysteresis. This insight reframes the long-standing design strategy by extending it beyond suppressing structural reconstructions to include control of perturbation-driven electronic instability. Future materials design should pursue two principles: stabilizing symmetry to sustain quasi-flat-band characteristics and engineering orbital hybridization to enhance their robustness against perturbations. This work rethinks the origin and mitigation of voltage hysteresis, bringing oxygen-redox cathodes closer to reliable operation at high voltages.
authors: Ang Gao, Yuxuan Guo, Yanbing Guo, Lin Gu

10.1002/adma.75377.title: Synthesis of Bulk Superconducting LiNbO 2 Crystals Through CaH 2 Reduction
10.1002/adma.75377.abstract: ABSTRACT We have synthesized layered superconducting LiNbO 2 crystals through a bulk phase transformation from LiNbO 3 single crystals via CaH 2 reduction. As the Nb valence is reduced from 5+ to 3+, the material undergoes a structural transformation to the resulting product, LiNbO 2 , which is accompanied by metallic behavior and a superconducting transition, T c onset, as high as 14.4 K. Secondary ion mass spectroscopy (SIMS) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) show that the resulting phase is hole-doped through de-lithiation during the reduction. Magnetization and AC susceptibility measurements from a tunnel diode resonator confirm the bulk nature of superconductivity with a superconducting volume fraction of ≈77% and an upper critical field approaching 26 T. Our study demonstrates extreme hydride reduction as an effective method to induce phase transformations with non-topochemical pathways and can be used to synthesize bulk materials with exotic properties.

10.1002/adma.75393.title: Thickness-Defined Transport Regime Toward Near-Ideal Area-Type Switching
10.1002/adma.75393.abstract: ABSTRACT Area-type memristors are attractive for analog in-memory computing, but their use is often limited by parasitic charge storage, causing readout drift, non-pinched hysteresis, and degraded readout fidelity. We show that near-ideal area-type switching emerges within a tunneling-governed transport regime in ultrathin layers that suppresses charging-related readout artifacts. By varying the thickness in TiN/Ta 2 O 5 /Pt in a range of 3-10 nm, we reveal the transition from filamentary switching to near-short-circuit transport with two gradual-switching modes with different readout stability. The 5-6 nm thickness window suppresses non-pinched hysteresis and short-time drift while preserving analog switching, yielding nearly polarity-symmetric hysteresis and readout, clear area scaling, and continuous near-linear conductance modulation. Our analysis indicates that trap-assisted tunneling dominates the stabilized-state response, whereas ionic redistribution governs pristine-state reconstruction and the stability boundaries. A compact model is derived for the 5 nm device which reproduces the quasi-static I-V behavior and the dynamic resistance evolution based on pulse-width-dependent characteristics. The verified model is provided as Verilog-A code enabling simulation in circuit design tools. Our results demonstrate that ultrathin scaling is a regime-defining design rule for near-ideal area-type operation in oxide memristors, implying a fundamental approach to fabricating robust multi-state memristors for in-memory computing applications.
authors: Cuo Wu, Junjie Zhao, Richard Schroedter, Jason Vincent, Hampus Hoffman, Leif Riemenschneider, Abdallh Herbawe, Hao Shen, Ronald Tetzlaff, Stefan Slesazeck, Gianaurelio Cuniberti, Thomas Mikolajick, Benjamin Max

10.1002/adma.75414.title: Axial Benzotriazole-Coordinated Ni Single Atoms Enable Rapid Interfacial Electron Transfer for Efficient Photocatalytic Acetylene Semi-Hydrogenation
10.1002/adma.75414.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic semi-hydrogenation of acetylene (C 2 H 2 ) to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) often suffers from inefficient interfacial electron transfer from the photocatalysts to adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Here, we demonstrate that axial coordination of benzotriazole (BTA) to Ni single atoms in C 3 N 4 (BTA-Ni SAs-C 3 N 4 ) facilitates interfacial electron-transfer processes. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, in situ transient surface photovoltage spectroscopy, in situ photochemical infrared spectroscopy, and theoretical simulations reveal that BTA-coordinated Ni SAs serve as the centers for rapid electron transfer by upshifting the Ni d-band center and strengthening the orbital overlap between Ni SA and adsorbed C 2 H 2 . Consequently, BTA-Ni SAs-C 3 N 4 achieves a very high C 2 H 4 production rate of 32.29 mmol g cat −1 h −1 with a C 2 H 4 selectivity of 97.6% under simulated solar irradiation, which is ∼4-times higher than that for Ni SAs-C 3 N 4 . The apparent quantum yield at 365 nm is up to 4.65%, superior to reported photocatalytic acetylene semi-hydrogenation. This work highlights the importance of interfacial charge transfer in photocatalytic acetylene hydrogenation and provides a rational strategy for designing high-performance photocatalysts.
authors: Linjia Li, Youyu Pang, Menghui Deng, Zhihan He, Hao Liu, Tengfeng Xie, Jichao Zhang, Zhenpeng Liu, Jian Zhang
