10.1002/adma.75404.title: Radiative Cooling Floating Covers Cool Lakes and Suppress Evaporation
10.1002/adma.75404.abstract: ABSTRACT Globally, warmer lakes disrupt thermal balance, causing hypoxia, salinization, biodiversity loss, and increased evaporation. Conventional floating covers used to reduce evaporation absorb sunlight and warm the underlying water, limiting suppression efficiency to less than the coverage ratio (η eff /Φ ≤ 1). Here, we break this limit by developing Superhydrophobic Radiative Cooling Covers (SRCC) via multi-level structural design. SRCC actively cools the water surface by combining high solar reflectance, strong mid-infrared emission, and superhydrophobicity. Experiments show SRCC lowers water temperature by 2.2°C versus uncovered water, achieving 93.1± 0.1% evaporation suppression at 91% coverage, yielding η eff /Φ > 1.0 for the first time. Large-scale simulations for nine Chinese lakes indicate that SRCC reduces water temperature by 4.87°C (vs. no cover) and by 12.44 °C (vs. black covers). This cooling could increase annual freshwater reserves by 10.78 km 3 across China under full deployment, equivalent to 20.9 L per person per day. Unattainable with conventional covers, SRCC uniquely mitigates thermal accumulation while enhancing freshwater storage, providing a quantifiable engineering solution to climate-driven water stress and enabling adaptive lake ecosystem management across regional and global scales.
authors: Hafiz M. Asfahan, Siyuan Jia, Syeda Mishal Zahra, Zhenyuan Xu, Jia Zhu, Wanlin Guo, Xiuqiang Li

10.1002/adma.74748.title: Superelastic Subcrystalline Rare-Earth Ceramic Nanofiber Aerogels Enable 1300°C-Stable Upconversion Luminescence
10.1002/adma.74748.abstract: ABSTRACT Real-time noncontact temperature detection is critical for the reliable operation of specialized robots in extreme thermodynamic environments. Upconversion (UC) luminescent materials, owing to their temperature-sensitive emission, offer a promising solution. However, traditional UC crystals are fundamentally limited by both severe thermal quenching above 250°C and intrinsic brittleness. Here, we break these barriers by developing a subcrystalline upconversion ceramic nanofiber aerogel through an interfacial phonon engineering strategy. Our approach embeds active rare-earth nanocrystals within an amorphous alumina matrix, creating a tensile-strained heterointerface that softens local phonon modes and efficiently scatters high-frequency vibrations. This unique “phonon cage” architecture suppresses nonradiative decay pathways, enabling stable UC emission at the unprecedented temperature of 1300°C. Furthermore, the subcrystalline structure induces a higher-order sinusoidal buckling behavior, endowing the aerogel with thermomechanical superelasticity. The aerogel fully recovers from 95% compressive strain and survives over 1000 fatigue cycles, retaining >80% of its elasticity after 100 rigorous compression cycles under 1300°C thermal load. This work paves the way for noncontact thermal sensing in extreme environments.
authors: Chenhao Ding, Jiawei Wu, Weiyan Zhu, Maoquan Zhang, Xinyi Wang, Qian Liu, Xinyu Li, Liyuan Fu, Shude Liu, Jianhua Yan

10.1002/adma.74931.title: Native Defects-Induced Fermi-Level Pinning and Diffuson-Mediated Thermal Transport in BiSbSe 3 Thermoelectrics
10.1002/adma.74931.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultralow thermal conductivity is widely recognized as a core characteristic of promising thermoelectrics, yet many such materials still fail to realize high thermoelectric performance. Te-free BiSbSe 3 embodies this contradiction: its intrinsically ultralow thermal conductivity makes it promising for medium-temperature thermoelectric applications, while stable p -type transport remains elusive and the optimization limits of both conduction types remain unclear. Here, we reveal that native defects and Sb containing lone-pairs jointly govern its transport behavior. Electron microscopy analysis and first-principles calculations confirm that Se vacancies and cation-on-Se antisite defects possess low formation enthalpies, stabilizing n -type conduction, compensating holes, and pinning the Fermi level away from the valence band maximum. Moreover, strong near-band-edge Sb-Se hybridization softens Sb-dominated low-frequency optical phonons, promoting acoustic-optical coupling and diffuson-like thermal transport at high temperatures. By matching theory and experiment, we identify carrier mobility degradation at high donor concentrations as the main limitation for n -type BiSbSe 3 . Our calculations predict that eliminating Fermi-level pinning could enable p -type BiSbSe 3 to achieve an excellent average ZT of ∼ 1.4 over 300-800 K. These findings not only clarify the long-standing underperformance of ultralow thermal conductivity thermoelectric compounds, but also establish a universal chemical design framework for optimizing Te-free thermoelectrics.

10.1002/adma.75398.title: Cyclic Nonequilibrium Processing of Halide Solid Electrolytes for Low-Pressure Operation of all-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/adma.75398.abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish ionic transport and high rigidity of inorganic solid electrolytes (SSEs) necessitate ultra-high external pressures in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), posing a major barrier to their deployment. Herein, we propose a cyclic nonequilibrium thermal process for Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC) solid electrolyte, which is implemented through repeated quenching to concurrently optimize ionic transport and deformability. The initial quench refines particle size, whereas subsequent quenching induces local amorphization, thereby suppressing grain boundary resistance and enhancing compressibility. Meanwhile, additional Li vacancies are introduced, accelerating bulk phase ionic transport. These coupled mesoscopic and microscopic structural evolutions increase the room-temperature ionic conductivity (IC) of LIC from 1.3 to 6.8 mS/cm, while reducing the Young's modulus from 42.3 to 17.6 GPa. The optimized LIC enables a stable cycling of ASSBs at a low operation pressure of 2 MPa with a high areal capacity of 7.7 mAh/cm 2 , highlighting cyclic nonequilibrium processing as a promising route for practical ASSBs.
authors: Wuliang Feng, Peiyao Wang, Qingli Wen, Li Shen, Chenyao Ma, Xudong Chen, Zhenming Xu, Jianwen Liang, Shigang Lu, Jiujun Zhang, Yongyao Xia, Xingbao Zhu, Xueliang Sun, Yufeng Zhao

10.1002/adma.75390.title: Advances in Bio-Integrated Edge Computing Systems for Smart and Connected Health
10.1002/adma.75390.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in bio-integrated healthcare technologies have enabled continuous, high-resolution monitoring and active therapeutic intervention through wearable, implantable, and ingestible platforms. In parallel, edge computing has emerged as a critical framework for processing biomedical data locally, enabling low-latency, energy-efficient, and privacy-preserving operation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bio-integrated edge computing systems for smart and connected health, focusing on the co-design of computing, sensing, and energy strategies. We first examine computing approaches, including conventional von Neumann architectures and emerging paradigms such as compute-in-memory and neuromorphic systems, for on-device data processing and decision-making. We then discuss sensing strategies that enhance signal fidelity and enable efficient information representation at the biointerface. Finally, we review energy solutions that enable continuous, autonomous operation. By integrating these domains, this work outlines pathways toward scalable, adaptive, and fully autonomous edge healthcare systems.
authors: Gyuwon Kim, Seungwon Yoo, Tae Woog Kang, Yunuo Huang, Woon-Hong Yeo

10.1002/adma.75030.title: Rare-Earth-Cluster-Mediated Long-Range Electronic Modulation Activates Zn Atomic Sites for Oxygen Reduction Catalysis
10.1002/adma.75030.abstract: ABSTRACT Activating the inert Zn ( d 10 ) centers via precise ligand-field engineering to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance is highly appealing yet challenging. Herein, we report a general long-range electronic structure regulation strategy to construct ultrafine rare-earth oxide clusters anchored proximal to Zn single-atom sites (LaO x -Zn-SA/CNCl), aiming at boosting ORR activity. Benefiting from the tailored long-range electronic modulation by LaO x clusters and the hierarchical porous carbon support that maximizes Zn atom utilization, the catalysts exhibit a high half-wave potential of 0.90 V along with remarkable stability in alkaline media. This represents a non-precious-metal, rare-earth-based electrocatalyst among the best reported so far. A zinc-air battery (ZAB) integrating LaO x -Zn-SA/CNCl as the cathode catalyst delivers a maximum power density of 177.3 mW cm −2 at 225 mA cm −2 . Theoretical calculations reveal that the proximal LaO x clusters remotely modulate the electronic structures of Zn sites, enhancing electron-transfer efficiency by strengthening electronic interactions. With the optimized electronic state of Zn sites, the adsorption of key intermediates is balanced to alleviate the energy barriers of the rate-determining step. This work provides insights into the long-range electronic regulation of transition-metal single-atom sites within a hierarchical rare-earth cluster-coupled microenvironment for efficient electrocatalysis.
authors: Yuying Jiang, Menggang Li, Shuijing Yu, Hu Liu, Zhenhui Ma, Shaojun Guo

10.1002/adma.75397.title: High-Performance Low Threshold Voltage n-Type OECTs via a Stepwise Cyanation of Quinoxaline-Based Polymeric Semiconductor
10.1002/adma.75397.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving both low threshold voltage ( V th ) and high performance in organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) is critical for low-power, high-sensitivity bioelectronics, yet simultaneously achieving low V th and high device performance remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, we propose a stepwise cyanation strategy to modify quinoxaline-based polymeric semiconductors to mitigate this dilemma. Benefiting from the strong electron-withdrawing ability of cyano substituents, QxCN-CNTVT functionalized with cyano groups on both donor and acceptor units exhibits a deep LUMO level of −4.23 eV, one of the deepest among reported n -type ionic-electronic conductors. As a result, OECTs based on QxCN-CNTVT demonstrate excellent comprehensive performance, with a high µC* value of up to 168.89 F cm −1 V −1 s −1 and a low V th of 0.13 V, while maintaining superior operational stability (retaining ∼80% of the initial current after 10,000 s of continuous operation and 10,000 full switching cycles). Furthermore, QxCN-CNTVT is successfully applied to complementary inverters for efficient amplification of electrooculogram (EOG) and electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, as well as NAND and NOR logic gates for integrated logic functions. This work not only alleviates the widely observed imbalance between performance and V th in n -type OECTs but also provides a versatile molecular design strategy for next-generation low-power bioelectronic devices.
authors: Songlin Mo, Guohong Hu, Chao Deng, Yue Wan, Shaodan Cai, Hongxiang Li, Liang-Wen Feng, Wei Huang, Jianhua Chen

10.1002/adma.75395.title: Hypoxia-Tolerant Supramolecular Nanomicelles for Pyroptosis-Enhanced NIR-II Phototheranostics
10.1002/adma.75395.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor hypoxia, limited solid-tumor imaging, and insufficient systemic antitumor immunity remain major challenges to effective cancer phototheranostics. Here, a molecular conformation engineering strategy is developed to construct TBBP, which features a strengthened electron donor, a moderately twisted conformation, extended π-conjugation, and a robust molecular skeleton free of labile olefinic π-bridges. TBBP exhibits excellent photostability, broadband second near-infrared (1000-1600 nm) emission, and efficient photothermal conversion (42.17%). Supramolecular assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 affords stable TBBP nanomicelles, TBBP NPs, that selectively generate superoxide radicals (O 2 −• ) and retain potent Type I photodynamic therapy (PDT) activity under hypoxia. Photoactivated TBBP NPs further induce mitochondrial dysfunction and caspase-3/GSDME-mediated immunogenic pyroptosis, promoting dendritic cell maturation and CD8 + T cell infiltration. In a bilateral 4T1 tumor model, TBBP NPs enable high-contrast second near-infrared (NIR-II) imaging, while synergistic Type I PDT and photothermal therapy elicit systemic antitumor immunity, achieving 92.0% primary tumor inhibition and 47.7% distant tumor inhibition. This work establishes a molecular conformation engineering strategy and extends its functionality through supramolecular assembly, synergistically integrating NIR-II imaging, hypoxia-tolerant Type I phototherapy, and photoimmunotherapy, thereby providing a generalizable molecular design principle for the development of next-generation multifunctional organic phototheranostic agents.
authors: Xing Wang, Kunyan Dong, Zhichao Wang, Yuqi Tang, Quan Li

10.1002/adma.75399.title: Boundary Guided Liquid-Bridge Adhesion for Robotic Pick-and-Release
10.1002/adma.75399.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid-bridge-mediated adhesion provides conformal contact with rough surfaces and gentle interaction with fragile microstructures, making it attractive for object manipulation. However, controlling liquid-bridge formation and retraction under non-ideal interfacial conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a switchable liquid-bridge adhesion strategy using a two-tiered stamp with spatially patterned wettability. Boundary-guided pinning confines liquid spreading to form a stable bridge for pickup and guides liquid retraction toward bridge breakup for controlled release. This design converts liquid-bridge adhesion from an uncontrolled capillary phenomenon into a controllable interfacial mechanism. The strategy enables preload-free adhesion switching, tunable adhesion forces, robust manipulation across surfaces with diverse roughness and wettability, and damage-free contact with fragile microstructures. Integrated with a robotic platform, the stamp functions as a liquid-bridge-based robotic end effector for pick-and-place manipulation and robotic placement, providing a route toward ultra-gentle manufacturing and microelectronic assembly.
authors: Jinsheng Zhao, Muyang Li, Jianchao Chen, Zhixiao Hou, Yun Wang, Wei Chen, Jiangang Zhang, Yu Tan, Aoji Zhu, Yu Chai, Xiangyu Li, Mingxing Shi, Lidong Yang

10.1002/adma.75152.title: Over 20% Efficiency in As-Cast Organic Solar Cells Enabled by Flory-Huggins Parameter Engineering
10.1002/adma.75152.abstract: ABSTRACT The realization of high-efficiency as-cast organic solar cells (OSCs) represents a key step toward simplified processing and scalable fabrication for commercialization. However, achieving high-performance as-cast devices remains challenging because it demands delicate balance between donor-acceptor self-aggregation and miscibility. Herein, we fabricate as-cast OSCs through Flory-Huggins parameter (χ) engineering that precisely regulates donor-acceptor miscibility during solution casting. The chloroform-carbon disulfide (CF:CS 2 ) mixed solvent, with tailored solubility and evaporation kinetics, dynamically modulates χ to form an optimized bulk heterojunction featuring desirable phase separation and a well-balanced fibrillar network. This design affords efficient exciton dissociation, facilitated charge transport, and suppressed recombination in the blend. Consequently, as-cast D18:L8-BO device processed with the CF:CS 2 solvent system attained a PCE of 20.11% (certified as 19.69%) alongside enhanced photostability, representing the highest efficiency reported for as-cast devices. Besides, high PCEs of 18.89% and 15.12% are achieved in thick-film (300 nm) and large-area (20.17 cm 2 ) as-cast devices. Moreover, a quantitative correlation between PCE and the interaction parameter χ is established, providing a quantitative guide for narrowing the miscibility window and identifying the optimal composition. These findings validate the efficacy of χ-parameter-mediated miscibility engineering in regulating blend phase behavior and provide a framework for advancing efficient as-cast OSCs.

10.1002/adma.75348.title: Methanesulfonic Acid as a Dual-Role Reagent for Porous Polymer Network Design
10.1002/adma.75348.abstract: ABSTRACT The need to develop new materials for energy and environmental sustainability has drawn significant attention in recent years due to population growth, depletion of raw materials, and rising costs. Porous materials are at the center of this quest, necessitating facile approaches for their synthesis, as well as for both pristine and post-synthetically modified sorbents. This is crucial to reduce chemical waste and hazards involved in the process. Methanesulfonic acid (MSA) is currently being explored as a reagent for the design and fabrication of porous polymer networks (PPNs), with several successful reports so far in the literature. This perspective highlights the overall properties and benefits of MSA for the design of PPNs. A better understanding of MSA's capabilities will open new frontiers and help overcome the limitations of difficult-to-scale PPNs. This is because although these PPNs are robust, they still suffer major techno-economic setbacks that hinder their integration into industrial processes. In addition to the cost of starting materials, which pose a challenge to commercialization, the synthetic approach also contributes significantly. As MSA can play the role of both a solvent and an acid catalyst in a reaction, it is a promising dual-role reagent for the design of PPNs.
authors: Kelechi Festus, Arnab Ghosh, Ankit Mondal, Theresa Ariri, Suman Mandal, Ahana Sarkar, Urme Podder, Qingsheng Wang, Hong-Cai Zhou

10.1002/adma.75407.title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO2 and N2
10.1002/adma.75407.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy-intensive Bosch-Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO 2 capture and reduction, N 2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two-step tandem platform combining ionic-liquid-modified metal-organic framework (IL@PCN-250-Fe 2 Co) with a trinuclear copper-based covalent organic framework (HTP-Cu 3 -imi-COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO 2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP-Cu 3 -imi-COF couples the generated CO with ambient N 2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·g cat −1 ·h −1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 . In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole-functionalized HTP segments act as hole-rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N 2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu 3 clusters serve as electron-rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.
authors: Nan-Nan Zhang, Ling-He Kong, Zhi-Hao Zhao, Xiu Qiao, Tian-Shu Song, Yan Sun, Ya Wang, Lu-Hua Shao, Hong Dong, Feng-Ming Zhang

10.1002/adma.75418.title: Cation-Framework-Preserving Oxygen-Vacancy Engineering for Broadband Infrared Emission in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
10.1002/adma.75418.abstract: ABSTRACT High-temperature radiative ceramics require broadband infrared emission and stable structures, but the defects that enhance emission can also weaken oxide lattices. Here, we regulate oxygen vacancies in (MnCrFeNiCu) 3 O 4 , a high-entropy spinel oxide (HEO), by vacuum annealing without changing the nominal cation composition. This approach regulates oxygen nonstoichiometry without introducing an additional cation-substitution variable. The binary Mn-Cr reference has band-averaged emissivities of 0.668 and 0.726 over 0.78-2.5 and 2.5-16 µm, respectively. Pristine HEO increases these values to 0.919 and 0.863, while the optimized HEO-O V -5 h reaches 0.932 and 0.902. Multication incorporation broadens electronic states near the band edges. Oxygen removal creates vacancy-derived states, redistributes charge, and changes local M─O coordination. The vacancy-derived states are consistent with localized d - d excitation, intervalence charge transfer, and polaron-related absorption, while changes in M─O coordination broaden vibrational absorption. Together, these electronic and local structural changes are consistent with the enhanced infrared emissivity. The spinel framework and high emissivity remain largely preserved after annealing at 1000°C for 5 h. These results show that oxygen vacancies can be regulated within a stable multication spinel to combine broadband infrared emission with high-temperature stability.
authors: Cheng-Yu He, Ge-Ting Sun, Wei-Ming Wang, Bao-Hua Liu, Zhong-Wei Lu, Xiang-Hu Gao

10.1002/adma.75081.title: Achieving High Spatial Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy Studies in Closed Liquid Cells
10.1002/adma.75081.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LCTEM) is a rising technique for probing dynamic processes and structural transformations in liquid environments at the nanoscale. However, its broader application is largely constrained by limited spatial resolution, which arises from electron scattering by the encapsulating membranes and the liquid layer. Recent advances in instrument design, micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS)-based cells, and ultrathin window materials have substantially improved imaging quality, yet achieving atomic-scale resolution in liquids remains a formidable challenge. This review provides a comprehensive overview of such strategies developed to enhance the spatial resolution of LCTEM, emphasizing the roles of liquid layer thickness, MEMS design, and cell configuration. We highlight representative approaches, such as reducing liquid and membrane thicknesses, optimizing MEMS architectures, and employing grid-based liquid cells, and discuss their underlying mechanisms and recent progress. Finally, we outline current challenges and future opportunities for achieving high-resolution, multifunctional LCTEM systems capable of capturing dynamic processes in realistic liquid environments.
authors: Siqi Guo, Hongyu Sun, Le Shu, Xuejin Ge, Raquel Aymerich-Armengol, Siyuan Zhang, Long Ren, Ningyan Cheng, Christina Scheu, Binghui Ge

10.1002/adma.75419.title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery-Type Operation: A Re-Functionalized Ti-MOF for Solar Energy Storage
10.1002/adma.75419.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient harvesting, storage, and on-demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy-driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti-based bipyridine MOF, COK47-bpy, and its ReCl(CO) 3 -functionalized analogue, ReCl47-bpy , as photochargeable materials for time-decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and “electron sink” sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible-light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47-bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g −1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution with electron-to-H 2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO-supported layers, ReCl47-bpy |FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g −1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re-functionalized Ti-MOFs as versatile platforms for solar-driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF-based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next-generation MOF-based energy devices.
authors: Shufan Wu, Chuyi Liu, Vasilis Petropoulos, Evgenia Dmitrieva, Giulio Cerullo, Erling Thyrhaug, Jürgen Hauer, Julien Warnan, Roland A. Fischer

10.1002/adma.75382.title: “Water-in-Water” Biphasic Electrolyte for Aqueous Zinc-ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75382.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by unstable Zn metal interfaces, where nonuniform Zn 2+ transport induces concentration polarization and accelerates parasitic reactions. Here we show that Zn 2+ flux can instead be regulated by aqueous-aqueous interfaces. A fully aqueous “water-in-water” (W/W) biphasic electrolyte, comprising dextran (Dex)-rich phase droplets (∼10 µm) suspended in a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-rich aqueous phase, creates phase boundaries that continuously buffer local Zn 2+ accumulation and redistribute ions during plating and stripping. As a result, Zn||Zn cells cycle stably for 1100 h at 10 mA cm −2 and 10 mAh cm −2 , and Ah-level Zn||NaV 3 O 8 pouch cells sustain long-term operation. This work demonstrates an aqueous electrolyte architecture in which interfacial electrostatics, rather than solvent chemistry, governs Zn 2+ transport.
authors: Yilang Yao, Dun Wang, Xiaoke Wang, Xianbin Kuang, Xiangyong Zhang, Cuiping Han

10.1002/adma.74638.title: Mitochondria-Targeted Pyroptosis Orchestrated by Photodynamic Microneedle Patches Potentiates Melanoma Immunoradiotherapy
10.1002/adma.74638.abstract: ABSTRACT The lethality of melanoma stems from its high metastatic propensity, intrinsic apoptosis resistance, and a profoundly immunosuppressive microenvironment, which collectively undermine conventional radiotherapy and immunotherapy. Here, we develop a spatiotemporally precise therapeutic strategy using mitochondria-targeted photodynamic microneedles ( mito TPS-MNs) to orchestrate GSDME-mediated pyroptosis and potentiate systemic immunoradiotherapy. Upon transdermal photoactivation, mito TPS induces intense, mitochondria-confined reactive oxygen species (ROS) bursts, triggering a caspase-3/GSDME-dependent pyroptotic cascade while simultaneously disrupting mitochondrial respiration to alleviate tumor hypoxia. This dual-action mechanism sensitizes melanoma to x-ray irradiation, achieving near-complete regression of primary tumors and remodeling “cold” tumor microenvironments into immunologically “hot” niches. The explosive release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) from pyroptotic cells functions as an in situ cancer vaccine, promoting dendritic cell maturation, the systemic recruitment of CD8 + cytotoxic T lymphocytes, and potent abscopal responses against untreated distant metastases. Our work establishes mitochondria-directed pyroptosis as a mechanistic switch to bypass the inherent apoptotic resistance of melanoma, providing a clinically translatable strategy to convert localized interventions into systemic immunity against advanced melanoma.
authors: Ziyao Lu, Xinyu He, Yuwei Wang, Hui Chen, Yuxiao Gu, Yutong Shi, Huiyu Bu, Hengte Ke, Huabing Chen, Lu Xu, Kai Yang, Hui He, Zhengqing Guo

10.1002/adma.75416.title: Tuning N-Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni1Aun-SrTiO3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis
10.1002/adma.75416.abstract: ABSTRACT Inefficient generation of N-related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N 2 , has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N-related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni 1 Au n active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu-STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N 2 adsorption/activation and effective generation of N-related intermediates to facilitate C-N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg g cat. −1 , with successful crystallization of a collectible solid-phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction-temperature programmed desorption-mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N 2 , which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N 2 and confirm the formation of critical N-related intermediates (e.g., *NH 2 ) on the NiAu-STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C-N coupling intermediate (*NH 2 COO - ) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O.
authors: Dong Li, Shaochuan Zhai, Jinhu Wang, Junyu Gao, Ning Xu, Chao Zhou, Zafer Eroglu, Önder Metin, Li-Ping Zhang, Li-Zhu Wu, Yunxuan Zhao, Tierui Zhang

10.1002/adma.74746.title: Interfacial Dynamic Oxygen Exchange Preserves C─O Bonds for Selective CO2-to-Ethanol Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adma.74746.abstract: ABSTRACT Intermediate-valence copper (Cu + ) is essential for preserving C─O bonds during the electrochemical reduction of CO 2 to ethanol, yet its progressive over-reduction to Cu 0 under operating potentials inevitably dictates C─O bond cleavage and shifts selectivity toward ethylene. Herein, we propose an interfacial dynamic oxygen exchange strategy to stabilize Cu + sites and steer the ethanol reaction pathway. We realize this mechanism by engineering a few-layer ceria-coated cuprous oxide (Cu 2 O@CeO 2 ) catalyst featuring an oxygen vacancy-rich heterointerface (Ce−O V −Cu). Operando spectroscopic measurements and density functional theory calculations reveal that these interfacial oxygen vacancies act as core mediators; by continuously capturing and migrating oxygen species derived from CO 2 , they effectively arrest the reduction of adjacent Cu + siteversuss. Crucially, this dynamic interface dictates the asymmetric C─C coupling of *CH 2 and *CHO, successfully preserving the C−O bond during the subsequent protonation of *CH 2 CHO to *CH 3 CHO. Consequently, the optimized catalyst delivers an outstanding ethanol Faradaic efficiency of 68.5% at −1.1 V versus RHE and exhibits robust operational stability exceeding 150 h, substantially outperforming pristine Cu 2 O. This study establishes vacancy-mediated dynamic oxygen exchange as a robust strategy for preserving key oxygen-containing functional groups in highly selective CO 2 -to-ethanol electrosynthesis.
authors: Jiwei Li, Jiaying He, Deyu Zhu, Chenfeng Xia, Mingzhi Wang, Liang Dong, Lebin Cai, Wensheng Fang, Yaqiong Su, Fei Song, Wei Guo, Bao Yu Xia

10.1002/adma.74747.title: Side-Chain-Induced Interlayer Slipping in Metalloporphyrin COFs Enables Microenvironment and Spin-State Regulation for Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
10.1002/adma.74747.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) involves a cascade of intrinsically coupled processes, rendering the independent optimization of catalytic kinetics and thermodynamics challenging. In this study, we introduce a structural regulation strategy via steric-driven interlayer slipping engineering of metalloporphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to decouple and simultaneously optimize the catalytic microenvironment and the spin state of the active metal center. Through regulating the length of alkoxy side-chains, conventional AA stacking is transformed into a moderately serrated slipped configuration (AA*). Kinetically, the resulting slipped nanochannels enhance local hydrophobicity and spatial confinement, thereby greatly enriching in-channel CO 2 concentration and suppressing hydrogen evolution. Thermodynamically and electronically, this interlayer slipping reconstructs the ligand field of catalytic Co sites and maximizes vertical π-d exchange interactions. As a result, this triggers a collective spin transition from isolated low-spin ( S = 1/2) monomers to a high-spin ( S = 3/2) state, which significantly prolongs charge carrier lifetimes and optimizes the adsorption and activation of the *COOH intermediate. Consequently, the optimized CoP-COFs deliver a record CO production rate of 71.4 mmol g −1 h −1 with 90% selectivity among porphyrin-based COF photocatalysts. This work establishes stacking engineering as a versatile strategy for decoupling entangled reaction steps to enable efficient solar fuel production.
authors: Jie He, Qingxuan Chen, Minxian Zhang, Wenhao Zhao, Aoni Xu, Jinqiang Zhang, Hongqi Sun, Shaobin Wang, Xiaoguang Duan

10.1002/adma.74700.title: Nonorthogonal Polarization-Multiplexed and Detachable Diffractive Processors
10.1002/adma.74700.abstract: ABSTRACT Polarization multiplexing provides an elegant route for parallel all-optical processing, yet its intrinsic orthogonality fundamentally limits channel capacity and interlayer interaction in diffractive systems. We present a detachable diffractive processor that leverages nonorthogonal polarization multiplexing to overcome these bottlenecks. The processor features a convolutional-like architecture composed of detachable diffractive layers, enabling global and interlayer function multiplexing with accelerated training and expanded versatility. Experimentally, we realize 12 independent functions-4 classifiers and 8 holograms-across 4 polarization-decoupled channels in a dual-layer system and extend to 18 channels supporting 6 classifiers and 36 holograms using a triple-layer configuration. Furthermore, we demonstrate a multi-level optical encryption framework that combines image transformation and holographic generation. This work establishes a scalable framework for multifunctional diffractive computing, enabling compact processors, high-capacity holography, and secure optical information technologies.
authors: Xiaofei Zang, Zhiyu Tan, Zhe Gao, Xiaomin Chen, Fei Ding, Yiming Zhu, Songlin Zhuang

10.1002/adma.74589.title: Perception-Feedback Mapping Strategies for Flexible Human-Machine Interfaces
10.1002/adma.74589.abstract: ABSTRACT The field of flexible human-machine interfaces (HMIs) has been evolving rapidly with progress in materials science, structural design, device fabrication, and system integration. Developments of advanced flexible sensing and feedback devices have remarkably expanded the perceptual modalities, feedback capabilities, and functional scope of these systems. However, the broader deployment of flexible HMIs depends not only on the device performance of sensing/feedback components, but also on the control strategy that translates sensed signals into command outputs for feedback modules. This review highlights recent progress in such perception-feedback mapping strategies for flexible HMIs. Representative sensing and feedback modules, together with common system-level physical architectures, are briefly introduced as a basis for analyzing the relationship between sensed inputs and feedback outputs. A systematic framework is then proposed based on the principle of signal flow from the perception to the feedback side, allowing perception-feedback mapping strategies to be classified into command-based mapping, continuous mapping, and closed-loop control. Comprehensive discussions on these three categories of mapping strategies are presented, covering their operating principles, system implementation, and practical applications. Finally, we discuss current challenges and future directions toward more robust, generalizable, and integrated flexible HMI systems.
authors: Ruoxi Yang, Shiwei Xu, Wenbo Pang, Yihui Zhang

10.1002/adma.74707.title: In Situ Reconstruction of a Highly Integrated Cu/Cu2O/MoO2 Dual Heterojunctions for High-Performance CO2 Photothermal Catalysis
10.1002/adma.74707.abstract: ABSTRACT During heterogeneous photothermal catalysis, catalysts are prone to undergo random and disordered structural evolution, which poses a severe challenge to the construction of advanced photothermal catalytic systems integrating photoexcited charge carrier separation, molecular activation, and active-site engineering. In this work, we employ an in situ reconstruction strategy to fabricate a highly integrated Cu/Cu 2 O/MoO 2 composite catalyst using Cu 3 Mo 2 O 9 as the precursor under a CO 2 /H 2 reaction atmosphere. The as-constructed Cu/Cu 2 O Schottky junction and Cu 2 O/MoO 2 p-n junction form a dual-heterojunction structure, enabling efficient separation of photogenerated charge carriers. Meanwhile, amorphous MoO 2 with abundant oxygen vacancies and Cu/Cu 2 O provide functionally complementary activation sites for CO 2 activation and H 2 dissociation/spillover, respectively. Benefiting from the efficient synergistic interplay among the three components (Cu, Cu 2 O, and MoO 2 ), the Cu/Cu 2 O/MoO 2 catalyst enables the efficient conversion of CO 2 via the photothermal reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction, delivering a superior CO production rate of 14.65 mmol g −1 h −1 alongside ultra-long stability, retaining high activity across an impressive 215-h continuous reaction run. This study offers a new avenue for the construction of integrated functional photothermal catalysts with high performance via an in situ reconstruction approach.
authors: Xingjuan Li, Yuhao Guo, Qinhui Guan, Na Li, Zheyi Sun, Yiyao Sun, Weiguo Huang, Huiyu Luo, Shengqun Tang, Canyu Yuan, Bao Pan, Jiani Qin, Jing Li, Tingjiang Yan

10.1002/adma.74750.title: Data-Driven Accelerated Discovery of LNMCO Cathodes Materials via 37-Dimensional Parameter Space Mining With a Cascaded Neural Network
10.1002/adma.74750.abstract: ABSTRACT The vast, unexplored synthesis space of LNMCO cathode materials contains potential solutions to the long-standing trade-off between energy density and stability. To navigate this high-dimensional space, a predictive tool capable of accurately mapping the complex relationships between synthesis parameters and electrochemical performance is essential. Here, a cascaded neural network (CaNN) architecture was designed to simulate the material synthesis workflow. This model synchronously maps 37 process dimensions within the composition-processing-structure-property-performance (CPSPP) paradigm. By utilizing a cascaded structure, the output of upstream prediction tasks serves as the input for downstream tasks, enabling the capture of hierarchical dependencies that govern material properties. This design choice proved highly effective, achieving superior predictive accuracy with an overall coefficient of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.85. Furthermore, SHAP analysis was integrated to open the model's “black box,” demonstrating a mechanism-informed approach where predictions align closely with the underlying physical laws of structural inheritance. Experimental validation of nine candidates spanning diverse compositions and synthesis routes confirms the predictive accuracy of the strategy (prediction errors < 10%), establishing a “CaNN modeling → Latin Hypercube Sampling → Wa Screening → Experiments validation” framework for the accelerated discovery of high-performance cathode materials.
authors: Chenfeng Wang, Quanjiang Li, Lihong Zhang, Fei Liu, Ning Yang, Zundong Xiao, Aoxuan Wang, Xingjiang Liu, Rijie Wang

10.1002/adma.74708.title: Nonporous Metal-Organic Framework Enables Record-High Uranium Extraction and Complete Diglyme Degradation
10.1002/adma.74708.abstract: ABSTRACT Nuclear energy accommodates rising energy demand of artificial intelligence yet poses environmental risks, making uranium extraction from wastewater important. We herein report a nonporous metal-organic framework CuTTB-3 as cathode in an H-type electrolytic cell (two compartments separated by an anion-exchange membrane) for uranium extraction. Unlike single-chamber cell limited by diglyme-induced redissolution of uranium deposits, CuTTB-3-based H-type configuration facilitates 99.8% uranium extraction within 1 h and complete diglyme degradation. This system overcomes concentration limits of 100 g L −1 diglyme and 100 mg L −1 uranyl in conventional setups. It retains >96.4% extraction efficiency over 15 cycles, achieving a cumulative U(VI) extraction amount of 28855 mg g −1 within 10 h and an extraction rate of 2886 mg g −1 h −1 , both record-high values among reported materials. A flow-cell setup treated 1 L simulated wastewater, delivering 96.8% extraction efficiency and cumulative capacity of 19360 mg g −1 . Comparisons with porous analogue CuTTB-4 confirm structural robustness and interfacial charge transfer kinetics dominate electrochemical uranium extraction. Different from traditional adsorption-based uranium extraction materials that rely heavily on porostiy, this work realizes efficient uranium extraction via an electrochemical deposition route based on a nonporous MOF, which expands the application scenario of nonporous materials in radioactive wastewater treatment.
authors: Yingtong Lv, Hao Zhang, Zijian Li, Rong He, Wenkun Zhu, Yan Liu, Maobing Shuai, Zhiwei Hu, Jian-Qiang Wang, Linjuan Zhang
