10.1002/adma.74711.title: Realization of Air-Stable Two-Dimensional Superconductor Nb2Pd3Te5 With Quasi-One-Dimensional Pair Density Modulation
10.1002/adma.74711.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional (2D) superconductors provide a fertile platform for exploring reduced-dimensional superconductivity and emergent quantum phenomena. Incorporating quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) structural motifs into 2D superconductors offers a powerful route to engineer strong electronic anisotropy, enabling unconventional superconducting states and anisotropic superconducting transport functionalities. However, such systems remain rarely realized. Here we report the realization of a 2D superconductor Nb 2 Pd 3 Te 5 , exhibiting an intrinsic quasi-1D pair density modulation. Monolayer and bilayer Nb 2 Pd 3 Te 5 is synthesized via van-der-Waals epitaxy. Using ultralow-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy, we observe the quasi-1D crystal structure and superconductivity below ∼0.6 K with a pronounced quasi-1D pair density modulation. Remarkably, both monolayer and bilayer Nb 2 Pd 3 Te 5 show strong air stability. Our findings establish atomically 2D Nb 2 Pd 3 Te 5 as a robust and promising platform for exploring novel low-dimensional quantum phenomena and anisotropy-enabled superconducting devices.
authors: Jiayi Wang, Hui Guo, Hao Zhang, Haowei Chen, Peixuan Li, Xianghe Han, Ziang Wang, Siyu Xu, Qian Fang, Haohao Xu, Shixuan Du, Chengmin Shen, Hui Chen, Wang Yao, Hong-Jun Gao

10.1002/adma.74678.title: Engineering Metal-Pocket Cooperativity in Single-Atom COF Nanozymes for Selective Cascade Catalysis
10.1002/adma.74678.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanozymes have emerged as robust and scalable alternatives to natural enzymes, offering high catalytic activity and structural stability. However, reproducing the exquisite selectivity of enzymatic catalysis, particularly their ability to operate with high precision in complex reaction systems, remains a central challenge. Herein, inspired by the heme-pocket architecture and cooperative regulation in cytochrome P450, we report a nanozyme multilevel programming strategy based on a single-atom covalent organic framework (COF) platform constructed from heme-like metal-porphyrin nodes and linkers bearing chiral amino-acid residues, enabling selective editing of metal catalytic centers and enzyme-mimetic pockets to control catalytic activity, chemoselectivity, and stereochemical outcomes. As a proof of concept, we employ a biomimetic chiral cascade that couples methanol dehydrogenase-like alcohol oxidation with a chymopapain-inspired asymmetric aldol reaction to probe and optimize metal-pocket cooperativity within the nanozyme. The programmed MnPor-Pro-based nanozyme delivers high product yields, excellent chemo- and stereoselectivity, and outstanding recyclability in the cascade reactions, indicating the effectiveness of this strategy. This work provides a rational design insight for engineering highly selective nanozymes capable of addressing complex, multistep transformations, significantly bridging the gap between artificial and natural enzymatic systems.
authors: Ziping Li, Qijun Sun, Yawen Hao, Haotian Wen, Shery Chang, Fengwang Li, Jiangtao Xu, Kang Liang

10.1002/adma.74487.title: Sustainable Poly(Lactic Acid)/Graphene Oxide Bioelectronic Platform for Neurotransmitters Sensing and Tunable Stimulation of Astrocytes
10.1002/adma.74487.abstract: ABSTRACT Biocompatible and biodegradable electrode platforms were developed using laser-scribed poly(lactic acid)/graphene oxide (PLA/GO) composites, prepared via an innovative waterborne dispersion method. Laser treatment enabled the formation of graphene/graphite-like structures. By varying the fluence of the laser used, it was possible to modulate the physico-chemical properties of the conductive traces obtained, finally leading to materials characterized by tunable sheet resistance, chemical structure, and morphology. Thanks to the low charge transfer resistance and the peculiar electrocatalytic and antifouling properties observed, the platforms were applied as electrochemical sensors for the detection of various biomarkers in biological fluids, namely ascorbic and uric acid, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) and catecholamine-based neurotransmitters, outperforming commercial carbon screen-printed electrodes. Contextually, laser-scribed electrodes were used to demonstrate the effectiveness of a novel approach for selectively stimulating Ca 2 + signaling in astrocytes. The results here reported open the possibility to apply laser-scribed PLA/GO as innovative eco-sustainable solutions for simultaneous treatment of pathological conditions and monitoring of the resulting neurotransmitter expression in in vitro and in vivo models.
authors: Alessandra Scidà, Giulia Cazzador, Roberta Fabbri, Matteo Calosi, Alessandro Silvestri, Andrea Candini, Fabiola Liscio, Franco Corticelli, Aikaterini Konstantoulaki, Andrea D'Iorio, Marco Caprini, Vincenzo Palermo, Monica Bertoldo, Valentina Benfenati, Chiara Zanardi, Emanuele Treossi

10.1002/adma.74752.title: Enhanced Mechanical Recycling of Polymer Mixtures by a Trifunctional Dynamic Crosslinker
10.1002/adma.74752.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical recycling of mixed post-consumer apolar/polar polymers, due to their mis-matched polarity and inherent immiscibility, is typically a downcycling process yielding brittle materials. An emerging method that can enhance recycling of such mixtures into dynamically crosslinked, high-performance thermosets is a dynamic crosslinker (DC) platform; however, current DCs typically require an external catalyst and, due to their insufficiently high peak activation temperature ( T a <190°C), are limited to a subset of applicable polymers and unsuitable for industrial melt-extrusion processing of high melting temperature ( T m ) polymers. Herein, we report a trifunctional DC incorporating three sought-after properties: thermally robust pyridotriazole cores as the high- T a (245°C) crosslinking sites compatible with reactive extrusion up to 270°C; dynamic siloxane linkages as the robust yet exchangeable bonds; and pyridine/ester functionalities as the internal catalysis sites devoid of external catalysts. Overall, this self-catalyzed, high- T a DC can compatibilize waste plastic mixtures containing high T m polymers and impart the recycled mixtures with superior thermoset properties such as enhanced creep resistance and thermomechanical stability while being melt-(re)processable.
authors: Xavier Westworth, Essa Shamsan, Yunpeng Gao, Nevaya Carr, Eugene Y.-X. Chen

10.1002/adma.74631.title: Interlayer Water Activation Supplemented Dual Oxygen Evolution Reaction Channels in Layered Double Hydroxides for Efficient Seawater Electrolysis
10.1002/adma.74631.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct seawater electrolysis powered by renewable electricity offers a promising avenue for sustainable production of green hydrogen, yet the challenges of chloride-induced corrosion and sluggish kinetics of oxygen evolution reaction (OER) persist with electrocatalysts. Here, a sulfur-modified CoFe-layered double hydroxide catalyst (S-CF· n H 2 O) is developed to address the above activity and stability issues, in which sulfur etching-assisted targeted reconstruction occurs and yields high-density accessible active sites both on the surface and in the interlayer galleries; meanwhile, sulfate ions derived from sulfur oxidation adsorb on catalyst and create an electrostatic Cl − -repelling barrier. Featuring interlayer space as a supplementary reaction region and an electrostatic-protecting sulfate layer, S-CF· n H 2 O catalyst achieves exceptional OER activity (with an overpotential of 370 mV at 1 A cm −2 ) and unprecedented durability exceeding 12 000 h in alkaline seawater; the seawater electrolyzer assembled from S-CF· n H 2 O also demonstrates stable operation for 10 000 h at 600 mA cm −2 . In situ spectroscopic and isotope tracing analyses reveal a distinct oxide pathway mechanism with the interlayer water, in contrast to the adsorbate evolution mechanism occurring at the catalyst outer surface. This work conceptually reveals the robustness of interlayer chemistry for the design of high-performance LDH-based catalysts.
authors: Rongli Fan, Gaoxiang He, Minyue Zhao, Huihui Yan, Bin Gao, Zhonghua Li, Huiting Huang, Xizhang Wang, Weichang Hao, Jianyong Feng, Zhigang Zou, Zhaosheng Li

10.1002/adma.74685.title: Bio-Inspired Phase-Transition Logic Gates for Autonomous Thermal Management
10.1002/adma.74685.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional thermal management strategies rely predominantly on passive heat dissipation or open-loop external control, struggling to address the transient and heterogeneous thermal loads of modern micro/nanodevices. Inspired by the sense-perceive-act closed-loop feedback of biological perspiration, we propose an autonomous thermal management strategy that encodes a first-order solid-liquid phase transition as a molecular logic gate. Within this phase-change-gated polymer network (Perspire X), the melting of polyethylene glycol (PEG) acts as a physical threshold. Surpassing this critical temperature triggers a macroscopic network arrangement, directly translating thermal sensing into an accelerated on-demand water release. We define a logic-gating figure of merit (LG-FOM) of 2.62 to quantify this behavior, demonstrating the discretized and switchable regulation of coupled mass and heat transport channels. Consequently, the material exhibits non-linear cooling amplification, achieving a 20.8-fold extension in effective cooling duration and a 13.5°C temperature drop compared with traditional phase-transition cooling materials. Furthermore, it demonstrates robust mechanical integrity alongside an exceptional thermal buffering capacity that effectively buffers the simulated pulsed thermal fluctuations under the tested conditions. Transcending traditional passive heat sinks, this phase-transition-gated transport mechanism outlines a scalable, materials-level thermodynamic programming strategy for next-generation electronics and intelligent energy systems.
authors: Yabi Yang, Wanpeng Liu, Bao Yu Xia, Xiang Lu, Jinping Qu

10.1002/adma.74615.title: ROS-Scavenging Single-Component Polymeric Nanocarriers for Precision siRNA Delivery in Pulmonary Fibrosis Therapy
10.1002/adma.74615.abstract: ABSTRACT Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive refractory lung disorder with limited effective therapies. Although RNA interference (RNAi) holds promise for IPF treatment, current delivery systems are hampered by complex preparation, redundant components, and an inability to modulate oxidative stress, which severely compromises their therapeutic outcomes. Herein, we design a single-component, lung-targeted nanosystem, PPN@siIL11, that simplifies formulation while integrating dual functions of efficient siRNA delivery and reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging. Upon intravenous administration, this streamlined platform exhibits enhanced pulmonary accumulation, effectively silences the profibrotic gene IL11, and suppresses fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transdifferentiation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. Concurrently, it scavenges overproduced ROS to alleviate oxidative stress-mediated lung damage. Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrate the potent anti-fibrotic efficacy of PPN@siIL11. By overcoming critical drawbacks of conventional multi-component carriers, this multifunctional single-component platform establishes a translatable approach for RNAi-based IPF therapy, with potential applicability to other lung diseases.
authors: Yuxin Yang, Hua Zhang, Jianjun Du, Wen Sun, Xiaojun Peng, Jiangli Fan

10.1002/adma.74732.title: Geometric Complementarity and Electrostatic Fluctuation Control in Dual-Asymmetric Acceptors for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.74732.abstract: ABSTRACT Asymmetric molecular design has emerged as an effective strategy for developing high-performance acceptors for organic solar cells (OSCs). Here, we introduce a dual-asymmetric topology strategy, in which the stereochemical configurations of both the central core and terminal groups are co-engineered. Using this approach, we synthesized an isomeric pair, Th2Cl-a-2Cl and Th2Cl-b-2Cl and benchmarked them against the singly asymmetric a-CH-Th2Cl and Th2Cl-4Cl. We find that the distinctive steric conformation of Th2Cl-a-2Cl promotes a geometrically complementary, interlocked packing motif within the crystal lattice. This not only reinforces the three-dimensional network connectivity but, more importantly, gives rise to a more uniform local electrostatic environment at the molecular-skeleton scale. As a result, Th2Cl-a-2Cl exhibits weaker and more balanced environment-induced electrostatic fluctuations along the backbone, which helps reduce local electrostatic perturbations during charge transport. Consequently, PM6:Th2Cl-a-2Cl devices deliver a champion PCE of 20.18% with a high fill factor (FF) of 80.88%, while significantly suppressing the non-radiative recombination loss (Δ E 3 ) to 0.190 eV. These results establish geometric complementarity and electrostatic homogeneity, achieved through topological engineering, as an effective route to improve the efficiency of OSCs.
authors: Jiye Chen, Ruohan Wang, Peiran Wang, Hanzhe Shi, Wenkai Zhao, Longyu Li, Jian Liu, Zhaoyang Yao, Chenxi Li, Xiangjian Wan, Yongsheng Chen

10.1002/adma.74739.title: Ultra-broadband Epsilon-Near-Zero Ultrathin Metafilms Assembled by 2D Nanosheets Overcoming Size Limitation in Metamaterials
10.1002/adma.74739.abstract: ABSTRACT Broadband epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials are crucial for 6G (sixth generation mobile networks) signal stability, biochemical sensor accuracy, and intelligent weapon systems. Here, the ultrathin ( d ∼10 µm) 2D metafilms achieving low-frequency ultra-broadband ENZ (10 kHz-1 MHz, d / λ ∼10 −10 ) are constructed via the self-assembly of nanosheets (MXene and graphene oxide) and interface engineering. High-resistance interfaces and wrinkles can block free carriers, suppressing long-range plasma and Drude-type negative dielectric response, while these carriers tend to accumulate locally at the interfaces and enhance Debye-type positive dielectric response. These two pathways achieve the ultra-broadband ENZ behavior via the synergistic cancellation effect between these two responses with comparable intensity and dispersion characteristics. The ENZ (|ε′|<1) with a 100-fold ultrabroad bandwidth (10 kHz-1 MHz) is obtained, 10 kHz of ENZ also updates the low-frequency limit of ENZ in materials. Besides, the thickness of 10 µm is achieved in metafilms, a smallest d / λ value (∼10 −10 ), overcoming the size limitation of ENZ media. The effectiveness of the ultra-broadband ENZ is verified in electromagnetic tunneling devices, where metafilms can replace complex artificial arrays. This work establishes a new material-genesis strategy for ultra-broadband ENZ rather than artificial metamaterial arrays, easily applicable across the entire electromagnetic spectra.
authors: Mingxiang Liu, Peitao Xie, Yuru Wang, Zidong Zhang, Runhua Fan, Qing Hou, Yao Liu

10.1002/adma.74726.title: Targeting Nonclassical Monocytes via Artificial Cell-Microneedles for Precision Psoriasis Therapy
10.1002/adma.74726.abstract: ABSTRACT Current therapies for inflammatory skin diseases predominantly rely on broad systemic immunosuppression and lack precision toward defined immune-cell subsets. Here, we identify CX3CR1 + nonclassical monocytes (NCMs) as an inflammatory monocyte subset that contributes to the amplification of psoriasiform inflammation, as supported by integrated analyses of human single-cell transcriptomics, genetic depletion, and adoptive-transfer models. To preferentially engage these disease-associated NCMs, we engineer an artificial cell-microneedle platform, termed CX3@GUV-DMF, comprising CX3CL1-functionalized, drug-loaded giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs) embedded within a dissolvable hyaluronic acid (HA) microneedle array. Following intradermal insertion, surface-presented CX3CL1 actively navigates GUVs to pathogenic CX3CR1 + NCMs, facilitating the targeted, sustained release of the loaded drug. In vivo evaluations and transcriptomic profiling demonstrate that this localized immunomodulatory strategy attenuates inflammatory myeloid activation, neutrophil infiltration, and Th17-associated responses while promoting restoration of epidermal barrier-associated programs. These findings establish a materials-enabled strategy for subset-oriented immune modulation and local inflammatory-niche remodeling, advancing inflammatory skin therapy beyond nonspecific immunosuppression.
authors: Qian Chen, Xiaodong Zhou, Tian Sun, Hantao Li, Siqi Mai, Yong Miao, Sirong Chen, Jinhong Qin, Xunru Liang, Xin Li, Pengchao Zhao, Liming Bian

10.1002/adma.74690.title: Photothermal-Photoelectric Synergistic Management in High-Entropy Alloys for Full-Spectrum Solar CO2-to-CH4 Conversion
10.1002/adma.74690.abstract: ABSTRACT Current photothermocatalysts, characterized by inadequate photogenerated electrons for accelerating reaction kinetics as well as excessive demand for high light intensity, face major obstacles to practical application. In this study, a heteroarchitectured photothermocatalyst is presented by integrating the FeCoNiCuCr (FCNCuCr) high-entropy alloys (HEAs) photothermal layer, the Al doped ZnO (AZO) photoelectric layer, and the thermal radiation blocking component of chromium-plated glass (Cg). The obtained Cg/FCNCuCr/AZO photothermocatalyst exhibits an unprecedented CO 2 -to-CH 4 conversion performance, with CH 4 yield reaching 5082.9 µmol g −1 h −1 , which is 14 and 4 times that obtained from pristine FCNCuCr HEAs and Cg/FCNCuCr, respectively, surpassing the state-of-the-art photothermocatalysts and photocatalysts for gas-solid atmospheric pressure CO 2 conversion with H 2 O supplied as proton source. Thanks to effective photothermal management, the Cg/FCNCuCr/AZO heteroarchitectured photothermocatalyst achieves full-spectrum solar absorption by minimizing thermal radiation, thereby realizing excellent photothermal conversion capability. Meanwhile, the sputtered AZO photoelectric layer is integrated to establish an interfacial Schottky barrier, harnessing the photoelectric synergy, and further reducing the reaction barrier for CO 2 -to-CH 4 conversion. The present photothermal-photoelectric synergistic management strategy enlightens the design of high-performance photothermocatalysts for solar driven CO 2 conversion.
authors: Guofu Wang, Wenjie Zhang, Qingqing Guan, Chung-Li Dong, Ting Peng, Binglan Wu, Yiqing Wang, Penghui Guo, Bo Kou, Xianglei Liu, Shaohua Shen

10.1002/adma.74491.title: Data-Driven Materials Science for Energy-Sustainable Applications
10.1002/adma.74491.abstract: ABSTRACT Materials science is underpinned by structure-property relationships that govern the function of a material. These relationships can be encoded into algorithms and integrated into machine-learning models that enable the prediction of materials and their cognate properties. However, machine-learning models are largely being trained on computed data owing to a worldwide shortage of real-world (experimental) datasets. This review describes how to capture and collate experimental data from scientific literature using artificial-intelligence (AI) methods to produce materials-domain-specific datasets or language models. Their application in AI-driven enquiries that facilitate progress in energy-sustainable materials science is then illustrated via six case studies that cover: training machine-learning models, data-driven materials discovery, optimizing manufacturing processes, mapping phases of materials, forecasting materials-centric research trends, and classifying types of materials using automated prompt engineering. The future of materials-domain-specific datasets, language models, and decision-making workflows using AI agents is then envisioned for the energy sector. The intrinsic challenges of accessing historical dark data in materials science are then described and contrasted with timely opportunities for leveraging massive amounts of experimental data from laboratories in going forwards; by exploiting electronic-lab notebooks, high-throughput experiments, and digital-twin technologies. These opportunities are illustrated for energy-sustainable materials science, especially the photovoltaic and battery industries.

10.1002/adma.74676.title: Heterojunction-Guided Reconstruction Toward Ru-Co Bridged Dual Sites for Efficient Oxide-Path Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adma.74676.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxide path mechanism (OPM) offers a compelling route to bypass the activity-stability trade-off of conventional oxygen evolution catalysis. However, its deliberate activation has largely relied on doping strategies to create heterometallic dual sites, which suffer from limited electronic tunability. Here, we demonstrate a fundamentally different approach that combines heterojunction engineering with guided in situ reconstruction. By integrating ruthenium oxide with a cobalt-nickel telluride heterostructure, we exploit the pronounced surface reconstruction of tellurides under anodic potentials to in situ generate a metastable CoO 2 phase featuring high-valent cobalt. This reconstructed phase intimately couples with neighboring RuO 2 to form well-defined Co-O-Ru bridged dual sites, which are proposed as the pivotal centers for OPM-enabled O─O coupling. The telluride framework further acts as an electronic modulator, stabilizing ruthenium while promoting high-valent cobalt formation. This synergy yields a catalyst with an overpotential of 213 mV at 100 mA cm −2 and a mass activity 103 times that of commercial RuO 2 . When deployed in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, it operates at 1 A cm −2 with a cell voltage of 1.78 V for over 800 h. Our work establishes heterojunction-induced reconstruction as a powerful strategy to unlock OPM catalysis, moving beyond conventional doping toward dynamically assembled active interfaces.
authors: Qingao Li, Huanhuan Zhang, Shijie Shen, LiLi Zhang, Ping Fang, Lin Gu, Wenwu Zhong

10.1002/adma.74677.title: Energy-Efficient Spin Hall Nano-Oscillators Using Near-Compensated CoGd Ferrimagnets
10.1002/adma.74677.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) based on ferromagnets face practical limitations due to high threshold current densities and large external magnetic field requirements. Ferrimagnets provide an attractive alternative due to their unique magnetic dynamics and potential for energy-efficient spintronic devices. In this study, we report rare-earth−transition-metal (RE−TM) ferrimagnetic SHNOs utilizing Co 1-x Gd x alloys, in which compositional tuning enables high-performance operation near the magnetization compensation. The optimized SHNO operates at a low current density (1.43 × 10 7 A/cm 2 ), a small magnetic field (5 mT), and exhibits a narrow linewidth (0.61 MHz) simultaneously, showing an order-of-magnitude improvement over its ferromagnetic counterparts. This enhanced performance arises from high spin-orbit torque efficiency, low magnetic anisotropy, reduced effective magnetization, and minimized nonlinearity near the compensation point. These results establish RE−TM ferrimagnets as a promising material platform for next-generation spintronic devices and offer new strategies for realizing energy-efficient, high-performance spintronic oscillators.
authors: Jiayu Lei, Raghav Sharma, Shishun Zhao, Fanrui Hu, Yuchen Pu, Chenhui Zhang, Rahul Mishra, Hyunsoo Yang

10.1002/adma.74718.title: Nitrogen-Directed Diamond Nanothreads for Ultrahigh-Sensitivity Humidity Sensing and Noncontact Human-Machine Interfaces
10.1002/adma.74718.abstract: ABSTRACT Diamond nanothreads (DNThs) are an emerging class of one-dimensional carbon materials that combine exceptional mechanical robustness with structural flexibility and tunable surface chemistry. While significant progress has been achieved in the synthesis and structural characterization of DNThs, their functional applications remain relatively unexplored. Here, we employ pyrazine as a nitrogen-containing precursor to synthesize diamond nanothread materials under high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) conditions (10 GPa and 400°C). Structural characterization suggests the formation of predominantly sp 3 -bonded one-dimensional carbon frameworks containing abundant polar surface functionalities. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of the one-dimensional architecture and hydrophilic surface sites, the fabricated DNThs-based humidity sensors exhibit outstanding performance over a broad humidity range (11%-96% RH), including ultrahigh sensitivity (1679.11/%RH), rapid response (5.2 s) and recovery (5.4 s), excellent reproducibility, and long-term stability. Mechanistic investigations indicate that efficient water adsorption and humidity-induced ionic conduction play critical roles in the sensing process, while the one-dimensional framework facilitates efficient charge transport. Furthermore, by integrating DNThs sensor arrays with a microcontroller platform, we demonstrate a non-contact human-machine interface (HMI) capable of gesture recognition and touch-free phone dialing. This work highlights the potential of diamond nanothread-based materials for next-generation intelligent sensing and interactive electronic systems.
authors: Wenwen Liu, Hang Liu, Shoulong Lai, Wuyou Zhang, Yingjie Zhang, Siling Liu, Jinxu Qin, Xiangdong Yang, Xigui Yang

10.1002/adma.74682.title: Metastable Polymers for Circular 3D Printing
10.1002/adma.74682.abstract: ABSTRACT Reducing waste and enabling material reuse are central goals for sustainable advanced manufacturing. In light-based 3D printing, this requires moving beyond permanent networks toward systems that can be easily returned to their original molecular building blocks, while preserving good performance. Here, a shift toward metastable, 3D printable polymers is introduced, which are intrinsically programmed for controlled depolymerization under mild conditions, enabling circular recovery. This concept is realized using self-immolative polymers (SIPs), which undergo triggered, domino-like depolymerization upon activation of a specific labile unit. These polymers are formulated for high-resolution digital light processing 3D printing, yielding mechanically robust structures. Upon exposure to a defined trigger, the printed networks rapidly (in seconds) and completely disassemble under ambient conditions, regenerating their pristine monomers. These are recovered in near-quantitative yield and subsequently reprocessed into chemically identical printable polymers. This metastability-driven approach establishes a transformative pathway for circular 3D printing.
authors: Johannes Markhart, Philipp Mainik, Eva Blasco

10.1002/adma.74680.title: Beyond Nanoporosity: A CO2-Conditioned Glassy Matrix Contributes to the Brittle-to-Ductile Transition of Nanocellular Polyetherimide
10.1002/adma.74680.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanocellular polyetherimide (PEI) exhibits enhanced toughness and impact resistance compared to the initial solid precursor, an effect usually attributed to the presence of nanometric cells within a confined glassy polymer matrix. In this work, we examine whether the CO 2 saturation step used in gas dissolution foaming can affect the mechanical response by modifying the thermodynamic state of the glassy polymer. Thermal annealing without CO 2 increases the yield stress and reduces ductility, whereas solid PEI saturated with CO 2 and subsequently fully desorbed shows lower yield stress, an increase in tensile ductility, and an improved impact response. Density, gas transport, WAXS, and PALS measurements were used to further analyze this state, showing that the effect of CO 2 leads to a subtle modification of the glassy matrix, changing the packing and gas accessible regions of the matrix. It is proposed that this matrix state, together with the nanocellular architecture, contributes to the brittle-to-ductile transition observed in nanocellular PEI. Our work highlights that optimization of the mechanical properties of nanocellular polymers should not only focus on the key characteristics of the final cellular morphology, but also on the conditions that define the state of the polymer matrix surrounding the pores before and during foaming.
authors: Félix Lizalde-Arroyo, Frederik Van Loock, Victoria Bernardo, Tuuli Peltola, René Bes, Alberto Tena, Miguel Ángel Rodríguez-Pérez, Judith Martín-de León

10.1002/adma.75204.title: High-Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy
10.1002/adma.75204.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape-memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s −1 , and a peak power density of 6105 W kg −1 . Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10-fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing-flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.
authors: Chang Xu, Zhuofan Zhang, Zhibing Chen, Chenglin Jia, Jinying Yuan, Zhongqiang Yang

10.1002/adma.75411.title: Self-Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery
10.1002/adma.75411.abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme-rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano-engineered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist-loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs-N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor-associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK-cell-associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs-N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain-related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.
authors: Mengbin Ding, Baoli Zhou, Yijing Zhang, Yuhan Zhang, Xinting Liu, Yulu Hu, Tianze Du, Yong Kang, Li Wang, Xiaoyuan Ji

10.1002/adma.75284.title: Negative-Thermal-Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage
10.1002/adma.75284.abstract: ABSTRACT The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium-ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na + intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore-filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW 2 O 8 . The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high-rate and long-term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (−20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.
authors: Gaobo Chang, Hanqing Zhao, Cheng Huang, Shulian Lei, Junxiang Wang, Zeyu Qiao, Kun Lin, Steven S. C. Chuang, Zhong Li, Xianran Xing, Jieshan Qiu

10.1002/adma.75420.title: Polyacrylate-Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High-Performance Artificial Muscles
10.1002/adma.75420.abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate-based DEFAs (PA-DEFAs) from a bimodal-networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s −1 . The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core-to-shell flow-rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch-free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg − 1 , and a peak power density of 443 W kg − 1 -outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel-connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta-ray with modular fault-tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA-DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing-compatible platform for next-generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.
authors: Mengke Shi, Jiangshan Zhuo, Junbo Peng, Huifeng Dong, Ofoq Normahmedov, Shengchao Jiang, Lvting Wang, Lu Jiang, Junhong Pu, Ye Shi

10.1002/adma.74827.title: Entropy-Encoded Electronic Reconstruction in High-Entropy Nanozymes Enables Cofactor-Free Monooxygenase-Like Catalysis
10.1002/adma.74827.abstract: ABSTRACT Flavin-dependent monooxygenases (FMOs) catalyze redox reactions central to antibiotic degradation and metabolic detoxification, yet replicating their intricate cofactor-dependent electron transfer in synthetic systems has remained elusive. Here, we report an electronic modulation strategy that enables cofactor-free FMO-like catalysis within a high-entropy alloy nanozyme (HEAzyme-Cu 1.5 ). We induce localized electron cloud enrichment that shifts Cu 3 d orbitals toward the Fermi level, establishing a self-sustained redox channel without flavin cofactors. This atomic-scale entropy-driven alignment bridges the functional gap between natural cofactor-dependent enzymes and artificial catalysts, demonstrating for the first time that complex redox cascades traditionally confined to biological systems can be reconstructed purely by materials design. This entropy-driven electronic reconfiguration enables near-zero barrier O 2 activation and rapid hydroxylation with a kinetic constant. Integrating this multifunctional HEAzyme into a portable hydrogel sensor platform achieves real-time antibiotic detection down to 11-25 nM and > 90% degradation within 20 min in complex water samples. This work establishes a universal design principle for programmable enzyme mimetics, where atomic-scale entropy, electronic-state alignment, and multimetal cooperation converge to emulate and transcend biological catalysis. Such entropy-encoded redox systems offer a transformative route toward intelligent bioinspired materials for environmental remediation, green synthesis, and metabolic engineering.
authors: Xiaodi Niu, Kailong Yang, Leixiao Cui, Ning Huo, Song Wang, Hongsu Wang

10.1002/adma.75440.title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation-Anion Co-Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/adma.75440.abstract: ABSTRACT Multivalent cation-anion co-(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge-compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre-intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge-compensation mechanism-organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg 2 + -TFSI − as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm − 2 and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm − 2 at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm − 2 , surpassing leading Mg-ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co-(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high-performance energy storage.
authors: Huabin Kong, Jianxin Ou, Lei Fang, Chuangchuang Duan, Xuanbing Chen, Yancheng Chen, Siying Chen, Le Yang, Xianji Qiao, Fuda Yu, Yanbin Shen, Liwei Chen, Hongwei Chen

10.1002/adma.74897.title: Descriptors to Dynamics: A Materials and Device Perspective on in-Materio Physical Reservoir Computing for Neuromorphic Edge Intelligence
10.1002/adma.74897.abstract: ABSTRACT Reservoir computing is attractive for edge intelligence because it not only reduces training overhead but also turns transient material physics into computation. In in-materio systems, memory, nonlinearity, separability, and efficiency are not added later at the circuit level; they emerge from defect kinetics, ionic motion, interfacial barriers, percolation pathways, and related dynamics. This perspective therefore treats material descriptors as design variables rather than post hoc explanations of device behavior. Accordingly, six design rules connect measurable material properties to useful reservoir function: timescale matching, operating-regime nonlinearity, controlled stochasticity, observable state dimensionality, reversible and energy-relevant operation, and robustness across an operating range. To make these rules actionable, the framework introduces a staged experimental workflow, a minimum quantitative characterization set, attribution controls separating material dynamics from input encoding and readout design, and a cross-layer reporting checklist. The focus remains material- and device-based in-materio physical reservoirs for edge and in-sensor processing, while the descriptor-to-dynamics logic is transferable to other physical reservoirs. The framework is then extended to reservoir-by-sensing platforms, where sensing and temporal processing coexist within one substrate. Finally, reporting of operating conditions, state observables, stability, and energy boundaries supports fair comparison and helps move proof-of-concept demonstrations toward deployable materials systems.

10.1002/adma.75447.title: Stress-Resistant Plant Cell-Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
10.1002/adma.75447.abstract: ABSTRACT Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient-temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold-chain dependence and suppressing solution-phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice-induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress-resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF-8) for mechanical support, a water-retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn 2 + coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze- and dehydration-driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post-rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra-low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf-life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient-temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.
authors: Xia Zheng, Lingqi Wang, Huimei Cao, Youhua Lu, Kun Tao, Xiaoran Chen, Zhang Liu, Jianjun Wang

10.1002/adma.75417.title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
10.1002/adma.75417.abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero-energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross-linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro-/nano-porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long-wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice-sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.
authors: Feifei Wang, Lengwan Li, Long Bai, Zhiyi Liu, Laijun Li, Zhi Li, Jiahao Ni, Kai Xu, Bin Zhao, Gang Pei, Qiaoqiang Gan, Alexei P. Sokolov, Ming Tian, Peng-Fei Cao

10.1002/adma.202520711.title: Robust Sodium-Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte-Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
10.1002/adma.202520711.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next-generation energy-storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high-concentration, localized high-concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion-conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in-situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine-learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium-metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead-sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high-performance, practical sodium-metal batteries.
authors: Sikandar Iqbal, Usman Ghani, Xuebing Zhu, Yun Bai, Jinlong Jiang, Ying Zhang, Huiqin Huang, Fakhr uz Zaman, Hua Kun Liu, Shi-Xue Dou, Chao Wu

10.1002/adma.75455.title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation-Type Framework Anodes for Fast-Charging Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75455.abstract: ABSTRACT Intercalation-type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast-charging sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation-type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic-scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M-Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g −1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low-barrier, nanoscale ion-conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high-rate battery materials.

10.1002/adma.75439.title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide-Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase-Like Activity for Liver Protection
10.1002/adma.75439.abstract: ABSTRACT Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)-mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active-site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide-hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic-organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure-activity analysis showed that GPX-like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide-hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide-hybrid analogue, and conventional metal-based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione-dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide-hybrid material protected against acetaminophen-induced and rifampicin-induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide-hybrid frameworks as effective GPX-like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress-associated liver diseases.
authors: Fangman Chen, Madi Sun, Ziping Wu, Peiyu Chen, Xiaochun Xie, Quanxin Ning, Xin Zhao, Shaowen Wang, Dan Shao, Yunlu Dai, Hanyao Huang, Kam W. Leong, Chao Yang

10.1002/adma.75436.title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
10.1002/adma.75436.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium-ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value-added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two-dimensional material nanosheets (In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs/Fe-Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high-value chemicals. The best-performing photocatalyst (Fe 1.0 Cu 0.5 ) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g −1 . Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy-kelvin probe force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O 2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high-value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value-added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.
authors: Amin Talebian-Kiakalaieh, Shiying Ren, Wenzhong Ji, Yun Liu, Bingquan Xia, Jingrun Ran, Shi-Zhang Qiao

10.1002/adma.75408.title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics
10.1002/adma.75408.abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell-type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route-specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell-resolved biodistribution, long-term safety, repeated-dose immunogenicity, cross-study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high-throughput screening, machine learning, and data-driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next-generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue- and cell-selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.
authors: Jiaxin Li, Jianping Liu, Nan Wang, Keyi Zhang, Wen Zhang, Mengze Gao, Zhiguo Lu, Xiaoyuan Chen, Yan Li

10.1002/adma.75389.title: Chiral Phonon-Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non-Magnetic Ferroelectric
10.1002/adma.75389.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non-magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non-magnetic ferroelectric generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon-induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non-equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin-Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin-current generation. Polarization-resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization-dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non-magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

10.1002/adma.75410.title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid-State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
10.1002/adma.75410.abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of new solid-state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile-ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile-ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion-migration barriers spanning Li-, Na-, K-, and Mg-ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆ d , a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile-ion-neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short-range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low- from high-barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆ d in a high-throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast-ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast-ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆ d links diverse ion-transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.
authors: Ramanuja Srinivasan Saravanan, Charles E. Schwarz, Felix Adams, Kiyan Amirian, Yifei Mo

10.1002/adma.75435.title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross-Linked Polymer Enables Long-Calendar-Life Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75435.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross-linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross-linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in-situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion-derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg −1 ) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

10.1002/adma.75428.title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
10.1002/adma.75428.abstract: ABSTRACT In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non-fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady-state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited-state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel-type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence-dependent lifetimes (30-200 ps) governed by singlet-singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long-lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin-film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager-like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge-generation mechanisms in Y6-based photovoltaic systems.
authors: Daniel Kroh, Xinyue Xu, Trevor A. Smith, Anna Köhler

10.1002/adma.75367.title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4${\rm CoNb}_4$Se8${\rm Se}_8$
10.1002/adma.75367.abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three-dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination-resolved micro-ARPES, fine photon-energy mapping, spin-ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three-dimensional fermiology of the layered g -wave altermagnet , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H-. We resolve the spin-split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin-ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time-reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry-protected nodal -K direction. We further report a weak low-temperature anomaly near T 0 ≈ 50-60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature-dependent micro-ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum-resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

10.1002/adma.75434.title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow-Power Transistor Technologies
10.1002/adma.75434.abstract: ABSTRACT As complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub-2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub-60 mV/dec steep-switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field-effect transistors (TFETs), negative-capacitance field-effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold-source field-effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub-60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.
authors: Xuezhou Ma, Xiyu Tan, Dehuan Meng, Lian-Mao Peng, Chenguang Qiu

10.1002/adma.75443.title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid-Anchored Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Wide-Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75443.abstract: ABSTRACT The anchoring group of self-assembled monolayer (SAM) hole-transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high-performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21 , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual-action mechanism of pyridine-Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate-metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid-dissociation constants ( K a ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide-bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open-circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all-perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi-dentate pyridine-carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next-generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

10.1002/adma.75454.title: Vitamin C-Induced Photo-Redox Threshold Enables High-Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen
10.1002/adma.75454.abstract: ABSTRACT Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter-scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell-matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible-light-activated Ru(II)bpy 3 2+ /sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near-immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo-redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high-fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post-printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post-printing and cell-laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell-instructive 3D microenvironments.
authors: Bin Wang, Amelia Hasenauer, Kristian Ivkovic, Ann-Sophie Frind, David Fercher, Marcy Zenobi-Wong

10.1002/adma.75442.title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E-Waste-Derived Au Enables Low-Voltage H2 and Scalable FDCA Production
10.1002/adma.75442.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low-potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value-added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion-template-assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH) 2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride-coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low-voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow-electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm −2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low-potential aldehyde oxidation from high-potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low-voltage hydrogen production with high-value biomass conversion.
authors: Chengcheng Cai, Wanting Wang, Kaiyue Jiang, Sen Yang, Guangyong Bo, Huijing Ma, Yixin Zhao, Xufang Qian, Tianfu Wang

10.1002/adma.75431.title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long-Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75431.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n -decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10-DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high-LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.
authors: Zhichao Hou, Wenqiang Lu, Hongbao Zheng, Guowei Zeng, Shibo Zhao, Nan Chen, Heng Jiang, Dong Zhang, Fei Du

10.1002/adma.75427.title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress-Regulation Units for Practical Silicon-Carbon Anodes
10.1002/adma.75427.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon-carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high-energy lithium-ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation-induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress-regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon-carbon anodes. Heteroatom-doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion-induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li + insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen-doped silicon-carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g − 1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g −1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine-learning-guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed-pore design. This work establishes closed-pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low-expansion silicon-carbon anodes.

10.1002/adma.74877.title: Charge Confinement in an Ordered High-Entropy Intermetallic Breaks the Activity-Poisoning Trade-Off for Glycolic Acid Electrosynthesis From Polyethylene Terephthalate
10.1002/adma.74877.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective electrooxidation of ethylene glycol (EG) from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) hydrolysate to glycolic acid (GA) offers a sustainable route for plastic upcycling but is hindered by insufficient activity at industrially relevant current densities and severe catalyst deactivation caused by poisoning intermediates. Here, we design a two-dimensional ordered high-entropy intermetallic, HEI (PdPtRh)(InBi)ene, based on a Pd 1 In 1 -type body-centered-cubic framework. The ordered lattice induces pronounced p- - d hybridization and charge redistribution, giving rise to a charge-confinement effect at the active sites. Operando infrared spectroscopy, CO stripping, and theoretical calculations reveal that this confined electronic environment precisely regulates the evolution of the key poisoning intermediate *COCH 2 OH, weakening its accumulation while preserving efficient EG activation. As a result, HEI (PdPtRh)(InBi)ene achieves a current density of 554.21 mA cm −2 at 0.9 V in PET hydrolysate (PETH). Furthermore, it maintains stable operation for 90 h in a flow cell at an industrially relevant current density of 200 mA cm −2 , delivering an average GA Faradaic efficiency of 99.22% and an average GA production rate of 1.85 mmol h −1 cm −2 . These findings demonstrate charge-confinement engineering as an effective route to regulate poisoning-intermediate behavior in electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation.

10.1002/adma.75126.title: Bare-Die Antiferromagnetic Computing
10.1002/adma.75126.abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconductor electronic devices are increasingly constrained by fundamental quantum tunneling effects and charge-based mechanisms, which severely limit further miniaturization, write-speed scaling, and environmental robustness of silicon-based technologies. These limitations are particularly prohibitive for deep-space exploration, where extreme temperatures, ultra-strong magnetic fields, and intense radiation rapidly incapacitate conventional electronics without massive shielding. Here, we present an intrinsically resilient, strain-mediated antiferromagnetic MnIr/PMN-PT edge processor that operates reliably as a bare die under temperatures up to 500 K, magnetic fields of 55 T, and radiation doses of 1.5 Mrad. By exploiting an Input-Modulated In Situ Self-Refreshing Encoding mechanism, the device performs nonlinear feature extraction and classification directly from raw analog signals, enabling an analog computing architecture that requires no time-frequency transformation. This architecture achieves 99.8% accuracy in speech recognition without digital preprocessing and 100% accuracy in astronaut visual object recognition. Furthermore, an all-hardware integrated drone vision system demonstrates real-time in situ command execution and autonomous navigation, delivering a terahertz-level response frequency and an ultra-low energy consumption of approximately 0.2 fJ per operation. This work expands the functional scope of antiferromagnetic devices beyond memory and logic, establishing them as a promising materials platform for energy-efficient physical computing and autonomous intelligence in extreme environments.

10.1002/adma.74612.title: Solar-Driven Spin-State Optimization in Co-Based Catalysts for Enhanced Photothermal Ammonia Synthesis
10.1002/adma.74612.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-state engineering of active sites represents a key strategy for boosting catalytic performance, as demonstrated in thermal ammonia synthesis. However, conventional promoter-mediated ground-state spin modulation is inherently limited by the electronic structure of the catalyst, imposing a ceiling on achievable spin tuning efficacy and hindering further advances. In this work, we developed a series of cobalt (Co) nanoparticle-based catalysts for photothermal ammonia synthesis. By introducing Ru single atom into the Co nanoparticles, along with the addition of barium as a promoter, spin-state engineering of Co nanoparticles was optimized under light irradiation, boosting the production rate by 3 times compared to thermal catalytic conditions. In-situ characterization studies revealed that the hot electrons accumulate on the catalyst surface and shift the Co active sites toward a lower-spin configuration. Supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate that this light-induced spin state change modulates the electronic interaction between Co and N 2 , weakening the N≡N bond and lowering its dissociation energy barrier, thereby facilitating N 2 activation. This work demonstrates that spin regulation in Co-based catalysts is an innovative design principle for developing more efficient photothermal catalysts for ammonia synthesis and other applications.

10.1002/adma.202522858.title: A Hierarchical Plug-and-Supply Flap (PASF) for Instant Perfusion and Oxygen Delivery in Large Soft Tissue Repair
