10.1002/adma.75360.title: Strain-Insensitive Conductors for Stretchable Electronics
10.1002/adma.75360.abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable electronics are rapidly evolving from simple planar configurations to complex, three-dimensional (3D) multifunctional architectures. However, traditional stretchable conductors frequently suffer from severe resistance fluctuations under mechanical deformation. To address this challenge, this review systematically summarizes two core design paradigms for achieving robust strain insensitivity. The first paradigm, corresponding to structurally strain-insensitive conductors, relies on a top-down geometric decoupling strategy that physically dissipates strain through 3D buckling or kirigami structures. The second paradigm, corresponding to intrinsically strain-insensitive conductors, employs a bottom-up network reconstruction strategy that leverages the fluidic adaptability of liquid metals or the dynamic sliding of nanofillers to sustain continuous percolation networks under stress. Beyond these fundamental paradigms, we comprehensively evaluate precise fabrication processes and critical system-level integration challenges, with a particular focus on in-plane modulus mismatch and Z -axis interlayer shear failure. Importantly, this review highlights the indispensable role of strain-insensitive conductors in advanced applications, demonstrating their unique capability to eliminate motion artifacts in bioelectronics, lock resonant frequencies in wireless communications, and ensure thermal safety in high-power actuation platforms. Finally, we outline future trajectories for large-scale industrial manufacturing and long-term in vivo stability, aiming to accelerate the commercialization of technologies within this interdisciplinary field.
authors: Tong Zheng, Shengxin Xiang, Jianqiang Gao, Qiongfeng Shi, Xinkai Xie, La Li, Guozhen Shen, Jun Wu

10.1002/adma.75365.title: Advanced Nanomedicines for Cancer Metabolic Therapy
10.1002/adma.75365.abstract: ABSTRACT Abnormal metabolic reprogramming is a recognized hallmark of cancer, yet the clinical translation of cancer metabolic therapy (CMT) by conventional chemo-drugs remains a great challenge due to their poor drug targetability, short circulation time, and low bioavailability. Nanomedicines, owing to their great feasibility in rational designs, facile fabrication, and excellent biocompatibility, offer a powerful platform to overcome the drawbacks of current clinical drugs and enable precise modulation of cancer metabolism. In this review, we provide a critical overview of recent advances in nanomedicine-based CMT. We first summarize the reprogrammed metabolic landscape of cancer cells and the metabolic crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment. Then, nanomedicine strategies targeting glucose, lipid, amino acid, nucleotide, and carboxylic acid metabolism are summarized and discussed in a comprehensive way, with an emphasis on nanomaterial design principles and regulatory mechanisms. Finally, key challenges and future prospects for clinical translation are discussed, aiming to establish nanomedicine-enabled CMT as a next-generation paradigm for effective and safe cancer treatment.
authors: Qiu-Yi Duan, Chun Tian, Xi Cheng, Liying Wang, Minfeng Huo, Jianlin Shi

10.1002/adma.75438.title: Biomass DNA: An Emerging Building Block for Advanced Materials
10.1002/adma.75438.abstract: ABSTRACT Since the structural discovery of DNA's double helix, it transitioned from a genetic carrier to a cornerstone of programmable nanotechnology and materials science. However, while synthetic DNA with predesigned sequences has dominated DNA-based materials, biomass DNA, naturally derived from bulk biological resources, has emerged as a powerful large-scale engineering material. This review outlines biomass DNA-derived materials and their multifunctional applications, framed as a “Biomass DNA Tree,” representing biomass resources as roots, duplexes as stems, and advanced materials as leaves. For example, we examine the transformation of biomass DNA into sophisticated 3D-crosslinked hydrogel matrices for (bio)engineering, and their further processing into recyclable bioplastics, which supports carbon neutrality. Furthermore, we highlight biomass DNA organogels and fibers, as well as its utilization for energy storage, including supercapacitors, batteries, and interphase layers. Beyond these core areas, the review highlights breakthroughs applying DNA as functional materials for catalysis, soft robotics, OLEDs, medical patches, neuromorphic devices, and photoconductors. By addressing challenges and providing perspectives on future opportunities, this review aims to catalyze the next generation of materials science, emphasizing the role of biomass DNA in advancing biopolymer-based applications.
authors: Yuwei Hu, Itamar Willner, Li Niu

10.1002/adma.75449.title: Mechanoactive Biomaterials for Cell-Matrix Mechanotransduction
10.1002/adma.75449.abstract: ABSTRACT Cells and extracellular matrices (ECMs) form mechanically coupled feedback loops in which cells generate forces, remodel their surroundings, and respond to mechanical information returned by the matrix. Conventional biomaterial models have established how passive matrix properties, including stiffness, viscoelasticity, architecture, and ligand presentation, regulate this feedback, but they provide limited control over the dynamic mechanical inputs transmitted through living tissues. Mechanoactive biomaterials address this limitation by converting external or encoded triggers into mechanical inputs with defined timing, magnitude, frequency, and spatial localization. Here, we compare mechanochemical hydrogels, light-responsive matrices, thermoresponsive systems, and optothermal mechanoactuators according to the material response, the mechanical input experienced by cells, spatial, and temporal control, reversibility, cytocompatibility, quantification, and translational constraints. We discuss how these platforms engage integrin-focal adhesion signaling, mechanosensitive ion channels, cytoskeletal and nuclear mechanotransduction, YAP/TAZ activity, and TGF-β activation. We conclude with design principles for selecting reversible or persistent actuation, matching mechanical parameters to receptor and tissue mechanics, and advancing mechanoactive platforms toward predictive in vitro models.
authors: Yi-Tung Lu, Alison E. John, Marc A. Fernández-Yagüe

10.1002/adma.75459.title: Spontaneous Capture, Enrichment, and SERS Sensing of Polystyrene Micro/Nanoplastics Enabled by Condensed Plasmonic Coacervate Droplets
10.1002/adma.75459.abstract: ABSTRACT Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co-encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three-dimensional droplet-confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 10 9 , excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano- and micro-scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food-contact materials.
authors: Junbo Li, Ziyi Zhang, Yuhan Gao, Chunyi Wei, Yaxin Ma, Hongwen Xu, Haixu Chen, Yuxuan Zhou, Xiaomeng Ma, Yunfei Xie, Xin Huang, Wei Ji

10.1002/adma.75453.title: Interface-Mediated Architectural Engineering of Silicon for Solid-State Batteries: Current Status and Future Outlook
10.1002/adma.75453.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid-state lithium batteries promise superior performance and enhanced safety over current lithium-ion batteries. As lithium metal encounters intrinsic challenges, high-capacity silicon anodes have gained increasing attention to satisfy the growing demand for higher energy density and safety. However, the commercialization of such systems is impeded by challenges including large volume variation, poor interfacial contact, sluggish charge transport, inferior performance, and excessive pressure reliance. This review discusses fundamental challenges and interface-mediated architectural engineering strategies. Based on the coupling mode of silicon and solid electrolyte, the developed architectures are classified into three representative categories, with emphasis on their design principles, multiscale construction methodologies, and enhancement mechanisms. In light of the latest advances, this review systematizes the architectural paradigms, and clarifies the synergistic correlations between interfacial compatibility, electron and ion transport, stress relaxation, and side reactions between silicon and solid electrolyte. Scalable manufacturing protocols and sustainable monitoring approaches are then delineated toward practical applications. Finally, the review summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these classifications and outlines future directions for advancing stable, safe, scalable, and sustainable silicon-based electrode technologies for viable solid-state batteries with enhanced energy density, power capability, durability, and manufacturability at low-pressure operation.
authors: Yifei Ma, Yuli Cai, Nimra Khan, Yingjie Ma, Xianglong Li

10.1002/adma.75463.title: Supramolecular Adhesives with Tunable Crystallinity for Extreme Environments
10.1002/adma.75463.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high-performance adhesives capable of withstanding harsh environments-specifically ultralow temperatures, water, acid, base and organic solvents-via low-cost, scalable manufacturing remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the architecture of spider silk, we report a facile strategy to fabricate a solvent-free supramolecular adhesive composed of tannic acid (TA) and poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL). Integrated theoretical and experimental investigations uncover the critical role of crystallinity modulation in governing adhesion performance. The resulting adhesive achieves an exceptional strength of up to 8.5 MPa at ambient temperature (25°C) and 6.6 MPa at cryogenic temperature (−196°C), outperforming existing commercial hot-melt adhesives. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable stability in corrosive underwater environments (acidic, alkaline, and saline) and organic solvents. This work not only establishes a novel bioinspired design paradigm for adhesives operating under extreme conditions but also paves the way for the scalable production and practical applications of supramolecular materials.
authors: Yiteng Cai, Zekang Lu, Shuitao Gao, Jiachen Guo, Letian Yuan, Huaiyu Song, Xiaojuan Bai, Jianbin Huang, Yun Yan

10.1002/adma.75467.title: Atomic-Level Regulating Layer-by-Layer Zinc Deposition by High-Entropy Single-Atoms Electrolyte Additive
10.1002/adma.75467.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid-solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy-dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high-entropy single-atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn 2+ concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn 2+ transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn 2+ from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn 2+ flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn 2+ supersaturation and guiding layer-by-layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn 2+ transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm −2 , and 800 h even at 50 mA cm −2 , with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm −2 . Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal-ion batteries.
authors: Xiude Liu, Jinlong Zhang, Fusheng Luo, Zeyu Yan, Junkai Zhu, Yifei Zhang, Kai Yuan, Jun Huang

10.1002/adma.75235.title: Bridging Biosensing and Hardware-Level Data Security With a Conjugated Radical Polymer
10.1002/adma.75235.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of biological signal processing with hardware-level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox-mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical-containing backbone. By establishing a material-level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.
authors: Hoyeon Lee, Jaehyoung Ko, Dinh Cung Tien Nguyen, Yeong Kwon Kim, Daeun Kim, Soo Jin Cho, Sung Gap Im, Byung Chul Jang, Byung Joon Moon, Yongho Joo

10.1002/adma.75421.title: Minimally Invasive In Vivo Fabrication of Multiscale Biohybrid Systems
10.1002/adma.75421.abstract: ABSTRACT Multiscale biohybrid systems integrating living materials with minimally invasive in vivo fabrication offer new opportunities for precise diagnosis, physiological monitoring, and tissue regeneration. This review provides a unified perspective on their design and therapeutic integration, organizing recent advances across multiscale material design, minimally invasive fabrication, spatiotemporal co-engineering, and functional applications. Three emerging principles are identified: multiscale coupling bridges material architectures with cellular and tissue responses; spatiotemporal coordination integrates precise in vivo construction with dynamic material and biological evolution; and sensing-regeneration feedback extends biohybrid systems from passive repair toward responsive therapeutic regulation. Building on these principles, we highlight machine learning-assisted material discovery, multi-site fabrication, and intelligent feedback control as key directions for developing adaptive, closed-loop therapeutic systems. Together, these insights provide design guidance for translating minimally invasive multiscale biohybrid systems toward next-generation patient-centered healthcare.
authors: Zhixing Ge, Yuji Gao, Elgene Chng Junyuan, Truong-Son Dinh Le, Lanfeng Liang, Yu Zhang, Chwee Teck Lim

10.1002/adma.75343.title: Nanoarchitectonics With Static-Dynamic Synergistic Interfacial Remediation for Practical Zinc Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75343.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc metal batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost, yet their practical deployment remains limited by dendrite growth, parasitic reactions, and the gradual failure of interfacial protection during prolonged cycling. Here, we report a static-dynamic synergistic interfacial remediation strategy in which a preconstructed In/Sb interfacial layer is coupled with a dynamically responsive electrolyte additive to mitigate continuous interfacial degradation. Specifically, a dual-phase In/Sb composite layer (ISZ) is formed on Zn by spontaneous galvanic replacement, providing a compact and chemically stable interface that promotes uniform Zn deposition and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, In 3+ in the electrolyte dynamically participates in anode-side regulation during cycling, assisting defect-responsive interfacial regeneration. Owing to this synergy, the ISZ-In 3+ system delivers both improved initial deposition behavior and sustained interfacial stability during repeated plating/stripping. Symmetric cells operate stably for nearly 6000 h at low areal capacity, for about 500 h under 40 mA cm −2 /20 mAh cm −2 , and for over 1000 h at an ultrahigh Zn utilization rate of 95%. This strategy is further extended to Br 2 /Zn batteries, where pouch cells stably operate for nearly 3600 h and 700 h at areal capacities of 12.5 and 25 mAh cm −2 , respectively. In addition, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling over 3600 h, and a low-N/P pouch cell (N/P = 1.46) cycles for nearly 1400 h, while a 400 mAh pouch cell achieves a component-level energy density of about 80 Wh kg −1 , excluding the electrolyte and pouch packaging. This work provides a practical interfacial design strategy for high-capacity, long-life aqueous Zn batteries.
authors: Apeng Li, Mingming Wang, Jintao Qi, Xiang Li, Ze Xu, Lei Yang, Kunjie Ding, Yahan Meng, Shaoming Huang

10.1002/adma.75433.title: Pollen-Engraved Dual Porosity Ceramic Beads From Liquid Marbles for Environmental Remediation
10.1002/adma.75433.abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid marbles, renowned for their non-wetting behavior, have been extensively investigated in the fields of controlled delivery, droplet reactors, and biomaterial storage. However, the transition in wetting interactions between the liquid droplet and the coating particles has not been clearly studied, and leveraging this transformation for new applications remains unexplored. Here, we use UV irradiation along with mechanical vibration to switch the wetting state at the liquid marble interface from Cassie-Baxter to Cassie-impregnating during a one-step process that converts liquid marbles into ceramic green bodies. Renewable biowaste pollen is, for the first time, employed to impart both surface patterning and internal porosity together with a photocured polymer, yielding dual-porosity ceramic adsorbents that achieve up to 2.88 times higher pollutant removal efficiency, particularly for heavy metal ions and nanoplastics. Furthermore, different pollen species exhibit distinct pollutant selectivity, underscoring their potential for environmental remediation.
authors: Chenchen Zhou, Jun Hao Mo, Ruiyan Ni, Zihao Guo, Yanzhang Xu, Xinyue Zhang, Hanna Kim, Jian Li, Ibrahim Shahrudin Mohammed, Munho Kim, Bernard P. Binks, Nam-Joon Cho

10.1002/adma.75446.title: Functional Group Transposition Enables Antiparallel-Parallel Packing Switching in Dithieno[3,2-b:2′,3′-d]pyrrole Self-Assembled Molecules for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75446.abstract: ABSTRACT Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium-tin-oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole-transport-layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor-donor-acceptor type self-assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho-/para- positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well-ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 10 14 Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 10 13 Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state-of-the-art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8-BO:BTP-eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8-BO:BTP-eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm 2 ). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co-engineers interfacial order and active-layer morphology toward high-performance organic optoelectronics.
authors: Huayi Liu, Junjie Wen, Bo Yan, Lingyan Sun, Wentian Han, Yisui Feng, Zuhao You, Yihe Qi, Jiang Zhu, Haotian Li, Kaili Huang, Xin Chang, Hui Li, Cheng Zhang, Yeonju Park, Woojin Shin, Young Mee Jung, Hyunbok Lee, Wenxu Liu, Yao Liu

10.1002/adma.75460.title: Supercapacitors Under Nonequilibrium Conditions: Mechanisms and Design Principles
10.1002/adma.75460.abstract: ABSTRACT Supercapacitors have attracted considerable interest as high-power energy storage devices for grid frequency regulation, backup power systems, and fast-response applications, which are increasingly operated under conditions far from equilibrium, including floating states, high-frequency cycling, rapid charge and discharge, wide temperature windows, and high-voltage regimes. Under these nonequilibrium conditions, performance and stability are governed by coupled kinetic and thermodynamic processes, including ion transport limitations, interfacial polarization, electrolyte decomposition, and structural stress evolution. These processes span multiple length and time scales, from ion desolvation and surface reactions through pore-level transport mismatch to macroscopic degradation. This review presents a unified perspective on the mechanisms that govern supercapacitor behavior under nonequilibrium conditions. Representative operating scenarios are analyzed to identify three common degradation origins, namely, transport mismatch, interfacial instability and thermo-mechanical coupling. Building on this mechanistic understanding, rational material-design principles are derived on ion transport regulation, interfacial chemistry regulation, electrolyte optimization, and structural adaptability. Finally, future research directions are discussed for bridging the gap between laboratory evaluation and real-world operation and for guiding the development of robust supercapacitors for dynamic energy storage applications.

10.1002/adma.75468.title: Programmable Structural Color Lifetimes via Activation Energy Engineering for Spatiotemporally Encoded Dynamic Optical Encryption
10.1002/adma.75468.abstract: ABSTRACT Spatiotemporally programmable structural color holds great promise for high-security optical encryption, yet precisely tailoring the lifetime of structural color across a broad temporal range spanning multiple orders of magnitude remains a significant challenge in polymer systems. The lifetime of structural color is intrinsically governed by the segmental relaxation kinetics of the underlying polymer network, which has been largely overlooked in the rational design. Here, we report a dynamic surface grating with programmable structural color lifetime, in which the optical evolution process is precisely encoded by tuning the activation energy through crosslinking density and amplitude control. Driven by segmental relaxation, the grating amplitude gradually decays over time, redistributing diffracted energy back to specular reflection and causing a gradual fading of structural color. By spatially encoding the relaxation activation energy via photomask-assisted UV exposure, the structural color lifetime governed by local amplitude decay kinetics can be independently programmed across different regions, spanning an unprecedented temporal range from 300 s to over 240 days. This strategy enables diverse applications, ranging from stimulus-responsive optical encryption and time-resolved multilevel information encryption to practical cold-chain integrity monitoring, establishing activation energy as a broadly applicable handle for temporal programmability in dynamic optical systems.
authors: Dengchong Feng, Shirui Wu, Shuting Zhang, Yu Chen, Jingru Liang, Yuzhao Yang, Qi Guo, Zhongke Yuan, Yusheng Chen, Xudong Chen

10.1002/adma.75470.title: Design of Bridging-Oxygen-Modulated Fe-Ni Dual-Atom Sites With Multifaceted Stabilization for Durable Cathode Catalysis in Rechargeable Zinc-Air Batteries
10.1002/adma.75470.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs) require durable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts. However, the long-term stability of metal-nitrogen-carbon atomic-site catalysts (M-N-Cs) remains challenged by electrochemical corrosion and reactive oxygen species (ROS)-induced damage arising from multiple degradation pathways, which collectively demand comprehensive solutions due to the “buckets effect” of instabilities. Herein, we develop a robust FeNi-N-C dual-atom catalyst (DAC) featuring a bridging µ 2 -O electron modulator for long-life RZAB catalysis, retaining 80% of its initial energy efficiency after 2800 h. Theoretical simulations and experimental evidence support multifaceted stabilization of the N/O-coordinated vicinal Fe-Ni configuration. The µ 2 -O bridge improves intrinsic structural stability, decreases electron density on adjacent metal and N atoms to mitigate N-site protonation and intermediate-induced metal stripping, and promotes an O─O cleavage pathway that suppresses H 2 O 2 /ROS accumulation. These findings provide a coordination-engineering strategy for designing durable M-N-C catalysts for long-life RZABs.
authors: Wenbo Shi, Qian Zhang, Kai Zhu, Chenhong Liu, Tiefeng Liu, Rui Gao, Jialiang Pan, Yang Yuan, Qing Zhang, Lijun Zheng, Jun Lu, Zhengyu Bai

10.1002/adma.75481.title: In Situ Constructed Pore-Chain Interlocked Networks in Polyimide-Covalent Organic Framework Nanocomposites Enable Ultralow k Dielectrics for High-Fidelity Signal Transmission
10.1002/adma.75481.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultralow k porous polymer dielectrics have been widely explored for Integrated circuit (IC) interconnects, 5G/6G communications, and wearable devices. However, disordered pore structures and poor interfacial adhesion remain a major challenge, thus making it difficult to decouple the k -tanδ trade-off. Here, we employ hollow covalent organic frameworks (H-TD-COF) as multifunctional molecular anchoring nodes to construct robust pore-chain interlocked networks in polyimide nanofibrous films. The amino-functionalized COF shells participate in the in situ growth of polyimide (PI) chains, thus enabling interlocked interfaces that fundamentally restrict segmental mobility and suppress dipolar relaxation. Subsequent electrospinning technique allows anchored chains to be stretched along the fiber axis and immobilizes them within an oriented fibrous architecture. This simultaneously disrupts long-range charge migration pathways while preserving stress-transfer and heat-dissipation continuity. The resulting PI-g-COF (4) nanocomposites with 4 wt% H-TD-COF loading achieve an ultralow dielectric constant of 1.50 and dielectric loss of 0.001 at 1 kHz, with highly stable dielectric properties up to 250°C. Notably, device-level measurements further reveal a signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SINAD) of 22.30 dB under 200 MHz crosstalk interference, showing a 52.2% improvement over commercial polyimide. This work lays solid foundations for nanoscale interfacial regulation in porous polymer nanocomposites towards ultralow k dielectrics.
authors: Jingxin Liu, Yu Xin, Yinghui Sun, Tian Xia, Yichen Li, Yanfeng Lyu, Lingzhi Nie, Diwen Zhou, Jiayi Hong, Chengkun Xie, Xunlin Qiu, Xiaoyun Liu, Peiyuan Zuo, Yueping Niu, Qixin Zhuang

10.1002/adma.75391.title: Optically Tunable Chiral Magnetic States and Exchange Engineering via Charge-Transfer Excitation in a van der Waals Antiferromagnet CrPS4
10.1002/adma.75391.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling magnetism with light in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets could enable ultrafast, energy-efficient spintronics. However, selectively writing distinct magnetic phases, such as chiral magnetic states (e.g., spin spirals and skyrmions) for memory and collinear states for logic, within a single material remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic, photon-energy-selective writing of magnetic order in the air-stable antiferromagnet chromium thiophosphate (). Its ligand-to-metal charge transfer gap serves as an intrinsic switching threshold: excitation below this gap drives - transitions to stabilize chiral magnetic states due to a spin-spiral phase, while excitation above activates a photo-doping mechanism that renormalizes magnetic exchange and induces a collinear phase. These optically defined states are distinguished through polarization-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy and probed via a proximal monolayer tungsten diselenide (). By establishing optical selectivity in a single material, our work provides a reconfigurable platform for opto-spintronic circuits where memory and logic functions can be dynamically toggled with light.
authors: Muhammad Hassan Shaikh, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Chitraleema Chakraborty

10.1002/adma.75466.title: Industry-Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET-Cu Current Collectors
10.1002/adma.75466.abstract: ABSTRACT Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film-typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)-as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high-temperature operation. Here, we report an industry-scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al 2 O 3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll-to-roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min −1 , substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al 2 O 3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte-induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long-term cycling. The as-resulting Al 2 O 3 -coated PET-Cu CC (PET@Al 2 O 3 -Cu CC) enables 3-Ah graphite//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C-comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET-Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low-cost and industry-scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost-efficient and high-energy LIBs.
authors: Lei Zhao, Chaofan Liang, Weichen Du, Zhikang Liu, Zhiqiang Man, Donghai Wang, Hongbin Xie, Nan Qin, Henghui Xu, Zhen Li, Long Qie, Yunhui Huang

10.1002/adma.75144.title: Sub-nm 2 Ferroelectric Domains via Charged 180° Walls in ZrO 2
10.1002/adma.75144.abstract: ABSTRACT Flat phonon bands in fluorite ferroelectrics ( or ) shrink polar domains laterally to an irreducible half-unit-cell width (0.27 nm) within which the vertical arrangement of dipoles is expected to remain uniform. Here, we report on the direct observation of nonuniform and nearly discrete vertical arrangements of dipoles in thin films consisting of closely spaced head-to-head (HH) and tail-to-tail (TT) charged 180 walls, each exhibiting a distinct bulk-like structure. These charged domain walls (CDWs) further compress the irreducibly narrow, laterally stacked domains vertically to a thickness of 1-2.75 nm, yielding in-plane domains with sub- footprints-among the smallest ever reported for any ferroelectric material. The HH and TT walls form due to their flat longitudinal optical (LO) polar bands, and the former are electrostatically stabilized by bound-charge compensation via interstitial oxygen atoms, which act as natural structural defects at the HH walls. Moreover, these walls are predicted to be conducting and to exhibit ultralow propagation barriers, with HH walls (1.6 meV) being far more mobile than TT walls (22.3 meV), indicating strong potential for low-voltage, domain-wall-based nanoelectronics.

10.1002/adma.75458.title: Magneto-Propelled Micromotors for Integrated Capture and Catalytic Upcycling of Micro/Nanoplastics
10.1002/adma.75458.abstract: ABSTRACT The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical-Mn/N-doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time-resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near-complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au-micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N-doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO 4 •- -mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate-determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale-up conditions, with a machine learning model ( R 2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno-economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value-added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.
authors: Zhiqin Geng, Xin Huang, Zhouyang Long, Zhimin Li, Lingfeng Duan, Yunsheng Shang, Weiqing Han, Kajia Wei, Xiaochen Dong, Lulu Qu

10.1002/adma.75441.title: High-Entropy Materials as a Design Paradigm for Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75441.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-temperature (LT) operation remains a major barrier to the practical deployment of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) because reduced thermal activation magnifies coupled limitations in bulk Na + transport, phase stability, and interfacial kinetics, resulting in strong polarization growth, rapid capacity loss, and poor rate capability. Conventional optimization approaches based on incremental compositional tuning target a single bottleneck at a time and therefore struggle under sub-zero conditions, where transport and interphase evolution become tightly intertwined. High-entropy materials (HEMs) offer a distinct design paradigm in which configurational disorder is used as a controllable variable to reshape thermodynamics and kinetics, stabilize vulnerable frameworks, and broaden the distribution of accessible Na + migration pathways. In this review, we analyze how entropy engineering influences LT performance across cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, and interfaces, emphasizing mechanistic links between realized disorder, transport activation penalties, and the accumulation of interfacial resistance in the solid-electrolyte interphase and cathode-electrolyte interphase. We synthesize quantitative descriptors and minimum reporting metrics that enable meaningful comparison across studies, and we highlight a unifying entropy-percolation framework connecting bulk ionic conduction with solvation/desolvation and interphase transport in liquid systems. We conclude by outlining key trade-offs, manufacturability constraints, and research directions required to translate high-entropy strategies into robust LT-SIB operation.
authors: Yaping Yan, Junlong Sun, Xiaohong Shang, Ping Chen, Liru Xiong, Changzheng Xin, Zixu Sun, Hua Kun Liu, Andreu Cabot

10.1002/adma.75437.title: Biodegradable Capacitive-Coupling Bioelectronics for Wireless Electrical Stimulation and Longitudinal Electrophysiological Monitoring of Peripheral Nerve Regeneration
10.1002/adma.75437.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrical stimulation accelerates peripheral nerve regeneration, yet current strategies are limited by wired interfaces, percutaneous leads, nondegradable components, and poor capacity for dynamic functional monitoring within the same subject. Here, we report biodegradable capacitive-coupling bioelectronics (CCB), an implantable platform integrating wireless electrical stimulation, regenerative guidance, and longitudinal electrophysiological monitoring. The CCB comprises biodegradable molybdenum electrodes, Mo-wire interconnects, and a textile-reinforced electroactive bioelectronic nerve guidance conduit (Bio-NGC). Capacitive coupling between external and implanted electrodes enables battery-free wireless delivery of electrical cues to regenerating nerves, while the same architecture allows repeated recording of regenerated compound nerve action potentials (CNAPs). In a rat sciatic nerve defect model, CCB-mediated stimulation enhances Schwann cell (SC) activation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, axonal regeneration, remyelination, angiogenesis, and motor recovery, with multiple outcomes approaching those of autograft repair. Mechanistic analyses revealed coordinated neurovascular remodeling, pro-regenerative immune modulation, calcium-related signaling, AMPK-associated energy metabolism, and neurotrophic factor expression. Importantly, CCB-enabled monitoring captured regeneration trajectories in the same animal without repeated nerve exposure, showing temporal trends consistent with conventional wired electrophysiology. This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic-monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.
authors: Yunjie Jin, Renyuan Sun, Wenliang Liu, Xianzhen Dong, Yiru Yang, Shicong Chen, Chunlin Wen, Kun Yang, Weilin Xu, Chao Xu, Zhiqiang Luo, Hongjun Yang

10.1002/adma.74820.title: Interface Reconstruction Reviving Dead Na Enables 3,800-Cycle Ah-Level Anode-Free Sodium Batteries
10.1002/adma.74820.abstract: ABSTRACT The accumulation of inactivated or ‘dead’ Na is the primary cause of rapid capacity decay in anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs). These dead Na is typically encapsulated by a passivated solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which renders it electrochemically inactive. Current strategies have primarily focused on suppressing dead Na formation, yet its reactivation has rarely been explored. Here, we reactivate dead Na by electrochemically reconstructing the interface through a tailored overdischarge method, thereby recovering the lost capacity and extending cycle life. Specifically, this reactivation process selectively dissolves the passivating SEI surrounding dead Na to restore its activity, while simultaneously rebuilding a thin, homogeneous, and NaF-rich interphase that ensures subsequent stable cycling. Collectively, by periodically using the method, an Ah-level anode-free pouch cell realizes 3,800 cycles at 2C with 83.5% capacity retention, representing a 343% enhancement over the best cyclability in the previous report. Besides, a practical 5 Ah anode-free pouch cell (181.1 Wh kg −1 ) also exhibits stable cycling over 2,500 cycles with 93.7% capacity retention, comparable to the performance of commercial LiFePO 4 batteries, demonstrating great application potential. Moreover, with proven effectiveness across diverse electrolytes and cathodes, this dead Na reactivation method offers a universal and effective pathway toward practical realization of AFSBs.

10.1002/adma.74740.title: 2D Abrupt Nano-Junctions Blending sp-sp2 Bonds on Atomically Precise Heterostructures
10.1002/adma.74740.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional heterostructures combining sp - sp hybridization-blending graphene with graphyne-based allotropes-offer substantial potential for enhancing the tunability of electronic and transport properties while providing significant structural flexibility, which are desirable characteristics for next-generation nanoscale electronics. Despite such potential, their experimental realization remains elusive, as synthesized carbon heterostructures are limited to doped, graphene-based systems exhibiting exclusively sp hybridization. Here, the on-surface synthesis of covalently bonded sp - sp lateral heterostructures between graphene nanoribbons and graphdiyne networks on Au(111) is demonstrated. Atomic-resolution scanning tunneling microscopy, combined with density functional theory, reveals the formation mechanism of the covalent interfacial bonds between nanoribbons and graphdiynes, also highlighting the key role of surface chemistry. Bromine atoms, deriving from the molecules dehalogenation and chemisorbed along the nanoribbon, inhibit junction formation, but bonding efficiency can be boosted up to 66% by controlled removal of these byproducts. Electronic structure and transport calculations show that the 2D heterostructure by itself is characterized by disentangled properties for the two subsystems, forming an atomically narrow junction, enabling voltage-tunable spatial current separation in two dimensions. These results define a viable strategy for engineering graphene-based sp - sp heterostructures, paving the way for the design and synthesis of all-carbon nanoscale electronic architectures.
authors: Alice Cartoceti, Simona Achilli, Masoumeh Alihosseini, Adriana E. Candia, Enrico Beltrami, Paolo D'Agosta, Alessio Orbelli Biroli, Francesco Sedona, Andrea Li Bassi, Jorge Lobo-Checa, Carlo S. Casari

10.1002/adma.74738.title: Interrupting Surface-to-Bulk Domino Propagation: A Thermal Failure Mitigation Strategy for Layered Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/adma.74738.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered transition-metal oxide cathodes are pivotal for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs)-powered energy-storage systems. However, the relentless pursuit of high performance is severely bottlenecked by intrinsic thermal safety concerns, where structural degradation and interfacial instability can trigger catastrophic thermal runaway. Herein, a thermally triggered domino effect, manifesting as a destructive chain reaction that initiates with severe interfacial side reactions at the cathode surface and sequentially propagates toward profound bulk structural collapse, is identified as the headstream of thermal failure. To mitigate these vulnerabilities, a scalable crystalline-state composite strategy is proposed by integrating micrometer-scale layered oxides with nanosized olivine-structured oxides (LMFP). This rationally designed architecture also synergistically realizes volumetric compacted density up to 3.75 g cm −3 and 86% capacity retention over 1000 cycles. Specifically, LMFP affords a dual-spatial stabilization: it directs the formation of a robust inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphase while simultaneously functioning as an internal thermal barrier to effectively interrupt this detrimental chain reaction, resulting in 61.3°C and 21.4°C thermal failure delay for both cathodes and ampere-hour-level cells, respectively, which creates more than 16 min for evacuation during thermal runaway. This work elucidates a previously overlooked surface-to-bulk failure mechanism and delineates a highly viable trajectory for designing intrinsically safe, highly stable cathode architectures.
authors: Yulong Wang, Shiqi Liu, Jingru Huang, Haozhe Du, Tian Wang, Fangzheng Liu, Xianwei Guo, Chengshan Xu, Haijun Yu

10.1002/adma.74605.title: Review of Inorganic Separator Engineering for Next-Generation Lithium-Sulfur Batteries: Compromise or Cornerstone?
10.1002/adma.74605.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries are promising next-generation energy-storage systems, but their practical application remains limited by polysulfide shuttling, sluggish redox kinetics, and interfacial instability. Separator engineering offers an effective route to regulate sulfur chemistry. This review summarizes metal compound-based separators as active interfacial architectures that promote polysulfide adsorption and catalytic conversion while regulating ion and electron transport. To evaluate diverse separator systems, we propose a Practical Relevance Index (PRI)-guided framework that integrates intrinsic electrochemical improvements with system-level constraints. A localized figure of merit is further introduced to interpret performance trends without direct cross-study ranking. Recent advances in metal oxides, sulfides, nitrides, carbides, and MXene-based separators are discussed, with emphasis on heterostructures, defect engineering, electronic-structure regulation, and atomic-scale design. Particular attention is given to constraint-aware strategies that connect interfacial chemistry with practical energy density. Finally, major challenges and future directions are outlined, including reaction-pathway regulation, operando characterization, system integration, and scalable manufacturing. This review provides a unified framework for designing practical, high-energy-density Li-S batteries.

10.1002/adma.74594.title: Oxalate Catalytic Pathway Over Fault-Twinned PdRh Bimetallene Enables Ultrastable Mg-CO2 Batteries
10.1002/adma.74594.abstract: ABSTRACT The reversibility of Mg-CO 2 batteries relies on stabilizing the oxalate pathway, yet conventional catalysts, such as noble metal catalyst, transition metal catalyst, and redox mediator, tend to over-stabilize oxalate intermediates, impeding their desorption and leading to carbonate formation, challenging the stability of Mg-CO 2 batteries. In this work, we propose a binding-weakening electronic modulation strategy that balances CO 2 activation and MgC 2 O 4 release for greatly enhancing the reversibility of Mg-CO 2 batteries. We demonstrate that the fault-twinned PdRh bimetallene, where Rh incorporation downshifts the Pd d -band center for weakening oxalate adsorption and Rh-derived conduction states enhance CO 2 activation, can well catalyze the reversible CO 2 conversion. Meanwhile, strain fields from abundant stacking faults create undercoordinated Pd sites that facilitate CO 2 → C 2 O 4 2− conversion. This dual regulation stabilizes the oxalate pathway that previous catalysts could not sustain for achieving ultrastable cycling over 700 h with minimal polarization (1.10 V discharge, 1.21 V charge), which represents a benchmark for both durability and energy efficiency among Mg-CO 2 batteries. The work establishes a new mechanistic foundation for rational pathway control in multivalent CO 2 electrochemistry.
authors: Wenbo Liu, Shengjie Liu, Fenyang Tian, Ning Li, Lu Li, Zongqiang Sun, Yang Hu, Mingchuan Luo, Xiaoxu Zhao, Yongsheng Yu, Rui Xu, Menggang Li, Shaojun Guo

10.1002/adma.74868.title: A Voltage-Stabilizing MXene Additive Electrolyte Mitigates Interference From External Force on the Charge-Discharge Process for Multifunctional Hybrid Structural Supercapacitors
10.1002/adma.74868.abstract: ABSTRACT In structural energy storage devices (SESDs) that simultaneously store electrochemical energy and bear mechanical loading, the external force will normally affect the electrochemical performance of SESDs. One example is that, under cyclic bending stress, voltage ripples emerge in charge-discharge curves, which cause voltage instability. In this study, we demonstrate that these voltage ripples originate from spatially heterogeneous electric field distribution within the mechanically deformed region. By using polarized electric fields formed through hydrogen bonding networks in MXene additive electrolyte, we can effectively homogenize the distribution of the electric field, thereby attenuating voltage ripples and smoothing the voltage curves. Moreover, the uniform electric field distribution promotes uniform Zn deposition and extends the device lifespan. As a result, the fabricated Zn-ion-based structural hybrid supercapacitor (CSHS) with MXene additive electrolyte exhibits a capacity retention of 93.6% after 10 000 three-point bending cycles at a strain of 0.5%, much higher than that of CSHS without the addition of MXene (80.4%). The investigation into the suppression of voltage ripples of SESDs paves a viable way to design high-performance structural power sources capable of exhibiting stable voltage under mechanical loading.
authors: Jing Zhang, Liqi Bai, Junyi Yu, Gao Chen, Hao Li, Sha Yin, Yongbo Fan, Anchalee Duongthipthewa, Zezhou Lin, Qingqing Wang, Yiuwing Mai, Haitao Huang, Limin Zhou

10.1002/adma.74698.title: Controllable Particle Packing via Scalable Layer-by-Layer Assembly of Anode Particles for Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.74698.abstract: ABSTRACT Particle packing in battery electrodes is pivotal to the fast-charging performance of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, precise control of particle packing structure remains a major challenge in electrode fabrication, primarily owing to the absence of robust interfacial bonding between micron-scale particles. Herein, we propose a novel layer-by-layer single-layer particle assembly technique to fabricate electrodes with well-defined particle packing structures. Using this approach, we prepared a 12-meter-long graphite (Gr)/hard carbon (HC) hybrid anode featuring a body-centered cubic (BCC)-like structure, which maximizes intimate Gr/HC contact interfaces and facilitates solid-state Li + transport. Coupled with LiFePO 4 (LFP) cathodes, the as-fabricated anode exhibits a high-capacity retention of 80.7% after 1650 cycles at 4C. From an electrode design standpoint, this controllable particle-packing strategy paves the way for a universal framework for developing sustainable, long-cycling, and fast-charging electrodes, potentially applicable to many types of battery anodes and cathodes.
authors: Zhiyong Wang, Yun Zhao, Jiyi Zhu, Xinyang Yue, Bo Lan, Zhenyu Guo, Maria-Magdalena Titirici, Hu Xu, Honggang Yu, Haizu Jin, Zheng Liang

10.1002/adma.202505096.title: DNA-Based Loop-Amplifier Fluorescence Signaling Networks Enable Rapid Quantitative Pathogen Detection of Periprosthetic Microbial Bone Infection
10.1002/adma.202505096.abstract: ABSTRACT Periprosthetic microbial bone infection (PMBI) is a serious pathological condition that may lead to terrible consequences without timely therapeutic intervention. However, the clinical management of PMBI is challenged by the difficulties in the efficient and accurate identification of microbial pathogens. For this purpose, we report a DNA-based loop-amplifier fluorescence signaling network (DLFSN) for the efficient and accurate detection of pathogenic microbes in the context of PMBI. The DLFSN system comprises an Amplifier Unit A and a Quantifier Unit B. Specifically, Amplifier Unit A transforms pathogenic microbial genetic materials into fluorescent DNA molecules through an entropy-driven automated reaction loop, leading to efficient and precise amplification of pathogen-specific genomic input signals. Subsequently, Quantifier Unit B converts the quenched fluorescent intermediate products into an activated state, thus allowing the precise identification of the genetic signature of pathogenic microorganisms in a quantitative manner. DLFSN demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy comparable to gold standard PMBI diagnostic technologies, including tissue section staining and qPCR, while the actual assay time was much lower at only around 30 min for real-life patients. The DLFSN system provides a promising precision diagnostic tool for early PMBI diagnosis, holding promise to improve orthopedic outcomes in the clinic.
authors: Siyu Guo, Xijiao Ren, Xiang Cui, Dong Sun, Chi Ma, Zhonghua Xu, Fei Luo, Yueqi Chen, Jinming He, Yuan Zhang, Kaiyong Cai, Zhong Luo, Licheng Zhang

10.1002/adma.74855.title: Toward Ultrahigh-Rate Li-Cl2 Batteries via an Electron Pump Strategy
10.1002/adma.74855.abstract: ABSTRACT Rechargeable lithium-chlorine (Li-Cl 2 ) batteries hold great promise due to their high energy density, yet their performance is limited by sluggish electron-ion transport at the solid-solid interface between the electrode and insulating LiCl. Here, we construct a MoSe 2 /TiN heterostructure featuring a built-in electric field-driven electron pump, which simultaneously enhances electronic coupling and achieve rapid activation of LiCl. This design enables rapid extraction of electrons from LiCl during charging, efficiently promotes LiCl dissociation and significantly reduces interfacial diffusion resistance by transforming the reaction interface from localized points into a homogeneous plane through strong electronic coupling. The resulting Li-Cl 2 battery achieves an ultralow polarization of 0.18 V and outstanding rate performance up to 50 A g −1 . Moreover, a cylindrical cell configuration demonstrates stable cycling over 35 cycles with a capacity retention of 70 mAh. This work offers both a high-performance cathode and fundamental insight into interfacial charge-mass transfer regulation in multi-phase battery systems.
authors: Wenting Feng, Xinru Wei, Fengliang Cao, Guanzhong Ma, Chenyu Ma, Zihui Liu, Han Wang, Xiaowei Zhang, Jinglei Xu, Debin Kong, Linjie Zhi

10.1002/adma.74846.title: Bifunctional Catalysis Drives Efficient and Ethanol-Producing Aqueous Zn-CO2 Batteries
10.1002/adma.74846.abstract: ABSTRACT Bifunctional electrocatalysts that simultaneously drive CO 2 reduction (CO 2 RR) and oxygen evolution (OER) in neutral electrolytes are essential for aqueous Zn-CO 2 batteries (AZCBs), but conventional designs prioritize CO 2 RR and are often incompatible with OER, resulting in low energy efficiency, poor reversibility, and rapid degradation of batteries. Here, we introduce a unified catalyst architecture integrating Cu and Ni single atoms with boron-, nitrogen-co-doped carbon (CuNi@BNC-T). Heteroatom co-doping stabilizes high single-atom loadings, enhances metal-support interactions, and suppresses carbon corrosion, while N-coordinated Cu + and Ni 3+ sites cooperatively boost CO 2 RR-OER, enabling ethanol formation and low-overpotential OER. This strategy achieves a 0.7 V voltage gap at 5 mA cm −2 , 522 h cycling at 20 mA cm −2 , and first ethanol production via AZCBs with energy efficiency of 88% (flow-cell). By elucidating previously unresolved degradation pathways, this work also correlates catalyst dynamics with battery failure, establishing design principles for durable bifunctional catalysts in aqueous Zn-CO 2 systems.
authors: Divyani Gupta, Jinshuo Zou, Anoja Kawsihan, Jodie A. Yuwono, Zhaoliang Wu, Jun Yu, Yameng Fan, Sailin Liu, Jianfeng Mao, Zaiping Guo

10.1002/adma.74866.title: Self-Powered Liquid TVNG Sensor for Robot Tactile and Gustatory Dual-Mode Sensing System
10.1002/adma.74866.abstract: ABSTRACT Tribovoltaic nanogenerator (TVNG) offers self-powered, low impedance, and high direct current transient response, making it highly suitable for robotic sensing. However, the poor performance and lack of intelligent sensing terminals in the solid-solid TVNG of the contact separation mode have limited its advanced applications. We present a self-powered liquid TVNG sensor (LTVNGS) coupling sliding and contact-separation modes, integrated with deep learning for robotic tactile and gustatory dual-mode sensing system. The low-resistance aqueous solution at the metal-semiconductor interface promotes the charge transport efficiency of LTVNG, and the sensitivity has been improved from the nA to the µA level. The working mechanism of LTVNG was revealed, and the principle of enhancing sensitivity in the solid-solid noncontact LTVNGS through the qualitative and quantitative analysis of the GO dispersion solution was explained. Besides, LTVNGs achieve prediction of water droplet height. Furthermore, LTVNG achieves tactile material and gustatory liquid recognition with an average identification accuracy exceeding 98%, assisted by deep learning models through the perception of different materials and liquids. This work provides a scientific framework for multimodal TVNG and its application in intelligent robots, offers an innovative approach for robot liquid analysis, and enhances the ability to identify hazardous liquids and the HMI.
authors: Wenyan Qiao, Linglin Zhou, Xinyuan Li, Minghao Jiang, Zhihao Zhao, Jie Wang, Gui-Bin Bian

10.1002/adma.74843.title: Lock-and-Key Intermediate Binding on Spinel Octahedra Enables Selective Urea Electrolysis
10.1002/adma.74843.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective urea electro-oxidation to benign N 2 gas over toxic ionic byproducts is crucial for sustainable hydrogen production and wastewater remediation, yet achieving the desired N─N coupling remains a formidable challenge. In this study, we propose an atomic-scale geometric matching strategy by pioneering an edge-sharing octahedral bridged spinel catalyst (MNCON). Through Mn 3+ incorporation into an N-modulated inverse NiCo 2 O 4 platform, we construct a robust Ni oct ─O─Mn oct edge-sharing network that precisely matches the interatomic spacing required for bridge-coordinated binding of key intermediateds and promotes electron delocalization. This structural synergy stabilizes the critical *NHCONH intermediate, lowers the thermodynamic energy barrier by 1.74 eV relative to the counterpart, and significantly accelerates N─N coupling. Consequently, MNCON simultaneously steers product selectivity toward benign N 2 /CO 2 with detrimental ionic byproducts reduced by approximately fourfold compared to NCO and delivers a UOR potential of 1.41 V vs. RHE at 300 mA cm −2 . The catalyst maintains structural durability for 500 h at 500 mA cm −2 , alongside steady hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) performance. Integrated into a UOR||HER electrolyzer, the symmetrical cell operates stably for over 400 h in artificial urine at a low average cell voltage of 1.31 V (10 mA cm −2 ). This edge-sharing accommodation paradigm provides a viable route for designing highly selective electrocatalysts.
authors: Chu-Yi Luo, Shao-Kuan Chen, Hui-Jian Zhang, Xiao-Tong Wang, Zhao-Qing Liu

10.1002/adma.74447.title: Nano-Architected Metallic Metamaterial With Enhanced Fatigue Resistance via Dislocation Starvation
10.1002/adma.74447.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal single crystals often suffer from severe strain localization under cyclic loading due to the absence of grain boundaries that act as crystallographic obstacles, resulting in their low fatigue resistance despite their advantages in applications requiring microstructural stability. This study demonstrates that this intrinsic trade-off can be overcome by exploiting dislocation starvation that arises as metal single crystals are reduced to the nanoscale. Tension-compression fatigue tests on 300 nm-wide nickel (Ni) single crystals reveal a fatigue-crack initiation limit exceeding 800 MPa, more than an order of magnitude higher than that of bulk Ni single crystals. In situ transmission electron microscopy experiments directly capture dislocation starvation during cyclic loading, confirming that strain localization, which typically serves as a precursor to fatigue-crack initiation, is completely suppressed. Based on this mechanism, a nano-architected Ni single-crystal metamaterial is designed to macroscopically harness dislocation starvation. Despite a relative density of only ∼50%, the metamaterial exhibits a fatigue-crack initiation limit about twice that of homogeneous Ni single crystals. These findings introduce a dislocation-starvation-driven design principle for simultaneously enhancing fatigue resistance and reducing weight in metal single crystals, thereby opening a new paradigm beyond the conventional limitations.
authors: Kota Sugisaka, Yamato Ishizaka, Hiroki Ikeda, Shigeo Arai, Masataka Abe, Yoshitaka Umeno, Hiroyuki Shima, Takashi Sumigawa

10.1002/adma.74730.title: Moiré-Induced Symmetry Breaking of Charge Order in van der Waals Heterostructures
10.1002/adma.74730.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered materials that stack different lattice symmetries are rare in nature. Misfit layered chalcogenides, which combine square and hexagonal lattices of rocksalt monochalcogenides and transition-metal dichalcogenides, provide a platform to explore how incommensurability and explicit symmetry breaking impact collective electronic phases. Here we use low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy to probe the misfit compounds (MS) 1+δ TaS 2 with M = Pb, Sn and track how the misfit interface reshapes the electronic ground state of the embedded 1H-TaS 2 monolayers. High-resolution STM imaging and Fourier analysis reveal that the charge-density wave (CDW) is incommensurate and exhibits spatially inhomogeneous, short-range correlations. Strikingly, the CDW exhibits a pronounced and anisotropic response to the uniaxial moiré potential imposed by the misfit layer: its coherence lengths and ordering wavevectors become inequivalent, demonstrating a strong nonlinear coupling between the intrinsic CDW instability and the symmetry-breaking moiré field. First-principles-informed multiscale modeling suggests that this reorganization arises from the combined effect of interlayer charge transfer and the spatially anisotropic energy landscape introduced by the misfit interface. In contrast, superconductivity is comparatively insensitive to the moiré, revealing a uniform, single full-gap consistent with s-wave pairing. Our results establish heterosymmetry stacking as a route to engineer correlated states in van der Waals materials.
authors: Sandra Sajan, Laura Pätzold, Tarushi Agarwal, Clara Pfister, Haojie Guo, Sisheng Duan, P. V. Sruthibhai, Mariana Rossi, Maria N. Gastiasoro, Sara Barja, Ravi P. Singh, Tim Wehling, Miguel M. Ugeda

10.1002/adma.74834.title: Real Time Self-Monitoring of Adhesion State via Machine Learning-Assisted Traffic Light Color-Coding in Silicone-Based Smart Superglue
10.1002/adma.74834.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite significant advancements in robust adhesive materials, convenient monitoring adhesion strength under service conditions before adhesion failure is essential yet challenging. In this study, structurally novel silicone-based conductive adhesive from comb-shaped supramolecular elastomers is reported, featuring self-monitoring of adhesion state in real time manner via machine learning-assisted traffic light color-coding approach. Comb-shaped supramolecular ion-conducting polysiloxane P(Ba- co -Apy- co -DMS) are first constructed via effective hydrosilylation, yielding pendant H-bonding barbiturate (Ba) and ionic liquids (Apy) moieties. Adhesion-sensitive electrical properties and experimental database are therefore constructed from P(Ba- co -Apy- co -DMS) via digitally transforming of adhesion strength into capacitance signals. Such database is further used to train a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates 1D convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) with long short-term memory (LSTM) units. This model learns the capacitance-adhesion mapping and translates the encoded signal features into States 1, 2, and 3. Moreover, a traffic light color-coding approach on the perceptions of adhesion strength is developed, green, orange, and red LED light symbols are respectively associated with States 1, 2, and 3 leveraged from deep learning architecture, reflecting tight, stretched, and fractured adhesion. Our conductive adhesives illustrate the Internet of Things-empowered adhesion state and structural health monitoring, offering promising opportunity to boost intelligentization and informatization of classical materials.
authors: Qizhe Deng, Yanfeng Zhang, Yantao Xu, Da Zheng, Senbin Chen, Jintao Zhu

10.1002/adma.74710.title: Deterministic Field-Free Switching of Perpendicular Magnetization by Bulk Mirror Symmetry Broken Bi1−xSbx (012) with High Spin Hall Conductivity
10.1002/adma.74710.abstract: ABSTRACT Out-of-plane spin-orbit torque generation in mirror-symmetry-broken materials is a promising approach for current-induced field-free magnetization switching. However, the key challenge lies in identifying materials with high in-plane spin Hall conductivity that simultaneously generate large out-of-plane spin-orbit torque for low-power spintronic applications. Previously studied low-symmetry materials, in which mirror-symmetry breaking is confined to the surface and the spin Hall conductivity is low, have not resolved this challenge. Here, we demonstrate deterministic field-free magnetization switching enabled by the bulk-mirror-symmetry-broken topological material Bi 1− x Sb x (012) with high in-plane spin Hall conductivity. The power consumption is two orders of magnitude lower than that of heavy-metal-based devices. Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance measurements confirm the bulk origin of the out-of-plane spin-orbit torque in Bi 1− x Sb x (012), yielding an out-of-plane spin Hall conductivity of (for x = 0.2), which is 5.6 times larger than that of TaIrTe 4 . Our results establish bulk mirror-symmetry engineering as an effective strategy for designing energy-efficient field-free spin-orbit torque devices.
authors: Seungwon Rho, Youngmin Lee, Jaeseok Huh, Jaehan Park, Hyeong-Jun Son, Dowoo Pyeon, Mann-Ho Cho

10.1002/adma.74821.title: Non-Destructive and High-Fidelity Sensing of Plant Water Content Enabled by Near-Infrared Luminescent Metal Halides
10.1002/adma.74821.abstract: ABSTRACT Real-time, accurate water monitoring is a crucial technical foundation for industrial, environmental, and biological research. However, traditional detection methods typically include destructive processes and suffer from response delays. Near-infrared (NIR) luminescent metal halides offer a novel solution to this challenge, but they still face issues such as ultraviolet excitation and low photoelectric conversion efficiency. Herein, a luminescent material was synthesized based on the blue-light-excited lead-free perovskite Cs 2 HfCl 6 :Te 4+ /Mo 4+ , in which energy transfer (ET) from Te 4+ to Mo 4+ enables highly efficient NIR luminescence in the 800-1200 nm wavelength range. Upon encapsulation with a commercial blue light chip, the fabricated NIR light-emitting diode device achieved a photoelectric conversion efficiency of up to 16.1%. By utilizing the absorption characteristics of water molecules in the NIR spectrum and receiving signals via a sensor, an interactive learning process based on a neural network machine learning algorithm was employed, achieving an estimation accuracy of up to 98.6% for plant water content. This non-destructive and precise NIR detection module provides a new solution for the real-time monitoring of crop physiological status and holds broad application prospects in the fields of precision agriculture and plant science.
authors: Yaning Zhao, Guodong Zhang, Jiaying Rong, Mingyue Gao, Peipei Dang, Tianjun Zhang, Hao Suo, Zhijun Wang, Ziyong Cheng, Panlai Li, Jun Lin

10.1002/adma.74828.title: Laser-Defined Reaction Topology Enables Controllable Solid-State Transformations for Scalable Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.74828.abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling reaction pathways in solids is critical for scalable semiconductor fabrication, yet remains fundamentally challenging in solution-processed systems due to constrained mass transport and diffusion-limited conversion. In perovskite photovoltaics, the widely adopted sequential two-step deposition method is particularly limited by dense PbI 2 precursor layers, which impede ion diffusion and lead to incomplete conversion and defect formation. Here we report a photonic strategy to spatially regulate solid-state reaction pathways by engineering micro- and nanoscale channels within PbI 2 layers. Laser-induced structures act as deterministic diffusion pathways, enabling controlled ion transport and spatially guided infiltration of organic salts, thereby transforming a diffusion-limited process into a spatially coordinated reaction. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photonic structuring redistributes the local electronic environment and lowers the activation barrier for phase transformation, resulting in accelerated conversion, enhanced crystallinity, and reduced defect density. The resulting perovskite films exhibit improved carrier dynamics. Perovskite solar modules with an aperture area of 22.95 cm 2 achieve a record power conversion efficiency of 22.83%, retaining over 90% of their initial performance after 1,500 h under maximum power point tracking. This work establishes photonic control of reaction pathways as a general framework for controlled solid-state transformations.
authors: Kaihuai Du, Haoran Zhang, Aili Wang, Xuebing Wen, Chunna Huang, Mengde Zhai, Hang Lin, Jialin Zhang, Lvzhou Li, Antonio Abate, Mohammad Khaja Nazeeruddin, Guixiang Li, Weijia Zhou, Jianning Ding

10.1002/adma.74826.title: Superspace Architecture-Driven Energy Funneling in Layered Halide Perovskite Nanoplatelets
10.1002/adma.74826.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered hybrid perovskites offer a versatile platform for tailoring light-matter interactions, where alternative stacking of inorganic and organic layers creates complex couplings that disrupt the conventional crystal symmetry. Standard crystallographic models fall short of capturing the temperature-dependent stacking disorder and multiplet excitonic features in these systems. Here, we introduce a four-dimensional superspace framework, employing a phenomenological atomic modulation function, to describe the symmetry-breaking interactions in Ruddlesden-Popper L 2 FA n -1 [Sn 0.022 Pb 0.978 ] n I 3 n +1 (L: oleylamine, n ≥ 2) nanoplatelet superlattices. Temperature-tunable optical spectra reveal microcavity-like excitonic confinement, while ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy uncovers sub-picosecond energy funneling through modulated quantum wells, facilitating a measurable and stable self-powered photoresponse across a broad spectral range at room temperature. A rare coexistence of negative thermal expansion and quenching arises from anisotropic octahedral distortions and electron-phonon interactions. These findings establish a new structure-function paradigm for designing thermally reconfigurable optoelectronic materials via engineered lattice modulation in hybrid perovskite superstructures.
authors: Vishwadeepa Hazra, Naresh Aggarwal, Santanu Mal, Mohammad Ubaid, Koushik Pal, K V Adarsh, Sayan Bhattacharyya

10.1002/adma.74824.title: Molecularly Engineered Degradable PCTPU-PAA Dielectrics With Boosted Carrier Mobility for Retina-Mimic Neuromorphic Visual Sensors Toward Closed-Loop Green Flexible Electronics
10.1002/adma.74824.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional polyurethane-based dielectrics are mostly nondegradable fossil-derived materials lacking effective end-of-life management, leading to massive electronic waste and unsustainable life cycles-key barriers to the green transition of flexible electronics. Despite their desirable stretchability and self-healing, inherent limitations in dielectric polarization and interfacial modulation restrict optoelectronic performance, creating an unresolved trade-off between functionality and sustainability. Guided by green chemical engineering and circular economy principles, we designed a degradable polycarbonate-based thermoplastic polyurethane (PCTPU) by incorporating PC soft segments into the polyurethane backbone, and constructed a robust non-covalent hydrogen-bonding network via poly (amic acid) (PAA) blending to synergistically regulate dielectric polarization and interfacial compatibility. The PCTPU-PAA composite exhibits excellent mechanical performance and enhanced self-healing property. Notably, when integrated into organic neuromorphic visual sensors (ONeuVS), the composite enables a ∼7.6-fold enhancement in carrier mobility versus bare PCTPU sensors. It also endows ONeuVS with enhanced retinal-like photoresponsiveness, achieving 92.67% accuracy in handwritten digit recognition while reducing neural network training costs. Critically, a scalable multi-solvent stepwise separation method achieves efficient degradation and recovery, realizing a closed-loop life cycle. This work establishes a scalable molecular engineering strategy for high-performance, sustainable flexible dielectrics and devices, breaking the performance-sustainability trade-off and facilitating their large-scale green applications.
authors: Zijie Yang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Weiyu Wang, Hui Yang, Bin Wang, Deyang Ji, Wenping Hu

10.1002/adma.74789.title: Unlocking Ultra-Long Cycling Stability in Fluorophosphate Cathodes via Electrostatic Interaction Regulation and Enhanced V─O Covalency
10.1002/adma.74789.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyanionic Na 3 (VO) 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F is a promising cathode for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) due to its stable structural framework and high operating voltage. However, its practical application is hindered by low electronic conductivity and sluggish Na + diffusion kinetics, which originate from the strong Coulombic attraction between Na + and the framework anions, and the Na + -Na + repulsion. In this study, we propose a novel anion engineering strategy involving simultaneous Br doping and Na vacancy. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal that the partial substitution of O 2− with less electronegative Br − induces local charge redistribution, which enhances V 3d─O 2p orbital hybridization and strengthens V─O covalent bonds, improving structural stability and narrowing bandgap. The resulting charge compensation creates sodium vacancies that alleviate electrostatic repulsion among Na + ions, facilitating Na + diffusion. Moreover, Br doping expands interlayer spacing and mitigates charge transfer resistance. Consequently, the electrode exhibits exceptional long-term cyclability (62.07 mAh g −1 after 90,000 cycles at 20 C) and superior rate capability (85.93 mAh g −1 at 100 C). The full cell paired with a hard carbon achieves high energy density and excellent cycling stability. This work provides a feasible and effective anionic doping approach for designing long-life SIBs.
authors: Zengrong Mao, Jiarui Lin, Rui Jiang, Shenghong Yang, Sheng Ouyang, Xiaoyan Shi, Junling Xu, Lianyi Shao, Zhipeng Sun

10.1002/adma.74791.title: A Transparent, High Refractive Index and Abbe Number Polymer for Visible Metalens by High Fidelity Nanoimprinting
10.1002/adma.74791.abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneously achieving high visible transparency, high refractive index ( n ), and a large Abbe number ( υ D ) in organic polymers remains a fundamental challenge. Here, a facile and efficient dual sulfur-mediated Michael addition strategy is reported to synthesize transparent high refractive index polymers (HRIPs) with large υ D . By combining main backbone de-conjugation to preserve visible transparency with rational side-chain engineering for n -tuning, the optimal polymer (H4) achieves an ultrahigh n of 1.86 at 589 nm alongside a large υ D of 34.93 and robust stability. Moreover, polymer H4 exhibits remarkable performance in nanoimprint lithography, replicating features down to 75 nm with aspect ratios up to 8.5 and a low volumetric shrinkage of only 3.23%. Notably, a nanoimprinted metalens prototype fabricated from H4 delivers a relative focusing efficiency of 49.8% at 550 nm (NA = 0.5), approaching the theoretical design value (52.94%). Therefore, the high refractive index polymer H4 bridges molecular design and manufacturable meta-optics, showing tremendous potential in scalable, flexible, next-generation photonic platforms by translating side-chain polarizability engineering into practical wavefront control.
authors: Jianrong Guo, Hongbin Chen, Ziyu Wang, Yuan-Yuan Cheng, Ji chao Fu, Siqi Liu, Jun Hu, Binting Huang, Shiyang Shao, Yuanda Liu, Fangfang Huang, Chaobin He

10.1002/adma.74617.title: Spatial Planarization Controls Optical Anisotropy for Efficient and Stable Blue-Emitting OLEDs
10.1002/adma.74617.abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, we report a spatial planarization strategy for asymmetric Ir(III) complexes that simultaneously improves exciton stability and optical outcoupling in blue OLEDs. By incorporating bulky tert -butylcarbazole (tBuCz) units into tridentate N-heterocyclic carbene ligands, the molecular geometry is sterically confined into a more coplanar and anisotropic configuration. This structural planarization increases exciton binding energy and shortens the radiative lifetime, thereby stabilizing bound excitons against thermally activated dissociation while accelerating radiative exciton consumption. At the same time, the enhanced geometric anisotropy induces a highly horizontal emitting dipole orientation (EDO) of approximately 95%, enabling efficient intrinsic light extraction. Beyond its role as an emitter, the planarized Ir(III) complex further has a cooperative alignment effect in hyper-OLED architectures. This structural and electrostatic templating effect transfers molecular alignment to the terminal multiple-resonance TADF emitter v -DABNA, leading to secondary dipole ordering with an EDO of 98%. As a result, the optimized blue hyper-OLED achieves ultra-narrow emission at 470 nm with a full width at half maximum of 22 nm, a maximum external quantum efficiency of 36.9%, and an operational lifetime (LT 50 , time to 50% initial luminance) of 446 h at 1000 cd m −2 . These results establish spatial planarization as a powerful molecular design principle for coupling exciton stabilization, dipole orientation control, and interfacial alignment transfer, providing a general strategy for efficient and stable blue OLEDs.
