10.1002/adma.75326.title: A Multifunctional Ionograsper Enabling Ion-Redistribution Proximity Sensing and Structural-Reconfiguration-Driven Bidirectional Actuation (Adv. Mater. 59/2026)
authors: Yong Min Kim, Jin Han Kwon, Hyeon Woo Yang, Sungryong Kim, Gyeong Rok Lee, Hong Chul Moon

10.1002/adma.75480.title: Engineering Bidirectional Neuromodulation: A Review of Neural Excitation and Inhibition Technologies
10.1002/adma.75480.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. Yet neural activity can require regulation in opposing directions across different cellular, circuit and pathological states, motivating bidirectional neuromodulation that can both enhance and suppress neural activity. In this review, we examine the mechanisms and technologies that enable such bidirectional control across electrical, optical, thermal, mechanical, magnetic and chemical modalities. We compare these approaches in terms of spatiotemporal performance, penetration depth, specificity and safety, and examine the materials, transduction strategies and device architectures used to implement bidirectional neural control. We further discuss the applications of bidirectional neuromodulation in neuroscience research and the treatment of neurological disorders. Finally, we discuss the technical challenges and future directions toward more precise, independent and integrated bidirectional control, including its extension to closed-loop adaptive regulation.
authors: Xue Cai, Yuxin Liu, Xing Sheng

10.1002/adma.75474.title: Self-Segregated Buried-Interface Regulation Resolves Kinetic-Environmental Coupling for Ambient Flexible Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75474.abstract: ABSTRACT Ambient fabrication of flexible perovskite solar cells is fundamentally limited by a detrimental kinetic-environmental coupling at the buried interface, where moisture ingress and nonoptimal crystallization mutually compromise film quality-yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using dual-side in situ photoluminescence, we overturn the conventional top-down model by revealing simultaneous nucleation at both gas-liquid and liquid-solid interfaces during antisolvent-assisted solution processing, but find that outward solvent evaporation delays α-phase conversion at the buried interface relative to the surface, creating kinetic mismatch that exacerbates moisture attack and defect accumulation. To address these kinetic and environmental constraints, we design a self-segregating multifunctional molecule, 2-[(3-trifluoromethyl)phenyl]amino-3-pyridinecarboxylic acid (NFA), which spontaneously enriches at the buried interface to synchronize dual-interface crystallization while simultaneously passivating defects, optimizing energy-level alignment, and constructing a hydrophobic barrier against moisture ingress. Consequently, this self-segregated kinetic-environmental regulation yields record ambient flexible photovoltaic performance with power-conversion efficiencies of 24.84% (0.09 cm 2 , certified at 23.75%) and 21.46% on mini-modules (13.8 cm 2 ). The optimized devices maintain 96.26% of their starting efficiency following 1000 h damp aging at 85 ± 5% RH. Our work establishes self-segregated interfacial regulation as a rational route to address kinetic and environmental constraints in scalable flexible photovoltaics.
authors: Chenxin Zhao, Erxin Zhao, Xuan Ji, Tinghuan Yang, Tianqi Niu, Nan Wu, Zheng Zhang, Di Zhao, Xuexia He, Kui Zhao

10.1002/adma.75356.title: Ultrasound-Activated Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework Synergistically Enhances Antitumor Immunity by Epigenetic Reprogramming and Pyroptosis Induction
10.1002/adma.75356.abstract: ABSTRACT Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory form of cell death, elicits robust antitumor immune responses. However, pyroptosis-based cancer immunotherapy is hampered by the epigenetic silencing of gasdermin E (GSDME) through hypermethylation of the DFNA5 gene. To overcome this limitation, we engineered an innovative nanosystem by first synthesizing a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive decitabine prodrug (DTO), which was subsequently encapsulated within hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks to form the HDTO nanoplatform. Upon ultrasound (US) activation, the HDTO nanoplatform exhibited potent ROS generation, enabling two complementary functions: (1) triggering decitabine release to demethylate DFNA5 and restore GSDME expression and (2) activating caspase-3, thereby initiating the caspase-3/GSDME-mediated pyroptotic pathway. This apoptosis-to-pyroptosis switching mechanism significantly enhanced immunogenic cell death and potentiated antitumor immunity. In vivo studies demonstrated that US-activated HDTO induced robust pyroptosis, remodeled the tumor microenvironment, and elicited superior antitumor immune responses, resulting in marked suppression of tumor growth and metastasis. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that HDTO + US-induced pyroptosis depleted nonimmune cells while expanding monocyte and neutrophil populations, demonstrating effective immunoreprogramming. This study establishes a novel therapeutic paradigm that synergistically integrates epigenetic modulation with pyroptosis induction to enhance the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy.
authors: Fan Zhuang, Jingjing Li, Chenguang Shi, Cuixian Li, Beilei Lu, Mengqi Yan, Wenping Wang, Huijing Xiang, Yu Chen, Beijian Huang

10.1002/adma.75457.title: GaSex Nanoparticles Modulate Neutrophil Function and Mitigate NET-Driven Osteogenic Impairment in Osteomyelitis Therapy
10.1002/adma.75457.abstract: ABSTRACT Osteomyelitis remains a major clinical challenge; however, current therapeutic strategies do not sufficiently address host immune defense, inflammatory microenvironment remodeling, or bone regeneration. Here, we show that excessive accumulation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) in infected bone tissues contributes to osteomyelitis-associated apoptosis and impaired osteogenesis. NETs disrupt PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitochondrial quality control in osteoblast lineage cells, thereby promoting apoptosis, whereas inhibition of NET formation alleviates these pathological changes and improves bone repair in mice. Bone defects are aggravated in Prkn -knockout mice upon the induction of osteomyelitis, supporting the functional role of PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy in the repair of infected bone. As a therapeutic strategy, gallium-selenium nanoparticles (GaSe x ) exert potent antibacterial activity, redirect neutrophils from NET formation toward phagocytosis, preserve osteoblast mitochondrial homeostasis, attenuate excessive mitophagy, and ultimately promote the repair of infected bone defects in rats. Collectively, these findings support NET-driven osteoblast mitochondrial injury as a critical repair-limiting mechanism in osteomyelitis and establish GaSe x as a redox-regulating platform that modulates this mechanism while preserving neutrophil antibacterial defense.
authors: Kai Ye, Xuanzhe Liu, Zifan Pei, Chenyi Jiang, Xiaofen Zhang, Lin Lin, Qihang Fang, Binyu Chen, Longxiang Shen, Liang Cheng, Peng Ding, Xianyou Zheng

10.1002/adma.75401.title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300-Cycle Ah-Level Anode-Free Sodium Batteries
10.1002/adma.75401.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode-targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode-specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)-dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record-high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg − 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode-free full cells based on Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (NFPP), Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP), and NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.
authors: Ning Jiang, Qiaonan Zhu, Liqiang Wu, Weihao Wang, Tai Peng, Jinhui Zhao, Jiawei Wang, Guangze Yang, Xinyu Liu, Shuai Dong, Bin Zhou, Daojun Yang, Hua Wang

10.1002/adma.75444.title: Decoupling Protection and Doping Unlocks Asymmetric Zn Single Atoms for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
10.1002/adma.75444.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise manipulation of the coordination environment in single-atom catalysts is crucial yet challenging for boosting oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) performance. Here we present a sacrificial-guided etching strategy to activate intrinsically passive d 10 Zn centers in single-atom catalysts, wherein Bi(NO 3 ) 3 -mediated protection preserves ZnN 4 coordination by mitigating excessive etching, while NaCl-driven Cl doping imparts a remote electron-withdrawing effect, concertedly modulating the electronic structure of the Zn centers. This decoupling strategy, which assigns protection and doping to distinct species, unlocks asymmetric Zn single atoms with dual precision over coordination number and dopant configuration. The resulting catalyst achieves an exceptional ORR half-wave potential of 0.916 V, surpassing commercial Pt/C, and delivers a record peak power density of 258 mW cm −2 with outstanding cycling stability exceeding 450 h in zinc-air batteries. Integrated theoretical and in situ spectroscopic analyses reveal that Cl incorporation disrupts the symmetric ZnN 4 electronic structure, optimizes the d-band center, and alters unoccupied orbital hybridization, thereby accelerating O 2 protonation and boosting the overall catalytic activity. This work establishes a well-defined strategy for the precise construction of single-atom metal centers, providing insights into the development of high-performance non-precious metal electrocatalysts.
authors: Pengcheng Zhao, Xinchen Xu, Liu Yang, YuXuan Wu, Yong Zheng, Zhongwei Chen

10.1002/adma.75461.title: Hollow Conjugated Microporous Polymers Anchored With ZnxCd1-xS Quantum Dots: An Additive-Free Photocatalyst for H2O2 Synthesis via S-Scheme Charge Transfer
10.1002/adma.75461.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a green alternative to the anthraquinone process, but single-component photocatalysts suffer from rapid charge recombination. Here, we construct an S-scheme heterojunction by growing Zn x Cd 1-x S (ZCS) quantum dots (QDs) in situ on hollow conjugated microporous polymers (CMPs) containing selenadiazole units ( h PSe). The hollow CMPs scaffold provides high surface area, abundant pores for QDs embedding, efficient mass transfer, and enhanced light harvesting, while the selenadiazole units promote strong interfacial coupling. In pure water without any sacrificial agent, the optimal ZCS@ h PSe-2 composite achieved an outstanding H 2 O 2 production rate of 15.13 mmol g −1 h −1 with a synergy factor of 1.53 and an apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 8.82% at 400 nm, operating exclusively via the 2e − ORR. The dramatic performance is attributed to the S-scheme charge transfer mechanism, which preserves the strong redox potentials of both components and suppresses bulk charge recombination. This work demonstrates that rational integration of QDs with hollow CMPs provides a viable pathway toward efficient, additive-free photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis.
authors: Jie Jie Kang, Jian Yi, You Cheng Xing, Xue Li, Tao Cai

10.1002/adma.75002.title: Elasticity-Driven Periodic Polarization Patterns in a Chiral Ferroelectric Nematic Fluid
10.1002/adma.75002.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric nematic phases are a new class of polar fluids in which spontaneous polarization is directly coupled to the orientational order, providing unique opportunities for creating self-organized materials with spatially modulated electric polarization and nonlinear optical response. Here we report the spontaneous emergence of polarization-modulated textures in a chiral ferroelectric nematic material close to the transition to the chiral twist-bend ferroelectric nematic phase. By systematically varying cell thickness and surface anchoring conditions, we map the formation of these modulated states, revealing stripe, square, and hexagonal morphologies determined via confinement conditions. These structures are directly translated into periodic modulation of the nonlinear optical response, as evidenced by second harmonic generation imaging. Comparison with an elasticity-based theoretical framework and numerical free energy minimization shows that the instability originates from the softening of the bend elastic constant in the chiral nematic phase as the system approaches the lower-temperature heliconical polar phase. The resulting elastic frustration, combined with confinement, drives the formation of spatially periodic director distortions, highlighting ferroelectric nematic fluids as a promising platform for self-assembled nonlinear optical materials.

10.1002/adma.74798.title: Multi-Physical Field Coupling Mechanisms and Multi-Scale Design for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
10.1002/adma.74798.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) are regarded as a pivotal developmental route for next-generation energy storage technologies owing to their inherent safety and promising high-energy-density capability. Focusing on multi-physical field coupling and aiming to achieve high safety and high energy density simultaneously, this review systematically summarizes the multi-scale design strategies of ASSLBs. At the intrinsic material scale, this work summarizes the performance characteristics, failure mechanisms and optimization approaches of high-voltage/high-capacity cathodes, high-energy-density anodes, and diverse solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). From the electrode-electrolyte interfacial perspective, particular emphasis is placed on the multi-physical field coupling failure evolution of cathode-electrolyte and anode-electrolyte interfaces, alongside the modulation mechanisms of interfacial modification and structural engineering on interfacial contact, ionic conduction, volume variation effects and structural durability. At the full-cell system scale, optimization designs including cell configuration refinement, monolithic integration manufacturing, and synergistic thermal management and safety engineering are elaborated. Finally, addressing the current challenges in the field, such as ambiguous dynamic multi-physical-field coupling fundamentals and the infeasibility of real-time prediction on coupled failure behaviors, this review concludes with prospects for the establishment and implementation of an in-situ multi-physical-field characterization framework, delivering experimental foundations and theoretical guidelines toward the multi-scale synergistic optimization of ASSLBs.

10.1002/adma.74959.title: Glucose-Derived Circular Thermoset Platform Breaks the Industrial Trilemma of Recyclable Structural Polymers
10.1002/adma.74959.abstract: ABSTRACT The long-standing trilemma of scalable green synthesis, industrial processing compatibility, and balanced performance-circularity represents the core barrier limiting real-world deployment of recyclable thermosets. Here, we report an exogenous catalyst- and solvent-free one-pot strategy with ∼100% atom economy to fabricate glucose-derived built-in dynamic covalent thermosets from three industrial bulk feedstocks: glucose, maleic anhydride, and pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate). The optimal formulation achieves an unprecedented balance between >130 d of room-temperature shelf life (no gelation) and 2-min gelation at 150°C, delivering engineering-grade tensile strength up to 113 MPa, 17.5 MPa steel lap shear strength, and drop-in compatibility with industrial vacuum-assisted resin infusion for large carbon fiber composite manufacturing. We demonstrate complete room-temperature closed-loop recycling: nondestructive recovery of high-value carbon fibers with full performance retention, and matrix degradation products (73.2%-83.1% isolated yield) upcyclable into high-performance epoxy curing agents. Thermal reprocessing provides an additional reuse pathway for manufacturing scrap. Our cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment confirms 81.4% lower CO 2 -equivalent emissions than virgin bisphenol A epoxy carbon fiber composites. This work establishes a generalizable, industrially deployable paradigm for circular high-performance thermosets, resolving the long-standing trilemma impeding recyclable thermosets deployment.

10.1002/adma.75394.title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress-ROS-Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy
10.1002/adma.75394.abstract: ABSTRACT In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-ROS-inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress-centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER-regulating heterojunction (ERR-HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti 3 C 2 MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti 3 C 2 heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H 2 O 2 to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK-CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue-regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR-HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self-perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection-associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress-ROS-inflammation cycle inhibition.
authors: Wanxi Chen, Wenxuan He, Wenyu Dai, Bin Li, Fan Yang, Tian Chen, Rui Shu, Ding Bai, Yi Deng, Hui Xu

10.1002/adma.75462.title: Electronic Coupling and Dual-Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate-to-Ammonia Conversion
10.1002/adma.75462.abstract: ABSTRACT Rational design of dual-site catalysts to decouple complex multi-electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO 3 RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4-electron step reduces NO 3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4-electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4-electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well-defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co 7 Fe 3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO 3 RR through synergistic dual-spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH 3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn-nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm −2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.
authors: Lin Gao, Zhuofan Wang, Xue Wang, Li Ma, Meihong Fan, Xingquan He, Zexing Qu, Zhongmin Su, Tewodros Asefa

10.1002/adma.75475.title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
10.1002/adma.75475.abstract: ABSTRACT Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high-performance perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next-generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase often accompanies CsPbBr 3 crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive-mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3-carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3-CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr 3 formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs 4 PbBr 6 and CsPbBr 3 phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr 3 phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.
authors: Jike Zhang, Tao Sheng, Gang Wang, Gu Li, Shaohui Liu, Xiaosong Qiu, Shengwen Li, Guanbao Wu, Yuan Wang, Guodan Wei, Jiale Chang, Rui Duan, Huan Liu, Shi Chen, Rui Chen, Jia Guo, Guichuan Xing, Handong Sun

10.1002/adma.75472.title: Engineered Excited-State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators
10.1002/adma.75472.abstract: ABSTRACT Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low-cost, high-performance x-ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu-I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin-orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x-ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation-induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation-state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu-I clusters with nearly identical x-ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited-state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water-resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV −1 and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm −1 . Furthermore, tandem integration with a high-Z scintillator enables selective density-discriminating x-ray imaging and micro-computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high-throughput development of promising metal-cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

10.1002/adma.75415.title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow-Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
10.1002/adma.75415.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic in-sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co-localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation-anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion-migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo-modulation is further attenuated by exciton-polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion-migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3-(1-vinyl-3-imidazolyl)-propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro- and photo-synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation-anion pair prevents long-distance ion-migration, ensuring strong cation-anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi-wavelength photo-synaptic modulation coupled with electro-synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application-relevant in-sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color-guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian-speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing-computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.
authors: Jingpeng Wu, Yi Zhao, Chaoxiong Guo, Pengyu Du, Xian Tang, Zechen Liang, Yiyu Chen, Xin Wang, Laju Bu, Guanghao Lu

10.1002/adma.75469.title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
10.1002/adma.75469.abstract: ABSTRACT AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next-generation ferroelectric in-memory computing architecture and radio-frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high-quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system-level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy-efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

10.1002/adma.75477.title: Harnessing Rare Earth Elements in Proteins and Functional Materials for Advanced Optical, Magnetic, and Mechanical Applications
10.1002/adma.75477.abstract: ABSTRACT Rare earth-proteins and their functional materials integrate unique physical properties of rare earth ions (RE 3+ ) with structural programmability of proteins, attracting increasing attention in a wide range of applications. Coordination with RE 3+ can enhance the rigidity and stability of certain proteins, even induce secondary structure transitions, and confer distinct physical properties onto functional materials. The programmability of amino acid sequences regulates coordination chemistry between proteins and RE 3+ , enabling the modulation of their optical and magnetic properties. Moreover, RE 3+ incorporation turns protein structures and aggregation state, leading to enhanced mechanical properties and adhesion strength. However, the development of such materials still faces significant challenges due to lack of molecular mechanism analysis and systematic rational design strategies. This review highlights the chemical structural analysis, rational design and synthesis strategies of rare earth-protein and their functional materials. In addition, their applications in optics, magnetics, and mechanics are summarized. Finally, their current challenges and future perspectives are discussed.
authors: Yumeng Jia, Wenhao Cheng, Jingjing Li, Juanjuan Su, Yawei Liu, Hongjie Zhang, Kai Liu

10.1002/adma.75432.title: A Novel pH-Activatable Nanozyme for Treating Breast Cancer Bone Metastasis by Regulating Cancer Cell Metabolic Reprogramming and the Tumor Microenvironment
10.1002/adma.75432.abstract: ABSTRACT Multi-omics analyses implicate enhanced oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) in breast cancer bone metastasis (BCBM). To target this metabolic vulnerability, we develop SPMMPA, a bone-targeted nanozyme comprising a Prussian blue core, a disulfide-bridged mesoporous silica interlayer, and a manganese oxide shell, functionalized with polyethylenimine, alendronate, and the Ser-Asp-Ser-Ser-Asp peptide. Its acid-enhanced catalytic activity promotes reactive oxygen species production and glutathione depletion, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced OXPHOS and adenosine triphosphate production, and downregulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha. Alendronate and silicon release contribute to reduced osteoclast activity and preservation of bone structure. Near-infrared irradiation further enhances treatment efficacy through photothermal heating below 48°C. In mouse models of BCBM, SPMMPA suppresses tumor growth and alleviates osteolysis, without overt toxicity in the assays performed. These findings support a pH-responsive catalytic strategy that couples disruption of tumor energy metabolism with protection of bone homeostasis.
authors: Qianqian Qiao, Haosheng Wang, Ying Chen, Xueying An, Chengzhi Wang, Depeng Fang, Peng Wang, Huan Li, Yan Liu, Zhihong Xu, Qing Jiang, Baosheng Guo

10.1002/adma.75486.title: Constructing Stretchable Superhydrophobic Perovskite Quantum Dot Films via Dual-Phase Synergistic Engineering
10.1002/adma.75486.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite quantum dots (PQDs) films intended for flexible optical applications are required not only to exhibit excellent luminescence performance, but also to simultaneously possess high stretchability, superhydrophobicity, patterned luminescence, and multicolor programmability under complex conditions such as large deformation, liquid intrusion, and long-term service. Here we propose a dual-phase synergistic engineering strategy, and in combination with replica molding and femtosecond laser direct writing technologies, achieve the construction of a biomimetic superhydrophobic surface and the controllable precipitation of PQDs while endowing the film with superelasticity. Benefiting from the dual-phase structure and biomimetic surface design, the film still retains more than 52% of its initial luminescence intensity and a water contact angle above 150° under 800% tensile deformation. This strategy is applicable to full-spectrum luminescent systems spanning 470-688 nm and supports proof-of-concept binary optical encoding. After continuous immersion in water for 240 days, the film still retains more than 90% of its initial luminescence intensity and more than 95% machine-learning recognition accuracy. This work provides a new strategy for the design of multifunctional flexible PQDs films with stable luminescence under deformation and water exposure.

10.1002/adma.75479.title: Quantification of Magnetic Interactions in van der Waals Heterostructures Using Lorentz Transmission Electron Microscopy and Off-Axis Electron Holography
10.1002/adma.75479.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic van der Waals (vdW) materials are promising for memory and logic applications because of their tunable magnetic properties and compatibility with vdW heterostructure devices. However, coupling between magnetic textures in stacked layers is difficult to resolve in conventional plan-view measurements because the magnetic signal is integrated over the sample thickness. Here, these interactions are quantified in Fe 3 GeTe 2 (FGT)/graphite/FGT heterostructures using cross-sectional Lorentz transmission electron microscopy and off-axis electron holography, enabling reconstruction of the local projected magnetic induction within and between the layers. Domain alignment weakens with increasing FGT separation, yielding a stray-field coupling length scale of nm for the cross-sectional geometry studied here, corresponding to the average separation at which domain misalignment first emerges. This length scale corresponds to an approximately 23% reduction in the interlayer magnetic induction relative to bulk FGT. The magnetic induction is reduced relative to bulk FGT up to 100 nm from a surface. Comparisons with model-based iterative reconstructions of the magnetization and micromagnetic simulations show that this near-surface reduction is due to demagnetizing and stray fields. These results quantify the magnetic induction in stacked vdW magnets and guide the design of devices that require controllable coupling between magnetic textures.

10.1002/adma.75503.title: Cesium Tin Iodide Perovskites Engineer the Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ Redox Reaction in Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75503.abstract: ABSTRACT Tin displays rich redox chemistry transitioning between metallic tin (Sn 0 ), stannous (Sn 2+ ), and stannic (Sn 4+ ) states, among which the Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ couple offers the highest theoretical potential ( >0.14 V vs. SHE) whereas remaining unrealized in practical batteries. Herein, we introduce the in situ and successive growth of CsSnI 3 single perovskite and Cs 2 SnI 6 double perovskite layers on the cathode surface during operation, enabling the first demonstration of the Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ redox reaction in zinc-ion batteries, with an increased potential to 0.39 V versus SHE due to enhanced tin-halide coordination. Further integrated into Zn||SnCl 4 full batteries, the design delivers dual discharge plateaus at 1.18 V (Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ ) and 1.28 V (I 0 /I − ), yielding a high areal capacity of 0.80 mAh cm −2 at 1 mA cm −2 and high energy density of 0.99 mWh cm −2 (660 Wh kg −1 , per SnCl 4 ·5H 2 O mass of the cathode). The three-electron transfer design exhibits considerable longevity, with Swagelok cells retaining 7000 cycles at 16 mA cm −2 and pouch cells sustaining 200 cycles at 4 mA cm −2 without capacity loss. By enabling the high-potential Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ redox reaction, the perovskite interlayer provides a cross-disciplinary strategy to advancing high-energy aqueous zinc-ion batteries.

10.1002/adma.75490.title: Bridging the Gap Between Photocatalytic Water Oxidation Half-Reaction and Stoichiometric Pure Water Splitting Over Ta 3 N 5 via Cocatalyst Engineering
10.1002/adma.75490.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite significant progress in photocatalytic half-reactions and photoelectrochemical water oxidation, achieving stable photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta 3 N 5 remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, the incompatibility of cocatalysts between alkaline photocatalytic water oxidation systems and pure water splitting is identified as a critical bottleneck, leading to serious N 2 generation through photocorrosion. To address this challenge, a highly dispersed RuCoO x cocatalyst is developed via a multi-step incipient wetness impregnation strategy. The optimized Pt@Cr 2 O 3 /Ta 3 N 5 /RuCoO x achieves stoichiometric pure water splitting with an apparent quantum yield of 0.72% at 420 nm, representing the highest value reported for Ta-based nitride/oxynitride photocatalysts to date. Mechanistic studies reveal that an enhanced interfacial electric field facilitates hole extraction, while a reduced formation barrier of key intermediates accelerates surface reaction kinetics, thereby overcoming the long-standing bottleneck in photocatalytic pure water splitting over Ta 3 N 5 . This work establishes cocatalyst compatibility as a key design consideration for stable photocatalytic pure water splitting and provides mechanistic insight for the rational design of advanced nitride and oxynitride photocatalysts.

10.1002/adma.75471.title: Spatial and Spectral Decoupled Meta-Window for Thermal Camouflage and Infrared Communication
10.1002/adma.75471.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal radiation carries energy and information, making simultaneous control of its spectral profile and spatial propagation crucial for infrared camouflage, signaling, and communication. However, most thermal materials prioritize spectral manipulation, leaving the propagation direction of broadband thermal signals underexplored and tightly coupled to the spectral response. Here, a spatial and spectral decoupled meta-window (SSDW) is demonstrated for independent control of the spectral profile and spatial distribution of broadband thermal radiation across 8-13 µm. By assigning directional reflection splitting and spectral tailoring to distinct geometric degrees of freedom, the SSDW exhibits visible haze, mid-infrared semitransparency, and broadband suppression of specular reflection, including at 10.6 µm. It maintains a stable apparent thermal signature both without external heat interference and under variations in external-source temperature, source incidence angle, and camera viewing angle. This enables visible-laser-infrared compatible camouflage, while preserving an outward channel for emergency signaling. As a proof-of-concept, the SSDW encodes the incidence direction of a 10.6 µm laser into spatial reflection patterns for assistive infrared communication, enabling reliable decoding over moderate angular variations. This work establishes spatial and spectral decoupling as a framework for thermal radiation engineering, extending control beyond radiative intensity toward coordinated heat and information pathways.

10.1002/adma.75492.title: Machine-Learning-Potential-Driven Volcano Relationship in Grain Boundary Amorphicity and Ionic Transport of Antiperovskite Solid Electrolytes
10.1002/adma.75492.abstract: ABSTRACT Ionic transport in solid-state electrolytes is governed by interfacial disorder and local chemical environments, yet their microscopic design principles remain challenging because large-scale interfacial kinetics are simulated using molecular dynamics (MD), where predictive design requires quantum-level accuracy. Here, we use an actively learned machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to bridge this scale-accuracy gap in halide-tunable antiperovskite solid electrolytes. By varying the local Cl − /Br − ratio and quantifying interfacial amorphicity and ion flux, we identify an MLIP-driven volcano relationship between structural disorder and ionic transport. Cl-enriched grain boundaries remain overly ordered, whereas Br − enrichment induces excessive disorder that disrupts migration. Intermediate halide compositions maximize ionic transport through moderately amorphous environments. Guided by this relationship, we design an anion-engineered grain boundary through selective halide tuning. These results establish controlled anion segregation as a strategy for reducing interfacial resistance and highlight MLIP-enhanced MD as a predictive framework for transport and disorder engineering in solid-state materials.

10.1002/adma.75494.title: Amorphization Unlocks Active Sites in Organic Small Molecules for Ah-Level Aqueous Ammonium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.75494.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of most organic rechargeable batteries is strongly hindered by insufficient active site exposure arising from strong molecular stacking. To address this issue, an amorphization strategy is implemented to disrupt strong intermolecular π-π stacking in the small molecule 2,3,7,8-tetraamino-5,10-dihydrophenazine-1,4,6,9-tetraone (TDT), thereby improving electrolyte accessibility and activating buried redox sites. Amorphous TDT exhibits a high specific surface area of 738 m 2 g −1 , delivers 242.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and retains 87.1% of its initial capacity after 817 cycles over 2900 h. In situ ATR-FTIR and EQCM-D measurements reveal that NH 4 + is preferentially adsorbed and stored through coordination and deprotonation, while interfacial NH 4 + accumulation induces localized hydrolysis to generate H 3 O + for subsequent proton storage. The TDT||CuFe-PBA full cell retains 100% of its initial capacity over 100 000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Moreover, the first Ah-level AAIB pouch cell delivers 1.037 Ah at an average voltage of 1.14 V, demonstrating the practical promise of amorphous organic small molecule for durable, high capacity AAIBs.

10.1002/adma.75476.title: Grain-Boundary-Facilitated Palladium Hydride Formation Enables Humidity-Tolerant Catalytic Hydrogen Sensing
10.1002/adma.75476.abstract: ABSTRACT Reliable hydrogen sensing under high absolute humidity remains a significant challenge owing to the competitive adsorption of water molecules on the sensing material surface. Here, we report a humidity-tolerant catalytic H 2 sensor based on a grain-boundary-rich palladium nanostructure (Pd GB ) that operates without any external heating. The Pd GB sensor functions reliably at 22°C-80°C and 0%-90% relative humidity, achieving a lower limit of detection (LLOD) of 100 ppm even at 80°C and 90% relative humidity (261 g m −3 absolute humidity, corresponding to a > 3000-fold higher molar concentration of water vapor relative to the LLOD of H 2 ), while satisfying ISO 26142 requirements for gas sensing. A machine-learning regression model integrated into a sensor prototype enables robust, quantitative determination of H 2 concentration across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions. Mechanistic investigations combining in situ XRD, temperature-programmed desorption, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the exceptional humidity tolerance originates from the Pd grain boundaries, which accelerate PdH x formation for weakening H 2 O adsorption and suppress humidity-induced interference. These findings reveal a previously unexplored synergistic mechanism and establish a general materials-design strategy for next-generation humidity-tolerant catalytic gas sensors.

10.1002/adma.75483.title: Beyond State of Charge: Electrochemical States and Trajectory Design in Organic Mixed Conductors
10.1002/adma.75483.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic redox, ion transport, solvation, structural reorganization, and mechanics, enabling diverse electrochemical functions but making their internal states poorly represented by scalar descriptors such as voltage, charge, conductivity, or nominal doping level. This Review establishes a state-centered framework that treats electrochemical operation as the writing, observation, reconstruction, and design of multidimensional, history-dependent state trajectories. A problem-specific minimal sufficient state basis is introduced to distinguish essential from redundant coordinates, while waveform history and spatial heterogeneity define when lumped descriptions remain valid. Optical, electrical, ion-specific, gravimetric, structural, mechanical, and temporal readouts are analyzed as selective projections whose complementarity determines state observability and hidden-state reconstruction. Within this framework, congruence, kinetic ordering, decoupling, observational degeneracy, and mapping drift become experimentally testable relationships rather than isolated phenomena. Electrochromics, organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs), electrochemical memories, actuators, reconfigurable systems, and energy-storage and conversion devices are then recast as technologies that select different trajectories through a shared electrochemical-state landscape. The framework ultimately connects molecular structure, electrolyte, morphology, device architecture, and driving protocol to the inverse design of observable, controllable, reversible, and durable electrochemical trajectories.

10.1002/adma.74794.title: Room-Temperature Skyrmionic Synapse in 2D Ferromagnet Fe 3 GaTe 2 Operating via Collective Spin Texture Transformation (Adv. Mater. 49/2026)

10.1002/adma.74782.title: Electrolyte Engineering Challenges and Opportunities for Next-Generation Aqueous Ammonium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adma.74782.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (AAIBs) have emerged as a promising post-lithium energy-storage technology, combining intrinsic safety with sustainable viability. However, unlike other aqueous-ion batteries, the engineering of AAIB electrolytes confronts a fundamental dilemma: their unique hydrogen-bond (HB)-rich environment, which enabling ultrafast NH 4 + transport, concurrently exacerbates water decomposition and undermines electrolyte stability. In this review, we present the first comprehensive analysis of the dual role of HB networks in AAIB electrolytes and delineate their consequences for battery performance. We then systematically examine and evaluate the prevailing strategies devised to circumvent this dilemma, specifically anion engineering, salt-concentration tuning, pH regulation, organic co-solvent design, functional-additive introduction, and semi-solid electrolyte construction, while concurrently discussing their respective trade-offs and future outlook. Finally, we outline future directions involving coupled-reaction batteries, interfacial modeling, machine-learning-assisted electrolyte discovery, and sustainable ammonium sourcing. These insights provide a framework for balancing ion-transport kinetics and electrolyte stability in next-generation AAIBs.

10.1002/adma.75021.title: An Adaptive Hydrophobic Interphase for Sustainable Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
10.1002/adma.75021.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Zn metal batteries (AZMBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage, but their practical deployment is plagued by the issues of Zn anode involving non-uniform plating/stripping, H 2 evolution, and low Zn utilization rate (ZUR). Herein, we report an adaptive hydrophobic interphase enabled by the adsorption/desorption of organic imidazolium cations that circumvent these challenges. Mechanistic studies reveal that typical monovalent inorganic cations (i.e., Na + , NH 4 + ) with higher hydration energy show considerably weaker electrostatic adsorption at the Zn interface than the selected organic cations, attributed to the charge-screening effect of solvating-water. Among the selected organic cations, imidazolium species outperform quaternary ammonium cations in the interface adsorption, with longer alkyl chains further enhancing this effect. The exemplified 1-propyl-3-methylimidazolium (Pmim + ) cation creates a water-depleted electric double layer that suppresses interfacial side reactions and homogenizes Zn 2+ plating. Moreover, Pmim + undergoes electric-field-induced desorption that allows the involvement of H 2 O during Zn 2+ stripping. The resultant dynamic hydrophobic interphase sustains compact Zn deposition and uniform stripping even at 25 mAh cm −2 (85.9% ZUR). Consequently, the formulated Pmim + -containing electrolyte enables the Zn electrode with a prolonged cycling life of 6000 h at 1 mA cm −2 and robust deep-cycling performance, and supports stable operation of full AZMBs under harsh conditions.

10.1002/adma.75430.title: Synergistic Interaction Engineering Enables Homogeneous Mixed-Cation Perovskite Single Crystals for High-Performance X-Ray Detection
10.1002/adma.75430.abstract: ABSTRACT Mixed A-site compositions are an effective route to boost the x-ray detection performance of perovskite single crystals, yet their growth is often accompanied by pronounced spatial compositional inhomogeneity. This macroscopic phase segregation originates from mismatched formation energies and crystallization kinetics among the different cation components, leading to internal composition gradients that hinder carrier transport but are rarely addressed in perovskite single-crystal research. Here, we report an acetic acid-enabled synergistic interaction-engineering strategy for growing phase-homogeneous mixed-cation perovskite single crystals. Acetic acid simultaneously lowers the formation barrier of the formamidinium-rich phase and suppresses the rapid assembly of the methylammonium-rich phase, thereby balancing their crystallization rates and eliminating compositional gradients across the crystal. Owing to the improved uniformity and crystal quality, x-ray detectors based on these single crystals deliver a sensitivity of 3.54 × 10 6 µC Gy −1 cm −2 , a low detection limit of 2.65 nGy s −1 , and excellent operational stability. This kinetic-regulation concept offers a practical pathway to homogeneous mixed-cation perovskite single crystals and supports their use in low-dose, high-performance optoelectronic devices.

10.1002/adma.202522591.title: Shear Alignment Polymer Extrusion 3D Printing of High-Loading Nanocomposites With Long-Range Ordered Nanostructures
10.1002/adma.202522591.abstract: ABSTRACT Additive manufacturing has long struggled to bridge nanoscale functionalities with complex macroscale geometries, particularly for nanocomposites with high nanofiller loadings and ordered structures. Herein, we report shear alignment polymer extrusion (SHAPE) three-dimensional (3D) printing, a strategy that uses high shear forces to align highly loaded nanomaterials (e.g., boron nitride (BN) nanosheets and carbon nanotubes) along defined directions in polymer matrices, enabling the scalable fabrication of macroscopic nanocomposites with complex 3D architectures. A key advancement is the development of high-loading filaments (e.g., 55 wt% BN in polylactic acid) and a high-shear extrusion system, overcoming the traditional challenges of poor processability and structural integrity in high-filler composites. Post-sintering yields pure nanomaterial architectures that fully replicate the 3D printed geometry with zero volume shrinkage and exceptional thermomechanical stability-withstanding temperatures above the polymer melting and decomposition without structural failure. These materials exhibit tailored functionalities: vertically aligned BN composites show enhanced thermal conductivity (1.07 W/m/K); horizontally aligned BN structures offer efficient thermal insulation (0.071 W/m/K); and BN membranes display robust mechanical performance (a compressive strength of 3.4 MPa). Generalizable to diverse nanomaterials (0D to 2D), SHAPE opens new avenues for cross-scale design in thermal management, energy storage, and advanced structural materials.

10.1002/adma.74368.title: Multidimensional Symmetry Engineering of Metasurfaces for Circular Dichroism and Advanced Photonics
10.1002/adma.74368.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral metasurfaces provide a powerful artificial platform for manipulating the spin, phase, and amplitude of light at the subwavelength scale. The ability to generate strong circular dichroism (CD), optical activity, and spin-selective light-matter interaction creates new opportunities in chiral sensing, emission, and nonlinear photonics within flat optics. However, navigating the vast and complex geometric parameter space to maximize chiroptical responses remains a formidable challenge. To address this problem, we categorize the core design principles from the perspective of symmetry breaking including in-plane symmetry breaking, out-of-plane symmetry breaking, and low-symmetry lattice engineering. Furthermore, this review highlights the transformative role of machine learning and inverse design in overcoming the computational bottlenecks of traditional heuristic optimizations. We then review the practical applications of these chiral platforms across both linear and nonlinear regimes, focusing on imaging and holography, chiral sensing and polarization detection, circularly polarized light (CPL) emission, and advanced nonlinear chiral functionalities. Finally, major challenges and future research directions are outlined to guide the rational design and scalable implementation of chiral metasurfaces in next-generation photonic systems.

10.1002/adma.75084.title: Reconstruction-Induced Bilayered Amorphous-Crystalline Hybrid NiOOH-Based Anode for Ultrastable Seawater Electrolysis
10.1002/adma.75084.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct seawater electrolysis represents a critical pathway for large-scale utilization of renewable energy in coastal and island regions without potential impacts on freshwater supply, yet being severely hindered by the corrosion of electrode materials in seawater. Conventional anion-based protection strategies often suffer from lattice degradation during activation or anion desorption in operation. Herein, we report a facile electrodeposition-anodization synthesized amorphous-crystalline hybrid NiFeCoCr anode featuring a vertically bilayered architecture, enabling ultrastable seawater oxidation for over 15 000 h at 500 mA cm −2 . During anodization, the partial sacrificial leaching of Cr forms an amorphous β-NiOOH phase surface layer, exposing abundant active sites to enhance OER activity. Concurrently, in situ generated CrO 4 2- anions stably adsorb and intercalate within the dense crystalline Fe/Co-doped γ-NiOOH underneath layer. The electrolyzer assembled with the NiFeCoCr anode delivers stable operation for over 2500 h in alkaline natural seawater and for 240 h in alkaline saturated NaCl electrolyte at 80°C.

10.1002/adma.75504.title: 3D Ordered Macroporous Cu-Based Multimetallic Alloy Enables Efficient Asymmetric C-C Coupling for Selective CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
10.1002/adma.75504.abstract: ABSTRACT The abundant Cu 0 /Cu δ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C-C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO x . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO 2 reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In-situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu δ+ (0<δ<1) sites at multimetallic interfaces is effectively regulated by other metals, inducing electronic heterogeneity and an asymmetric charge distribution on the Cu sites that facilitates asymmetric *CO-*CHO coupling. This work establishes the design principles for Cu-based multimetallic alloy with atomic-level customisation, demonstrating that the precise structural design and electronic structure of Cu δ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.

10.1002/adma.75482.title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low-Cost Solar Fuels
10.1002/adma.75482.abstract: ABSTRACT Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field-scale NP typically operates at sub-percent solar-to-biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double-digit solar-to-fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar-to-chemical conversion.

10.1002/adma.75495.title: Anti-Poisoning Tin Single-Atom Unlocks High-Activity Ruthenium Catalysts for Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
10.1002/adma.75495.abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) is constrained by the lack of efficient electrocatalysts for the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), primarily due tothe sluggishVolmer step and inefficient intermediate desorption. While Ru-based catalysts exhibit promising *H binding energy, their practical performance is compromised by poor water dissociation kinetics and susceptibility to active-site blockage by adsorbed species. Herein, we report a Sn-doped RuO 2 @Ru catalyst supported on carbon black, wherein atomically dispersed Sn modulates the electronic structure of RuO 2 via Sn─O bonds, simultaneously facilitating water dissociation, optimizing *H adsorption, and preventing *OH poisoning. The catalyst achieves exceptional performance with an overpotential of 9 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , positioning it among the most active HER catalysts reported to date. When integrated into a full AEMWE, it operates at 1.85 V and 1000 mA cm −2 with stability exceeding 300 h. Mechanistic studies suggest that Sn doping fine-tunes the *OH and *H binding energies, addressing the kinetic imbalance inherent in conventional Ru catalysts. This work highlights the effectiveness of atomic-level electronic engineering via an anti-poisoning strategy for designing efficient, stable alkaline HER electrocatalysts toward industrial hydrogen production.

10.1002/adma.75489.title: Engineering Thermoelectric-Electrocatalytic Coupling in RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 Heterointerface for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adma.75489.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is pivotal for diverse electrochemical energy conversion systems; however, it has so far been plagued by sluggish kinetics and excessive energy consumption. In this study, we proposed an innovative thermoelectric-electrocatalytic coupling strategy to enhance OER efficiency by constructing an Ohmic heterointerface through uniform integration of RuO 2 with thermoelectric oxide (PrCoO 3 ). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses revealed that the thermoelectric potential generated by PrCoO 3 selectively activates the intrinsically inert (101) facet of RuO 2 by lowering *OOH formation barrier, thereby substantially boosting the overall OER performance. Consequently, the RuO 2 /PrCoO 3 heterointerface delivered exceptional OER performance under a mild temperature gradient (Δ T ) of 175°C, achieving dramatic reduction in overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 from 300 mV (Δ T = 0°C) to 178 mV, 4 300% increase in current density, and negligible potential loss over 1,000 h. When the catalyst was assembled into an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer, the cell driven by spontaneous heating reached a low voltage of 2.18 V at a current density of 2.0 A cm −2 , with stable operation for 600 h. These insights into harnessing thermal gradient via integrated electrocatalytic system are crucial for the recovery of industrial waste heat and its conversion into high-value chemicals.

10.1002/adma.75118.title: Programmable Engineered Living Vehicles as Autonomous Biofactories for Synergistic Osteomyelitis Management and Bone Regeneration
10.1002/adma.75118.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional static biomaterials and synthetic nanomedicines struggle to penetrate recalcitrant biofilms and orchestrate tissue regeneration in deep-seated infections due to limited autonomous navigation and a lack of spatiotemporal responsiveness. Here, we conceptualize and develop a programmable engineered living vehicle (ELV) that functions as an autonomous biofactory for the synergistic management of drug-resistant osteomyelitis. Built upon a self-propelled Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 chassis with innate ecological dominance, these living biofactories are hierarchically equipped with environmental biosensors and logic-gated computing modules. Crucially, leveraging AlphaFold 3-guided molecular docking, we engineered multiscale thermo-responsive genetic logic circuits that enable precise, temperature-dependent biomanufacturing of bacteriolytic lysostaphin (LYS) and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) (≥37°C), coupled with a fail-safe thermal self-destruct mechanism (≥42°C). Furthermore, surface-engineered (DSS) 6 peptides confer robust hydroxyapatite affinity, acting as a bone-homing navigation module. In a rat osteomyelitis model induced by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), intravenously deployed ELV biofactories autonomously navigate to the infected niche, actively penetrate biofilms, and outperform vancomycin in pathogen clearance. Concurrently, localized payload secretion reprograms the osteo-immune microenvironment, significantly accelerating bone repair. This work establishes a versatile paradigm for next-generation smart living therapeutics, bridging synthetic biology with micro-engineering to address complex clinical challenges.

10.1002/adma.75512.title: Lewis-Basic Metal Sulfide Electrode Interfaces Unlock High Power Density Alkaline All-Iron Redox Flow Batteries
10.1002/adma.75512.abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline all-iron redox flow batteries (AIRFBs) are promising for safe, low-cost grid-scale energy storage using Earth-abundant elements. However, insufficient energy efficiency and power density limit practical deployment, while the interfacial kinetic origin of these losses remains unclear. Here, we identify sluggish outer-sphere electron-transfer kinetics of Fe-chelate anolytes as a key kinetic bottleneck governing polarization in alkaline AIRFBs and further link this bottleneck to limited outer Helmholtz plane (OHP)-region accessibility and weak interfacial electronic coupling. To overcome this limitation, we develop Lewis-basic sulfide interfaces that regulate the local Fe-chelate/electrode environment. These regulated interfaces convert inefficient diffusion encounters into productive sulfide-assisted outer-sphere electron-transfer events, thereby accelerating anolyte redox kinetics and suppressing polarization. An alkaline AIRFB assembled with a Ni 3 S 4 -modified electrode delivers an energy efficiency of 80.65% at 200 mA cm −2 and a peak power density of 501.2 mW cm −2 , compared with 65.69% and 185.5 mW cm −2 for the pristine cell. The Ni 3 S 4 -based cell further maintains an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.9%, an average energy efficiency of 77.8%, and stable operation over 3000 cycles at 200 mA cm −2 . This work reveals an interfacial kinetic bottleneck in alkaline AIRFBs and establishes Lewis-basic interface engineering as a strategy for high-power and low-cost long-duration energy storage.

10.1002/adma.75429.title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large-Area Tin-based Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adma.75429.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin-based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p-type small molecule, 4,4'-(5,6-bis(2-methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole-4,7-diyl)bis(2,5-difluoro-N,N-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic-angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H- 1 H double-quantum-single-quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning-rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high-quality Sn-based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap-assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG-PEDOT:PSS-based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1-cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04-cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.

10.1002/adma.75517.title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard-Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion-Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
10.1002/adma.75517.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard-carbon anode design lacks a precursor-level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed-pore formation. Here we establish a precursor-level cohesion-solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene-fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke-like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard-carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect-engineered carbon galleries. The solvent-selected AHC-80-1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide-temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10-kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC-80-1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle-to-gate life-cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC-80-1400 production reduces climate-change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor-stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

10.1002/adma.75487.title: Stabilizing Ru Sites via Lattice Oxygen Locking of Nb-Ru/RuO 2 to Break the Activity-Stability Trade-Off for Acidic Oxygen Evolution
10.1002/adma.75487.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly active and stable Ru-based catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential to accelerate the industrialization of proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). However, Ru-based catalysts inevitably follow the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM) during the actual reaction, which in turn triggers severe Ru dissolution. While shifting the reaction pathway to the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) improves stability, it often compromises catalytic activity. Herein, we design an Nb-doped Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure catalyst to inhibit the unstable LOM, and concurrently propose a favorable Brønsted Site-Promoted Proton Transfer (BSPT) mechanism derived from the AEM. Specifically, the synergy between Nb doping and Ru/RuO 2 heterostructure enhances activity by improving deprotonation capability and optimizing oxygen-intermediate adsorption, while simultaneously improving durability by stabilizing lattice oxygen and suppressing excessive oxidation and dissolution of Ru. Consequently, the Nb-Ru/RuO 2 delivers an overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm −2 with impressive durability over 3000 h. In a working PEMWE, it exhibits remarkable durability for 3000, 1200, and 900 h at 500, 1000, and 2000 mA cm −2 . This study offers novel design principles and theoretical foundations to advance efficient, low-cost PEMWE hydrogen production.

10.1002/adma.75522.title: A Glycan Key Unlocks Microglia Targeting and Reprogramming to Promote Functional Recovery After Spinal Cord Injury
10.1002/adma.75522.abstract: ABSTRACT Spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers uncontrolled neuroinflammation driven by dysfunctional microglia and pro-inflammatory-biased reprogramming, yet precise therapeutic strategies remain limited. Here, we report a novel glycan-targeted nanoparticle system (ICT@APD) designed to enhance the microglia-reprogramming potential of icaritin (ICT) while overcoming its inherent narrow therapeutic window. By functionalizing nanoparticles with 2,5-anhydro-D-mannitol (2,5-AM), a high-affinity ligand for the microglia-specific transporter GLUT5, ICT@APD achieves selective microglial uptake and amplifies the capacity of ICT to reprogram microglia toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype. The targeted reprogramming consequently creates a positive microenvironment that promotes axon regeneration, neuronal survival, and synaptic reconstruction, leading to significantly improved locomotor recovery after SCI. Our findings establish a novel glycan-mediated microglial targeting and reprogramming strategy for SCI repair, which may extend to other central nervous system disorders and provide a referenceable platform for the delivery of other therapeutic agents with a narrow therapeutic window.

10.1002/adma.75496.title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal-Organic Network for CO 2 Conversion
10.1002/adma.75496.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous-phase synthesis of a woven metal-organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6-trinitrobenzene-1,3,5-triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one-dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two-dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π-conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox-active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu-TNPG network was evaluated for visible-light-driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu-TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre-activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

10.1002/adma.75539.title: Threo-Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adma.75539.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo-chiral cation additive of (2 S ,3 R )-2-amino-3-hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl-induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral-center threo-configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically-favored parallel-to-lattice multi-site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective “lock-and-key” interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm 2 large-area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS-D-2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high-efficiency and ultra-stable perovskite photovoltaics.
