This specific interaction effectively activates the Li─S bond and substantially lowers the thermodynamic energy barriers, thereby improving the redox kinetics of polysulfide conversion. Consequently, the assembled Li-S batteries maintain a reversible capacity of 658 mAh g −1 at a high rate of 4 C and exhibit stable long cycling performance. Furthermore, the assembled 14 Ah-level pouch cell achieves an initial energy density of 547 Wh kg −1 and over 30 stable cycles. This work provides a practical approach for preparing cost-effective and efficient single-atom catalysts, supporting the industrial application of high-energy-density Li-S batteries.

10.1002/aenm.71380.title: Breaking the Polarity-Coordination Coupling in Electrolyte Design for High-Voltage Lithium Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71380.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte design is fundamentally constrained by the trade-off between high solvent polarity and weak Li + solvation, as polar solvents typically bind Li + strongly. Here, we establish a steric-electronic modulation strategy that decouples solvent polarity from Li + coordination, enabling a generalizable pseudo-weak solvation electrolyte design paradigm. Based on this principle, a steric hindrance-mediated electrolyte is developed combining 2,2,2-trifluoro-N, N-dimethylethylamide (DMTFA) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) with dual lithium salts. Despite its strong polarity, DMTFA exhibits weak Li + coordination due to the combined steric hindrance and electron-withdrawing effects of the -CF 3 group, enabling anion- dominated solvation structures. This coordination chemistry lowers Li + desolvation barriers and drives the preferential adsorption of a B- and P-rich interphase layer at the cathode surface, thereby protecting the cathode from HF corrosion. The resulting electrolyte achieves high ionic conductivity, intrinsic flame retardancy, and an electrochemical stability window exceeding 5.0 V. Cells employing LiNi 0.91 Co 0.06 Mn 0.03 O 2 cathodes demonstrate a capacity retention of over 90.0% after 100 cycles at 1 C rate and 4.8 V charge cut-off. The electrolyte enables approximately 1.6 Ah pouch cells to retain 84.97% capacity after 1800 cycles at 4.6 V.

10.1002/aenm.71304.title: Electrochemically Driven Refrigeration Based on Dissolution-Crystallization Cycle of Redox-Active Salts
authors: Yifan Zhang, Pei Liu, Yilin Zeng, Xuan Cai, Linfeng Wang, Huaiyu Ke, Xue Long, Hua Jiang, Wendong Yang, Zuoxuan Gan, Jiabao Sun, Jia Li, Jiangjiang Duan

10.1002/aenm.71352.title: Wide-Stable Dynamics Enabling Ultra-High Power Density in Compact Magneto-Mechano-Electric Energy Harvesters for Self-Powered Smart Grid Monitoring
10.1002/aenm.71352.abstract: ABSTRACT Cantilever-structured magneto-mechano-electric energy harvesters (MME-EHs) are considered as one of promising candidates for powering Internet of Things (IoT) devices by capturing ambient magnetic fields. However, conventional MME-EHs with volumes comparable to button cell batteries (≤1 cm 3 ) face a critical challenge in overcoming the output power density bottleneck to meet advancing IoT demands under weak excitations. In this work, we overcome this limitation by proposing a wide-stable energy harvesting strategy. Unlike conventional bistable systems that struggle to sustain high-energy interwell oscillations under weak excitations, or monostable systems restricted by steep potential wells, our design leverages nonlinear dynamics to engineer a broadened and flattened potential well that facilitates large-amplitude intrawell motion even under weak fields. This strategy significantly enhances magneto-mechanical coupling efficiency, enabling a compact MME-EH (effective volume 0.968 cm 3 ) to generate 0.89 mW output power under a weak magnetic field of 1 Oe at 50 Hz, representing an 89% enhancement over the original MME-EH. The output power density reaches 0.92 mW cm −3 Oe −2 , revealing a 26% improvement compared to state-of-the-art performance. Its potential for practical application is validated via a self-powered wireless sensor network (WSN) for grid monitoring and fire alarms, paving the way for maintenance-free, wide-area distributed WSNs.

10.1002/aenm.71634.title: Anion-Driven Solvent Degradation Networks in High-Concentration Battery Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71634.abstract: ABSTRACT High-concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion-mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion-mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride () and fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open-ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro-organic species. These results provide a molecular-level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion-solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.
authors: Esra Ulgey Akgun, Brett M. Savoie

10.1002/aenm.71701.title: Near-Micron Single-Crystalline Mn-Rich Cathodes With Exceptional Cycling Stability
10.1002/aenm.71701.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high-energy-density and long-term cycling stability in Mn-redox-based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni- and Co-free Li-ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn-redox cathodes using near-micron single-crystalline δ-phase cation-disordered rocksalt (δ-DRX), derived from Mn-rich DRX, delivering ≈640 Wh kg −1 with ≈97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to suppress oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high-throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase-pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO 2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high-temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high-temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single-crystalline Mn-rich DRX particles to the near-micron regime (D50 = 1.5 µm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle-size control in Mn-rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ-DRX as a stable, sustainable, high-performance, Ni- and Co-free cathode material.
authors: Eunryeol Lee, Tucker Holstun, Tara Mishra, Maciej Moździerz, Shilong Wang, Yanbao Fu, Peter Ercius, Alexander Pattison, Satoshi Hiroi, Koji Ohara, Vincent Battaglia, Haegyeom Kim, Akira Miura, Gerbrand Ceder

10.1002/aenm.71711.title: Interfacial Dipole Reorganization Enables Ultrafast Sodium Storage in Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71711.abstract: ABSTRACT As a promising cathode material for large-scale sodium-ion energy storage, Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na + kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk-to-interface coupling framework in which substitution-induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni 2 + with high crystal-field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni 2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d-p hybridization, and promotes medium-range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na-ClO 4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na + exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full-cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode-electrolyte interactions.
authors: Yuhang Xin, Hexiao Zhang, Kunyu Zhao, Yingshuai Wang, Qingbo Zhou, Yonghao Liu, Runqing Ou, Qianchen Wang, Hongcai Gao

10.1002/aenm.71699.title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3-Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71699.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium-ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid-state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low-melting-point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid-like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM-A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM-O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM-A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM-A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM-O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.
authors: Qian Li, Changyan Hu, Huan Yang, Haoyu Li, Waiqiao Li, Ruoyang Wang, Guanlin Lv, Peidong Li, Zhenguo Wu, Xiaodong Guo

10.1002/aenm.71709.title: Efficient Cascade Abiotic Synthesis of Sugar From CO2
10.1002/aenm.71709.abstract: ABSTRACT The capability of producing sugar compounds from carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), ideally based on abiotic systems, suggests an artificial, scalable strategy to provide potential solutions for both food and environmental issues. In this work, we report an inorganic, abiotic pathway for the synthesis of sugar from CO 2 without any enzymatic or biological components, comprising several electrocatalytic-catalytic cascade reactions. CO 2 is first electrochemically reduced to ethylene (C 2 H 4 ) on a Cu catalyst, and then oxidized to ethylene glycol by hydrogen peroxide in situ generated from the O 2 reduction. Ethylene glycol is further oxidized into glycolaldehyde on a platinum catalyst, and the overall CO 2 -to-glycolaldehyde Faradaic efficiency (FE) reaches ≈ 15.9%. Finally, the as-formed glycolaldehyde is coupled into C 6+ sugar compounds (i.e., higher-carbon carbohydrates products) via the Formose reaction, obviating the need to use biochemical/enzymatic reactions or any additional carbon-based molecules. Using this cascade reaction, we demonstrated an efficient CO 2 -to-sugar production rate of 2.1 g per day with a total carbon selectivity of 25.9%, featuring an attractive approach for producing sugars from CO 2 by renewable electricity.
authors: Ruilin Wei, Yuhang Huang, Lu Song, Maoyin Wang, Haoran Ma, Ximeng Lv, Boyu Hou, Jun Wen, Shuya Hao, Gengfeng Zheng

10.1002/aenm.71569.title: Deep Neural Network-Driven Development of Coking- and Sulfur-Resistant Nanostructured NiGa Alloy-Based Anodes for Solid Oxide Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71569.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) that directly convert natural gas into electricity are promising high-efficiency energy-conversion devices, yet conventional Ni-based anodes suffer from severe carbon deposition and sulfur poisoning, leading to rapid electrode deactivation. Although binary alloying effectively regulates surface reaction pathways and improves anode stability, its development largely relies on experience-driven trial-and-error screening. Here, we propose a rational screening framework that integrates microkinetic analysis with deep neural networks to identify the Ni-Ga alloy from a vast binary alloy chemical space. Density functional theory confirms that such a Ni-Ga alloy combines efficient methane activation with intrinsic resistance to carbon deposition. Guided by these predictions, we further construct a nanocomposite electrode with Gd 0.1 Ce 0.9 O 1.95 (GDC)-encapsulated Ni-Ga alloys (NiGa-GDC). Benefiting from alloy-induced electronic structure modulation and a nanocomposite electrode architecture, the NiGa-GDC nanocomposite anode exhibits exceptional electrochemical performance and coking resistance. In nearly dry methane fuel (3% H 2 O), a corresponding electrolyte-supported single cell achieves both high peak power density and durable operation, far outperforming the counterpart Ni-GDC nanocomposite anode. Moreover, the NiGa-GDC anode demonstrates remarkable resistance to sulfur poisoning. This study provides a new strategy for developing highly active and durable nickel-based nanocomposite anodes for the direct utilization of natural gas.

10.1002/aenm.71715.title: Disrupting Solvent Self-Association via Dipole-Dipole Interactions for Improved Performance of Perovskite Solar Cell
10.1002/aenm.71715.abstract: ABSTRACT High-quality perovskite films demand strongly coordinating solvents (SCS, e.g., DMSO, NMP) for crystal growth regulation, yet such solvents often leave residue and induce notorious voids. Prior work elucidated the voids distribution along the vertical direction but cannot explain their lateral dimensions and spatial patterning. Here, we find that the hundreds-of-nanometer lateral dimension and clustered morphology of buried voids originate from the self-association of SCS. The tailored-made 1-bromo-4-dimethylphosphoryl-benzene (BPPO) with inherently weak intermolecular interaction is introduced, which mainly exists in a monomeric form and can efficiently modify the buried interface by constructing dipole-dipole interactions with SCS. The self-association is disrupted, enabling uniform SCS distribution rather than forming big cluster, which accelerates the escape and ultimately eliminates voids at the buried interface. Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on BPPO show an efficiency increase from 25.2% to 27.2% (certified efficiency of 27.0%, aperture area of 0.0712 cm 2 ), with improved stability under ISOS-D-2 and ISOS-L-2 protocols. Furthermore, the BPPO-modified perovskite solar module (PSMs, aperture area of 17.4 cm 2 ) achieved an efficiency of 24.2%, demonstrating its excellent scalability.
authors: Yuqi Du, Wenxiang Xiang, Jiahui Li, Shanwen Wang, Jing Chen, Zhaokui Wang, Geping Qu, Zong-Xiang Xu, Xiangqian Shen, Liyuan Han, Yanbo Wang

10.1002/aenm.71697.title: Electrochemical and Mechanical Understanding of Extruded and Solvent-Cast Solid Polymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71697.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on Poly(ethylene oxide)-Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PEO-LiTFSI) are promising materials for solid-state batteries. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted on their electrochemical and mechanical properties, with SPEs prepared via two processing methods: extrusion and solvent casting. The effects of Al 2 O 3 addition and membrane thickness on SPE performance and cyclability were investigated. Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al 2 O 3 improved membrane stability. Thicker membranes exhibited larger polarization gradients, slower ion diffusion, and lower Sand times, leading to reduced electrochemical performance. Mechanical properties, including yield stress, storage modulus, and fracture toughness, were assessed using rheology and dynamic mechanical analysis. Extruded SPEs displayed higher stiffness and greater resistance to dendrite formation than solvent-cast membranes. Monotonic crack growth tests indicated that the presence of Al 2 O 3 increased fracture toughness, enhancing crack resistance and potentially extending cycle life. Overall, membranes produced via extrusion, containing Al 2 O 3 , and optimized for reduced thickness, combined superior electrochemical properties, making them strong candidates for solid-state battery applications, as demonstrated by their incorporation in multilayer cells.
authors: Elene Sasieta-Barrutia, June Blanco, Laida Otaegui, Aizeti Burgoa, Mikel Isasi, Michel Armand, Rikardo Hernandez, Aitor Villaverde, Maria C. Morant-Miñana

10.1002/aenm.71712.title: Selective Interfacial Coupling in Polymer Electrolytes Stabilizes High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes for > 500 Wh Kg−1 Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71712.abstract: ABSTRACT The interfacial chemistry of high-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is strongly governed by electronic coupling between electrolyte components and cathode surfaces. However, current strategies generally regulate coupling as an overall interaction-strength issue, overlooking the distinct contributions of individual electrolyte species and thereby limiting precise interfacial control. Here, we propose a selective interfacial coupling strategy by constructing an interfacial architecture comprising a coupling center and a weak-coupling environment. Specifically, 2-cyanoethyl acrylate (CA) acts as the coupling center, while a highly fluorinated acrylate (DFA) creates the weak-coupling environment. Their synergy reconstructs the interfacial molecular organization, suppresses undesirable coupling from non-target species, and preserves favorable CA-cathode interactions. Multiscale calculations and operando spectroscopy reveal the reconstructed interfacial structure and its dynamic evolution. The resulting enlarged Ni 3d-O 2p band-center separation stabilizes the TM-O electronic structure, suppressing lattice oxygen release, cation mixing, and transition-metal dissolution. Consequently, Li||Ni90 cells retain 78% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.7 V, while a 5 Ah pouch cell delivers 529.4 Wh kg −1 at 4.6 V. This work establishes selective interfacial coupling as an effective strategy for regulating high-voltage interfaces.
authors: Zixuan Wang, Zunbin Mao, Lu Wei, Zhuo Li, Xin Guo

10.1002/aenm.71704.title: Coupling Interfacial Defect Regulation With Lattice Relaxation in FACsPbI3 Perovskite
10.1002/aenm.71704.abstract: ABSTRACT FACsPbI 3 perovskites, free of volatile methylammonium and mixed halides, are among promising absorbers for efficient optoelectronics owing to their favourable bandgap and intrinsic stability. However, the structurally soft lattice makes their surfaces prone to distortion and defect generation, creating a heterogeneous interfacial energy landscape that promotes non-radiative recombination and ion migration. Here, we report an interfacial regulation strategy that stabilizes the surface/interface configuration of FACsPbI 3 through a defect-lattice coupling mechanism. Introducing morpholinium chloride at the FACsPbI 3 interface/surface enables coordination with undercoordinated lattice sites, thereby relieving local lattice strain, stabilizing surface Pb-I octahedral network, and reducing the density of defect states. This coupling between interfacial chemistry and lattice energetics increases vacancy formation energies, homogenizes the interfacial electronic environment, and suppresses defect-assisted recombination and ion migration. The resulting perovskite solar cells yield an efficiency of 26.67% with a 16.1 cm 2 -aperture mini-module reaching an efficiency of 22.79%. Moreover, the devices exhibit enhanced stability, retaining 95.8% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous operation. This work reveals a defect-lattice coupling paradigm that links interfacial chemistry, lattice energetics, and ion migration kinetics, offering a general route toward stable and high-efficiency soft ionic semiconductors.
authors: Hongshen Xie, Hanguang Fu, Tianchi Zhang, Yehui Wen, Wenbin Han, Biao Li, Xuegong Yu, Deren Yang, Yong Wang

10.1002/aenm.71707.title: Asymmetric C-C Coupling Driven by Heterostructured Ag-Bi Electrocatalyst Enables Selective CO2 Reduction to Ethanol for Microbial Growth
10.1002/aenm.71707.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (eCO 2 RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C 1 byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long-term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag-Bi electrocatalyst (Ag 1.65 @Bi 2 O 3 ) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C-C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO 2 to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at -0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C-C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by Saccharomyces cerevisiae in an integrated electrochemical-microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L −1 , which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO 2 RR and microbial fermentation.
authors: Zexin Xu, Miao Liu, Yanfeng Shi, Fei Li, Jin Liu, Yuanhong Xu

10.1002/aenm.71716.title: Ligand Electronics and Metal-Site Acidity Enable High-Voltage MOF Electrolytes for Quasi-Solid-State Lithium-Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71716.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) coupled with Ni-rich cathodes offer high energy density for next-generation energy storage. Their practical implementation, however, is limited by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial degradation under high voltage. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) would regulate ion solvation and stabilize electrode-electrolyte interfaces in quasi-solid-state electrolytes, yet the molecular origins of their oxidation stability remain unclear. Here, we identify ligand electronics and metal-site acidity as key descriptors for high-voltage-stable MOF electrolytes. Electron-withdrawing ligands lower the HOMO energy levels of MOFs, while hard Lewis-acidic Al sites further enhance oxidation resistance. Guided by this principle, we design a perfluorinated Al-based MOF, Al-FBDC, featuring a high oxidation onset potential of 4.82 V (vs. Li + /Li). Incorporating Al-FBDC into a composite cathode reconstructs the local electrolyte environment at particle-level interfaces, thereby suppressing parasitic reactions and cathode degradation under high-voltage operation. As a result, Li||Al-FBDC@NCM quasi-solid-state cells deliver excellent long-term cycling stability and rate performance, retaining 82% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C over 3.0-4.5 V, while maintaining robust performance even at 4.6 and 4.8 V cut-off voltages and with controlled electrolyte loading. This work identifies a general design principle for high-voltage-stable MOF electrolytes and offers a practical route toward high-energy-density LMBs.
authors: Yuzhu Tian, Yifei Xu, Kang Liang, Tianqi Deng, Wei Zhao, Qinghe Wang, Yurong Ren, Hao Bin Wu

10.1002/aenm.71713.title: Engineering Advanced Electrocatalysts for Energy-Saving Zinc−Air Hybrid Batteries: Concurrent Energy Storage Coupled With Chemical Upgrading
10.1002/aenm.71713.abstract: ABSTRACT Additive-assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries (ZAHBs) that couple favorable additive oxidation with oxygen reduction represent ideal energy storage candidates, distinguished by high theoretical energy density, reduced charging voltage, and functionality for electrochemical upgrading of organics or wastewater. Herein, a critical overview of ZAHBs is provided, commencing with the fundamental electrochemistry (including advantages, working mechanisms, cell configurations, and evaluation parameters) and the selection criteria for small-molecule additives (including theoretical potential, solubility, stability, toxicity, and volatility). We then summarize recent progress in three categories of ZAHBs (i.e., wastewater-purified, value-added, and redox-mediated), discussing alternative anodic oxidation reactions (e.g., alcohol, urea, hydrazine, and iodine oxidation) coupled with cathodic oxygen reduction, along with the underlying catalytic mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on catalyst design strategies spanning electronic (ligand engineering, heteroatom doping, electron delocalization, orbital hybridization, and built-in electric field), geometric (defect engineering, curvature engineering, and nano-confinement effect), and interfacial (high-energy interface, heterostructure, interfacial microenvironment, and core-shell structure) modulations. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future perspectives for advancing ZAHBs. This review offers valuable guidance for the rational design and practical deployment of next-generation energy devices.
authors: Xian-Wei Lv, Tao Meng, Mengyue Zhang, Xiaodong Meng, Zhongli Wang, Xuhuan Yan, Zhong-Yong Yuan, Jianxin Geng

10.1002/aenm.71719.title: High-Energy and Long-Life Na3V2(PO4)2F3 Cathodes via Multielement V-Site Modulation of Local M-O/F Bonding
10.1002/aenm.71719.abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium-ion batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage, but their energy density still lags behind lithium-ion systems. Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) is an attractive high-voltage polyanionic cathode, but fluorine loss generates low-voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 impurities that lower energy density and aggravate lattice deformation during cycling. Here, we report a multielement V-site charge modulation strategy, realized in Na 3-δ V 1.9 Zr 0.02 Ti 0.02 Cr 0.02 Fe 0.02 Al 0.02 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (ME-NVPF). The deliberate combination of high-valence Zr 4+ , Ti 4+ , and same-valence Cr 3+ , Fe 3+ , Al 3+ cations creates a heterogeneous M-O/F bonding network with multi-directional electrostatic interactions enhancing lattice-F retention that completely eliminates NVP impurities, lowers the Na + migration barrier, and reduces unit-cell volume variation to merely 2.87%. Consequently, ME-NVPF delivers a record-high energy density of 477 Wh kg −1 , sustains 11 000 cycles, operates across −40 to 80°C, and is further validated in 600 mAh-level pouch cells. This work establishes multielement compositional regulation as an effective strategy for designing high-energy, long-life, and all-temperature polyanionic cathodes.
authors: Zhichao Li, Fuqiang Li, Mushun Chen, Yanyu Sun, Shouyu Sun, Zifei Shi, Cheng Yang, Yu Liu

10.1002/aenm.71698.title: Site-Selectively Engineered MoS2/ReS2 Heterostructures for High-Performance Supercapacitors
10.1002/aenm.71698.abstract: ABSTRACT Layered MoS 2 holds great potential for supercapacitors; however, its intrinsically low electrical conductivity, sluggish electrochemical kinetics, and susceptibility to Mo dissolution severely hamper its electrochemical performance. Here, we propose a selective-doping-coupled heterostructure engineering strategy, in which atomic Fe preferentially incorporates into the MoS 2 domain, while the local structure of the ReS 2 component remains largely preserved, forming an Fe-doped MoS 2 /ReS 2 (Fe-MRS) heterostructure. Theoretical and experimental results reveal the formation of a built-in electric field at the Fe-MRS interface, driving electron transfer from ReS 2 to Fe-doped MoS 2 , reconfiguring the Mo-S electronic structure, while simultaneously strengthening Mo─S bonds and suppressing Mo dissolution. Moreover, Fe incorporation is energetically favored at octahedrally coordinated Mo sites within the MoS 2 domain, modulating the local electronic environment of the MoS 2 domain and thereby facilitating coupled electron/ion transport. Consequently, the Fe-MRS electrode delivers high specific capacitance and excellent cycling stability with a capacitance retention of 97.0% over 5000 cycles. Moreover, asymmetric supercapacitors assembled with the Fe-MRS anode achieve a high energy density of 55.2 Wh kg −1 at 1000 W kg −1 , maintaining good structural and mechanical robustness. This work offers clear guidance for leveraging selective doping to engineer heterostructures with enhanced electron-ion coupling for advanced electrochemical energy storage systems.
authors: Haodong Bi, Huilin Zhang, Jisong Hu, Ling Kang, Yusuke Yamauchi, Bin Ding, Shude Liu

10.1002/aenm.71714.title: Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges
10.1002/aenm.71714.abstract: ABSTRACT Designing high-performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade-offs. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial-and-error approaches. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) are transforming electrolyte research into a data-driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi-objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism-informed and transferable ML frameworks. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next-generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high-performance rechargeable batteries.
authors: Qianqian Liu, Chaojie Wang, Zeyi Zhang, Ming Xiao, Xiaokai Hao, Kunzhe Wang, Liguang Wang

10.1002/aenm.71708.title: Covalently Locked Donor-Acceptor Block Copolymer Nanoparticles Enable Efficient, Stable and Reproducible Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/aenm.71708.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all-conjugated donor-acceptor block copolymer, PBDB-T- b -PYT, in which covalent linkage between PBDB-T and PYT segments constrains nanoscale donor-acceptor organization and promotes intramolecular charge transfer. Compared with nanoparticles prepared from a physical PBDB-T:PYT blend, PBDB-T- b -PYT nanoparticles exhibit stronger photoluminescence quenching, more persistent charge-associated transient absorption features, and improved photoelectrochemical charge extraction. As a result, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) rates exceeding 120 mmol cm −2 g −1 h −1 (>450 µmol h −1 ) are achieved with low Pt loading (<3 wt.%). PBDB-T- b -PYT NPs retained 95% of the initial HER rate after 96 h of photocatalysis. Conversely, NPs prepared from physically mixed PBDB-T and PYT show lower activity and faster deactivation, consistent with morphology-driven losses. PBDB-T- b -PYT also maintains high performance across polymer batches, improving reproducibility. These results establish all-conjugated donor-acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

10.1002/aenm.71722.title: Synergy Between Controllable Sulfur Defect and NiS Cocatalyst Enabling Efficient Photoredox Coupling Catalysis
10.1002/aenm.71722.abstract: ABSTRACT Semiconductor-based photoredox coupling of selective oxidation of vanillyl alcohol (VOL) to vanillin (VAL) with H 2 evolution provides a sustainable alternative to conventional industrial VAL synthesis processes, yet its performance is often hindered by rapid charge recombination and insufficient active sites. Herein, we report a facile one-pot hydrothermal strategy to construct NiS-decorated Zn 3 In 2 S 6 (ZIS) nanoflowers with controllable sulfur vacancies (V S ) for efficient co-production of VAL and H 2 . Moderate concentrations of V S regulate the surface electronic structure and act as oxidation active sites to optimize VOL adsorption. Meanwhile, uniformly dispersed NiS cocatalysts serve as efficient electron relays and reduction active sites, accelerating charge migration and promoting H 2 generation. Benefiting from the interfacial synergy between V S and NiS, the optimal 1%NiS-ZIS-V S2 catalyst delivers an 18-fold enhancement in both VAL and H 2 production rates relative to pristine ZIS, together with excellent stability and broad substrate versatility. This work highlights the critical role of defect-cocatalyst synergy in designing advanced cooperative photoredox catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis.
authors: Chang-Long Tan, Bo Shen, Xiang Lan, Ming-Yu Qi, Zi-Rong Tang, Yi-Jun Xu

10.1002/aenm.71427.title: Multifunctional Diluent Enables High-Voltage and Flame-Retardant Potassium-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71427.abstract: ABSTRACT Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) emerge as a highly promising candidate system in large-scale energy storage, owing to their abundant resources, low cost, and potentially high operating voltage. However, the current development of PIBs still faces core bottlenecks such as unstable electrode-electrolyte interphase (EEI) at high voltages and flammability of electrolytes. Herein, a multifunctional solvent of ethoxy(pentafluoro)cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN) is used as the flame retardant, diluent, and interface regulator to design a non-flammable localized high-concentration electrolyte. Crucially, the introduction of PFPN (intrinsic flame retardant) not only significantly enhances the proportion of solvation structure of contact ion pair and cation-anion aggregate, but also promotes the formation of inorganic-rich EEI, thereby strengthening its inherent safety, ionic transport kinetics, interfacial desolvation, and high-voltage tolerance. Consequently, the optimized non-flammable electrolyte enables highly stable cycling of K||graphite (450 cycles), K||Mn-based Prussian blue analogs (Mn-PBA) cells (2.0-4.5 V, 3000 cycles), and Mn-PBA||graphite full-cells (2.0-4.3 V, 2200 cycles). This study provides guidelines for designing multifunctional electrolytes with both safety and high performance for PIBs and beyond.

10.1002/aenm.71381.title: Mechanism-Driven Atomic-Level Engineering Over RuO 2 -Based Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71381.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis (PEMWE) device with merits of high energy efficiency, rapid response, and operational flexibility represents one of the most promising technologies for green hydrogen production. However, the overall hydrogen production efficiency in PEMWEs is frequently constrained by kinetic limitations of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), due to intricate multi-step proton-electron transfer processes. RuO 2 -based catalysts remain limited stability, primarily due to intrinsic Ru site overoxidation and lattice oxygen loss during operation, which motivates intensive study into their understanding and mitigating these inactivation mechanisms. Different from traditional surface scale optimization, recent advances in RuO 2 catalyst have focused on mechanism-driven atomic-level engineering modification of both Ru sites and coordination environment to simultaneously enhance catalytic activity and stability. However, a comprehensive understanding that bridges the mechanistic complexity of OER with targeted atomic-scale intervention remains elusive, in response, this review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in RuO 2 -based nanocatalysts, with an emphasis on OER mechanisms, advanced in-situ/operando characterizations in PEMWE, and mechanism-based strategies for regulating stability at the atomic scale. Ultimately, this review concludes by delineating the primary challenges and outlining promising future research directions essential for advancing the practical application of RuO 2 catalysts in PEMWEs.

10.1002/aenm.71379.title: Design Principles of Electrocatalysts for Industrial-Scale Water Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71379.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic water splitting is central to the emerging hydrogen economy, yet its translation from laboratory discovery to industrial deployment remains constrained by the absence of catalytic systems that can sustain ampere-level current densities with high efficiency, durability and acceptable cost. This Review presents a principle-driven framework for the rational design of electrocatalysts for industrial-scale water electrolysis, beginning with the fundamentals of hydrogen production, the persistent lab-to-industry gap and the technical barriers associated with high-current operation. Descriptor-guided design concepts for hydrogen and oxygen evolution are first examined to clarify how electronic structure governs catalytic activity, followed by a systematic overview of transition-metal-based electrocatalysts and the major strategies used to regulate their performance, including defect, doping, high-entropy, phase, strain and heterostructure engineering, reconstruction, support, built-in electric fields and surface micro-environment modulation. These advances are further distilled into four overarching design principles for ampere-scale catalysis: intrinsic active-site and electronic-structure engineering, mass-transport optimization, robust catalyst-support integration and durability under extreme operating conditions. State-of-the-art cathodic, anodic, bifunctional and seawater-compatible systems are then assessed alongside integrated electrolyser platforms. Finally, operando characterization methods and industrial translation challenges, including scalability, device integration, long-term stability and policy alignment, are discussed to outline a roadmap toward truly industrial electrocatalysts.

10.1002/aenm.71564.title: Advanced Energy Materials at 15: Advancing the Energy Transition From Fundamental Insights to Practical Technologies
10.1002/aenm.71564.abstract: ABSTRACT This Special Issue commemorates the fifteenth anniversary of Advanced Energy Materials and reflects the evolution of energy materials research from fundamental discovery toward practical technologies. Assembled in conjunction with the 2025 Wiley Forum Spring Meeting, the collection brings together 28 Research Articles and 10 Reviews spanning photovoltaics and optoelectronics, electrochemical energy storage and conversion, flexible and distributed energy technologies, and data-driven materials discovery. Collectively, these contributions demonstrate how advances in materials chemistry, defect and interface control, multiscale characterization, scalable manufacturing, and predictive computation are enabling more efficient, stable, and deployable energy systems. The breadth of the collection underscores the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and of evaluating innovations under realistic technological constraints. The Special Issue is dedicated to the memory of Professor Taiho Park, whose scientific vision, leadership, and service left a lasting legacy in the field. Sincere appreciation is extended to all contributing authors, reviewers, and the editorial team whose efforts made this anniversary collection possible.

10.1002/aenm.202506803.title: Smart Exploration of Perovskite Photovoltaics: From AI Driven Discovery to Autonomous Laboratories
10.1002/aenm.202506803.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal halide perovskite solar cells have been developed as a front runner in next generation photovoltaic technology. However, such rapid development is hampered by complex relationships among material compositions, process routes, device architectures, and environmental conditions. The fabrication system is strongly coupled with many variables, which implies that existing empirical optimization methods are less capable to explore design space in high dimensions. Additionally, perovskite materials have sensitive intrinsic properties to environmental factors hence facilitating reproducible optimization across the composition space is notoriously difficult. Now, in this coupled system, artificial intelligence and machine learning have driven progress toward the understanding of the nonlinear composition-process-property relationships. But their predictive reliability is limited by patchy data and low reproducibility in manual experiments. Therefore, controlling lab environments and generating reproducible data with help from autonomous laboratories is paramount to accelerate predictive design. This review highlights recent progress in data driven materials discovery and closed loop experiments in perovskite research. We also report that AI guided process optimization is capable of identifying reproducible manufacturing windows. In parallel, robotic manipulation, high throughput synthesis with in situ monitoring and autonomous characterization are enabling systematic exploration of the multi-dimensional process space.

10.1002/aenm.202506810.title: Multiscale Perspectives on Perovskite Instability: From Atomistic Deformation to Device Degradation in Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.202506810.abstract: ABSTRACT This review elucidates where the operational instability of perovskite-based optoelectronic devices originates from by comprehensively exploring degradation phenomena from atomistic interactions to device scale. At thermodynamic equilibrium, the intrinsic stability of halide perovskites is reasonably good when considering the balance of intramolecular Asite covalent bonds, intermolecular A-X hydrogen bonds, and mixed ionic-covalent B-X bonding. Under operation, however, photoexcited or injected carriers become localized via trapping at surface and ionic defects and/or polaron formation in the soft Pb-halide framework, which induce Coulombic force to distort the crystal lattice and change atom-to-atom distances. Such effects lower ion migration barriers, enhance lattice distortion, and accelerate atmospheric reactions with ambient species, leading to quick degradation of perovskite crystals. In terms of device-level stability, holerich conditions and interfacial charge accumulation in heterostructured architectures are identified as particularly detrimental, directly linking carrier localization to device-level degradation. Based on these insights, we discuss composition engineering toward favorable large-polaron formation, defect passivation to suppress trap-assisted localization, and interfacial engineering within the heterostructured device. At the end, we propose advanced operation protocols that effectively relieve charge accumulation as key routes to realize durable perovskite optoelectronic devices.

10.1002/aenm.71046.title: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Energy Materials: Architectures, Training Strategies, and Applications
10.1002/aenm.71046.abstract: ABSTRACT Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) provide a practical route to bridge first-principles accuracy with the spatiotemporal scales required for modeling complex energy materials. By learning potential-energy surfaces from density functional theory (DFT) data, MLIPs enable atomistic simulations up to 10 4 -10 6 atoms over nanosecond timescales, thereby extending access to phenomena inaccessible to ab initio molecular dynamics. This review presents a phenomenon-oriented synthesis of MLIP development, spanning descriptor-based models, Gaussian process frameworks with uncertainty quantification, equivariant graph neural networks, and foundation models trained on large-scale datasets. We assess how architectural choices, training strategies (including active learning and multi-fidelity approaches), and dataset design influence accuracy, transferability, and computational efficiency across representative energy systems. Applications in solid-state electrolytes, battery electrodes, electrocatalysts, perovskite photovoltaics, and high-entropy materials are discussed with both performance metrics and methodological rationale. While MLIPs capture qualitative trends and relative property variations, absolute predictions remain sensitive to DFT functional choices, dataset representativeness, and treatment of long-range interactions. We address a structured validation framework linking model fidelity to experimentally relevant observables and system complexity. Also, we outline emerging directions including generative inverse design, autonomous discovery workflows, and foundation-model fine-tuning, highlighting opportunities and limitations for predictive deployment in energy materials research.

10.1002/aenm.71726.title: Using MIS Thermally Stimulated Currents for Degradation Dependent Energetic Landscape Evaluation in Triple Cation Mixed Halide Perovskites
10.1002/aenm.71726.abstract: ABSTRACT For perovskite solar cells (PSCs), despite the remarkable advancements in power conversion efficiency and environmental stability, degradation under operational conditions remains a barrier between research and commercialization. Understanding and monitoring the underlying physics of electronic band gap states during degradation as a result of ambient conditions is essential for further improvements in device stability. Here, advanced defect spectroscopy utilizing thermally stimulated currents (TSC) coupled to a metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) structure is used to determine the energetic landscape of band gap states in relevant state-of-the-art triple cation mixed halide (TCMH) perovskite samples to demonstrate the capabilities of this method. MIS TSC is used to resolve the electrical effect of degradation induced by ambient conditions and natural illumination. Coupling these findings to optoelectronic and structural analysis of individual perovskite layers and functional PSCs, a correlation between material degradation, device performance and trap state evolution can be obtained. We find that with aging under ambient conditions and exposure to light, in TCMH the electron trap density is reduced, while the density of detected hole states increases. For this unexpected behavior, we propose a change of trap type and polarity during degradation.

10.1002/aenm.71728.title: Reaction-Driven Coupled Transport-Nanostructure Evolution in SnSb Anodes for High-Energy All-Solid-State Li-Ion Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71728.abstract: ABSTRACT All-solid-state Li-ion batteries (ASSLIBs) require high-performance anodes exhibiting high capacity, high rate capability, and long-term cycling stability; however, existing anodes suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, particle pulverization, and unstable electrode-electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a SnSb anode overcoming these limitations via reaction-driven coupled transport-nanostructure evolution during electrochemical cycling is reported. The transport evolution originates from the reaction-driven formation of continuous mixed ionic-electronic conducting pathways and nanostructure evolution arises from repeated conversion and recombination reactions that induce stabilized nanocrystallization. This coupled evolution dynamically reconstructs mixed-conducting pathways during lithiation-delithiation, suppresses particle agglomeration, preserves intimate contact with the Li 6 PS 5 Cl solid electrolyte (SE), and lowers interfacial resistance, enabling rapid and highly reversible electrochemical reactions. A SnSb|NCM811 full cell delivers an areal capacity of 28.97 mAh cm −2 at an ultrahigh cathode loading of 200 mg cm −2 and maintains ultrafast rate capability over 1000 cycles at 10 C. Using an optimized 30-µm-thick SE sheet, the full cell is projected to achieve gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 355.7 Wh kg −1 and 1017.4 Wh L −1 , respectively. Pouch-cell demonstrations highlight the potential of SnSb for high-energy density ASSLIB applications and establish reaction-driven coupled transport-nanostructure evolution as an effective design principle for next-generation ASSLIB anodes.
authors: Je-Hyeon Han, Deok-Gyu Kim, Jung-Woon Yoo, Jeong-Myeong Yoon, Young-Han Lee, Do-Hyeon Kim, Pugalenthiyar Thondaiman, Chul-Ho Lee, Jeong-Hee Choi, Ki-Joon Jeon, Cheol-Min Park

10.1002/aenm.71717.title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self-Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few-Layer Nanosheets Grown From High-Curvature Micro-Interface for Fuel Cell
10.1002/aenm.71717.abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self-supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low-resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self-supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro-interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self-supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few-layer iCOF nanosheets at high-curvature micro-interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation-driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere-like morphologies in previously reported micro-interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil-in-water microemulsion interface using weakly surface-active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As-prepared iCOF few-layer nanosheets (1.3-1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self-supporting iCOF PEM (3.2-15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF-based membranes.
authors: Huimin Zhao, Bo Pang, Zihao Fan, Tianyu Liang, Xinran Li, Wanting Chen, Xuemei Wu, Fujun Cui, Gaohong He

10.1002/aenm.71724.title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF-8-Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High-Performance Light and Heavy-Duty PEM Fuel Cells
10.1002/aenm.71724.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering catalyst-ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT-PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework-8-derived 3D-hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D-hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton-conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half-cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin-type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR-free under H 2 -O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light- and heavy-duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress-test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst-ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass-transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high-performance LT-PEMFC.

10.1002/aenm.71721.title: Dual Anion-Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra-Stable PEO-Based Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP-Induced Side Reactions
10.1002/aenm.71721.abstract: ABSTRACT The incorporation of solvent N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO-Li + interaction and boosts Li + transport via strong Li + affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual-anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side-reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO 3 are introduced as dual-salt additives into an NMP-containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB- and NO 3 - with Li + , an anion-enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li + -NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion-derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10 −4 S cm −1 and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high-performance PEO-based solid-state lithium metal batteries.
authors: Weiya Li, Hongkai Hu, Kang Dong, Jiahao Geng, Mengqiu Li, Die Lai, TianTian Dong, Chi Zhang, Yongcheng Jin

10.1002/aenm.71720.title: Electric Double Layer-Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High-Utilization Zinc Anodes
10.1002/aenm.71720.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water-deficient EDL and hybrid organic-inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm −2 and 2 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.
authors: Yuao Wang, Tiantian Wang, Kangcheng Shen, Fengbao Qin, Mingrui Liao, Jian Ren Lu, Ke Ye, Dianxue Cao, Kai Zhu

10.1002/aenm.71723.title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
10.1002/aenm.71723.abstract: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high-valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC-NCM90) in low-cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo-doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + -migration and endowing the Mo 6+ -doped SC-NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC-NCM90. W-doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W- and Mo-doped SC-NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high-valence elemental surface doping as a dual-functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC-NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.
authors: Xiaolei Li, Hongjian Zhu, Feng Gao, Xiaohang Liu, Hao Huang, Wei Xu, Xue Wang, Philipp Kurzhals, Qiaobao Zhang, Weidong Zhou

10.1002/aenm.71461.title: Chemomechanically Adaptive MXene-Si-Ag Dual-Seed Interlayer Enabling Low-Pressure Sulfide all-Solid-State Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71461.abstract: ABSTRACT Sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) promise high safety and energy density; however, sustaining stable operation under low stack pressure remains challenging due to chemo-mechanical instability at solid-solid interfaces. Here, we report a chemomechanically adaptive MXene-Si-Ag hybrid interlayer that stabilizes Li metal-based anode interfaces in sulfide ASSBs. A mechanically compliant MXene framework maintains intimate contact with the sulfide solid electrolyte and accommodates interfacial stress evolution, while immobile Si and mobile Ag function as complementary lithiophilic seeds. Si provides persistent interfacial anchoring and continuous ionic pathways owing to its negligible solubility in Li, whereas Ag dynamically redistributes along Li flux to regulate nucleation and interfacial reaction kinetics. This immobile-mobile dual-seed synergy homogenizes Li transport without requiring strict spatial overlap of the seeds. When paired with high-loading NCM811 cathodes, the interlayer enables an areal capacity of 4.56 mAh cm −2 with 84.5% capacity retention over 500 cycles at 1C under 40 MPa. Notably, stable cycling is preserved even under ultralow stack pressure (0.21 MPa), delivering an initial Coulombic efficiency of 82.7% and 72.4% capacity retention after 200 cycles. This work demonstrates that coupling mechanical adaptability with dynamic lithiophilic regulation provides a practical pathway toward pressure-tolerant, high-energy sulfide ASSBs.

10.1002/aenm.71384.title: Multiscale Confinement Electrolyte Enables Low-Temperature Stable Aqueous Zinc-Iodine Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71384.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-iodine batteries are promising candidates for safe and low-cost energy storage but suffer from severe degradation under low-temperature and high-rate conditions due to electrolyte freezing, iodine dissolution, sluggish ion transport, and interfacial instability. Herein, we report a multiscale confinement electrolyte by introducing high-concentration Ca(ClO 4 ) 2 and a small amount of starch into a Zn(OTf) 2 system to regulate solvation structure, iodine chemistry, and electrode interfaces simultaneously. The strong hydration capability of Ca 2+ reconstructs the hydrogen-bond network, reduces water activity, suppresses ice crystallization, and preserves ion transport at subzero temperatures. Meanwhile, Ca 2+ confines iodide and polyiodide species through strong electrostatic interactions, thereby suppressing I 2 dissolution, inhibiting shuttle effects, and mitigating active material loss. Starch further constructs an interfacial confinement layer on the Zn anode, inhibiting parasitic reactions, reducing by-product formation, and guiding uniform Zn deposition. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, Zn||I 2 batteries deliver an exceptional rate capability of 15 A g −1 and achieve ultrastable cycling over 60 000 cycles at this ultrahigh rate. Moreover, the batteries operate reliably at -40°C, delivering over 3600 h of cycling at 0.5 A g −1 with 95.8% capacity retention. High-loading pouch cells and a preliminary 1.1 Ah-level demonstration further confirm the practical scale-up potential of this electrolyte strategy.

10.1002/aenm.71735.title: Decoupling Framework and Composition Engineering via Sequential Selenium Source Switching for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin Film Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71735.abstract: ABSTRACT Antimony selenosulfide (Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 ) has recently attracted intense interest as an earth-abundant, non-toxic, and bandgap-tunable photovoltaic absorber. However, conventional one-step deposition routes typically produce films with inadequate crystallinity and inhomogeneous elemental distribution through the film thickness, which severely hamper charge transport and limit device performance. Herein, we introduce an innovative selenium-source switching driven two-step sequential deposition (SDE) strategy that decouples framework formation from compositional engineering to overcome these limitations. First, a selenourea-based precursor is used to deposit a thick Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 film serving as a primary light-harvesting scaffold. Then, a sodium selenosulfate-based precursor solution is applied for secondary deposition. Owing to the high reactivity of this solution system, selenium species readily penetrate into the as-deposited film, inducing extensive ion diffusion and recrystallization throughout the bulk Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 material. This SDE strategy simultaneously optimizes the vertical Se/S grading, tailors the bandgap profile, and eliminates bulk deep-level traps and surface recombination centers. Consequently, the SDE-Sb 2 (S,Se) 3 device achieves a remarkable efficiency of 10.90%, placing it among the highest efficiencies for this material system. This strategy not only resolves the intrinsic bottlenecks of one-step techniques but also provides a generalizable route for synthesizing high-quality multicomponent chalcogenide films and offers new insights into ion-exchange kinetics during sequential deposition.
authors: Junwei Chen, Chenlong Gao, Fang Wu, Congrui Liu, Pengfei Wang, Zhihui Yang, Xiang Li, Tao Chen, Rongfeng Tang

10.1002/aenm.71710.title: A Tailored Multifunctional Lithium Organosilicate Salt Constructing Robust Interphases for High Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71710.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal batteries (LMBs) have attracted extensive attention due to their high energy density. However, when lithium (Li) metal is paired with high-voltage cathode materials, its practical application is limited by issues such as continuous oxidative decomposition of electrolytes and the incompatibility between electrolytes and aggressive electrodes. Herein, we synthesize a fluorinated lithium organosilicate salt (i.e., lithium fluorobis(fluoropinacolatoborato)silicate, LiPBS) to address the aforementioned challenges. The results show that the LiPBS can form a protective and rigid-flexible cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) on the cathode surface. Simultaneously, PBS − readily forms a coordination ion pair (CIP) with Li + , constructing an inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on the Li anode. Furthermore, Si─O groups in the LiPBS can effectively scavenge HF and H 2 O from the electrolyte. These advantageous properties enable LiCoO 2 (LCO, 1.89 mAh cm −2 )/Li (50 µm) coin and pouch cells to exhibit excellent cycling performance at high voltages and elevated rates-for example, retaining 82% capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C and 4.5 V, compared to 80% retention after only 67 cycles for the LiPF 6 -based counterpart. This performance is maintained even at an elevated temperature of 50°C. This work highlights the crucial role of lithium organosilicate salt in determining the electrochemical performance of LMBs.
authors: Ningxiang Zhu, Gaojie Xu, Guansheng Chen, Shenghang Zhang, Zhilin Yang, Yu Zhao, Qilong Chen, Peihao Yan, Xiong Shui, Cizhen Luo, Fengxiang Guo, Shitao Wang, Lixin Qiao, Botao Zhang, Zili Cui, Guanglei Cui

10.1002/aenm.71725.title: In Situ Defect Engineering of Atomically Dispersed Iridium on Mesoporous Mixed Oxide Frameworks for Robust PEM Water Electrolysis
10.1002/aenm.71725.abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling exceptional catalytic activity with operational durability at ultralow noble-metal loadings remains a central challenge for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. Herein, an in situ acid-etching-assisted defect engineering strategy is reported for constructing an ultrahigh-loading electrocatalyst (Ir@CM4) that predominantly features atomically dispersed iridium anchored on hierarchical mesoporous CeMn oxides. Directional Mn dissolution generates a dense oxygen vacancy network that traps Ir species, inducing a profound strong metal-support interaction to establish a highly electron-deficient, rigid Ir-O-Ce covalent framework. Consequently, Ir@CM4 delivers an exceptional mass activity of 948.15 A g −1 at 1.53 V versus RHE (31-fold higher than commercial Ir Black). In a PEMWE full cell with an ultralow loading of 0.28 mg Ir cm −2 , it sustains robust operation for 6350 h at an industrial-relevant 1 A cm −2 . Multimodal in situ tracking confirms that this covalent rigidity thermodynamically locks lattice oxygen, bypassing degradation-prone pathways to strictly enforce the highly stable adsorbate evolution mechanism. Density functional theory uncovers the quantum-mechanical origin: strong metal-support interaction-induced charge transfer downshifts the Ir d-band center to -3.93 eV, which circumvents traditional scaling relations by weakening antibonding orbital filling. This multiscale structural and electronic synergy effectively decouples the activity-stability trade-off, providing a translatable paradigm for industrial-grade acidic water electrolysis.
authors: Fenghua Zheng, Mengjie Liu, Guiru Zhang, Xiaoxuan Xu, Huiyuan Li, Xiaojing Cheng, Liuxuan Luo, Xiaohui Yan, Shuiyun Shen, Junliang Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71727.title: Tracing and Healing Multiscale Defects for Cost-Effective Lithium Carbonate-Derived Layered Oxide Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71727.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium carbonate (LC) is markedly cheaper than lithium hydroxide (LH) but remains underused for layered oxide cathodes because LC-derived materials perform poorly. Here, using a mid-Ni cathode, LiNi 0.65 Co 0.05 Mn 0.30 O 2 (N65), we trace this performance gap to LC-induced defects that span length scales, from atomic-scale disorder to nanoscale and microscale porosity. These defects originate from three features of the carbonate pathway that act across the solid, liquid, and gas phases, namely decoupled dehydration and lithiation, late melting of the carbonate, and a locally oxygen-deficient atmosphere from evolving CO 2 . Guided by this picture, we heal the defects with a single secondary heat treatment (SH) that adds an optimized amount of LH, simultaneously replenishing lithium, restoring an oxidizing atmosphere, and densifying the structure. The resulting N65-LC SH achieves discharge capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability comparable to those of the LH counterpart, while cutting the lithium precursor cost by 9% to 16% relative to conventional all-LH synthesis. More broadly, the gap between LH and LC is not an intrinsic property of the carbonate but a consequence of a precursor-specific pathway that, once traced, can be engineered around to unlock low-cost, high-performance Ni-based layered oxide cathodes.
authors: Jaesub Kwon, Innyoung Kim, Jong-Heon Lim, Doun Lee, Youngsu Lee, Kyoung Eun Lee, Hoyeon Shin, Young Jin Lim, Siyeong Park, Seok Mun Kang, Jaesang Yoon, Youngki Kim, Jihyun Kim, Eugene Kim, Younghyun Kim, Kyu-Young Park, Docheon Ahn, Yong-Tae Kim

10.1002/aenm.71729.title: Oxyhalide-Derived Nb-O-Cl Interfacial Frameworks for Mitigating Oxygen-Related Degradation and Facilitating Li+ Transport in High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes
10.1002/aenm.71729.abstract: ABSTRACT High-voltage Ni-rich cathodes coupled with sulfide solid electrolytes suffer from coupled instability of highly oxidized Ni-O configurations and Li + transport discontinuity under deep delithiation. Conventional oxide coatings mainly act as passive barrier layers that separate reactive contacts but remain structurally isolated from layered cathodes without simultaneously regulating interfacial chemistry and Li + transport. Here, we report an oxyhalide-enabled interfacial chemistry strategy based on a reconstructive Nb-O-Cl framework on LiNi 0.83 Co 0.07 Mn 0.10 O 2 cathodes (denoted as C-NCM). Derived from a mixed-anion LiNbOCl 4 (LNOC) precursor, the Nb-O-Cl framework undergoes mechanochemically assisted interfacial reconstruction, forming an amorphous oxyhalide interphase coupled with a Nb-containing near-surface region. Unlike passive oxide barriers, this chemically integrated architecture simultaneously reshapes the local Ni-O electronic environment and mediates interface-crossing Li + transport. Nb-O/Nb-O-Cl coordination redistributes local charge and is associated with improved retention of highly oxidized Ni-O configurations and mitigated oxygen-related irreversible evolution, while the Cl-containing oxyhalide framework provides an ionically conductive transition region that facilitates Li + migration across the cathode/electrolyte interface. Accordingly, C-NCM exhibits reduced sulfide-derived interphase formation and slower resistance growth, together with 88.17% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 4.5 V under high cathode loading. This work shifts cathode/sulfide-electrolyte interface design from passive oxide-barrier protection toward reconstructive mixed-anion interfacial chemistry.
authors: Kangzhe Yu, Zhan Wang, Xiao Huang, Lei Su, Leijie Zhang, Bingbing Tian, Musheng Wu, Chuying OuYang

10.1002/aenm.71718.title: Axial Cl-Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single-Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc-Air Batteries
10.1002/aenm.71718.abstract: ABSTRACT Single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M-N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single-atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF-8-derived ion exchange and gas-phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M-N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half-wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge-discharge cycling in zinc-air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge-type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.
authors: Zehao Tan, Peng Shen, Yangge Guo, Enping Wang, Jiabin You, Aiming Wu, Xiaojing Cheng, Jiewei Yin, Shuiyun Shen, Liuxuan Luo, Junliang Zhang

10.1002/aenm.71366.title: Dual-Functional Ru 2 P Nanoparticle-Decorated Ru/N,P-Doped Carbon Nanofibers for Efficient Hydrazine Oxidation-Assisted Hydrogen Production and Zinc-Air-Hydrazine Battery
10.1002/aenm.71366.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable electrocatalysts are essential to sustainable hydrogen (H 2 ) generation and advanced energy storage. Herein, Ru 2 P nanoparticles-decorated Ru/N,P-doped carbon nanofibers (Ru 2 P@Ru/NPCNFs) have been fabricated through an electrospinning-carbonization-thermal phosphorization strategy. The resulting material establishes itself as a premier dual-functional electrocatalyst. For the hydrazine oxidation reaction (HzOR), it requires a potential of only −0.013 V to reach 100 mA cm −2 , a significant improvement over the Ru/N-doped CNFs (NCNFs) sample. Concurrently, this catalyst drives the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at an industrial-grade current density of 1000 mA cm −2 with an overpotential of just 155 mV in 1 M KOH, exceeding the benchmark set by commercial Pt/C and most advanced reported catalysts. Leveraging these advantages, the synergistic effects enable an integrated water-splitting system assisted by hydrazine oxidation, driving a H 2 production rate 12 times higher than that of conventional water electrolysis. Furthermore, a rechargeable Zn-air-hydrazine battery is constructed, demonstrating excellent activity and durability. This work provides a versatile electrocatalyst and opens a new avenue for hybrid energy conversion and storage beyond conventional electrolysis.

10.1002/aenm.71420.title: Multi-Cation Synergy in Medium-Entropy Spinel Oxide for Practical Zn-Ion Pouch Cells
10.1002/aenm.71420.abstract: ABSTRACT Manganese oxide cathodes for aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising yet hindered by dissolution, structural collapse, and disproportionation, limiting their practical application. Herein, we report a multi-cation synergistic medium-entropy oxide (MEO) cathode with a spinel structure, Zn 0.86 Co 0.28 Ni 0.04 Cu 0.03 Mn 2 O 4 (ZCNCMO), designed to overcome these limitations. Theoretical and experimental analyses demonstrate that integrating multiple cations into a single spinel lattice leverages entropy stabilization to suppress elemental segregation, lattice distortion, and active species dissolution, thereby preserving structural integrity during cycling. As a result, the Zn-ZCNCMO battery delivers a specific capacity of 520 mAh g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , and retains a capacity retention of 98.3% after 2600 cycles at 2 A g −1 . The pouch cell delivers excellent stability over 1000 cycles and exhibits an energy density of 239.9 Wh kg −1 based on active materials and practically 56.3 Wh kg −1 , which is also integrated with solar and wind energy to power consumer electronics with exceptional safety under nail-penetration and cutting tests.

10.1002/aenm.71731.title: Charge-State-Controlled Surface Modifiers for High-Voltage and Stable Wide-Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/aenm.71731.abstract: ABSTRACT For wide-bandgap mixed-halide perovskites, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) surface reconstruction using bulky-cation spacers is widely employed to passivate surface defects and disrupt halide migration pathways. Nevertheless, under operational stress, conventional ammonium-based spacers can undergo deprotonation, destabilizing the low-dimensional surface layer and weakening its function. Herein, we report an organic-spacer charge-state control strategy for the surface modification of Cs 0.2 FA 0.8 PbI 1.8 Br 1.2 wide-bandgap perovskites. This strategy involves combining octylammonium (OA) with N -methylsulfanilic acid (NMSA) to form NMSAO, a charge-neutralized ammonium-sulfonate modifier state. This configuration induces an associated Ruddlesden-Popper-like quasi-2D phase at the perovskite surface that suppresses trap-mediated recombination, facilitates interfacial charge extraction, and disrupts halide-ion migration pathways. As a result, the NMSAO-treated perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.83% and an open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.326 V, compared with 17.30% and 1.197 V for the untreated control PSCs. Furthermore, the NMSAO-treated PSCs retain 93.59% of their initial PCE after 500 h of continuous illumination under ISOS-L-1 conditions and more than 93% after 500 h of thermal aging at 85°C. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a charge-neutralized organic spacer for quasi-2D surface reconstruction in wide-bandgap mixed-halide PSCs, improving both photovoltaic performance and operational stability.
authors: Subin Yu, Wooyeon Kim, In Choi, Bonkee Koo, Min Jae Ko

10.1002/aenm.71734.title: Operando Electro-Rheology: Unraveling Decoupled Ion Transport-Mechanical-Morphological Properties in Nanostructured Block Copolymer Electrolytes
10.1002/aenm.71734.abstract: ABSTRACT Block copolymer electrolytes exhibit a complex interplay between self-assembled morphology, ion transport, and mechanical properties under galvanostatic battery cycling. Here, we propose a novel operando methodology combining concurrent rheology and electrochemical measurements upon dc polarization for a lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI) doped polystyrene- block -poly (ethylene oxide) diblock copolymer electrolyte. Time-resolved measurements of the viscoelastic and electrochemical responses to the galvanostatic stimulus permit to uncover the effective response of the block copolymer electrolyte, tracking ion transport-mechanical-morphological properties simultaneously.
