The resulting electrode was further integrated with a self-healingPVA-PDA hydrogel electrolyte to assemble an all-in-one supercapacitor. Owing to the abundant catechol groups in PDA, the hydrogel electrolyte exhibited excellent self-healing capability and strong interfacial adhesion. Moreover, hydrogen-bonding interactions with the terminal groups on the MXene surface and π - π conjugation interactions with GNS contributed to the formation of a robust 3D network. Consequently, the MXene/GNS@CC electrode delivered an areal capacitance of 6880.60 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 . The assembled SHSC achieved an areal capacitance of 1152.03 mF·cm −2 at 1 mA·cm −2 and an areal energy density of 195.37 µWh·cm −2 at a power density of 0.61 mW·cm −2 . Additionally, the device retained 87.32% of its initial capacitance even after four cutting/healing cycles, indicating its broad application prospects in the field of flexible self-healing energy-storage devices.

10.1002/adfm.78983.title: Reprogramming Sphingolipid Metabolic and Redox Homeostasis with an Injectable Botanicals/Nanozymes Hydrogel for Inhibiting Postoperative Recurrence and Metastasis in Breast Cancer
10.1002/adfm.78983.abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative recurrence and metastasis in breast cancer remain major clinical challenges, primarily driven by persistent inflammation responses and secondary infections at surgical sites. These pathological processes trigger sphingolipid dysregulation and generate the redox imbalance for sustaining a chronic inflammation-metabolism feedback loop and promoting tumor regeneration. However, current therapeutic modalities frequently exhibit insufficient capacity to concomitantly attenuate inflammatory cascades, scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS), and restore metabolic homeostasis. Herein, we developed a multifunctional injectable botanicals/nanozyme hydrogel (CGHD) that restores redox balance and reprograms sphingolipid metabolism to inhibit tumor relapse. Under near-infrared irradiation, CGHD triggered cascade catalytic reactions that scavenged ROS and downregulated sphingosine and sphingosine kinase-1, thereby disrupting the inflammation-metabolism feedback loop driving tumor regeneration. In postoperative breast cancer models, CGHD accelerated wound healing and significantly suppressed recurrence and metastasis of residual tumors. Multi-omics analyses further showed that CGHD alleviated oxidative stress, remodeled sphingolipid metabolism, and suppressed NF-κB and TNF signaling. These effects decreased IL-6 and TNF-α expression while increasing IL-10 levels. Collectively, these findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a therapeutic target linking oxidative stress, inflammation, and postoperative tumor progression, highlighting CGHD as a promising strategy for recurrence prevention.

10.1002/adfm.78988.title: A Multifunctional Molecular Bridge at the Bottom Interface of Perovskite Solar Cells for Crystallization Regulation and Efficient Carrier Extraction
10.1002/adfm.78988.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted widespread attention from researchers worldwide and experienced rapid development in recent years. The bottom interface plays a crucial role in charge transfer and collection, and its status significantly affect the perovskite crystallization and the performance of PSCs. Thus, in this work, potassium trifluoromethanesulfonate (KFMA), was introduced as a multifunctional molecular bridge at the SnO 2 /Perovskite bottom interface to improve the interface status and the efficiency and stability of PSCs. Our results show that KFMA can interact with SnO 2 , passivate its surface defects, and optimize the interface energy level alignment, leading to enhanced charge transfer and promoted carrier extraction. Additionally, KFMA can regulate the growth of PbI 2 and perovskite crystallization, making more thorough transformation from PbI 2 to perovskite, giving a high-quality perovskite film. As a result, PSCs with a KFMA interface layer achieved an efficiency of 26.08% and long-term stability. After maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1 Sun illumination for 500 h, PCE of the KFMA-based device remained at 82.6% of the initial efficiency, while that of the pristine PSC just was left about 40%.

10.1002/adfm.78913.title: Dual-Interface Kinetics Activation Through Dipole-Induced Dynamic Liquid Crystal Interfacial Engineering for Efficient Solar Water Splitting
10.1002/adfm.78913.abstract: ABSTRACT Interface engineering is vital for improving the efficiency of semiconductor-based solar energy devices. Herein, we report a dipole-induced dynamic interface engineering strategy enabled by the nematic phase of 2-(4-((4-(heptyloxy)phenyl)ethynyl)phenyl)-5-methylbenzo[ d ]oxazole (PEMB-N) liquid crystal molecules. The rationally designed BiVO 4 /PEMB-N/FeNiOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.4 mA/cm 2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, alongside a solar-to-hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency of 7.2% and sustained photostability. A combination of density functional theory (DFT) calculations and experimental characterizations (in situ UV/vis spectroelectrochemistry and Kelvin probe force microscopy) elucidates that the enhanced dipole moment arising from benzoxazole functionalization, coupled with the dynamically tunable nematic phase of PEMB-N, facilitates the directional and multichannel extraction and migration of holes across the BiVO 4 /PEMB-N interface. Furthermore, at the PEMB-N/FeNiOOH interface, the well-ordered nematic phase effectively modulates the Fe d-band center and boosts the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. Importantly, this strategy is universally applicable to Ti-Fe 2 O 3 /PEMB-N/FeNiOOH photoanodes, demonstrating its broad compatibility with different photoanodes. These findings provide a “soft” interface engineering concept compared to conventional “rigid” interface modulation strategies for constructing high-performance solar-driven water splitting systems.

10.1002/adfm.78955.title: Polarization Properties Orientation Coupling Regulates Molecular Packing and Device Performance Beyond Dipole Moment Strength in Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78955.abstract: ABSTRACT Strong interactions between large dipole moment additives and host materials have been widely used to modulate molecular packing in organic solar cells (OSCs), while most studies focuses on dipole moment magnitude instead of the polarization properties orientation. Here, we challenge this oversimplified view by demonstrating that the polarization properties orientation-determined by both dipole orientation and polarizability anisotropy, rather than dipole magnitude alone - is the important factor. To quantify this, we introduce the “polarization properties orientation coupling degree” ( P ), which quantifies the matching of dipole orientation and polarizability distribution between additives and acceptors. Employing 1,4-diiodobenzene (DIB) and 1,3,5-triiodobenzene (TIB) as additives in the PM6:Y6 system with identical dipole moment magnitude but different orientation, we find that TIB exhibits a much higher p value (1.455 vs. 0.191), resulting in stronger intermolecular interactions. Consequently, TIB induces the formation of S-type and S′-type dimers of Y6, which optimizes exciton and charge transport behavior, boosting the performance from 17.53% to 18.08%. Furthermore, this principle is validated in high-performance systems of PM6:L8-BO (19.33%) and PM6:BTP-eC9 (19.23%), and shows significant advantages in large-area fabrication and reproducibility. This study highlights the significant role of polarization properties orientation, offering rational design strategy for high-performance OSCs.

10.1002/adfm.78948.title: In Situ Supramolecular Depolymerization Enables Bifunctional Buried-Interface Passivation in Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78948.abstract: ABSTRACT Introducing multidentate organic passivators has emerged as an effective strategy for defect passivation at the buried interface of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the active polar functional groups within these passivators are prone to supramolecular polymerization, which compromises passivation effectiveness. Herein, a supramolecular depolymerization strategy synergistically driven by thermal annealing and heteromolecular interactions is proposed. This approach enables the in situ depolymerization of the Zaltoprofen (Za) supramolecular structures introduced at the buried interface. The resulting depolymerized Za molecules are effectively anchored onto the underlying hole transport layer (HTL), while their molecular orientation is optimized to expose Lewis base coordination sites toward the perovskite layer. Consequently, enhanced coordination interactions with undercoordinated Pb 2+ are achieved, leading to more effective interfacial defect passivation and improved charge extraction. As a result, inverted PSCs based on a 1.57 eV bandgap perovskite exhibit a significantly improved power conversion efficiency ( PCE ), increasing from 24.05% to 25.61%. Moreover, the devices treated with this strategy demonstrate substantially enhanced operational stability compared with the pristine devices. This work provides a simple and effective strategy for activating supramolecular passivators and maximizing their defect-passivation capability in high-efficiency inverted PSCs.

10.1002/adfm.78931.title: Self-Powered, Ultra-Sensitive InGaAs/ITO Nanowire Radial Junction Infrared Photodiode for Low Flux Imaging at Room Temperature
10.1002/adfm.78931.abstract: ABSTRACT Shortwave infrared (SWIR) photodetection and imaging are of increasing importance for many emerging applications, such as optical and quantum communications, night vision, biomedical imaging and sensing. While planar InGaAs and Ge-based SWIR photodetectors are the current state-of-the-art, it is challenging to achieve single-photon level sensitivity at non-cryogenic temperatures due to their high dark current and thermal noise. Here, we demonstrate a highly sensitive self-powered InGaAs nanowire photodetector with single-photon-level sensitivity at 1310 nm. The device utilizes a p+ InGaAs/Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) radial heterojunction nanowire structure, enabling strong optical confinement and efficient carrier extraction. It demonstrates a detection sensitivity down to 118.1 pW at room temperature and 6.5 pW at 223 K, corresponding to two photons per pulse of a 1310 nm laser excitation at 20 MHz with the noise equivalent powers of 1.59 × 10 −13 W Hz −1/2 and 2.18 × 10 −15 W Hz −1/2 respectively. The photodetector maintains a high signal-to-noise ratio of 58 dB at 1550 nm and cut-off frequency of 15 MHz. Also, single-pixel imaging under illumination down to ∼580 µW cm − 2 , showcasing the robust imaging capability under extremely low-light conditions. Our results highlight the potential of nanowire-based heterojunction photodetectors for the development of next-generation, low-cost, high-performance SWIR photodetection and imaging technology.

10.1002/adfm.78800.title: Magnetically Induced Functional Fe 3 O 4 /Iron Foam Catalysts for Enhanced CO 2 -Assisted Ethane Dehydrogenation
10.1002/adfm.78800.abstract: ABSTRACT CO 2 -assisted ethane dehydrogenation (CO 2 -EDH) combines olefin production with CO 2 conversion, yet suffers from high temperatures and catalyst instability in thermal catalysis. This work establishes an alternating current magnetic field (ACMF)-mediated catalytic system using Fe 3 O 4 decorated on iron foam (Fe 3 O 4 /IF) as the induction catalyst, achieving significant enhancement of the CO 2 -EDH process under mild conditions. At 500°C, a temperature 200°C lower than that required in conventional thermal catalysis to reach a comparable conversion level, the system realized an ethane conversion of 22.2% with 97% ethylene selectivity. At an equivalent conversion level, the catalyst stability was improved by 15-fold compared to traditional thermal catalysis, with continuous stable operation for 80 h. The eddy current effect induced by the alternating magnetic field promotes electron transfer between Fe and Fe 3 O 4 and accelerates the oxygen redox cycle, thereby enhancing the reaction kinetics of the CO 2 -EDH process based on the Mars-van Krevelen (MvK) mechanism. This work provides an effective approach for improving the performance of alkane dehydrogenation under mild conditions and contributes new insights to the field of magnetically induced catalysis.

10.1002/adfm.78908.title: Coordination Competition Couples Oxygen Vacancy-Rich SnO x With Isolated Cu-N Sites for CO 2 -to-formate Electroreduction
10.1002/adfm.78908.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective CO 2 -to-formate electroreduction requires oxygen-deficient SnO x sites that stabilize O-bound * OCHO intermediates while resisting cathodic over-reduction. Here, we use a precursor-level coordination competition strategy to construct an oxygen vacancy (O v )-rich SnO x catalyst coupled with isolated Cu-N sites through controlled conversion of amino-functionalized Cu/Sn metal-organic frameworks. Competitive coordination of Cu and Sn with 2-aminoterephthalic acid (H 2 BDC-NH 2 ) is associated with altered precursor growth and a heterogeneous local environment, favoring the formation of defective SnO x domains during thermal conversion while enabling ligand-derived nitrogen sites to anchor redistributed Cu species. Spectroscopic investigations reveal that the optimized Cu-SnO x /NC catalyst contains abundant vacancy-related SnO x environments and predominantly isolated Cu-N configurations, which are associated with stabilized O-bound * OCHO intermediates and mitigated cathodic reconstruction of SnO x . Operando Raman spectroscopy further indicates persistent formate-related intermediates and comparatively lower bicarbonate accumulation during CO 2 electroreduction. Consequently, Cu-SnO x /NC achieves a formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96% at −100 mA cm −2 and maintains efficiencies above 85% over a moderate current density range in both alkaline and neutral electrolytes. Half-cell and full-cell energy efficiencies (EE) of 65% and 54%, respectively, were achieved in the flow cell and membrane electrode assembly (MEA). This work provides a coordination-competition strategy for durable high-rate CO 2 electroreduction.

10.1002/adfm.78966.title: Cooperative Dual-Directional π - π Stacking in Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78966.abstract: ABSTRACT The evolution from monomeric to dimeric self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) opens new opportunities for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet stronger π - π interactions in these larger architectures risk inducing aggregation over ordered assembly, making it challenging to maintain a well-balanced intermolecular packing. We design a symmetric indenocarbazole dimer (DIC) to harness cooperative face-to-face and edge-to-edge π - π stacking for directing intermolecular attraction into ordered, long-range assembly rather than uncontrolled aggregation. In stark contrast, its asymmetric indenocarbazole-carbazole conjugate (ICCB) suffers from random clustering and incomplete passivation. This ordered SAM template provides a homogeneous foundation for perovskite crystallization, delivering a champion PCE of 26.33% with an outstanding FF of 86.62%, significantly outperforming ICCB (24.80%), while retaining over 85% of its initial efficiency after 1600 h. Our findings establish molecular symmetry and dual-directional π - π interactions as critical design principles for high-performance dimeric SAMs.

10.1002/adfm.78531.title: Two-Dimensional Framework Materials as Building Blocks for Next-Generation Intelligent Biointerfaces
10.1002/adfm.78531.abstract: ABSTRACT The convergence of neural interfaces, wearable bioelectronics, and human-machine interaction is driving intelligent biointerfaces capable of sensing and responding to neural, physiological, and biomechanical signals. Realizing this vision demands a substantial advance in sensing and actuation hardware, which remains constrained by trade-offs in conventional bulk materials. This review proposes that two-dimensional framework materials, encompassing intrinsic 2D crystals, heterostructures, composites, and low-dimensional architectures, provide a transformative platform to overcome these barriers. The application scope is organized into five categories: implantable neural interfaces, non-invasive neural interfaces, physiological sensing, wearable human-machine interfaces, and soft actuation or haptic feedback. We establish a three-tier architecture. First, we catalog the requirements of piezoresistive, piezoelectric, capacitive, electromagnetic, electrostatic, and electrothermal sensors and actuators, identifying performance bottlenecks in bulk materials. Second, we trace these ceilings to microscopic origins: continuous electronic density of states, strong dielectric screening, coupled elastic-thermal phonon transport, and weakly tunable electron-phonon coupling that lock sensitivity, compliance, energy efficiency, and thermal safety into trade-offs. Third, we show how quantum confinement, attenuated screening, and broken symmetry in 2D materials decouple these constraints. We conclude by outlining a co-design strategy integrating heavy-element doping, symmetry engineering, interfacial design, and coupling phenomena to tailor 2D materials for next-generation intelligent biointerfaces.

10.1002/adfm.78977.title: Delocalized Electronic State Mediated NiCoOOH Enables Selective Urea-to-Nitrite Oxidation for Direct Urea Fuel Cells
10.1002/adfm.78977.abstract: ABSTRACT Selective oxidation of urea to nitrite (NO 2 − ) rather than N 2 is desireable for Direct urea fuel cells (DUFCs), doubling the electron yield per molecule while suppressing gas accumulation. Herein, we report a NiCoOOH model catalyst in which cobalt incorporation stabilizes electron-delocalized states around Ni sites, thereby steering the oxidation pathway toward selective urea-to-nitrite conversion. In situ Raman and infrared spectroscopies reveal that NiCoOOH triggers the formation of hydroxyl oxide species at potentials as low as 1.32 V vs. RHE while simultaneously promoting urea adsorption. The markedly attenuated *CO 2 vibrational signal indicates suppression of the N 2 -evolution and supports a reaction pathway in which OH − preferentially attacks the C─N bond. Consequently, NiCoOOH achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 84.7% for liquid nitrogen oxides (NO x − ), representing a 21.5% improvement over Ni(OH) 2 , and requires only 1.48 V to deliver 500 mA cm −2 with stable operation for 100 h. Leveraging these advantages, the catalyst enables a 380 mV voltage saving in urea-assisted water splitting. Furthermore, a flow-type DUFC affords a peak power density of 18.98 mW cm −2 , and a pouch-type DUFC successfully powers an LED and an electronic timer, confirming the practical viability of this urea-to-nitrite strategy in energy devices.

10.1002/adfm.78970.title: Finishing Touch via Metal Coordination: A Photoactivatable Organic Semiconducting Prodrug for Triply Synergistic Amplified Cancer Phototheranostics
10.1002/adfm.78970.abstract: ABSTRACT Photothermal therapy (PTT), photodynamic therapy (PDT), and NIR-II fluorescence imaging are each compromised by tumor hypoxia, thermotolerance, and insufficient contrast, respectively, limiting the efficacy of integrated phototheranostics. To address these challenges, we developed a multi-amplification theranostic nanoplatform (ReCO-TPP NPs) that initially exhibits weak NIR-II fluorescence, type I PDT, and PTT, yet undergoes substantial self-amplification upon light irradiation. A rhenium(I) carbonyl complex was covalently conjugated to a D-π-A-π-D fluorophore (DTP), and the heavy-metal center partially quenches the NIR-II emission and suppresses type I ROS generation. Upon tumor accumulation and 808 nm laser irradiation, the limited initial ROS cleave the rhenium-carbonyl bond, releasing CO and regenerating the free DTP fluorophore. This activation dramatically amplifies NIR-II brightness and type I photodynamic activity, while maintaining excellent photothermal performance. The liberated CO suppresses heat shock protein 70, dissipates mitochondrial membrane potential, and inhibits ATP synthesis, thereby sensitizing tumor cells to PTT and establishing a self-reinforcing ROS-CO-ROS cycle. Mitochondrial targeting via triphenylphosphonium further intensifies cellular damage. In 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, ReCO-TPP NPs enable deep-tissue NIR-II imaging with post-irradiation brightness enhancement and produce potent synergistic antitumor efficacy. This molecularly engineered “weak-to-strong” theranostic strategy offers a promising paradigm for precisely amplified cancer phototheranostics.

10.1002/adfm.77423.title: Operando Tracking of Oxygen-Vacancy Dynamics and Negative Capacitance in Ca-Doped BiFeO3
10.1002/adfm.77423.abstract: ABSTRACT Recent advances in mixed ionic-electronic conductors have highlighted the critical yet poorly understood role of non-stationary defect dynamics in shaping electronic functionality, motivating the need for operando methods capable of resolving ionic motion and electrical response on matched timescales. Here, we address this challenge by combining operando electrocoloration with snapshot electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to track oxygen-vacancy transport in lateral Bi 0.7 Ca 0.3 FeO 3- δ thin-film devices under direct current (DC) bias. Time-resolved optical imaging reveals the drift of oxygen vacancies and the emergence of vacancy-poor (p-type), vacancy-rich (n-type), and transient filamentary regions, which correlate directly with distinct transformations in the impedance spectra. The early response follows the Jamnik-Maier framework for mixed conductors with ion-blocking electrodes, while progressive spectral distortions require an additional resistor-capacitor (RC) branch associated with filamentary conduction, supported by Gaussian-process distribution-of-relaxation-times analysis. After the p- and n-type fronts merge, the system enters a new regime marked by a sign reversal in the low-frequency imaginary impedance and a robust negative-capacitance element ( C neg ≈ −3 × 10 −7 F), consistent with a frozen, over-screened space-charge configuration in a strongly asymmetric internal p-n landscape. These results establish operando EIS-electrocoloration as a powerful platform for probing non-stationary ion-electron dynamics and negative capacitance phenomena in solid-state electrochemical oxides.

10.1002/adfm.77388.title: A Thermodynamic Model of Antiferroelectics and Its Application to Electric Field Induced Antiferroelectric-Ferroelectric Transition in PbZrO3
10.1002/adfm.77388.abstract: ABSTRACT is a prototypical antiferroelectric which can be transformed into a ferroelectric under an applied electric field. The abrupt changes in net polarization and spontaneous strain could potentially be utilized for applications in energy storage and microelectromechanical systems. Here, we establish a thermodynamic model that simultaneously incorporates ferroelectric, antiferroelectric, and antiferrodistortive orders. We parameterize it using a combination of experimentally measured lattice parameters, critical transition fields, and dielectric constants as well as first-principles calculations of electric polarization and crystallographic analysis. We obtain a Clapeyron-like equation for describing the temperature dependence of critical electric fields for the antiferroelectric-ferroelectric phase transition, and their dependence on crystallographic directions. We then calculate the phase-transition-induced polarization jump and electromechanical responses of . Finally, we discuss how to include the phase transition between the ferroelectric and phases in our model. Our model can be employed to predict the ferroelectric and electromechanical responses of and implemented in the phase-field method to simulate the mesoscale domain evolution of under different thermodynamic conditions.

10.1002/adfm.77954.title: Bulk-Like Spin Cycloid and Fast Switching in Freestanding BiFeO3
10.1002/adfm.77954.abstract: ABSTRACT The spin cycloid characteristic of noncollinear antiferromagnets offers significant potential for energy-efficient, magnon-mediated spintronic applications. Multiferroic BiFeO 3 is among the most promising candidate materials because its antiferromagnetic order can be controlled by an electric field. However, in epitaxial BiFeO 3 thin films, substrate clamping and epitaxial strain modify the cycloidal magnetic structure while limiting efficient ferroelastic-ferroelectric switching. Here, we show that strain-released freestanding BiFeO 3 membranes overcome these limitations. Compared with substrate-clamped epitaxial thin films, a 100-nm-thick freestanding membrane exhibits ≈50% faster electric-field-driven ferroelectric switching and a spatially uniform, bulk-like single spin cycloid, as revealed by resonant elastic X-ray scattering. In contrast, the epitaxial thin film exhibits an expanded cycloid periodicity and slower ferroelectric switching dynamics, reflecting the influence of substrate-induced strain. Freestanding BiFeO 3 membranes therefore overcome substrate-induced constraints by simultaneously restoring the intrinsic bulk-like spin cycloid and enabling substantially faster ferroelectric switching. This combination of robust noncollinear antiferromagnetic order and efficient electric-field switching establishes freestanding BiFeO 3 membranes as a promising magnetoelectric platform for low-power magnonic and spintronic technologies, while enabling heterogeneous integration with Si-based devices.

10.1002/adfm.77492.title: Atom Probe Tomography as an Emerging Tool for Understanding Defect-Driven Mechanisms in HfO2-Based Ferroelectrics
10.1002/adfm.77492.abstract: ABSTRACT HfO 2 -based ferroelectrics are essential for the next generation of CMOS-compatible memory and logic devices, yet their performance is governed by a complex interplay between oxygen vacancies, dopants, and structural defects that remains an active area of investigation. These defects shape the function-critical dynamic phenomena, such as polar phase stabilization, wake-up, fatigue, and imprint. In this Perspective, we review the limitations of established high-resolution structural characterization techniques and propose atom probe tomography (APT) as a powerful tool for the 3D atomic-scale mapping of all constituent species in hafnia-based ferroelectric systems. By resolving individual dopants, vacancy clustering, and interfacial segregation, APT can facilitate a quantitative understanding of defect-property relations in hafnia-based ferroelectrics. We discuss current experimental challenges for APT application to ferroelectric oxides, demonstrate a proof-of-concept of atomic-scale reconstruction in a hafnia-based device stack, and highlight the potential of APT to guide the development of ferroelectric structures with enhanced reliability and performance.

10.1002/adfm.78919.title: Oxygen Evolution Electrocatalysts with Trinuclear, Mixed-Valence Iron Motifs on Electronically Aligned Carbon Dots
10.1002/adfm.78919.abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER), a bottleneck for water electrolysis, remains limited by the adsorbate scaling relations and sluggish interfacial electron transfer (IET). We address these challenges by anchoring mixed-valence Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ motifs on aspartic-acid-derived carbon dots (AspCDs). Spectroscopic analyses support trinuclear Fe 3 sites, which offer redox flexibility and proximal active centers. The Fe 3 site binds the substrate (OH − ) and is electronically coupled to the AspCD scaffold. Together with the work function-aligned scaffold for electron abstraction from OH − , these features establish effective inner-sphere IET from OH − , through the active Fe 3 center and the AspCDs host to the electrode. Simultaneously, the mixed valency buffers the charge build-up during the successive proton-coupled electron transfers. The catalyst drives fast and selective O 2 generation and minimizes H 2 O 2 formation, while sustaining at least ∼70 h of continuous operation with a gradual ∼90 mV total potential increase. Thus, the Fe 3 /AspCDs catalyst requires only 110 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm −2 , shows particularly effective kinetics with a low Tafel slope of 41 mV dec −1 , and has a turnover frequency of 2.1 s −1 . The design integrates crucial physicochemical properties for highly efficient OER, and the principle can be generalized to other systems toward further advances in the field.

10.1002/adfm.78934.title: Multidimensional-Encoded High-Fidelity Spectrometers With a Floating-Base Bipolar Junction
10.1002/adfm.78934.abstract: ABSTRACT Miniaturized computational spectrometers that combine spectrally tunable photodetectors with reconstruction algorithms offer a promising route toward compact, portable spectral sensing while maintaining performance comparable to traditional benchtop spectrometers. In single-detector computational spectrometers, a reconfigurable photodetector serves as spectral-encoding hardware, and the quality of its spectral response matrix critically determines peak-wavelength accuracy, noise tolerance, and reconstruction fidelity. However, conventional encoding schemes based on electrically tunable single photodetectors often rely on one-dimensional voltage sweeps, which can suffer from highly correlated response states and a practical trade-off among electrical tunability, broadband coverage, and reconstruction robustness. Here, we address this trade-off using a spectrally tunable floating-base bipolar-junction photodetector as a representative multidimensional encoder. By counter-tuning the interfacial barrier matching between balanced and unbalanced configurations, a single detector combines excitonic-resonance-enhanced response, monotonic short-wavelength absorption, and interlayer transport modulation of photoexcited carriers, thereby generating a richer and less correlated spectral response matrix. Multidimensional encoding of these complementary spectral response features enables more effective decoupling of encoded spectral datasets, even under sub-nanoampere photocurrent operation where noise and calibration errors can critically degrade reconstruction fidelity. Our strategy provides a versatile pathway toward high-fidelity, compact, and robust computational spectrometers for edge-level spectral sensing and intelligent optoelectronic systems.
authors: Sang-Hyeon Lee, Junho Min, Yonas Tsegaye Megra, Min-Hye Jeong, Hwi Je Woo, Jaewon Han, Junheon Ha, Gyunghyun Jang, Young Jae Song, Hyun-Soo Ra, Hoon Hahn Yoon, Jong-Soo Lee

10.1002/adfm.78711.title: Reflector-Free, Highly Confined Love-Like SAWs Enabled by a Phononic Metasurface for Real-Time Monitoring of Cell Dynamics
10.1002/adfm.78711.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices are widely used in sensing and biosensing but generally suffer from strong attenuation in liquid environments. Conventional approaches rely on reflectors to reduce these losses, yet these components remain difficult to optimize: limited device miniaturization and increased fabrication complexity. Here, we introduce an innovative design strategy that integrates a phononic metasurface with tailored electromechanical properties of the substrate to generate a type of shear-horizontal (SH) surface resonance modes that exhibit strong lateral confinement and extremely low radiation into both the substrate bulk and the free surface, eliminating the need for reflectors. This approach enables highly tailorable surface acoustic resonances with distinctive enhanced dynamic strain-energy confinement leading to significantly high-quality factors, particularly in water-loaded conditions. We show the fabrication and experimental validation of the proposed phononic metasurface-based SAW resonator and showcase its biosensing capabilities through real-time monitoring of cellular death.
authors: Jessica Monaldi, Julio A. Iglesias Martínez, Francis Kosior, Laurent Badie, Halima Alem, Frédéric Sarry, Mourad Oudich

10.1002/adfm.78837.title: Uniformly Anchored Dibenzothiophene-Armed Self-Assembled Molecule Regulates Perovskite Lattice for Efficient and Stable Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78837.abstract: ABSTRACT The molecular aggregation of self-assembled molecules (SAMs) and their weak anchoring to the perovskite layer result in interfacial non-radiative recombination and perovskite degradation, significantly impeding improvements in the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, we design a novel π -conjugated SAM, (4-(3,6-bis(dibenzo[b, d]thiophen-2-yl)-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl)phosphonic acid (4PADBT), to simultaneously address these challenges. The introduction of two non-coplanar dibenzothiophene (DBT) units onto the conventional 4PACZ backbone creates a large dihedral angle (∼70°), which effectively suppresses molecular aggregation and promotes the formation of uniform and well-ordered SAM films. Furthermore, the DBT groups act as a pair of anchoring arms, forming strong coordination bonds between sulfur (S) atoms and Pb 2+ ions at the buried interface. This uniform SAM layer and the strong interactions not only facilitate preferential (100) crystal orientation in the perovskite layer but also induce a lattice strain transition from tensile to compressive type, thereby effectively enhancing the structural stability and reducing defects. With these merits, the 4PADBT-based device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.25%, significantly higher than the 23.82% of the control 4PACZ device. Moreover, this design improves both thermal and operational stabilities, highlighting 4PADBT as a promising interfacial material for high-efficiency and stable PSCs.

10.1002/adfm.78939.title: Deep Q-Network-Guided TiO 2 /NOA61 Microstructures for Light Outcoupling and Angular Emission Redistribution in Blue Top-Emitting OLEDs
10.1002/adfm.78939.abstract: ABSTRACT Enhancing light outcoupling in blue top-emitting organic light-emitting diodes (blue T-OLEDs) requires optical architectures capable of redirecting internally confined energy into extractable radiative channels. However, the coupled geometric-compositional parameter space makes empirical optimization inefficient. Here, a deep Q-network (DQN)-guided strategy is developed to optimize TiO 2 /NOA61 microcylinder arrays for mode-redistribution-enhanced outcoupling in blue T-OLEDs. The cylinder radius, array period, and TiO 2 filling fraction φ are optimized as coupled variables, and the selected structures are nanoimprinted onto the Ag top electrode. Compared with the reference device, the optimal device with φ = 9.1% achieves a 52.6% increase in maximum luminance at 45.5°, where the emission peak is located at 464 nm. EQE rises from 18.66% to 21.75% at φ = 0 and 23.21% at φ = 9.1%, showing geometry- and composition-associated gains. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) and temporal coupled-mode theory (TCMT) analyses reveal that the enhancement originates from power-flow redistribution, loss-channel repartitioning, and strengthened oblique-angle radiative coupling, yielding a simulated angle-integrated outcoupling enhancement factor of 1.82. Beyond this blue device, the DQN framework provides a basis for future wavelength- and angle-specific outcoupling designs targeting directional luminance delivery and reduced off-cone optical waste in near-eye AR/VR displays.

10.1002/adfm.78976.title: Decoupling Solvation From Interfacial Adsorption: Chiral-Induced Low-Polarization Interface for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78976.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are constrained by severe dendrite growth and detrimental reactions of Zn anodes. While electrolyte additives have been widely explored, the role of molecular stereostructure (chirality) in regulating Zn anode interfacial chemistry and stability remains poorly understood. To answer this, the D- and L-proline amide were chosen as model enantiomers to systematically investigate the underlying stereochemical impacts. Despite nearly identical bulk solvation structures and desolvation energetics, the two enantiomers exhibit starkly different electrochemical behaviors, demonstrating that chirality dictates interfacial rather than bulk processes. L-proline amide favors a flatter and stronger adsorption configuration on Zn surfaces, which lowers nucleation barriers and homogenizes Zn 2 + flux, suppressing both kinetic and concentration polarization to enable dendrite-free deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells with L-proline amide achieve over 2500 h of stable cycling, Zn||Cu cells deliver 99.39% average Coulombic efficiency, and Zn||V 2 O 5 full cells retain 89.83% capacity after 1000 cycles. This work highlights chirality as an important descriptor for interfacial regulation and provides mechanistic insights into the stereochemical effects of electrolyte additives for the rational design of aqueous zinc battery electrolytes.

10.1002/adfm.78973.title: Synergistic Microphase Separation and Interfacial Microenvironment Regulation in Fluorinated Polybenzimidazole Membranes for Efficient Electrocatalytic CO 2 Reduction
10.1002/adfm.78973.abstract: ABSTRACT Anion exchange membrane (AEM) with high ion conductivity and effective interfacial regulation is crucial for electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction (ECR). Herein, we design a fluorinated polybenzimidazole (6FPBI) grafted with both piperidinium and trimethylammonium cations to fabricate a high-performance AEM. Benefiting from ether-free fluorinated backbone and dual cation group, 6FPBI-TP membrane exhibits IEC of 3.63 mmol g − 1 , suppressed water uptake of 50.44%, and suppressed swelling ratio (9.26%), alongside a tensile strength of 19.14 MPa. The 6FPBI-TP membrane exhibits a competitive OH − conductivity of 142.75 mS cm − 1 at 80°C and an elevated selectivity of 67%. Its moderately hydrophobic, positively charged surface optimizes the three-phase catalytic microenvironment, mitigating water flooding and suppressing the hydrogen evolution side reaction. In membrane electrode assembly, 6FPBI-TP membrane delivers FE CO of 94.4% at 150 mA cm − 2 , exceeding OPBI-TP membrane (89.1%). 6FPBI-TP membrane maintains stable electrolysis over 100 h, while OPBI-TP membrane fails after only 25 h. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a dominant vehicular OH − transport pathway and enhanced alkaline stability derived from ether-free fluorinated backbone. This dual cationic strategy not only constructs well-defined ion transport channels but also modulates the interfacial microenvironment, thereby affording a straightforward route to AEM with high stability and high selectivity for ECR.

10.1002/adfm.78927.title: Entropy-Engineered Fluorite Surfaces for Oxygen Catalysis and Humidity Tolerance in Reversible Protonic Ceramic Cells
10.1002/adfm.78927.abstract: ABSTRACT Reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs) require air electrodes with fast oxygen reduction/evolution reactions (ORR/OER) and excellent durability under low-temperature, high-humidity operating conditions. Herein, we report a rationally designed fluorite catalyst, Pr 0.025 Nd 0.025 La 0.025 Sm 0.025 Ce 0.9 O x (PNLSC), deposited on a PrBa 0.8 Ca 0.2 Co 2 O 5+δ (PBCC) backbone for constructing a hybrid air electrode with enhanced electrocatalytic activity and structural durability. Systematic electrochemical investigations, combined with entropy-dependent comparisons, demonstrate that the designed PNLSC coating can accelerate surface oxygen exchange kinetics, facilitate ionic transport, and suppress surface degradation in humidified atmospheres. In situ infrared spectroscopy analyses directly reveal the optimized surface hydration kinetics and suppressed hydroxyl-related surface degradation on the PNLSC hybrid electrode, providing mechanistic evidence for its enhanced oxygen reaction activity and proton transport. Furthermore, a maximum power density of 2.10 W cm −2 and an electrolysis current density of −3.23 A cm −2 at 1.3 V are achieved for the single cells with the hybrid electrode at 700°C, accompanied by excellent durability over 200 h and reversible cycling stability for 140 h. This work establishes an entropy-enabled fluorite surface engineering that couples accelerated electrocatalysis with intrinsic humidity resistance, offering a universal strategy for designing next-generation air electrodes in R-PCECs.

10.1002/adfm.78980.title: Interfacial Multidentate Chelation Enabled Anti-Aggregation Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78980.abstract: ABSTRACT The quality of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) and the defect density at the perovskite buried interface are key factors determining the performance of inverted perovskite solar cells (IPSCs). However, the inherent aggregation of SAM molecules at this interface limits further efficiency improvements. Herein, we develop an interfacial multidentate chelation (IMC) strategy that integrates anti-aggregation functionality into SAMs for buried interface regulation. Specifically, 2,2′:6′,2′′-terpyridine (TERPY) is introduced into the SAM of [4-(3,6-dimethoxy-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (MeO-4PACz). The π-π interactions between MeO-4PACz and TERPY suppress SAM self-aggregation, resulting in a compact and uniform SAM layer. Meanwhile, the three pyridinic nitrogen atoms in TERPY chelate with undercoordinated Pb 2 + defects through multidentate Pb-N coordination, reducing interfacial defect states. Benefiting from these dual effects, the champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of small-area (0.043 cm 2 ) and large-area (1 cm 2 ) IPSCs reach 26.23% and 25.43%, respectively. Encapsulated devices retain 82.75% of their initial PCE after 1300 h of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) under the ISOS-L-2 protocol. This work provides a feasible strategy for simultaneously regulating SAM assembly and passivating buried interface defects.

10.1002/adfm.78926.title: Oceanic In Situ Power via Chaotic Multi-Energy Harvesters
10.1002/adfm.78926.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide-area radiation and pollution affect the marine ecosystem and anthropogenic sustainability. A key implementation challenge is the lack of sustainable and on-site power supply technology. Here, we propose a multi-energy harvester integrated by wind-wave dual-driven triboelectric nanogenerators (WW - TENGs) with the chaotic pendulum structure. The system was designed with multiphase flow optimization, simultaneously collecting wind and wave energy from the marine air-sea interface. The peak power density of the device reaches 48 W/m 3 , with the energy conversion efficiency reaching 11.7%. Furthermore, we developed a marine radioactive monitoring system, which integrates in situ energy harvesting and powering and real-time monitoring. In general, this work introduces a multiphase-coupled energy harvesting and supply strategy, facilitating in-depth research into the dynamic changes of marine ecosystems and advancing the early deployment of protection measures.

10.1002/adfm.77922.title: Dirac-Source Linear X-Ray Detection Diode
10.1002/adfm.77922.abstract: ABSTRACT External readout electronics are optimally interfaced with X-ray detection devices that exhibit linear current-voltage (IV) characteristics to enable direct signal acquisition with minimal analogue signal conditioning. This not only simplifies the analogue front-end design but also enhances signal accuracy and system integration. Here, we present a Dirac source (DS) X-ray detection diode that employs a monolayer graphene top electrode integrated into a perovskite-based device architecture. In contrast to conventional devices with nonlinear, diode-like IV responses, the DS source device displays a linear and stable IV behavior over an extended voltage range (200 V). This linearity arises from the unique Dirac dispersion and linear density of states intrinsic to graphene. The graphene interface also enables ultra-low dark current densities (∼3 pA·cm − 2 at 1 V), approximately six orders of magnitude lower than those of standard metal-contacted devices. A Schottky-like barrier at the graphene/hole transport layer junction forms a back-to-back diode configuration, suppressing charge injection and minimizing leakage. Circuit-level modelling and numerical simulations support this mechanism and validate the role of the interfacial design. This device design concept represents a robust strategy for developing low-noise X-ray detectors with minimal readout complexity, offering strong potential for advanced imaging and radiation monitoring technologies.

10.1002/adfm.78924.title: Nanoamphizymes: Self-Assembled Amphiphilic Enzymatic Nanomaterials for High-Performance Biocatalysis and Biosensing
10.1002/adfm.78924.abstract: ABSTRACT Nanomaterials offer versatile platforms for biocatalysis by modulating enzyme stability and activity at the nano-bio interface. However, strong interfacial interactions often disrupt enzyme structure and cause substantial activity loss, while the largely empirical nature of enzyme-nanomaterial assemblies limits rational design. Here, we propose a rational strategy to regulate enzymatic activity by constructing amphiphilic enzymes that self-assemble into stable nanoparticles (NPs) in aqueous environments. Using 4-piperidino-1,8-naphthalimide-functionalized glucose oxidase (PPNI-GOx) as a model system, we systematically varied glutaraldehyde crosslinking to control NP size and catalytic performance. The optimized PPNI-GOx NPs displayed a catalytic efficiency comparable to, and even surpassing that of native GOx in solution, while achieving a remarkable 66-fold increase relative to previously reported GOx NPs. Integration of the optimized nanoamphizymes into an electrochemical glucose sensor afforded high sensitivity, broad linear range (up to 24 mM), low detection limit (53.3 µM), and excellent selectivity against common interferents. The sensor also demonstrated exceptional operational stability, retaining 92% of its initial response after 7 days of long-term testing. Collectively, this work establishes nanoamphizymes as a powerful and tunable platform for enhancing enzyme activity, stability, and sensor performance, offering a transformative strategy for developing high-performance biocatalysts and next-generation biosensing systems.

10.1002/adfm.78990.title: Planar Macromolecular Semiconductors Enable Fast Electron-Ion Transport Kinetics for High-Performance Zinc-Organic Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78990.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer cathodes featuring versatile designable redox-active motifs and structural anti-dissolution in aqueous electrolytes have attracted interest for advancing zinc-organic batteries. However, their implementation is hindered by insulating electronic properties and sluggish ion transport, both arising from twisted molecule chains with poor structural planarity, which limits active-site accessibility and capacity delivery. Here we design planar macromolecular semiconductors (PMSs) by fusing a four-electron pyrene-4,5,9,10-tetraone acceptor and a two-electron tetraminobenzoquinone donator into long-range conjugated polymeric skeletons through intermolecular π - π interactions. The highly π -extended planarity endows PMSs with a semiconducting property (7.64 × 10 −7 S cm −1 ) that promotes efficient electron delocalization, and yields the highest ion diffusion coefficient (6.52 × 10 −7 cm 2 s −1 ) among reported organic cathodes. Leveraging synergistic fast electron-ion transport kinetics, the long-range stacking of molecular planes minimizes conformational disorder, enabling near-complete utilization (98.4%) of redox-active quinone−phenazine motifs with an ultralow activation energy (0.19 eV). Consequently, Zn||PMSs battery liberates high capacities (442/263 mAh g −1 at 0.2/100 A g −1 ), alongside a long lifespan (60,000 cycles). Besides, PMSs cathode enables a 348 mAh zinc pouch cell with a high mass loading (20 mg cm −2 ) to operate stably for 1000 cycles. This work provides a promising direction to design planar organic semiconductors for boosting electron-ion migration kinetics toward better zinc batteries.

10.1002/adfm.78963.title: Proton/Oxygen Dual-Ion Gated Control of Skyrmion Nucleation via Tuning Orbital Asymmetry
10.1002/adfm.78963.abstract: ABSTRACT The pure voltage control of skyrmions represents a promising approach for developing skyrmion devices with low power consumption and high stability. However, existing methods still face long-standing challenges in terms of reliance on an assisted magnetic field and fast control of small-sized skyrmions at low voltages. This work proposes an ionic-liquid (IL) gating strategy based on the electric-field induced magnetoionic effect (EIME). The applied electric field activates H + /O 2− migration in the Pt/Co/Al 2 O 3 multilayer at a low voltage (±4 V), enabling the pure-voltage-controlled nucleation and annihilation of skyrmions in a reversible and non-volatile way. Microscopically, the electric-field-driven migration of dual ions modifies both the interface and bulk attributes such as the Co-O hybridization and orbital asymmetry of Co, thereby regulating both the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) and Heisenberg interactions through changes in orbital and spin moments. These findings clarify the indirect ion-skyrmion coupling mechanism at the electronic level and highlight a promising pathway for ion-governed skyrmion devices.

10.1002/adfm.78936.title: A Phosphazene-Polyphenol Network Binder Enables Catalytic Polysulfide Conversion and Intrinsic Flame Retardancy for Practical Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78936.abstract: ABSTRACT Practical deployment of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries is severely hindered by polysulfide shuttling, structural degradation from severe cathode swelling, and flammability risks. Herein, we construct a cross-linked macromolecular binder (HTP) by integrating bio-derived tannic acid, branched polyethyleneimine, and a phosphorus/nitrogen-rich phosphazene framework. This advanced spatial architecture yields abundant heteroatom-rich active sites that function synergistically to optimize both sulfur electrochemistry and thermal safety. Consequently, the S@HTP cathode demonstrates exceptional cyclic stability, exhibiting an ultralow capacity fading rate of 0.025% per cycle over 2000 cycles at 4 C. Under a sulfur loading of 5.4 mg cm −2 and an E/S ratio of 9 µL mg −1 , the S@HTP cathode still maintains a high areal capacity of 7.5 mAh cm −2 after 100 cycles at 0.1 C. Furthermore, the phosphazene framework facilitates the formation of a protective char layer and suppresses combustion propagation, imparting intrinsic self-extinguishing characteristics. This structural chemistry approach provides a multifunctional interface-regulation paradigm for secure, high-energy energy storage systems.

10.1002/adfm.78052.title: Emergent Deep-Ultraviolet Ferroelectrics: Structure and Polarization Mechanism
10.1002/adfm.78052.abstract: ABSTRACT Deep-ultraviolet (DUV) nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals can convert visible and near-infrared lasers into the DUV region, exhibiting significant applications in various fields, particularly in high precision measurements such as 229 Th-nuclear optical clock. However, as an ideal DUV NLO crystal, it must simultaneously satisfy multiple stringent requirements, which severely limit the number of available systems. Consequently, ferroelectrics with reversible spontaneous polarization that can modulate NLO coefficients through domain engineering to realize quasi-phase matching have attracted much attention. Nevertheless, the development of DUV ferroelectrics also faces challenges constrained simultaneously by symmetry requirements and the intrinsic coupling between polarization mechanisms and electronic structure. Therefore, this review systematically summarizes the structural types and polarization mechanisms of typical ferroelectrics. It also conducts analyses of paraelectric and ferroelectric phases for the few reported DUV ferroelectrics, providing an in-depth discussion of their polarization generation and switching mechanisms. On this basis, it proposes that the design of new DUV ferroelectrics should primarily rely on geometric distortion or local dipole ordering combined with ionic displacement, so as to enhance macroscopic polarization and NLO response. Therefore, this review will provide theoretical guidance for the development of new DUV ferroelectrics, thereby facilitating their applications in optoelectronics and quantum optics.
authors: Zujian Wang, Hongyuan Sha, Xiaoming Yang, Chao He, Fangfang Zhang, Xifa Long, Shilie Pan

10.1002/adfm.78055.title: Distance-Dependent Magnetic Resonance Tuning Sensors for Precise MRI-Based Theranostics
10.1002/adfm.78055.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) represents a cornerstone of non-invasive diagnostics, yet conventional contrast agents often lack the molecular specificity required to resolve dynamic biochemical processes. Distance-dependent magnetic resonance tuning (MRET) addresses this limitation by exploiting controllable dipolar coupling between paramagnetic enhancers and superparamagnetic quenchers. This mechanism underpins the development of activatable, adaptive, and quantitatively tunable MRI sensors that decode molecular interactions into measurable magnetic responses. In this Review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the physical principles, design strategies, and classification of MRET sensors, highlighting key strategies for tuning intercomponent interactions and modulating MRI signals. We further discuss representative biomedical applications of MRET sensors in biomarker-driven diagnostics, early lesion detection, longitudinal therapy monitoring, imaging-guided interventions, and in situ drug screening, enabling the direct visualization of dynamic biological events rather than merely anatomical changes. This Review aims to highlight the transformative potential of MRET sensors for advancing precision theranostics, inspiring further innovation in intelligent contrast agents and solidifying MRET as a cornerstone for next-generation functional and precision MRI.
authors: Ting Wu, Sijie Song, Kun Kang, Chen Chen, Yuhang Yao, Zhaowei Chen, Huanghao Yang

10.1002/adfm.78071.title: Intrinsic Large-Unit-Cell Systems for Advanced Thermoelectrics and Thermal Management
10.1002/adfm.78071.abstract: ABSTRACT The urgent demand for efficient thermoelectric conversion and precise heat management technologies drives the search for materials capable of simultaneously optimizing often-conflicting electronic and thermal transport properties. Intrinsic large-unit-cell (LUC) systems, such as high-entropy alloys, sub-nanometer clusters, porous frameworks, and amorphous materials, demonstrate hierarchically scaled structural complexity and are classified as “structural complexity-driven transport-modulating materials.” Characterized by severe lattice distortions, configurational entropy, nanoconfinement, hierarchical porosity, and inherent disorder, these materials intrinsically restrict phonon transport across multiple scales, enabling ultralow lattice thermal conductivity essential for high thermoelectric performance and thermal insulation. Concurrently, their vast compositional flexibility and complex electronic structures provide unique avenues for enhancing electrical conductivity and Seebeck coefficients via mechanisms like band convergence, resonant levels, and energy filtering. This review critically examines the fundamental mechanisms linking the intricate atomic architectures of LUC systems to their exceptional performance in thermoelectrics and thermal management. Furthermore, it highlights the indispensable role of machine learning in navigating their immense design complexity for accelerated discovery, inverse design, and decoding of intricate structure-property relationships, paving the way for next-generation thermoelectrics and thermal management.
authors: Peng-Fei Xu, Yu-Ting Li, Cheng-Xin Liu, Chang-Le Liu, Jin-Yang Xi, Chun-Yuan Song, Biao Xu, Ling-Hua Tan

10.1002/adfm.78121.title: Revisiting the Spectrum-Crystal Field Relationship of 3d3 Ion (Mn4+/Cr3+)-Activated Phosphors via a Recalibrated Database
10.1002/adfm.78121.abstract: ABSTRACT With tunable red-to-near-infrared (NIR) emissions, Mn 4+ - and Cr 3+ -activated phosphors have been extensively investigated in recent years and are emerging as alternatives to commercial rare-earth-ion-activated phosphors in various applications. However, the rational design of these phosphors remains a great challenge due to the long-standing inaccuracy and inconsistency in the spectrum-crystal field relationship. This work aims to revisit and clarify this relationship by constructing a uniformly recalibrated database. We correct empirical formulas and systematically recalculate spectral levels, Racah parameters, and crystal field parameters from reported data. The database integrates these newly derived parameters from diverse host structures, together with standardized configurational-coordinate models for Mn 4+ /Cr 3+ ions in octahedral sites. By providing an open platform to access accurate information, this reliable database paves the way toward data-driven design of 3d 3 ion-activated phosphors with tailored properties.
authors: Jiayu Wu, Zhenzhen Zhang, Jie Chen, Xiaoze Yuan, Zhongxian Qiu, Yuwei Zhou, Fan Ding, Shixun Lian, Xiaodong Wen

10.1002/adfm.77597.title: Van der Waals Ferroelectrics Toward Non-Volatile Nanoelectronics
10.1002/adfm.77597.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric materials exhibit controllable spontaneous electrical polarization under external electric fields, offering significant potential for high-density, high-speed, and energy-efficient non-volatile electronic device technology. However, the practical realization of conventional ferroelectrics has been impeded by issues such as lattice mismatch, interfacial challenges, limited compatibility with silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology, and compromised device reliability. In contrast, van der Waals (vdW) ferroelectrics are characterized by room-temperature ferroelectricity, atomic-scale thickness, dangling-bond-free surfaces, and weak interlayer interactions suitable for constructing tailored structures. These unique properties position them as an unprecedented platform to address the fundamental limitations of their conventional counterparts for developing non-volatile ferroelectric devices. Herein, we critically evaluate the current status of vdW ferroelectric research with a focus on their application in non-volatile device technology. We survey recent breakthroughs in material discovery and polarization control, analyze the device performance of both intrinsic and artificial vdW ferroelectrics through quantitative benchmarking against conventional technologies, and identify the key materials-level and device-level challenges-including polarization magnitude, switching kinetics, characterization reliability, defect dynamics, and scalable integration-that must be addressed to advance this field toward practical memory applications.
authors: Lin Wang, Yinfeng Long, Han Chen, Mingyue Yuan, Runlai Li, LinFeng Sun, Kian Ping Loh

10.1002/adfm.77930.title: Electrochemical Pathways for Nitrate Conversion to Ammonia: From Environmental Challenges to Ammonia Economy
10.1002/adfm.77930.abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrate pollutants in water systems pose significant health risks and contribute to eutrophication. The electrochemical nitrate reduction reactions (eNO 3 RR) is a promising approach to address nitrate pollutants while generating wealth-adding products. In this review, we explore the potential for applying eNO 3 RRs to reduce nitrate levels in real wastewater. First, we identify the importance of reducing nitrate concentrations in water. Next, we discuss the advances of electrocatalysts for eNO 3 RR based on the reaction mechanisms, highlighting the adoption of various catalytic systems in low-concentration wastewaters, providing new insights for applying eNO 3 RR in real pollutant systems. We also discuss the key challenges and technologies related to the development of scaling up eNO 3 RR devices and ammonia collection materials. Finally, we outline future research perspectives essential for realizing sustainable, high-performance, and cost-effective electrochemical nitrate removal and the generation of wealth-adding products. This review provides insights into catalyst design for nitrate reduction and strategies for converting nitrate pollutants to wealth-adding products.
authors: Xintong Li, Yunpeng Zuo, Xiaoran Zhang, Jieqiong Shan, Kenneth Mei Yee Leung, Bin Liu, Peter Strasser, Adrian Fisher, Zonglong Zhu, Xin Wang

10.1002/adfm.75914.title: Learning From Atoms: Machine Learning Enabled Design of Durable PtCo Fuel Cell Catalysts
10.1002/adfm.75914.abstract: ABSTRACT Predicting electrocatalyst performance under realistic conditions remains challenging due to the limitations of quantum mechanical (QM) methods. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled data-driven potentials that bridge quantum accuracy with realistic and nanoscale catalyst modeling. Here, a computational-experimental approach is presented to investigate the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and durability of intermetallic PtCo nanoparticles by integrating QM calculations with neural network potential (NNP) based real-sized simulation. The NNP, trained on Pt, Co, and PtCo systems, enabled accurate modeling of nanoparticles up to 5 nm containing several thousand atoms. ORR activity was elucidated through analysis of the d -band center, oxygen adsorption energies, free energy diagrams, and validated by rotating disk electrode (RDE) measurements. Dissolution potentials (U diss ) calculated via NNP revealed strong dependence on core configuration and particle size, with onion-like ordered PtCo showing the highest U diss . These trends were experimentally validated through accelerated durability tests (ADT), and the consistency between NNP and QM results confirms the model's predictive reliability. This combined theoretical and experimental approach provides a reliable and scalable pathway for understanding degradation mechanisms and designing durable fuel cell electrocatalysts.
authors: Jong Min Lee, Song Jin, Jeemin Hwang, Mun Seon Kang, Joonhee Kang, Sung Mook Choi, Min Ho Seo

10.1002/adfm.77789.title: Benzodifluoranthenes and Their π-Extended Derivatives: Syntheses, Structural Analyses, Properties, and Hole Mobilities
10.1002/adfm.77789.abstract: ABSTRACT New classes of arenes, benzo[1,2- b :5,4- b′ ]difluoranthene ( syn -B b D), benzo[1,2- b :4,5- b′ ]difluoranthene ( anti -B b D) and their π-extended derivatives, were regioselectively synthesized by rhodium-catalyzed intramolecular annulations of bis[2-(arylethynyl)phenyl]-substituted linear [3]phenylenes and biphenyleno[2,3- b ]biphenylenes, respectively. The structures and molecular stacking of these compounds were verified by X-ray crystallography. Notably, bis(4- n -butylphenyl)-substituted anti -B b D ( 2b ), characterized by a reorganization energy of 164 meV, organizes into either 2D “brickwork” or 1D slipped stacking motifs. These architectures facilitate robust electronic coupling integrals of 84 and 108 meV, respectively, which profoundly dictate the material's charge-transport dynamics. Solution-processed organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) based on 2b exhibited an exceptional hole mobility of 3.43 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , consistent with leading as-cast, solution-processed small-molecule semiconductors. This work not only establishes B b Ds as a promising class of high-performance semiconductors but also elucidates pivotal design paradigms for future solution-processable materials that form a critical connection between molecular topology, supramolecular aggregation, and charge-transport efficiency.
authors: Yi-Min Chang, Ting-Yu Wang, Yen-Chen Lin, Chien-Hao Lee, Cheng-Ping Tsai, Chu-Yen Tsai, Ming-Yu Kuo, Chu-Chen Chueh, Yao-Ting Wu

10.1002/adfm.77931.title: Anion-Interactive Anode Interfaces for Stable Anode-Free Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.77931.abstract: ABSTRACT Anode-free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) offer high energy density but face challenges of uncontrolled lithium nucleation, unstable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, and irreversible lithium loss. This study presents a nanofabrication-guided interfacial engineering strategy using a 3D nanotubular copper (Cu) current collector conformally coated with an ultrathin (∼10 nm) Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene nanosheet. This multifunctional, anion-interactive interface induces uniform lithium nucleation and enhances PF 6 − adsorption, directing the formation of a conformal, LiF-rich inorganic SEI throughout the 3D nanoarchitecture. Ex situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analyses reveal that preferential LiF nanoparticles form along the MXene layer, improving interfacial homogeneity and SEI robustness. Under lean-electrolyte conditions, anode-free full-cell tests (coin-cell type, Li-free MXene-NT Cu||NCM811) exhibit superior cycling performance, delivering 78.1 mAh g −1 at the 125 cycle with 99.06% Coulombic efficiency, whereas the bare Cu counterpart achieves only 44.9 mAh g −1 and 95.01%, respectively. These results highlight the importance of rational nanomaterial design and nanoscale interfacial modulation in enabling stable, high-performance AFLMBs.
authors: Eunji Kim, Hyunju Jung, Jinuk Kim, Sung-Jin Chang, Gyungtae Kim, Yun Chang Park, Yoon Kyung Seo, Kyung Jin Park, Sodam Choi, Kwangduck Seo, Hee Han, Su-Ho Cho, Chi Won Ahn, Vy Thuy Nguyen, Hyeyoung Shin, Minji Lim, Hee-Tae Jung, Yonghee Lee, Jinwoo Lee

10.1002/adfm.77978.title: Synergistic Enhancement of Luminescence Dissymmetry Factor and Quantum Yield via Hybrid Copper(I) Iodide Cluster and Cellulose Nanocrystal Bilayer Films
10.1002/adfm.77978.abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) has emerged as a cornerstone technology for next-generation chiral photonic applications. However, a fundamental trade-off between the luminescence dissymmetry factor ( g lum ) and photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) has remained the primary bottleneck preventing the widespread practical deployment of CPL materials. Herein, we report a breakthrough solution to this long-standing problem through a rational synergistic design that combines highly emissive copper(I) iodide clusters with chiral cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) photonic templates. The synthesized Cu 4 I 4 (2,5-DMePi) 2 clusters exhibit an ultrahigh PLQY of 97.20% and excellent stability, allowing their facile integration into flexible polymer films. By constructing a bilayer architecture consisting of the emissive Cu-I cluster film and a left-handed chiral nematic CNC template, we achieve the CPL performance that simultaneously delivers a near-unity PLQY and a large g lum value of −0.9421. Most strikingly, the CPL sign can be reversibly switched between −0.9421 and 0.1021 simply by changing the observation direction. These direction-tunable bilayer films with multimodal optical features are ideal for advanced optical anti-counterfeiting. Collectively, this work not only breaks the fundamental g lum factor-PLQY trade-off but also provides a generalizable strategy for the design of next-generation high-performance CPL materials.
authors: Jiahui Li, Shengzhe Jia, Hui Yan, Jiaoyu Peng, Haitao Feng, Mingyang Chen, Junbo Gong

10.1002/adfm.78044.title: Heterostructure-Induced Electronic Modulation Enables Spin-Polarized Co Sites for Balanced OH−/Ethanol Adsorption in Efficient Ethanol Oxidation to Acetate
10.1002/adfm.78044.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical ethanol oxidation to acetate enables energy-saving hydrogen production with value-added chemical generation. Cobalt-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising ethanol oxidation reaction (EOR) electrocatalysts, but reconstructed Co 3+ centers often bind OH − too strongly, causing active-site blocking and limited ethanol adsorption. Here, we construct a hierarchical NiS@Co-ZIF-L heterostructure on nickel foam through sequential in situ growth to modulate reconstructed Co sites. In situ Raman spectroscopy shows that interfacial NiS coupling lowers the onset potential for CoOOH reconstruction. DFT calculations indicate geometric perturbation of the Co-related coordination environment, while Co K-edge XAFS, EPR spectroscopy, and SQUID magnetometry support modified Co electronic structure and enhanced spin polarization consistent with high-spin Co-related sites. This electronic/spin modulation shifts the d-band center from −1.19 to −2.13 eV, moderates OH − binding, and reduces the computed C-H activation barrier from 1.39 to 0.55 eV. MD simulations suggest a more balanced interfacial OH − /ethanol distribution, consistent with potentially alleviated hydroxide-related site blocking. The optimized catalyst reaches 10 mA cm −2 at 1.29 V vs. RHE with 96.67% Faradaic efficiency and sustains 1 A cm −2 for 500 h in an AEM electrolyzer, with an acetate-production energy consumption of 4.02 kWh kg −1 .
authors: Shimao Lin, Jingyuan Zhang, Shuyi Yang, Chong Peng, Tiezhu Zhang, Tao E

10.1002/adfm.78051.title: Modal Analysis of Light Propagation, Polarization and Diffraction by Cholesteric Liquid Crystal Layers
10.1002/adfm.78051.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral liquid crystals (CLCs) are widely explored for polarization-selective photonic applications due to their photonic bandgap and strong Bragg reflection, yet a predictive framework linking bulk eigenmodes to external wave propagation remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce a Floquet-based theoretical framework that rigorously describes electromagnetic eigenstates in periodic helicoidal media and establishes a direct mapping between bulk 3D modes and their emission into external media. This approach enables quantitative prediction of key optical phenomena, including Bragg reflection, total internal reflection, and polarization-selective mode routing, in both planar and tilted CLC configurations. We experimentally validate these predictions through angular-resolved measurements, demonstrating excellent agreement with theory. Beyond visualization of dispersion relations, our framework provides a unified and predictive tool to engineer light transport in chiral photonic media. These results establish a predictive design framework for cholesteric photonic devices and highlight their potential for advanced diffractive optics, including emerging AR/XR applications.
authors: Ke Xu, Pouya Nosratkhah, Le Zhou, Shengzhu Yi, Giorgio Manzoni, Kristiaan Neyts

10.1002/adfm.78060.title: Thermoresponsive Liquid Crystalline Polymer Coatings Programmed by Field-Induced Topological Defects for Tunable Optical and Topographical Responses
10.1002/adfm.78060.abstract: ABSTRACT Self-assembly of nano- and microstructures in soft materials enables stimuli-responsive functionalities, yet scalable bottom-up approaches that combine high spatial precision with robust solid-state architectures remain limited. Liquid crystals provide a versatile platform due to their ability to host topological defects with well-defined optical and mechanical properties. Here, we introduce a field-induced nematodynamic templating strategy to program liquid crystal coatings prior to photopolymerization. Resonant standing waves generate large-area lattices of topological defects that are permanently encoded into a polymer network with high fidelity. The resulting coatings exhibit defect-specific surface topographies that are reversibly tunable with temperature, while preserving their ability to generate optical vortices and enabling thermally controlled phase and spectral responses. These results demonstrate that topological defects act as programmable units coupling optical and mechanical functionalities within a single platform. Beyond optics, the approach further enables spatial functionalization through guided incorporation of fluorescent particles, highlighting its potential for multifunctional coatings. This defect-encoded and field-programmable strategy provides a scalable route toward reconfigurable flat optics, adaptive surfaces, and sensing platforms.
authors: Jacques A. Peixoto, Mufeeduzaman Chavilkkadan, Alexander Fusi, Marko Beslać, Dirk J. Broer, Etienne Brasselet, Danqing Liu

10.1002/adfm.78062.title: Comparative Performance and Partial Load Cycling of Sodium-Metal Chloride Battery Modules With Mixed-Metal Fe,Zn and Ni,Fe Cells
10.1002/adfm.78062.abstract: ABSTRACT We present dynamic partial-load cycling data for high-temperature sodium-metal chloride battery modules employing nickel-free cathodes based on iron and zink. The cathodes in these Ni-free Na-(Fe,Zn)Cl 2 cells achieve 39% metal utilization and a theoretical energy density of 129 Wh kg −1 at cell level, corresponding to 372 Wh kg −1 at electrode level. Ten-cell modules incorporating this cathode were assembled and operated under realistic load conditions at 300°C. Dedicated characterization cycles enabled direct comparison with state-of-the-art Ni,Fe cathodes (30% metal utilization, 145 Wh kg −1 at cell level, 398 Wh kg −1 at electrode level). Although the Na-(Fe,Zn)Cl 2 modules exhibited lower peak power and current capability, they demonstrated competitive energy efficiency and stable cycling performance. Long-term cycling was performed under dynamic partial-load profiles simulating photovoltaic charging and household consumption. The protocol integrated a controlled cool-down phase and intentional overcharge cycles to evaluate safety under failure conditions. Reliable operation was demonstrated for approximately four months, delivering an average discharge capacity of 17 Ah per cell over 87 cycles at charging rates of C/4-C/6 and discharging rates of C/6. These results confirm the viability of Ni-free cathodes for high-temperature Na-metal chloride batteries, offering improved sustainability with acceptable rate-performance trade-offs for large-scale stationary energy storage applications.
authors: Enea Svaluto-Ferro, William Nash, Robert Zboray, Fabrizio Vagliani, Diego Basso, Alberto Turconi, Andrea Pozzi, Corsin Battaglia, Norbert Weber, Tom Weier, Meike V. F. Heinz

10.1002/adfm.78068.title: Colloidal Quantum Dots-Based Bioinspired Reconfigurable Photoelectrochemical Device for Broadband Underwater Imaging and Photosynaptic Memory
10.1002/adfm.78068.abstract: ABSTRACT Underwater artificial visual systems that couple visual perception with memory capabilities are of great significance for intelligent marine environmental monitoring, autonomous underwater robotics, and deep-sea resource exploration, thereby requiring intelligent optoelectronic devices with broadband spectral adaptability and multifunctional photodetection (PD)/photosynaptic (PS) functionalities. Here, inspired by the spectral adaptation and homing memory of Pacific salmon, we report a reconfigurable photoelectrochemical (PEC) device based on near-infrared (NIR) CuInSeS/ZnSe (CISeS/ZnSe) quantum dots (QDs), in which the Ag incorporation enables spectral adaptation through redshifted absorption while weakening non-adiabatic coupling (NAC) of QDs to suppress non-radiative recombination. As a result, the fabricated QDs-based PEC devices deliver a maximum responsivity of 1.47 A W −1 and a specific detectivity of 6.47 × 10 11 Jones in PD mode, exhibiting broadband photoresponse up to 980 nm and enabling multi-wavelength underwater optical imaging (UOI). In PS mode, the device further demonstrates biomimetic paired-pulse facilitation (PPF), short-term plasticity (STP) to long-term plasticity (LTP) transition, and learning-forgetting-relearning behaviors. By unifying broadband underwater perception and neuromorphic memory within a single device, this work provides a promising bioinspired strategy for next-generation underwater artificial visual systems and intelligent optoelectronic technologies.
authors: Liuliu Wang, Yisen Yao, Xin Li, Li Xia, Zhuojian Li, Liping Gu, Chengjie Wang, Arup Neogi, Feng Lin, Chong Wang, Zhiming Wang, Xin Tong

10.1002/adfm.78075.title: Nodal-Surface and Flat-Band Driven Large Room-Temperature Anomalous Nernst Effect in Epitaxial Ferromagnetic Weyl Metal Fe5Si3
10.1002/adfm.78075.abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic topological materials exhibit unconventional transport arising from the interplay between exchange-driven symmetry breaking and band topology. Beyond the point-like singularities of Weyl and Dirac fermions, extended degeneracies such as nodal surfaces and flat bands constitute an emerging frontier whose impact on Berry-curvature-mediated transport remains largely unexplored. Here, the anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) is investigated in epitaxial thin films of the Weyl nodal-line ferromagnet Fe 5 Si 3 . A pronounced transverse Nernst response of ∼1.50 µV K −1 is observed at room-temperature, accompanied by a giant anomalous Nernst angle of ∼0.56, indicating highly efficient entropy-to-charge conversion. The ANE follows a robust − TlnT scaling over a wide temperature range, supporting its intrinsic Berry-curvature origin. A substantial topological Nernst signal of ∼0.43 µV K −1 persisting above room-temperature is consistent with a possible contribution from real-space Berry-curvature linked to nontrivial spin textures. First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis reveal Weyl nodal lines, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) gapped nodal surfaces, and nearly flat bands near the Fermi level. The close agreement between calculated and measured anomalous Nernst conductivity supports an intrinsic origin, with these features providing a plausible electronic framework for the strongly energy-dependent Berry-curvature. These results establish Fe 5 Si 3 as a low-cost binary topological magnet for Berry-curvature-driven thermoelectric phenomena.
authors: Shubhashish Pati, Sonali Srotaswini Pradhan, Nanhe Kumar Gupta, Abhay Pandey, Nikita Sharma, Nakul Kumar, Saurav Singh, Yuya Sakuraba, V. Kanchana, Sujeet Chaudhary

10.1002/adfm.78084.title: Biomimetic Core-Shell Liposome Nanoparticles Deplete Lipoproteins and Enhance the Purity of Extracellular Vesicles from Human Blood
10.1002/adfm.78084.abstract: ABSTRACT Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) in human serum carry diverse biomarkers and hold great potential for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. However, their isolation is challenging due to the presence of highly abundant serum proteins, particularly lipoproteins that closely resemble the sEVs in size and density. Existing lipoprotein removal methods cannot effectively remove all types of lipoproteins and may lead to potential contamination. Herein, we developed a lipoprotein-depleting biomimetic core-shell liposome nanoparticle system composed of Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 cores coated with liposome bilayers (SL-NPs). These lipoprotein-mimicking nanoparticles exhibit efficient binding to lipoproteins that enable the selective removal of lipoproteins by low-speed centrifugation while preserving sEVs. When applied as a complementary treatment step, this NP depletion strategy further enhances the purity of sEVs isolated from human serum or human plasma using ultracentrifugation or chemical precipitation methods.
