10.1002/adfm.77807.title: Field-Free Switching of Spin-Orbit Torque Magnetic Devices via Symmetry Breaking: An Overview and Outlook
10.1002/adfm.77807.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-orbit torque (SOT) technology stands at the forefront of next-generation non-volatile memory and logic computing, promising superior endurance and ultrafast dynamics compared to conventional spin-transfer torque (STT) architectures. However, the persistent requirement of an external magnetic field for deterministic switching of perpendicular magnetization severely impedes high-density integration and commercial viability. This review systematically evaluates the evolutionary trajectory of symmetry-breaking strategies developed to overcome this bottleneck. The analysis progresses from early macroscopic structural engineering, such as wedged geometries and lateral asymmetries, to mesoscopic built-in effective fields driven by interfacial exchange coupling and chiral spin textures. Crucially, we identify a defining paradigm shift in the field: the transition from complex geometric modifications toward intrinsic material-level innovations, including low-symmetry crystals, vertical composition gradients (VCG), and synergistic dual-torque (STT-SOT) architectures. By resolving the trade-offs among switching efficiency, thermal stability, and structural complexity, these intrinsic and hybrid approaches offer a practical roadmap for integrating scalable, all-electrical SOT-MRAM with standard CMOS back-end-of-line (BEOL) processes. Finally, we establish a dual-track strategic roadmap: while long-term breakthroughs require parallel exploration of new exotic physics, we underscore the importance of focusing on mass production and foundry scalability at the current stage.
authors: Rundong Zhu, Sheng Wang, Zihan Deng, Kaixun Han, Guoxin Li, Xiaohang Li, Fangliang Gao, Xinman Chen, Shuti Li

10.1002/adfm.77999.title: Single-Crystal Perovskite High-Energy Radiation Detectors: From Bulk Crystals to Micro/Nano Integration
10.1002/adfm.77999.abstract: ABSTRACT High-energy radiation detection has various applications in medical imaging, industrial testing, and other fields. However, detectors made from traditional semiconductor materials struggle to meet the demands of modern applications, such as flexible wearable devices and low-cost, miniaturized detectors. To address this issue, single-crystal perovskite materials have been applied in the manufacturing of high-energy radiation detectors, owing to their enhanced optoelectronic properties and low-cost integration method. However, no review specifically discusses the relationship between crystal dimensionality, crystallinity, morphology modulation, and the performance of high-energy radiation detectors. In this review, we first systematically overview the relationship between crystal dimensionality, crystallinity, morphology modulation, and device performance in high-energy radiation detection. Then, the working mechanism and performance parameters of high-energy radiation detectors are thoroughly discussed. Furthermore, the fabrication techniques for bulk and micro/nano single-crystal perovskite are highlighted, and the influence of the nucleation and crystallization process on the fabrication of single crystals is also discussed. Moreover, the advances in high-energy radiation detectors based on single-crystal perovskite are systematically reviewed. Finally, the remaining challenges and future research prospects are presented. A detailed review of the development of perovskite single-crystal high-energy radiation detectors will inspire more researchers to join this field and highlight directions for the future.
authors: Kaixin Dong, Shasha Zhang, Yicheng Sun, Mengru Zhang, Junjie Liu, Dan Li, Zhonghao Wei, Yanlin Song, Yingjie Zhao

10.1002/adfm.78012.title: Covalent Organic Framework Polyamide Nanocomposite Membranes: From Chemical and Structural Regulation to Efficient Water Separation
10.1002/adfm.78012.abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane-based desalination and wastewater reclamation play an important role in addressing the global freshwater crisis. However, state-of-the-art polyamide (PA) composite membranes still suffer from inherent limitations, including the trade-off between permeability and selectivity, insufficient retention of small neutral solutes, susceptibility to fouling, and poor chemical stability. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), with their ordered crystalline structure, tunable pore function, and chemical stability, offer unprecedented opportunities for molecular-level regulation of PA membranes. Introducing COF nanomaterials into PA layers enables the construction of ordered transport channels for rapid water permeation and selective solute sieving. COF fillers also act as interfacial modifiers to regulate monomer diffusion and PA crosslinking during interfacial polymerization, reshaping membrane physicochemical properties. These synergistic effects simultaneously improve water permeance, solute rejection, fouling resistance, and structural stability. Given the rapid advancement of COF nanomaterials, this review summarizes progress in COF-based PA nanocomposite membranes for water separation, focusing on COF structural design, incorporation strategies, regulatory mechanisms, and the relationship between membrane structure and separation performance. Critical challenges in interfacial chemistry, scalable fabrication, and long-term stability are discussed, and future research directions toward practical applications are proposed. This review underscores the potential of COF-based PA nanocomposite membranes for efficient and sustainable water purification.
authors: Zhenxiang Pan, Adhithya Patabendige, Jian Sun, Jiang Zhan, Bizhen Zeng, Gang Han

10.1002/adfm.78038.title: Advances in Energy-Driven Atomic-Scale Post-Engineering of Nanomaterials
10.1002/adfm.78038.abstract: ABSTRACT Wet-chemical atomic-scale post-engineering can tailor nanomaterial atomic configurations and upgrade device performance, yet existing reviews only list discrete modification routes without unified energy-centered mechanisms, restricting industrial popularization. This work innovatively classifies all driving forces into chemical potential difference, thermodynamic bonding energy difference, and externally input energy. Around composition modulation, surface engineering, structural reconstruction, and interfacial assembly, the energy-driven rules of each regulation method are elaborated explicitly: chemical potential dominates lattice doping, bonding energies control surface modification, thermodynamic and external field energies induce crystal reconstruction, and weak interactions realize hierarchical nanoassembly. A complete energy mechanism system is built to unify scattered modification strategies. This work further analyzes practical prospects in catalysis, biomedicine, theranostics, and quantum devices, and systematically summarizes the critical obstacles hindering lab-to-industry translation, providing solid theoretical support for the basic research and large-scale industrialization of nanomaterial atomic post-engineering.
authors: Yujia Gao, Naiwen Liu, Wenxia Xu, Suping Li, Bin Li, Lei Wang, Jianping Lai

10.1002/adfm.78039.title: Aggregation-Induced Emission Luminogens (AIEgens): From Intrinsic Therapeutic Effect to Sensitization of Conventional Antitumor Modalities
10.1002/adfm.78039.abstract: ABSTRACT Traditional cancer treatment methods, such as chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, are often limited by poor treatment efficacy, poor targeting, and adverse side effects, as well as intrinsic or acquired drug resistance, which are mainly caused by the complex and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. The development of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) photosensitizers provides a promising strategy to address these challenges. In addition to being high-performance imaging agents, AIE luminogens (AIEgens) have inherent phototherapeutic capabilities, including photodynamic and photothermal effects, which can directly achieve tumor ablation. More importantly, they can act as multifunctional sensitizers to enhance the efficacy of traditional anti-cancer treatments, reverse drug resistance, alleviate tumor hypoxia, and reshape the immune microenvironment. This review summarizes the basic mechanisms and rational design of AIEgens, emphasizing their transformation from independent therapeutic agents to synergistic sensitizers for combined treatment. By combining imaging guidance, intrinsic therapy, and enhanced treatment sensitivity technologies, the AIEgens-based system provides a new model for precise, efficient, and safe integrated tumor diagnosis and treatment, which has profound significance for future clinical applications.

10.1002/adfm.77784.title: Engineering-Free Deterministic Spin-Orbit Torque Switching in Ultrathin Perpendicular Synthetic Antiferromagnets
10.1002/adfm.77784.abstract: ABSTRACT Spin-orbit torque (SOT) offers a promising route for energy-efficient magnetization manipulation in low-power spintronic devices. Synthetic antiferromagnet (SAF) structure, in particular, enhances device performance through ultrafast magnetization switching and magnetic stray-field resilience. However, achieving deterministic SOT switching in perpendicularly magnetized SAFs typically requires an additional in-plane magnetic field or structural engineering to break inversion symmetry, which complicates their practical implementation. Here, we demonstrate field-free deterministic SOT switching in ultra-thin perpendicular SAFs operating at room temperature, designed with a symmetric CoFeB (0.6 nm)/W/CoFeB (0.6 nm) structure. This switching occurs only under antiferromagnetic coupling conditions between the two CoFeB layers, and the switching chirality can be tuned via the spacer layer thickness and temperature. Micromagnetic modeling reveals that symmetry breaking arises intrinsically from the interplay between Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which stabilize the asymmetric Néel-Bloch mixed domain walls of both CoFeB layers. These domain walls manifest as dynamic spin textures with a net chiral driving force, enabling deterministic magnetization switching without the need for external fields or engineered structural asymmetry. Our findings provide a streamlined path toward practical applications of ultrathin SAFs in structurally simplified, fabrication-friendly SOT memory and logic devices.
authors: Wang Yao, Meiling Xu, Yadong Liu, Feiyan Hou, Tao Li, Tai Min

10.1002/adfm.77819.title: Intricate Low Hysteretic Phase Transitions of an Organic Plastic Crystal: Temperature Reliant Mechanical Properties
10.1002/adfm.77819.abstract: ABSTRACT Plastic crystals (PCs) have recently gained renewed interest due to their potential applications in emerging sustainable technologies. PCs, typically characterized by high entropic reversible solid-to-solid phase transitions, facilitate effective energy conversion and can be used as barocaloric materials in refrigeration technologies. However, the intricate relationship between their structure and physical properties associated with the solid-to-solid phase transformations remains underexplored. Moreover, studies focusing on phase transition temperature, hysteresis loop, and mechanical properties are scarce in the literature. Here, we show an ordered crystalline (OC, Phase III) 2-adamantanol (2-Aol) with two extremely low hysteretic reversible solid-to-solid phase transitions, one at 50°C, to a semi-ordered plastic crystal (SOPC) phase (Phase II) and the other at 115.6°C, to a fully re-orientational disordered phase (RD, Phase I). Furthermore, the mechanical properties, obtained using a variable temperature nanoindentation technique, show a significant drop in elastic modulus and hardness upon the OC-to-SOPC (III→II) phase transition, confirming the influence of the reorientational motions of molecules in the high-temperature phase.
authors: Shamim Ahmad, Amit Mondal, Manushree Tanwar, Rajesh Kumar, Chilla Malla Reddy

10.1002/adfm.77868.title: Nereis Jaw-Inspired Pretreatment-Free Direct Metallization on Pristine Polyimide Films for Flexible Electronics
10.1002/adfm.77868.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface metallization of polyimide (PI) films is essential for constructing conductive electrodes and interconnects in flexible electronics, directly determining device integration and reliability. However, the high inertness and low surface energy of PI necessitate complex pretreatment in conventional vacuum deposition, incurring high costs and substrate damage, while wet etching faces environmental burdens and poor compatibility, both failing to meet large-scale manufacturing demands. Inspired by the stable coordination of histidine in Nereis jaws, a coordination-directed molecular design strategy is proposed. By introducing nitrogen-containing heterocyclic units into PI molecular chains, intrinsic metal anchoring sites are constructed, enabling direct film metallization without destructive adhesion-promoting surface pretreatments. This process integrates with photolithography, printing, and direct writing for cross-scale controllable metallization, fabricating planar wiring and vertical interconnect access (VIA) structures for 3D high-density integration. The metallized PI films with azaindole-bearing diamine moieties achieve the highest 5B-grade adhesion and exhibit excellent environmental stability, tolerating repeated bending, high-temperature exposure, and ultrasonic impact. Commercial PI surface metallization can be achieved with minimal functional monomers and is directly compatible with electronic soldering and device integration. This strategy overcomes the trade-off between interfacial adhesion and substrate integrity, providing a viable pathway for scalable flexible electronics manufacturing.
authors: Yulin Li, Fen Zhao, Jianqiao Zhao, Heng Xu, Zhaoshi Yu, Yao Wang, Yi Shen, Jiangnan Dai, Guoli Tu

10.1002/adfm.77952.title: Electrically Conductive but Thermally Insulating PPy-Coated Nonwoven Fabric for Wearable Thermal Management, Electromagnetic Interference Shielding, and Sensing Applications
10.1002/adfm.77952.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible wearable electronics in the 5G/6G era require multifunctional fabrics integrating electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, sensing, electro-thermal conversion, and thermal insulation, yet these properties are inherently incompatible. Herein, we modified the surface of a 2D network in non-woven fabric (NWF) by doping Cl- into PPy (NWF-P-X) through a simple controllable layer-by-layer immersing-polymerization process. The introduction of Cl - -doped PPy shell constructed conductive networks within 2D NWF matrices, resulting in boosted electrical conductivity ( σ ) (65.13 S/m), electro-thermal conversion efficiency, and pressure-responsive sensing performance. The high σ endowed the NWF-P-X with great wide-frequency absorption-dominated EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE). The SET was beyond 25 dB (99.68377% shielding capacity) over 30 MHz-4.5 GHz and beyond 40 dB (99.99% shielding) over 8.0-40.0 GHz. The NWF-P-X also presented a rapid heat response under a low voltage (4.0 V) and a wide temperature range (29.6°C-107.4°C). Moreover, the NWF-P-X exhibited superior thermal insulation performance with low thermal conductivity (0.5537 W∙m −1 ∙K −1 in-plane; 0.0650 W∙m −1 ∙K −1 out-of-plane), where the porous structure and phase interfaces critically enable multifunctional compatibility for EMI protection, thermal management, and sensing applications.
authors: Baoxin Fan, Kang Fu, Cheng Xie, Junye Liao, Junzhe Shang, Liyan Xie, Zidong He, Tong Wu, Guoxiu Tong

10.1002/adfm.77963.title: Heterophase Engineering of Mechanochemically-Synthesised All-Inorganic Ternary Copper Iodide for Tuneable White Light Emission
10.1002/adfm.77963.abstract: ABSTRACT Ternary metal halides have recently emerged as promising optoelectronic materials due to their ambient stability and high photoluminescence quantum yields from the low dimensionality of electronic structures. Their strong exciton-phonon coupling enables broadband self-trapped exciton emission, advantageous for white light-emitting diode (WLED) applications. Particularly, the all-inorganic caesium copper iodide (Cs-Cu-I) system - comprising blue-emitting 0D Cs 3 Cu 2 I 5 and yellow-emitting 1D CsCu 2 I 3 phases - offers a broadband white light emission spectrum with facile chromaticity tunability and emission stability. However, mechanistic understanding of multiphase formation and corresponding multiscale structural information has been limited for Cs-Cu-I, as well as its influence on emission properties. Here, we employ mechanochemical synthesis (MCS) as a solvent-free, time-resolved platform to investigate solid-state reaction pathways by quenching at defined milling times, enabling correlation of structural evolution with photophysical responses. We observe a kinetically accessible formation pathway of a 0D/1D heterophase with a physical interface, with interfacial charge transfer and defect passivation effects that enhance the weakly-emissive 1D phase, from which we designed optimal synthesis routes for 0D/1D heterophase-based colour-conversion device applications. This work establishes a comprehensive structure-emission framework for Cs-Cu-I heterophase system and provides design principles and practical protocols for developing interface engineering in ternary metal-halide emitters in next-generation optoelectronics.
authors: Jaeyoon Cho, Yongjin Kim, Jae Il Kim, Woo Hyeon Jeong, Fan-Cheng Kong, Jeongjae Lee, Kyeong-Yoon Baek, Hyeonmin Choi, Takhee Lee, Philip C. Y. Chow, Bo Ram Lee, Keehoon Kang

10.1002/adfm.77974.title: Thickness-Tailored Magnetic Textures and Spin-Orbit Torque in Antiperovskite Mn3+xSn1-xN
10.1002/adfm.77974.abstract: ABSTRACT In antiperovskite antiferromagnets, film-thickness-modulated interplay between composition and magnetic ordering affords exceptional tunability of spin texture and spin-transport properties. Here, we systematically investigate the thickness-dependent magnetic textures and the spin-orbit torque (SOT) switching mechanism in . Structural and magnetic characterization indicates an evolution of the magnetic texture from non-collinear antiferromagnetic (NC-AFM) to ferrimagnetic with increasing film thickness. This transition is marked by polarity reversal in the anomalous Hall effect at a critical thickness of 25-30 nm. Correspondingly, the SOT switching polarity also reverses, accompanied by distinct field-dependent behaviors: NC-AFM-dominant samples require an in-plane assistant field of 0.3 T to achieve the maximum switching ratio, whereas ferrimagnetic samples require substantially lower fields of 0.03-0.1 T. The switching current density exhibits a non-monotonic thickness dependence, with optimal efficiency achieved at 30 nm. Critically, Joule heating elevates switching temperatures above the magnetic ordering point, indicating that seeded SOT plays a crucial role in the switching process across all thickness regions. These findings provide fundamental insights into the magnetic texture control for the development of high-density and low-power spintronic devices using antiferromagnetic or ferrimagnetic textures.
authors: Haodong Fan, Tingwei Chen, Gan Zhao, Liang Liu, Shiqi Liu, Zhongshu Feng, Yumeng Yang, Yingmei Zhu, Mengxi Wang, Yungui Ma, Tiejun Zhou, Bo Liu

10.1002/adfm.77995.title: Single-Polymer Multi-Valued Logic Enabled by Sequential Electrostatic-to-Electrochemical Doping
10.1002/adfm.77995.abstract: ABSTRACT Multi-valued logic (MVL) offers a promising approach to overcoming the intrinsic limitations of binary computing by enhancing data density at the device level. However, achieving stable and well-defined multi-level logic states within a single semiconductor channel layer remains a significant challenge. In this work, we demonstrate a ternary inverter based on a two-step doping mechanism in a single polymer semiconductor channel incorporated into an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT). The device exhibits a robust intermediate conduction state characterized by zero-differential transconductance (ZDT). The face-on molecular orientation and dense alkyl side-chain packing initially impede ion penetration, giving rise to surface-confined electrostatic gating at low gate voltages ( V G ), before transitioning to bulk volumetric electrochemical doping at higher V G . This sequential doping mechanism yields a wide and stable ZDT plateau, an effect that is less pronounced in polymer semiconductors adopting edge-on orientations or amorphous microstructures. This work highlights the critical role of molecular orientation and side-chain packing in realizing distinct multi-level logic states, offering design guidelines for MVL circuits.
authors: Dong Hyun Park, Min Su Kim, Jae Hyun Han, Seung Hyun Baek, Kyu Yeon Kim, Jin-Kyun Lee, Jiyoul Lee, Keun Hyung Lee

10.1002/adfm.78000.title: Tetracyclic π-Extended Multi-Resonant TADF Emitters for Green PSF-OLEDs With 37.7% EQE and BT.2020-Compatible Top-Emitting Devices
10.1002/adfm.78000.abstract: ABSTRACT In phosphorescence/TADF-sensitized fluorescence (PSF/TSF) OLEDs, the use of multi-resonance (MR) emitters as terminal emitters enables the simultaneous achievement of high color purity and high device efficiency. However, achieving both properties simultaneously remains a significant challenge. Herein, we developed a series of green MR-TADF emitters, namely Ph-DBF, Me-NapBF , and Ph-NapBF , by expanding the peripheral planarity of the B/N emitting unit through the incorporation of a tetracyclic naphtho[2,3-b]benzofuran structure. This enhanced rigidity suppresses structural deviations in the excited state, resulting in narrow full-widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of <23 nm and near-unity photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs). Linear extension of π-delocalization through aromatic rings bathochromically shifts the emission and strengthens the absorption bands, concurrently increasing the molar extinction coefficient (ε), a critical factor influencing the exciton-harvesting efficiency of terminal emitters. The increased ε values of these emitters enabled bottom-emitting PSF-OLEDs with external quantum efficiencies up to 37.7% ( Ph-NapBF ) and 35.5% ( Me-NapBF ), maintaining 33.3% and 30.9% at 1000 cd m −2 , respectively. Furthermore, the corresponding top-emitting OLEDs exhibited pure green emission with CIE(x,y) coordinates of (0.17, 0.79), meeting the BT.2020 green color standard, and achieved a high current efficiency of 277.2 cd A −1 .
authors: Eo Jin Jeon, Truong Thi Thuy, Nikita Abitkar, Paramasivam Palanisamy, Jiheon Kim, Myungsun Sim, Athithan Maheshwaran, Jang Hyuk Kwon

10.1002/adfm.78006.title: Spin-State Modulation of Cobalt Centers for Boosting Electrochemical Ammonia Synthesis
10.1002/adfm.78006.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional low-spin Co 3 O 4 suffers from weak orbital hybridization with oxygenates ( * NO x and * H 2 O), leading to slow reaction kinetics for ammonia synthesis during electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO 3 RR). Herein, we demonstrate the precise spin-state engineering of octahedral Co 3+ sites in spinel Co 3 O 4 through a facile yet effective thermally induced lattice distortion. Spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal this lattice distortion reshapes the localized d-orbital energy levels, thereby fundamentally driving a transition from the thermodynamically stable low-spin configuration to a highly active high-spin state. Mechanistically, the unpaired e g electrons of high-spin Co 3+ strengthen orbital hybridization with oxygen-containing intermediates ( * NO x and * H 2 O). This enhanced binding not only promotes the adsorption and cleavage of these species but also ensures a sustained supply of protons via accelerated water dissociation, thereby synergistically accelerating the NO 3 RR toward NH 3 . Consequently, the optimized high-spin Co 3 O 4 delivers an exceptional Faradaic efficiency of 93.36% and an NH 3 yield rate of 1.17 mmol/h/cm 2 . Moreover, techno-economic analysis shows a two-electrode membrane-electrode assembly (MEA) reactor coupling NO 3 RR with GOR (NO 3 RR//GOR) enables favorable economic performance with a total revenue of 7651 USD/t NH 3 . This work presents a facile synthetic route toward highly active electrocatalysts via distortion-driven spin-state regulation, providing a promising strategy for sustainable electrochemical ammonia synthesis.
authors: Shixuan Ge, Xinxin Fu, Peiyang Li, Xiaoyong Wu, Yangyang Zhang, Zhongyi Liu, Bin Liu, Jun Li

10.1002/adfm.78011.title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution of 2D Templates Enables Synchronized Crystallization and Efficient Charge Extraction in Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78011.abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving uniform crystallization across the entire film depth remains a critical challenge in the two-step fabrication of perovskite films, where mismatched crystallization rates between the top and bottom regions often result in structural heterogeneity. Here, we develop a spatio-temporally evolved 2D template-assisted strategy by incorporating meta -fluorophenethylammonium iodide ( m -F-PEAI) into the PbI 2 precursor solution to enhance the perovskite film quality via a two-step solution method. The in situ formed ( m -F-PEA) 2 PbI 4 2D perovskite redirects the thermodynamic phase transformation by providing a coherent crystallographic framework that synchronizes crystallization kinetics along the vertical direction. Furthermore, this 2D perovskite serves as a spatio-temporal template: it directs monolithic grain growth during crystallization, while the residual 2D perovskite remains at grain boundaries in the final film. By modifying the local potential landscape, the 2D perovskite facilitates charge extraction, overcoming the charge-blocking behavior associated with traditional passivating layers. It synergistically works with the monolithic grains to enable efficient macroscopic charge transport rather than merely passivating defects. As a result, the template-assisted devices exhibit improvement in photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.03% with an anti-reflective film. Moreover, the unencapsulated devices demonstrate improved storage stability under N 2 and dry-air conditions, along with enhanced operational stability.
authors: Chuiyu Li, Quanfeng Li, Qingbao Zhao, Xinqian Xie, Xiang Hong, Songwang Yang

10.1002/adfm.78017.title: Crystalline Triazine/Heptazine-Based Carbon Nitride With Built-in Electric Field for Synergistic Photoproduction of Hydrogen Peroxide and Xylose Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.78017.abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic coupling of biomass oxidation with H 2 O 2 production offers a sustainable route for solar-to-chemical conversion, but its efficiency is limited by slow charge separation and surface reactions. Herein, we report a KCl-assisted co-precipitation-calcination method to synthesize highly crystalline carbon nitride (MCAK) featuring a triazine/heptazine-coupled framework and surface-enriched atomic K dispersion. This unique structure introduces cyano defects and creates a strong built-in electric field that reduces the exciton binding energy from 116.50 meV (bulk carbon nitride, BCN) to 74.57 meV, thereby promoting charge separation. As a result, MCAK achieves an exceptional H 2 O 2 production rate of 12470.4 µmol/(g × h) under white light in O 2 -50.6 and 37.8 times higher than that of BCN and supramolecular carbon nitride (MCA), respectively-with negligible decay in air. Simultaneously, it oxidizes xylose to xylonic acid with 73.3% selectivity. Mechanism studies reveal that the performance originates from enhanced O 2 adsorption and an optimized two-electron oxygen reduction pathway driven by the built-in electric field. This work demonstrates a synergistic design strategy that integrates crystallinity control, intramolecular heterojunction engineering, and built-in field intensification for efficient bifunctional photocatalysis.
authors: Yufei Chen, Weitong Wang, Ningyu He, Xinyin Zhang, Mengyue Niu, Binghan Zhou, Subing Zhao, Xiaojun Song, Fuli Mu, Kaixuan Li, Xue Xia, Jimin Du, Zehao Li

10.1002/adfm.78030.title: Upcycling Spent LiMn2O4 into High-Performance LiMnxFe1-xPO4 Cathodes Via Synergistic Leaching Followed by Direct Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.78030.abstract: ABSTRACT Improper disposal of spent lithium-ion batteries causes environmental pollution and resource waste. Conventional recycling of low-cost LiMn 2 O 4 (LMO) involves complex, multi-step processes including leaching, extraction, separation, precipitation and resynthesis, leading to poor environmental and economic viability. Herein, a novel upcycling strategy is proposed, where spent LMO is directly converted into high-performance LiMn x Fe 1- x PO 4 (LMFP) cathodes through a H 3 PO 4 -ascorbic acid synergistic leaching followed by direct regeneration. Concretely, H 3 PO 4 serves as both a leaching agent and phosphorus source, while ascorbic acid acts as an auxiliary leaching agent with reducing and complexing capabilities. Their synergistic action ensures efficient Li/Mn leaching, and the resulted leached solution is subjected to solvothermal synthesis followed by calcination to upcycle olivine-structured LMFP. By introducing Macrogol 400 as a surfactant, the uniformity of the Fe-Mn precursor is improved, and a 3D conductive carbon network is constructed to accelerate the transportation of lithium-ion and electron. Consequently, the regenerated LMFP exhibits outstanding electrochemical performance, achieving a specific discharge capacity of 140.72 mAh g −1 at 1 C and 87.31% capacity retention after 1000 cycles. Economic assessment reveals a profit of 4.850$ kg −1 of spent LMO. This study provides a new approach for the green and short upcycling of spent cathode materials.
authors: Jinping Shuai, Xinxi Duan, Bo Xu, Fagen Zhou, Kehong Li, Shuoying Lv, Dong Wang, Guangsheng Huang, Minyu He, Weizao Liu, Xuewei Lv

10.1002/adfm.78034.title: Electrical Tuning of Ferrimagnetic Spin Alignment Angle and Compensation Temperature in Pt/IrMn3/CoGd Multilayers
10.1002/adfm.78034.abstract: ABSTRACT Compensation temperature ( T M ) is a characteristic parameter for a ferrimagnetic (FIM) material that requires careful consideration in the functional applications of FIM spintronics. Attempts at precise and localized control of T M have remained rare and challenging, but apparently a worthy issue for the expansion of spintronics to include FIMs. Conventional approaches such as thermal annealing or ion injection suffer from limited spatial selectivity and switching speed. Here, we show a novel route to control the T M of FIM by manipulating the alignments of the constituent spins through spin-orbit torque (SOT)-controlled exchange couplings with adjacent antiferromagnets. At the interface between antiferromagnetic IrMn 3 and FIM CoGd multilayers, it was found that the antiferromagnet established firm exchange couplings with Co atoms, but negligible couplings with Gd. Such selective coupling modified the traditionally known collinear antiparallel arrangement of CoGd spins into a noncollinear spiral spin configuration, and the T M was found to correspondingly change significantly. Additionally, precise tuning of FIM properties through the modulation of SOT amplitude and application time was demonstrated, establishing an efficient electrical pathway for controlling the compensation phenomena in ferrimagnetic systems.
authors: Won-Chang Choi, Tae-Bo Sim, Kwonjin Park, Tae-Hwan Kim, Soobeom Lee, Bao Xuan Tran, Soojung Kim, Chun-Yeol You, Jung-Il Hong

10.1002/adfm.78050.title: Bioinspired Oxygen Functional Group Density Governs Hydrovoltaic Energy Harvesting for Soil-Moisture-Driven Plant Monitoring
10.1002/adfm.78050.abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrovoltaic generators convert ambient water flow into electricity, yet their power output has plateaued for lack of a quantitative link between surface chemistry and electrokinetic performance. Here we identify oxygen functional group density as that missing descriptor. The design is inspired by plant root cell walls, where oxygen-rich ─COOH and ─OH groups electrostatically recruit mobile cations to drive nutrient uptake. We translate this chemical logic into a Cellulose-scaffolded Oxygen-functionalized Hydrovoltaic Generator (CO-HyGEN), pairing a long-fiber Hanji cellulose scaffold with a graphene oxide interface. Across a graded series of carbon architectures, physicochemical, surface-electronic, and electrochemical signatures converge on a consistent picture: zeta potential, work function, hydrovoltaic output, and charge-storage response exhibit systematic dependence on the oxygen functional group density. Beyond passive wettability, the oxygen-rich graphene oxide interface behaves as an electrochemically active participant rather than an inert conduit, strengthening the electrical double layer through denser electrostatic recruitment of counterions, consistent with its more negative zeta potential and higher work function. Deployed around the root zone of a living plant, CO-HyGEN arrays autonomously harvest soil moisture to power wireless Bluetooth sensing, demonstrating a plant-electronics symbiosis that extends interface-engineered hydrovoltaics toward bio-integrated energy systems.
authors: Sunmin Jang, Sumin Cho, Joo Sung Kim, Soban Ali Shah, Donghan Lee, Yu-seop Kim, Jisoo Oh, Kwanggyu Hyun, Sunghoon Lee, Takao Someya, Jihoon Chung, Hyun Chan Kim, Dongwhi Choi, Hee Jae Hwang

10.1002/adfm.77436.title: Gradient-Engineered Separator for Room Temperature Sodium-Sulfur Batteries: Enabling Effective Polysulfides Conversion and Uniform Sodium Deposition
10.1002/adfm.77436.abstract: ABSTRACT Room temperature sodium-sulfur (RT Na-S) batteries are promising for energy storage, yet suffer from polysulfide shuttling and sodium dendrite issues. Herein, we report a gradient-engineered separator asymmetrically coated with ZIF-67 and ZnF 2 on a polypropylene membrane to address both interfacial issues. On the cathode side, the ZIF-67 layer acts as a “catalytic trap”, providing physical confinement of polysulfides through its microporous structure and chemical adsorption via Co-S bonding, while its Co sites catalytically accelerate polysulfide redox conversion at the cathode interface. On the anode side, the ZnF 2 layer functions as an “ion regulator”, homogenizing Na + flux across the anode interface through its polar surface and inducing the formation of a mechanically robust, NaF-rich solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) that effectively suppresses dendrite penetration. This integrated gradient design enables exceptional electrochemical performance, achieving stable sodium plating/stripping for over 2000 h at 1.0 mA cm −2 and a high reversible capacity of 1476 mA h g −1 at 0.1C in Na-S full cells with 76% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 0.5C. This work demonstrates that a gradient-engineered separator, via simultaneously optimizing the cathode and anode interfaces, provides a powerful strategy for developing safe, high-performance RT Na-S batteries.
authors: Junshu Wu, Ting Lei, Yuhao Xiang, He Zhao, Yi Zeng, Maowen Xu, Yuruo Qi

10.1002/adfm.77687.title: Mono-Material Polydisulfides for Pressure Sensitive Adhesive Tapes With Closed-Loop Recyclability
10.1002/adfm.77687.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional PSAs are multi-layer materials that contain numerous additives, rendering them non-recyclable. Efforts to develop more sustainable PSAs have predominantly focused on the adhesive layer with less attention toward the backing layer, which is typically a petroleum-derived plastic. Herein, we report a strategy to create “mono-material” PSA tapes from biogenic polydisulfide copolymers where both the plastic backing and adhesive layer are chemically recyclable. The copolymerization of α-lipoic acid and its ester derivative, ethyl lipoate, yields high-molecular-weight polydisulfides ( M w > 400 kDa) with low glass transition temperatures (<−30 °C) and unique viscoelastic properties including extremely low moduli (<100 kPa) and exceptional adhesion strength (peel capacity > 400 N·m − 1 ) which was superior to commercial PSA tapes. The adhesive copolymer was treated with an alkaline solution to form a non-adhesive ionomer congener that was 1000-fold stiffer with plastic-like mechanical properties. The ionomer backing and elastomeric adhesive layer were adhered without additives or compatibilizers to form a complete PSA tape. Furthermore, the entire tape was depolymerized to recover the original monomeric components and repolymerized to afford materials with comparable properties. These discoveries establish a fully closed-loop, additive-free PSA platform in which both the adhesive layer and backing originate from a single dynamic polymer.
authors: Woojung Ham, Tyler M. Witt, Charles M. Hui, Joshua C. Worch

10.1002/adfm.77695.title: A High-Strength, Moldable, and Sustainable Bioplastic Enabled by Water-Mediated Dual-Bond Reconstruction and Crystal Structure Deformation
10.1002/adfm.77695.abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental pressures from petrochemical plastics have accelerated the search for sustainable, biomass-derived materials. However, current research predominantly relies on energy-intensive, complex bottom-up fabrication processes, often yielding bioplastics with insufficient mechanical properties, poor processability, and limited thermal stability. This study reports a water-mediated strategy based on crystal structure deformation and a proposed dual-bond network comprising reconstructed hydrogen bonds and possible aldehyde-mediated covalent or hemiacetal/acetal-type interactions to transform natural wood into a lightweight, high-strength, acid-resistant, organic solvent-resistant, thermally stable, transparent, and recyclable bioplastic (referred to as plasticized wood). This strategy employs alkaline treatment and oxidant activation to disrupt crystalline cellulose, while water enhances chain mobility and reactivity and may facilitate aldehyde-hydroxyl bonding interactions during hot pressing. Subsequent water removal reconstructs the hydrogen-bond network, while spectroscopic changes indirectly support possible aldehyde-mediated network strengthening. The resulting plasticized wood exhibits exceptional mechanical properties, achieving a longitudinal tensile strength of ∼250 MPa and a flexural strength of ∼85 MPa, together with stability, recyclability, chemical degradability, and clear degradation behavior under soil-burial conditions. This work provides a sustainable pathway for biomass valorization and highlights plasticized wood as a viable and environmentally friendly alternative to conventional plastics.
authors: Lanxin Xue, Xianxian Lin, Zhulin Li, Shuaiming He, Yiqiang Wu

10.1002/adfm.77732.title: Gradient Defect Architecture for Ultrahigh Energy Storage in Lead-Free Relaxor Ferroelectrics
10.1002/adfm.77732.abstract: ABSTRACT Next-generation pulsed power electronics demand miniaturized dielectric capacitors with exceptional energy density. However, achieving this remains challenged by the intrinsic trade-off between polarization capability and dielectric breakdown strength in lead-free perovskites. Here, we overcome this fundamental limit via a “gradient defect architecture” strategy that constructs a heterogeneous architecture comprising a highly polarization disordered surface layer and a relatively ordered polarization interior within a 0.88Bi 0.48 Na 0.48 Ba 0.04 TiO 3- 0.12Sm 1/3 NbO 3 ceramic. Crucially, by geometrically modulating the volume fraction of these functional layers, the optimized ceramic achieves an ultrahigh recoverable energy density of 22.3 J cm −3 under an ultrahigh electric field of 1840 kV cm −1 . The disordered surface layer acts as a robust charge-blocking barrier to elevate breakdown strength, while the highly polarizable relaxor interior layer sustains a strong polarization response to secure high energy capacity. These findings establish a generic design paradigm for utilizing intrinsic manufacturing gradients to transcend geometric scaling limits, offering a viable pathway for developing high-performance energy storage materials.
authors: Weisan Fang, Xiaoming Shi, Junlin Wu, Jiecheng Liu, Qin Feng, Changlai Yuan, He Qi

10.1002/adfm.77756.title: Rejuvenated Mitochondria Restore Metabolic Plasticity to Orchestrate Angio-Osteogenic Coupling for Osteoporotic Bone Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.77756.abstract: ABSTRACT Impaired synergistic crosstalk between angiogenesis and osteogenesis, accompanied by subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction, constitutes a critical barrier to achieving effective bone regeneration under osteoporotic conditions. However, available strategies that exploit mitochondrial dynamics as a regulatory node to guide regenerative outcomes remain largely unexplored. Here, we developed a multifunctional layered double hydroxide (LDH) based nanohybrid incorporating dexamethasone (DEX) and metformin (MET), denoted as DEX@LDH/MET, which induced a rejuvenation like mitochondrial state in bone mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and reprogrammed cytoskeletal organization via septin 7 (SEPT7) GTPase activation. This coordinated regulation enabled suppression of dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1) mediated mitochondrial fission, thereby driving mitochondrial metabolic plasticity characterized by structural integrity, mitochondrial membrane potential, and mitochondrial homeostasis. Functionally, engineered mitochondria (eMITO), derived from BMSCs treated with DEX@LDH/MET, were transferable to vascular endothelial cells (VECs) and thus enhanced their proliferation and angiogenic activity. In an ovariectomy induced osteoporosis model, this intercellular mitochondrial transfer strategy markedly promoted vascularization and restored trabecular bone microarchitecture. Overall, this study establishes a cytoskeleton constrained mitochondrial regulatory framework for organelle engineering and intercellular mitochondrial transplantation, positioning mitochondrial rejuvenation as a targetable mechanism for organelle level regenerative therapy.
authors: Huiyi Yang, Bianbian Zhao, Tao Chen, Xu Zhu, Xiao Hu, Simin Song, Zhibo Liu, Zhaojie Wang, Rongrong Zhu, Liming Cheng

10.1002/adfm.77809.title: Vector-Field Control and Emergent Basal-Plane Anisotropy of Magnetic Textures in Noncentrosymmetric (Fe0.63Ni0.3Pd0.07)3P
10.1002/adfm.77809.abstract: ABSTRACT ( is a room-temperature magnet with symmetry that hosts a rich variety of topological spin textures. Here, we report a combined resonant small-angle x-ray scattering and ptychography study of ( in vector magnetic fields over a broad temperature range. We demonstrate deterministic vector-field control of magnetic stripe domains, where in-plane fields continuously rotate their orientation via a transition from a chiral stripe to an achiral fan configuration. Furthermore, at 50 K and below, the stripe orientation becomes metastably pinned and retains its field-trained direction. While the magnitude of the wavevector is nearly isotropic within the basal plane at room temperature, a pronounced temperature evolution of anisotropic interactions emerges upon cooling. In particular, non-trivial anisotropy axes develop at 20-50 K reflecting the combined effects of magnetocrystalline anisotropy, anisotropic exchange, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), whose effective orientation is found to rotate with temperature. These results establish ( as a model system for vector-field control of chiral spin textures and reveal a previously unrecognized temperature-driven evolution of the effective DMI landscape in a noncentrosymmetric magnet.
authors: Victor Ukleev, Oleg I. Utesov, Lorenzo Ubilla, Chen Luo, Radu-Marius Abrudan, Peter Wild, Holger Kropf, Moritz Winter, Sebastian Schneider, Alexander Tahn, Bernd Rellinghaus, Tim A.
