In the end, this review concludes with the current challenges and future perspectives of multi-functional hemostatic materials.
authors: Shuxuan Zhang, Yuxin Liang, Rong Zhu, Xiaoxuan Tang, Chang He, Xiaoling Jin, Xinyue Sun, Shaofang Zhang, Yun Qian, Yumin Yang, Jue Ling

10.1002/adfm.79037.title: All-Sputtered Oxide n-p Heterojunction Anti-Ambipolar Transistors for Semantic Segmentation Networks
10.1002/adfm.79037.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic vision provides an efficient route for extracting meaningful information from visual inputs and supporting intelligent perception in dynamic environments. However, visual scenes acquired under excessive or insufficient illumination often contain distorted contrast, weakened boundary information, and shifted input distributions, which degrade semantic segmentation accuracy before network computation. Conventional synaptic or neuromorphic hardware systems usually require additional normalization or preprocessing steps to compensate for such input distortion, limiting the direct integration of signal regulation at the device level. In this work, an all-sputtered oxide anti-ambipolar transistor (AAT) based on an IGZO/TeSeO x heterojunction is introduced as a device-level preprocessing element for illumination-robust neuromorphic vision. IGZO/TeSeO x AAT exhibits a well-defined Gaussian-like anti-ambipolar transfer characteristic, with a peak-to-valley current ratio of 1.17 × 10 3 and a maximum negative transconductance of −240.8 nS, enabling effective attenuation of excessive input signals. The resulting Gaussian-like anti-ambipolar response is used to construct Gaussian smoothing and Laplacian of Gaussian filtering kernels. Applied to semantic segmentation under overexposed and underexposed conditions, the proposed preprocessing scheme improves pixel-wise classification consistency and achieves 86.1% pixel accuracy.
authors: Hojeong Jo, Donghyun Kang, Seungwoo Baek, SeongCheol Jang, Wangmyung Choi, San Nam, Hyunho Jang, Hocheon Yoo, Yong-Hoon Kim, Hyun-Suk Kim

10.1002/adfm.79084.title: Hydrogen-Bonded Supramolecular Networks of Carboxyl-Functionalized Hexaazatriphenylene for Ultradurable Aqueous Proton Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79084.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous proton batteries offer rapid proton transport kinetics and cost-effectiveness, yet imine-based electrode materials suffer from low active-site utilization, sluggish kinetics, and electrolyte dissolution. Herein, we design and synthesize hexaazatriphenylene-hexacarboxylic acid (HATN-6COOH), whose abundant carboxyl groups construct a hydrogen-bonded supramolecular architecture that simultaneously addresses these limitations through three synergistic mechanisms: (i) electron-withdrawing modulation of the electronic structure, (ii) construction of efficient proton transport pathways via the Grotthuss mechanism, and (iii) suppression of active-material dissolution through supramolecular stabilization. Consequently, HATN-6COOH delivers a high specific capacity of 201 mAh g − 1 at 0.5 A g − 1 , outstanding rate capability (89.1% retention at 10 A g − 1 ), and exceptional cycling stability (90.4% retention after 30 000 cycles at 5 A g − 1 ). Operando Raman, ex situ XPS, and FTIR analyses confirm reversible H + storage at C═N sites, with the carboxyl C═O groups remaining inactive under the operating potential window, while dissolution tests verify that the hydrogen-bonded network effectively prevents active-material leaching in strong acidic electrolytes. A HATN-6COOH//MnO 2 full cell retains 82.6% capacity after 30 000 cycles, validating practical applicability. This work proposes a promising molecular design strategy for high-performance organic batteries via rational supramolecular engineering.
authors: Yilin Zhao, Bin Feng, Wei Wang, Yiqian Shi, Yiming Zhao, Qing-Yun Guo, Aimin Ge

10.1002/adfm.79086.title: In Vivo Dynamic-Torque Driven DNA Manipulation via a Magnetic Micromotor
10.1002/adfm.79086.abstract: ABSTRACT The biological environment in vivo is complex, posing a great challenge for the deployment of DNA nanostructure-based precision nanomedicine. Despite the development of DNA nanostructures responsive to environmental cues, it remains difficult to manipulate DNA with spatiotemporal precision in vivo. Here, inspired by the mechanical unwinding process of DNA in nature, we propose an in vivo dynamic-torque driven DNA manipulation strategy enabling DNA structural reconfigurations with minute-scale temporal resolution and centimeter spatial precision. By coupling the rod-shaped magnetic micromotors (MMs) with a rotating magnetic field (RMF), this strategy enables mechanical DNA manipulation under a low field strength of 20 mT and extends the working distance by an order of magnitude compared to conventional manipulation methods. By orchestrating the RMF frequency, DNA with distinct force thresholds (12-54 pN) and GC contents (22%-100%) can be manipulated precisely. Ultimately, by introducing this strategy in biological systems, a theoretical torque of more than 76.6 nN·nm (an equivalent force of 85.2 pN) can be exerted in the tumor within 5 minutes, therefore manipulating DNA in cellular systems and in vivo efficiently and opening new avenues for precise nanomedicine in complex biological environments.
authors: Xiaolei Chen, Yingying Wang, Yuan Li, Li Peng, Jiaqi Yuan, Zhenguang Li, Yunhe Zhao, Xinjian Fan, Cheng Lv, Yu Cheng

10.1002/adfm.78985.title: Engineering Biohybrid Mycelium Fibers through Hierarchical Structuring and Biomineralization
10.1002/adfm.78985.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineered living materials (ELMs) that utilize fungal cells have emerged as a class of functional materials, owing to their ability to self-assemble, adapt, and regenerate. Filamentous fungi growth promotes the formation of a network of interwoven threads, or mycelia, that is of rising interest as a sustainable and versatile material; however, broader application is constrained by comparatively lower strength than synthetic or natural materials. In order to develop mechanical strength, strategies from nature, such as structural hierarchy and mineralization, are leveraged in the material design. In this study, a bioink composed of alginate and a modified strain of the filamentous fungus Aspergillus niger capable of silica mineralization is extruded to create fibers of interconnected mycelium. After fiber incubation, fungal cells exhibit radial hyphal growth extending from the core fiber, which can be tuned by capillary force alignment. Mineralization demonstrates approximately double the stiffness and strength of dried mycelium fibers. Further, twisted and braided fibers exhibit a two- to three-fold increase in elongation at break compared to single fibers. The results show that mycelium morphology and mechanical properties can be tuned through mineralization, growth conditions, and processing.
authors: Olivia Pear, Jenna Stanislaw, Alexander Luce, Taylor Donen, Kelly Balch, R. Kōnane Bay

10.1002/adfm.78986.title: A Miniaturized Autonomous Thermomagnetic Generator
10.1002/adfm.78986.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermomagnetic generators (TMG) are promising devices for converting low-grade waste heat into electricity. Self-actuation using permanent magnets is the key to autonomy. Tailoring thermomagnetic materials in the form of flexible and freestanding films is a way toward high power-density through fast, and efficient heat transfer. Design optimization, and the use of micromagnets represent a unique opportunity toward miniaturization. Here, the operation and performance of a TMG using a flexible freestanding Gd film as the active substance, and an array of NdFeB micromagnets as field source is presented. The Gd film self oscillates under the effect of the magnetic field gradient, entering in contact with the heat source, and the heat sink alternatively. At an operating frequency of Hz, a designed piezoelectric spring converts the mechanical oscillation into electrical energy, reaching up to power-output with temperature difference. The magnetic field gradient acting over the thermal switch, and triggering the caloric response of this thick Gd film, is generated by an array of thick NdFeB micromagnets, which produces a T variation in field strength over a gap. The power density normalized to the combined volume of the Gd film and of the magnet reaches up to .
authors: Morgan Almanza, Doan Nguyen Ba, Nesrine Belkadi, Erika Fontana, Jean-Eudes Duvauchelle, Sukhendu Sadhukhan, Loïc Becerra, Thibaut Devillers, Massimiliano Marangolo, Fabien Parrain, Nora M. Dempsey, Martino LoBue

10.1002/adfm.78890.title: Electron-Sponge S-Scheme Heterojunctions via Mo-N Bridging Enable Highly Selective Photocatalytic CO2 Methanation
10.1002/adfm.78890.abstract: ABSTRACT The kinetic limitations of multi-electron transfer present a fundamental challenge to achieve selective CO 2 photoreduction to CH 4 . This work pioneers an interface electron-flux intensification strategy by constructing a Mo-N-bridged S-scheme phosphomolybdic acid (PMA)/carbon nitride (CN) heterojunction synergistically coupled with the electron-sponge functionality of PMA, directing charge transfer and electron utilization pathways. PMA/CN-2 materials exhibit remarkable CO 2 -to-CH 4 conversion rate of 20.76 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 , representing a 148.3-fold over CN (0.14 µmol·g −1 ·h −1 ), while the CH 4 selectivity sharply rises from 6.37% (CN) to 98.95% (PMA/CN-2). X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) and femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TAS) spectroscopy reveal that N-Mo-O 5 coordination environment can regulate interfacial charge kinetics triggering ultrafast migration and consequent accumulation of photo-induced electrons. Furthermore, in situ measurement, Gibbs’ energy changes and crystal orbital Hamilton populations (COHP) analysis elucidates the electronic modulation of Mo centers in Mo-N-bridged PMA/CN heterojunction contributes to enhanced bonding with *CH 3 O at Mo-O 5 active sites for accelerating CH 4 generation. This manuscript establishes a foundational strategy for engineering atomically bridged S-scheme heterojunctions with regulated electron dynamics, advancing the development of artificial photosynthesis systems for selective CO 2 -to-fuel conversion.
authors: Jintao Dong, Zhishuai Wang, Yi Zhang, Chang Ma, Hailong Chen, Shengqun Cao, Bin Wang, Yixuan Gao, Huaming Li, Jiexiang Xia, Hongwei Huang

10.1002/adfm.79060.title: Heterojunction-Associated Low-Coordinated Copper Sites Enable pH-Asymmetric Paired Electrolysis of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
10.1002/adfm.79060.abstract: ABSTRACT Paired electrolysis of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) enables the concurrent production of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) and 2,5-bishydroxymethylfuran (BHMF) as polymer precursors in an energy-efficient manner. Its practical implementation is hindered by the scarcity of paired electrodes that can operate under disparate anodic/cathodic environments, as well as by limited process-level understanding for pH-asymmetric paired operation. Here, potential-directed partial reconstruction of a common Cu 2 O nanowire scaffold generates anodic LC-Cu 2 O/CuO and cathodic LC-Cu/Cu 2 O electrodes. Atomic-resolution microscopy and x-ray absorption spectroscopy collectively reveal heterojunction-containing mixed-valence frameworks enriched in low-coordinated Cu sites. Operando Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical measurements, and density functional theory calculations further reveal that on the anode, HMF adsorption is promoted and the regeneration of Cu III species is accelerated, while on the cathode, water dissociation is enhanced to produce reactive hydrogen, collectively facilitating the overall HMF conversion. Integrating LC-Cu 2 O/CuO and LC-Cu/Cu 2 O into a pH-asymmetric cell verifies the superiority of a reinforced cation-exchange membrane over a bipolar membrane in reducing the cross-membrane potential drop, delivering a combined products Faradaic efficiency of 182.1%, an energy efficiency of 21.9%, and 100 h stability with suppressed products crossover. This work bridges electrode engineering and pH-asymmetric device design, advancing paired electrolysis toward practical biomass electrorefining.
authors: Pengfei Li, Tuxin Huang, Yuge Sun, Junhao Wang, Xiaopeng Feng, Xuan Guo, Ziheng Cui, Fenghui Ye, Yunming Fang

10.1002/adfm.79021.title: Light-Directed Molecular-to-Device Perspective in Azobenzene-Based Liquid Crystalline Soft Materials
10.1002/adfm.79021.abstract: ABSTRACT Azobenzene is a prototypical photoresponsive molecule that undergoes reversible trans -to- cis isomerization upon light irradiation, accompanied by substantial changes in dipole moment, molecular geometry, and intermolecular interactions. These photoinduced molecular-level transformations can be amplified across hierarchical liquid crystal (LC) assemblies, enabling precise control of mesophase transitions, structural alignment, and macroscopic material properties. Recent advances in molecular engineering have extended the role of azobenzene from simple molecular switches to versatile building blocks for hierarchically ordered and reconfigurable soft materials. This review highlights how the incorporation of azobenzene into nematic, smectic, columnar, and helical LC mesophases enables tunable optical, mechanical, electrochemical, and energy-related responses. Emerging applications are discussed across various fields, including smart windows with dynamic light modulation, polarization-dependent optical sensors, light-driven soft robotic actuators, and molecular solar thermal storage systems. By connecting fundamental photochemical mechanisms with device-level performance, azobenzene-LC systems demonstrate how molecular-level responsiveness can be translated into programmable, multifunctional, and scalable materials. This review provides an integrated molecular-to-device perspective on the design principles, current challenges, and future opportunities in azobenzene-based liquid crystal systems, with the aim of stimulating future advances in light-controlled soft matter technologies.
authors: Mintaek Oh, Yu-Jin Choi, Minwoo Rim, Dae-Yoon Kim, Kwang-Un Jeong

10.1002/adfm.79029.title: PGM-Free Catalysts for Oxygen Evolution Reaction for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
10.1002/adfm.79029.abstract: ABSTRACT Proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) holds a promise for large-scale and highly efficient hydrogen production through electrocatalytic water splitting. Its widespread commercial adoption, however, is hindered by its reliance on expensive and scarce platinum group metals (PGMs) as the electrode catalyst materials. This is particularly the case at the PEMWE anode where the costly iridium is required to promote oxygen evolution reaction (OER). This article provides a brief review of the recent progresses and challenges in searching for PGM-free OER catalysts as the low-cost replacement of PGM catalysts, as well as our perspectives on future research directions from rational catalyst design to their potential industrial deployment.
authors: Shichen Guo, Minghao Xie, Chukwunwike O. Iloeje, Di-Jia Liu

10.1002/adfm.78981.title: Architecting Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Bioelectronics: From Channel Micro-Engineering to Microarray Systems
10.1002/adfm.78981.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) have emerged as transformative devices that revolutionize next-generation electronics to bridge ionic/electronic signaling at the interface between biological and microelectronic systems. This review systematically explores fundamental breakthroughs in OECT channel material engineering and device manufacturing across micro/nanoscales for emerging bioelectronic systems, emphasizing microarchitecture design and patterning strategies that unlock advantages including enhanced transistor performance, high speed, improved mechanical durability, high-fidelity integration, as well as biocompatibility. We first briefly introduce the device physics underpinning OECTs and state-of-the-art material innovations, focusing on nanostructure-dominated mixed ionic-electronic conduction. Subsequently, we elaborate on tailored microscale channel architectures, encompassing 1D fibers, 2D micro/nanoporous films, and 3D soft hydrogel networks to address both electronic and mechanical challenges. Furthermore, we highlight advances in scalable fabrication techniques such as printing/photolithography-based approaches and vertical architectures for developing high-density flexible OECT arrays. In addition, diverse bioelectronic applications are summarized, including biosensing, signal processing, implantable biointerfaces, and brain-inspired computing, demonstrating the versatility of OECTs. The discussion concludes by outlining future directions to enhance device reliability and scalability, addressing critical challenges such as material stability and integration complexity. Through this comprehensive analysis, we provide a roadmap for advancing OECT micro/nanotechnology, inspiring future research and accelerating its adoption in bioelectronics.
authors: Mahroza Kanwal Khan, Yinghui Zhong, Yifei He, Wan Yue, Yaokang Zhang, Zhuang Xie, Xuechang Zhou

10.1002/adfm.79082.title: Mechanoluminescence in Sr3P4O13 Enabled by Contact Electrification-Induced Energy Transfer
10.1002/adfm.79082.abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanoluminescence (ML) materials, capable of converting mechanical action into light emissions, hold great promise for stress-sensing applications. However, the lack of general design principles for developing efficient and self-powered ML materials has significantly impeded progress in this field. Herein, we report a novel class of self-powered Sr 3 P 4 O 13 (SPO) ML materials enabled by energy transfer from electron-hole pair recombination induced by contact electrification. Through combined analyses using piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), thermoluminescence (TL) spectroscopy, triboelectric potential measurements, temperature-dependent ML spectra, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations of charge density difference, the underlying ML mechanism is elucidated as contact electrification-induced energy transfer. Systematic investigation of SPO:Bi and a series of SPO:RE (RE = Eu, Tb, Dy, Sm, Er, Tm) phosphors reveals that activator ions possessing spin-allowed broadband absorption are favorable for achieving efficient ML, a correlation that extends consistently to radioluminescence (RL) and cathodoluminescence (CL) behaviors. Leveraging the favorable luminescence performance, we demonstrate proof-of-concept applications in a single material platform that integrates handwritten signature authentication, structural health monitoring, X-ray imaging, optical temperature sensing, and multi-stimulus information encryption. This work provides fundamental insights into contact electrification-induced ML and establishes important design guidelines for developing efficient ML materials and their versatile applications.
authors: Yue-Fei Xiang, Ming-Hao Wang, Tao Liu, Xin Huang, Lei Zhong, Mao-Feng Hua, Jia-Jia Kong, Jun-Cheng Zhang, Feng Wang, Lei Zhou, Ming-Mei Wu

10.1002/adfm.79018.title: Proximity-Tuned Magnetic and Transport Anomalies in All-Epitaxial Fe5−xGeTe2/WSe2 Van der Waals Heterostructures
10.1002/adfm.79018.abstract: ABSTRACT Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures combining two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnets and semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) offer highly promising opportunities for tailoring 2D magnetism through interfacial proximity effects, enabling unique physical phenomena inaccessible in 3D systems and achieving functionalities beyond conventional spintronics. However, current fabrication of vdW heterostructures still relies heavily on the manual stacking of exfoliated 2D flakes, leading to critical challenges in scalability, interfacial quality, thickness control and device integration. This work reports on the realization of all-epitaxial, high-quality Fe 5− x GeTe 2 (FGT)/WSe 2 heterostructures exhibiting perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) and room-temperature ferromagnetism. The FGT/WSe 2 system demonstrates temperature-driven magnetic transitions, higher-order PMA contributions and large anisotropic magnetoresistance, highlighting sublattice-specific contributions to magnetic and transport properties. Notably, the FGT/WSe 2 heterostructures display unconventional physical phenomena, including thickness- and temperature-dependent sign reversal of exchange bias, a reversed thickness trend in the unconventional Hall effect, and a non-monotonic PMA-thickness dependence. These anomalies indicate pronounced interfacial contributions arising from proximity effects enhanced by epitaxial interface quality. Collectively, this study provides deep insights into the magnetic and transport properties of FGT/WSe 2 vdW heterostructures, establishing a scalable platform for exploring emergent 2D physics and developing next-generation 2D spintronic functionalities.
authors: Hua Lv, Tauqir Shinwari, Kacho Imtiyaz Ali Khan, Jens Herfort, Chen Chen, Joan M. Redwing, Mehak Loyal, Gerhard Jakob, Mathias Kläui, Achim Trampert, Bernat Mundet, Belén Ballesteros, Manfred Ramsteiner, Roman Engel-Herbert, Michael Hanke, João Marcelo J. Lopes

10.1002/adfm.79066.title: Optoelectronic Synergy and Multimodal Neuromorphic Computing in SnS2/h-BN/NbOCl2 Van Der Waals Floating Gate Architecture
10.1002/adfm.79066.abstract: ABSTRACT The kinetic basis by which a single charge-storage layer supports both short-term plasticity (STP) and persistent long-term plasticity (LTP) remains unresolved. Using a SnS 2 /h-BN/NbOCl 2 van der Waals floating-gate architecture, we provide three complementary lines of evidence. Removing NbOCl 2 reduces the memory window from 92.2 to ∼2 V, identifying NbOCl 2 as the dominant charge-storage medium. Variable-temperature post-stimulus relaxation (310-330 K), analyzed by biexponential fitting and Arrhenius regression, resolves two kinetically distinct components: a weakly activated component (WAC, E a,1 ≈ 0.026 eV) with fast relaxation, consistent with transient STP conductance modulation, and a thermally activated component (TAC, E a,2 ≈ 0.111 eV) with much slower relaxation, consistent with persistent LTP retention. Their approximately 4-fold effective activation-energy difference provides quantitative kinetic evidence for two distinct temperature-dependent relaxation behaviors associated with the same NbOCl 2 layer. Sigmoidal fitting of the memory index yields a crossover power density P c = 26.49 µW/cm 2 , separating a predominantly volatile response at P < P c (Path A) from a larger persistent contribution at P > P c (Path B). Transient electrostatic screening and tunneling-assisted charge neutralization are proposed as the underlying processes. The device achieves 92.81% MNIST and 93.2% spoken-digit recognition accuracy, demonstrating promise for multimodal neuromorphic computation.
authors: LongXiang Li, Yingli Zhang, Zunfa Wang, Yuhang Jia, BoXiang Lan, WenCong Zhang, ZiWen Wang, XinXin Zhang, Man Jiang, Hua Xu

10.1002/adfm.78907.title: High-Strength, Environmentally Stable Wood Fiber/Polyamide/Polyethylene Composites Enabled by High-Temperature Compatibilization With Triple-Crosslinked Interface
10.1002/adfm.78907.abstract: ABSTRACT Introducing a binary matrix of engineering and general-purpose plastics is an effective strategy to synergistically enhance the mechanical performance and cost-effectiveness of wood fiber-reinforced composites by leveraging the complementary properties of different polymers. However, achieving such hybrid composite structures often suffers from processing differences and interfacial incompatibility among components. Herein, a straightforward and scalable high-temperature compatibilization strategy is proposed to fabricate wood fiber/polyamide/polyethylene composites (WPAECs) with a triple-crosslinked network interface, through reactive blending of the matrix followed by optimization of processing temperature. The WPAECs constructed from polyamide/polyethylene matrix and hydrothermally treated wood fibers can achieve mechanical strengthening by the uniform internal structure and triple cross-linking interactions (physical interlocking, covalent bonds, and hydrogen bonds), resulting in high flexural strength of 72.33 MPa while maintaining a low density of 1.10 g cm −3 . Moreover, the mechanical strength of WPAECs can be further enhanced by optimizing the wood fiber content. WPAECs also exhibit advantageous environmental stability, including low-temperature toughness, low water absorption rate (below 2.33%), and good heat resistance. Coupled with abundant raw materials, ease of processing, and scalable and recyclable fabrication, WPAECs provide a promising pathway toward high-performance and sustainable structural component applications.
authors: Zhengtong You, Wei Liu, Zhifang Zhou, Qingcheng Wang, Haoyuan Zhang, Yonggui Wang, Zefang Xiao, Qingwen Wang, Haigang Wang, Yanjun Xie

10.1002/adfm.79007.title: A Bilayer Bioelectronic Implant with Piezoelectric-Driven Immunomodulation and Bioactive Whitlockite for Bone Regeneration
10.1002/adfm.79007.abstract: ABSTRACT The loss of endogenous electrical signals after bone injury, coupled with infection and oxidative stress, often impedes natural healing. Here, we develop a bilayered scaffold integrating a piezoelectric nanofibrous membrane with a conductive antioxidative hydrogel for coordinated antibacterial defense, immunomodulation, and bone regeneration. The top layer comprises electrospun P(VDF-TrFE) doped with polarized whitlockite (PPW), generating local electrical potentials under mechanical or mild ultrasonic stimulation. The bottom layer consists of lignin-stabilized silver nanoparticles embedded in a polyacrylamide network (ALP), providing broad-spectrum antibacterial activity and ROS-scavenging in vitro. In vitro, the piezoelectric signals enhanced ALP activity and collagen I expression by 1.35-fold, while the ALP hydrogel drove macrophage polarization from M1 toward M2. In a rat bilateral 3-mm full-thickness calvarial defect model, the ultrasound-stimulated scaffold increased bone volume fraction 2.3-fold, improved new bone formation and partial cortical bridging, and nearly doubled VEGF expression at 4 weeks relative to the ALP hydrogel group, though residual defects remained at 8 weeks. Concurrently, the scaffold upregulated TGF-β and Runx2 while markedly suppressing TNF-α, indicating an accelerated transition from inflammation to repair. These results demonstrate a synergistic strategy in which piezoelectric stimulation and biochemical protection jointly orchestrate osteogenesis, angiogenesis, and immunomodulation for bone tissue engineering.
authors: Qirui Gong, Zhihan Zhang, Guangxu Wang, Xuan Yu, Lihong Fan, Tiantian Chen, Huixuan Sun, Xiao Zheng, Shengxiang Tao, Yingying Chu, Yue Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79069.title: Electrostatic-Sieving Zn2+ Transport in a Biodegradable HSiO2-Crosslinked Cationic Hydrogel Enables Ultralong-Life Zinc-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79069.abstract: ABSTRACT Quasi-solid-state aqueous zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) represent a promising platform for next-generation energy storage, yet their practical implementation is hindered by an inherent trade-off among ionic conductivity, Zn 2+ transference number, and mechanical robustness in gel electrolytes. Herein, we report a rationally designed cationic composite hydrogel electrolyte PAM-N + /HSiO 2, that breaks this long-standing performance bottleneck. The hydrophilic cationic -N + R 3 side chains anchor SO 4 2− anions via electrostatic interactions to drive directional Zn 2+ migration, while concurrently weakening the Zn 2+ solvation effect to promote uniform Zn deposition. Consequently, the PAM-N + /HSiO 2 electrolyte simultaneously achieves a high Zn 2+ transference number of 0.75 and an exceptional ionic conductivity of 27.06 mS cm −1 . Moreover, the rigid siloxane cage of HSiO 2 serves as a multifunctional covalent crosslinker, forming a robust 3D network (elongation at break > 1000%) that effectively resists dendrite penetration. The assembled Zn||Zn symmetric cell delivers stable cycling for 5182 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1332 h at 5 mA cm −2 , and the Zn||V 2 O 5 cell maintains excellent cycling stability over 2275 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Notably, this hydrogel electrolyte also exhibits remarkable flame retardancy and biodegradability, opening new avenues for high-performance, eco-friendly quasi-solid-state energy storage.
authors: Wei Wang, Huiqing Meng, Jiaqi Wang, Shengshu Ye, Junsong Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78922.title: Unexpected Asymmetric Mn-Sb Site Mixing and Reentrant Spin-Glass State of MnSb2Te4
10.1002/adfm.78922.abstract: ABSTRACT Mn-Sb site mixing directly impacts both the magnetic and topological properties of MnSb 2 Te 4 [MST]. This study reveals that, contrary to previously believed, these anti-sites can be unevenly distributed within the crystal. The use of High-Resolution Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy [STEM] combined with Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy [EDS] allowed us to identify a local inversion-breaking asymmetry in the anti-site distribution within the septuple layers of a polycrystalline sample of MST. This reduced-symmetry structure warrants further exploration due to its prospect for combining topology and magnetism with other effects, such as the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction [DMI], non-linear optics, and piezoelectricity. Direct current [DC] magnetic measurements confirmed the well-established ferrimagnetic properties of the compound, while alternating current [AC] magnetometry revealed a newly observed reentrant spin-glass state, representing an important finding for defect-driven magnetism in topological insulators. A simplified microscopic picture is presented in which antiferromagnetic pockets arise from Mn-Te-Mn super-exchange interactions between Mn defects and Mn planes. The observations are supported by Density Functional Theory [DFT] calculations performed on simplified defect models, which highlight scenarios in which asymmetric site mixing can be energetically favored over symmetric arrangements.
authors: Gustavo Chavez Ponce de Leon, Ahmad Dibajeh, Gert ten Brink, Majid Ahmadi, Suyang Sun, Wei Zhang, Bart Jan Kooi, George Palasantzas

10.1002/adfm.79079.title: Breaking the Psoriatic Inflammation-Proliferation Loop Through a Dual-Engineered High-Entropy Alloy Featuring Predictable Multi-Enzyme Activity and STAT3-Sponge Function
10.1002/adfm.79079.abstract: ABSTRACT Psoriasis is sustained by a self-amplifying loop in which reactive oxygen species (ROS) drive proinflammatory cytokine release, while activated JAK-STAT3 signaling reciprocally elevates keratinocyte ROS production. Current nanozyme strategies mainly target the ROS arm, leaving the upstream STAT3 signaling insufficiently addressed. In this study, a dual-engineering paradigm combining atomic composition design and surface charge engineering was established on PtPdCuFe high-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) to disrupt both arms. All-atom simulations revealed that local atomic neighborhoods governed their surface electronic structures and enzyme-like activities. In imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriatic mice, these compositions attenuated epidermal hyperplasia through the restoration of suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 (SOCS1), which bridged ROS rebalancing to JAK-STAT suppression; meanwhile, residual STAT3 activation remains unresolved. Surface charge engineering across five chemistries yielded a therapeutic hierarchy (negative > neutral ≈ positive > zwitterionic > polyvinylpyrrolidone). Proteomics, isothermal titration calorimetry, and proximity ligation assays demonstrated that anionic surfaces electrostatically sequester STAT3. Prior treatment also attenuated, without abolishing, recurrence upon IMQ rechallenge, and subcutaneous delivery was well-tolerated for over 28 days. The dual mechanism coupled an inside-out pathway (SOD-catalyzed SOCS1 restoration) with an outside-in pathway (electrostatic STAT3 capture), establishing catalytic-electrostatic dual-loop disruption as a paradigm for anti-inflammatory therapy.
authors: Huiyue Zhao, Sile Shen, Yuanqiang Chen, Zhihong Chang, Renwei Lu, Peng Gao, Changrun He, Yaojie Peng, Qing Lin, Zhao Wang, Yu Li, Ming Zhao, Hong-Ming Ding, Hongwei Wang, Da Huo

10.1002/adfm.78878.title: Microstructure-Defect Engineering of Spinels for Self-Powered and Recoverable Near-Infrared Mechanoluminescence
10.1002/adfm.78878.abstract: ABSTRACT Different from traditional stimulus-responsive luminescence systems, near-infrared mechanoluminescence (NIR-ML) materials have unique advantages in biomechanical sensing and deep-tissue imaging. Their unique mechano-optical conversion ability makes them promising candidates for emerging smart platforms; however, unclear mechanisms underlying self-recoverable and self-powered ML have hindered their further development toward practical applications. Here, we report a series of Cr 3+ -activated ML phosphors through spinel microstructure-defect engineering in centrosymmetric hosts. By systematically regulating defect types, we clarify the distinct energy origins and mechanisms of self-recoverable and self-powered ML, both of which are governed by defect-piezoelectric coupling effects. Here, Self-recoverable ML mainly originates from intrinsic point defects associated with electron capture and release process during pre-irradiation, while self-powered ML arises from anti-site defects associated with local structural distortion. Furthermore, by combining binary coding with convolutional neural network algorithms, a proof-of-concept NIR biomechanical monitoring and sensing model is designed to simulate luminescence during human biting. These findings elucidate the structure-defect-piezoelectric-luminescence relationship and provide rational design principles for high-performance NIR ML materials toward potential practical applications.
authors: Yao Xiao, Puxian Xiong, Peishan Shao, Haiqiang Fang, Pan Zheng, Yumin Yin, Shengbin Xu, Chengan Wang, Enhai Song, Changhong Linghu, Bruno Viana, Jiulin Gan

10.1002/adfm.77744.title: From Atoms to Cells: First-Principles Mapping of MXene-TMD Heterostructures for Next-Generation Metal-Ion Batteries
10.1002/adfm.77744.abstract: ABSTRACT MXene-transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures combine tunable surface terminations with redox-active layered hosts, offering a versatile platform for next-generation metal-ion batteries. This review introduces an evidence-graded, atoms-to-cells framework that maps interface-controlled descriptors-termination chemistry, interlayer spacing, charge redistribution, and mechanical compliance-from atomic-scale computation to cell-level performance across lithium, sodium, potassium, zinc, magnesium, calcium, and aluminum chemistries. Density functional theory (DFT) evidence is compiled separately from experimental evidence to enforce falsifiability: each design-rule claim is graded as convergent, computation-led, experiment-led, or open. Computation reveals that MXene termination identity (-O/-OH/-F) shifts work functions by up to ∼3.5 eV and dominates adsorption energetics, diffusion barriers, and interfacial stability, while TMD phase (2H vs. 1T/1T′) controls conductivity and ion accessibility. Experimentally, MXene-TMD architectures consistently improve rate capability and cycling stability through restacking suppression and electronic percolation, yet most demonstrations remain at low areal loading, and interface persistence under realistic conditions is rarely verified. Critical gaps-including MXene oxidation drift, cost-performance parity with carbon scaffolds, and insufficient operando validation-are identified alongside a decisive roadmap prioritizing termination-aware design, thick-electrode benchmarking, and closed-loop descriptor-to-observable validation chains for practical deployment.

10.1002/adfm.79042.title: Flash Joule Heating Enabled Defect Healing and Graphite-CNT Interfacial Fusion for Spent Graphite Upcycling
10.1002/adfm.79042.abstract: ABSTRACT The regeneration of graphite anodes from spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for sustainable battery recycling. Existing strategies typically rely on energy-intensive graphitization or hazardous chemical treatments, which are either ineffective in repairing intrinsic defects or environmentally unsustainable. Here, we show that spent graphite largely retains its graphitic framework and therefore requires selective healing of localized defects and removal of surface residues, rather than complete structural reconstruction. We develop an ultrafast thermal strategy using flash Joule heating (2273 K within 0.1 s, held for 10 s), which simultaneously repairs lattice defects and removes surface residues with minimal thermal budget. Moreover, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are integrated into graphite and ultrafast thermal treatment enables interfacial fusion between CNTs and graphite domains, reconstructing long-range conductive pathways across particles. This process transforms CNTs from passive conductive additives into active structural reconstruction agents. As a result, the regenerated graphite exhibits enhanced structural integrity and electron transport, delivering superior rate capability, cycling stability, and low-temperature performance. In addition, the process suppresses thermal-shock-induced powder loss and significantly reduces energy consumption. This work establishes a mechanism-driven strategy for defect-selective healing and conductive-network reconstruction in spent graphite, providing a promising and sustainable pathway for lithium-ion battery recycling.

10.1002/adfm.79092.title: Synergistic Passivation Effects of Li-Al Co-Doping Enables >15% Efficient Kesterite Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.79092.abstract: ABSTRACT Cation doping has been widely explored to mitigate disorder in kesterite Cu 2 ZnSn(S, Se) 4 photovoltaics, yet further efficiency gains are hindered by the inability to simultaneously suppress deep-level defect clusters, enhance carrier concentration, and preserve bulk transport properties. Here, we report a Li-Al co-doping strategy that introduces synergistic passivation effects (SPEs) within the absorber. Unlike simple additive doping, the co-substitution of Li + and Al 3+ at Zn 2+ sites with Li preferentially occupying Zn sites in the presence of Al, as confirmed by first-principles density functional theory (DFT) open-circuit voltage calculations, enables a unique charge self-compensation and lattice strain balance mechanism, which collectively reshapes the defect landscape. This approach effectively suppresses detrimental [2Cu Zn +Sn Zn ] clusters while promoting beneficial [V Cu +Zn Cu ] clusters, and concurrently increases carrier concentration and built-in potential. Comprehensive spectroscopic and electrical characterizations reveal that the SPEs originate from energetically favorable defect complexes such as [Li Zn +Al Zn ], enabling atomic-scale tuning of recombination dynamics. As a result, the champion device achieves a notable efficiency of 15.49% with a high open-circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.608 V ( V OC,def = 0.286 V), and exceptional operational stability over 3910 h. This work establishes a generalizable materials design principle, i.e., engineering synergistic charge compensation between complementary dopants for overcoming voltage deficits in multi-cation semiconductors beyond kesterites.
authors: Jingyi Meng, Xinyu Zhang, Linxin Gao, Yixiang Xiao, Chun Guo, Yanping Song, Busen Zhai, Sisi Jia, Wenjie Zhu, Lunkan Shen, Dipeng Xu, Huanhuan Sun, Bin Yao, Zhenghua Su, Jichun Ye, Sixin Wu

10.1002/adfm.78549.title: Hydrogen Selenide Gas Therapy Integrated With NIR-II Multimodal Imaging for Precision Theranostics of Cervical Cancer
10.1002/adfm.78549.abstract: ABSTRACT Cervical cancer treatment is hindered by drug resistance, systemic toxicity, and poor real-time monitoring of therapy. Herein, we present an intelligent nanotheranostic platform, recombinant human serum albumin (rHSA)-indocyanine green (ICG)-Bi 2 (SeO 3 ) 3 (HIB) based on hydrogen selenide (H 2 Se) gas therapy and multimodal imaging. In response to high glutathione (GSH) levels in the tumor microenvironment and under 808 nm laser irradiation, HIB NCs achieve on-demand H 2 Se release, which sensitizes photothermal/photodynamic therapy and promoted autophagy by regulating heat shock proteins 70 (HSP70) and oxidative stress pathways, as validated by bioinformatics. Distinct from conventional gas agents, HIB NCs enable real-time, non-invasive dynamic monitoring of H 2 Se distribution and therapeutic responses using an integrated near-infrared II (900-1700 nm, NIR-II) fluorescence/computed tomography (CT)/photoacoustic (PA)/laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI) multimodal strategy, overcoming the lack of in vivo H 2 Se sensing. In the cervical cancer lymph node metastasis model, HIB NCs could identify diseased lymph nodes more quickly for tracing and exhibit good biocompatibility. This study explored H 2 Se as a potent anti-metastatic gas messenger and constructed a clinically translatable platform that combines precise gas release, multimodal dynamic monitoring, and synergistic phototherapy.

10.1002/adfm.78964.title: Remote Activation of Wnt Signaling and Cell Proliferation by E-Cadherin Magnetomechanical Stimulation
10.1002/adfm.78964.abstract: ABSTRACT The ability to remotely and precisely manipulate intracellular signaling pathways is crucial for fundamental research and therapeutics. The Wnt/β-catenin cascade regulates cell proliferation, differentiation, and tissue regeneration, but current pharmacological activation methods lack spatiotemporal control and induce off-target effects. Here, we introduce a pioneering magnetogenetic toolkit to modulate the Wnt/β-catenin pathway through magnetomechanical stimulation of E-cadherin, a key cell adhesion molecule intimately linked to β-catenin dynamics. Magnetic nanoparticles functionalized with the extracellular domain of E-cadherin (MNPs@E/EC15) selectively bind cellular E-cadherins. Applying a low-intensity, low-gradient magnetic field via a custom stimulator generates localized mechanical forces that trigger E-cadherin mechanotransduction. This stimulation induces β-catenin membrane release, nuclear translocation, and Wnt target gene activation, confirmed by transcriptomic profiling and a luciferase reporter assay. These molecular changes translate into enhanced cell proliferation and accelerated gap closure. This work establishes an innovative, non-invasive tool for probing E-cadherin mechanobiology and remotely modulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Unlike other mechanotransduction tools, this approach enables simultaneous, high-spatiotemporal modulation of multiple cells using low-intensity magnetic fields adaptable for in vivo designs. Our findings open promising avenues for studying mechanotransduction and developing targeted regenerative therapies based on mechanical stimulation.
authors: Christian Castro-Hinojosa, Pablo Martínez-Vicente, Lucía G. Recaredo, Susel Del Sol-Fernández, Pilar Gomollón-Zueco, Yilian Fernández-Afonso, Raluca M. Fratila, María Moros

10.1002/adfm.79116.title: Low-Frequency Vibration Damping Polyurethane Elastomers with High Mechanical Robustness via Constrained Pendant Chains
10.1002/adfm.79116.abstract: ABSTRACT Low-frequency vibration damping in polyurethane elastomers remains difficult to reconcile with mechanical robustness. Effective dissipation of low-frequency vibration requires the characteristic relaxation time of polymer chains to match the timescale of slow external oscillations. However, such long-timescale chain relaxation is typically associated with stress relaxation, creep and irreversible deformation, compromising mechanical robustness. Here, we report a polyurethane elastomer that addresses this trade-off through a constrained pendant-chain architecture, in which grafted pendant chains are locally constrained at their roots while retaining flexible terminal alkyl segments. This architecture is created by placing urea and urethane motifs at the pendant-chain roots, where neighboring pendant-chain units assemble into a reversible hydrogen-bonded association network. This reversible network kinetically constrains pendant chain relaxation, shifts the characteristic relaxation toward longer timescales and thereby enhances low-frequency damping. Meanwhile, the association network provides dynamic physical crosslinks that restrict backbone slippage and preserve structural integrity. The optimized polyurethane elastomer exhibits a loss factor of 0.98 at 1 Hz while maintaining a tensile strength of 60.2 MPa. These results establish constrained pendant chain engineering as a molecular design strategy for polyurethane elastomers that combine low-frequency vibration attenuation with high mechanical performance.
authors: Xiang Han, Tianyu Wang, Chenxi Huyan, Zhiyuan Ma, Haoxiang Li, Dong Liu, Fei Chen, Liqun Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79089.title: Low-Potential Generation of High-Valence Metal Sites Activates Lattice Oxygen for Ampere-Level 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural Electrooxidation
10.1002/adfm.79089.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) offers a sustainable route for biomass valorization, yet maintaining high Faradaic efficiencies (FE) at industrially-relevant current densities remains challenging. Here, we report a rationally engineered nickel-cobalt nitrate hydroxide with an edge-rich and through-pore structure, which rapidly reconstructs at exceptionally low potentials into an active NiCoOOH phase enriched with high-valence metal sites. Combining isotope labeling experiments, molecular probe studies, and first-principles calculations reveals that these high-valence metal sites activate otherwise inert lattice oxygen to form reactive oxygen intermediates ( * O lat -O • ). These intermediates significantly reduce steric hindrance in the transition state, thereby lowering the activation barriers for O─H and C─H bond cleavage during the oxidation of HMF. This breakthrough enables the catalyst to achieve ampere-level current densities of 1520 mA·cm −2 at 1.60 V vs. RHE, while maintaining a near-quantitative FE FDCA of 97.7 ± 0.7% even at 1000 mA·cm −2 . Practical applicability is demonstrated in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer, which operates stably for 100 h with single-pass FDCA yields exceeding 98%. These findings establish the potential of lattice oxygen activation as a foundational design strategy for developing high-performance electrocatalysts tailored to industrial-scale biomass refineries.
authors: Jiansong Wang, Rui Chen, Yipu Xu, Chang Wang, Liu-Liu Shen, Gui-Rong Zhang, Donghai Mei

10.1002/adfm.79114.title: Dual-Site Defect Passivation and δ-Phase Engineering for High-Efficiency and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79114.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic-inorganic perovskite solar cells are limited by surface defects and instability. Conventional ammonium-salt passivation often forms insulating 2D phases that hinder charge transport. Here, we report ethylammonium trifluoroacetate (EATFA) as a bifunctional surface treatment for FAPbI 3 films. EA + and TFA − synergistically passivate A-site and halide-site defects, respectively, while inducing an extraction-efficient δ -EA x FA 1- x PbI 3 surface layer instead of a 2D phase. This dual-site δ -phase engineering suppresses non-radiative recombination, optimizes energy-level alignment, and improves charge extraction. As a result, EATFA-treated devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 25.54%, with a high V oc of 1.17 V and FF of 84.00%, along with enhanced stability, retaining >90% efficiency over 960 h under continuous illumination. This work provides a coherent passivation strategy that concurrently addresses efficiency and stability challenges in perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Zhenqiang Shen, Lianghe Hu, Renjie Ding, Xinrui Qi, Yi Liu, Wenjun Luo, Zhigang Zou, Bing Wang

10.1002/adfm.79072.title: In Situ Observation of Dynamic Defect Evolution and Phase Transition in Mn-Doped Sb2Te3
10.1002/adfm.79072.abstract: ABSTRACT Defect engineering has long been a primary strategy for optimizing thermoelectric materials. Understanding the dynamic behavior of atomic defects under real working conditions is crucial for revealing structure-property relationships. Here, we combine in situ atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) with density functional theory (DFT) to unravel the dynamic evolution of manganese (Mn) dopants in the p-type mid-temperature TE material antimony telluride (Sb 2 Te 3 ). Initially, Mn forms both interstitial defects and Mn Sb substitutional defects. Upon heating, thermally activated Mn diffusion leads to Mn-Sb mixed regions, degraded interfacial coherency, and a structural α-to-δ phase transition. This dynamic structural evolution contributes to a suppression in lattice thermal conductivity and modest ZT enhancement at high temperatures. Our work directly links dynamic structural evolution to transport properties, offering new insights into defect engineering that could be synergistically combined with other optimization methods to design advanced thermoelectric materials.
authors: Wenjun Lv, Wenjun Cui, Hanwen Wang, WeiXiao Lin, Yongqiang Li, Junjie Ding, Wen Zhao, Gangjian Tan, Xiahan Sang

10.1002/adfm.79119.title: Bulky Molecules Tailor Solvent Packing Fraction of Electrolytes for High-Voltage Sodium-Ion Battery
10.1002/adfm.79119.abstract: ABSTRACT High-voltage sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) suffer from rapid degradation caused by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, which are strongly influenced by the local solvation environment near the electrode surface. However, conventional electrolyte design focuses on tuning Na + -solvent interactions while overlooking solvent packing within the solvation shell. Herein, we reveal that a bulky molecular solvent mediates restricted solvent packing around Na + , with its reduced packing efficiency quantitatively described by the fractal dimension ( D f ). The enlarged molecular volume creates a more open solvation environment, facilitating anion participation and promoting ion clusters dominated by contact ion pairs (CIPs) and small aggregates (SAGGs). The resulting inorganic-rich interphase suppresses electrolyte oxidation and interfacial parasitic reactions, enabling stable high-voltage operation. Sodium iron sulfate (NFS) paired with the bulky-solvent electrolyte retains 80% capacity over 1407 cycles at 1 C. An Ah-level HC||NFS pouch cell retains 81.53% capacity after 500 cycles. A practical pouch cell further achieves 115.05 Wh kg −1 and retains 80.87% of its capacity after 150 cycles. This work demonstrates that restricted solvent packing can modulate ion association and interfacial chemistry, providing a molecular design consideration for high-energy SIBs.
authors: Yuewei Cui, Shilong Dong, Jiahao Wang, Shuang Wu, Mao Guo, Anqi Zhang, Qiang Liu, Bingkun Wu, Kai Zhang, Youxuan Ni, Zhenhua Yan

10.1002/adfm.79100.title: Overcoming the Heterointerface Energetics Changes in Perovskite Photovoltaics With Nondestructive Halide Exchange
10.1002/adfm.79100.abstract: ABSTRACT Surface passivation is essential for high-performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, passivator-induced carrier accumulation in potential wells and the reduction of ion migration activation energy caused by heterointerface energy changes pose significant challenges to device stability. Herein, we demonstrate a nondestructive halide exchange strategy with IBr-treatment to pre-construct a positive work function change without incorporating exogenous impurities. By simply varying concentration, this strategy enables continuous adjustment of the heterointerface energetics to suit various perovskites and passivators. The pre-constructed positive work function change avoids the generation of the potential well during perovskite surface passivation, preventing the electron accumulation and facilitating interfacial hole extraction. Upon the IBr-treatment, the PSCs achieve outstanding power conversion efficiency of 24.70% with PEAI passivation, 26.19% for small-area device and 24.48% for 1-cm 2 device with CHEAI passivation. The devices retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 1500 h continuous light illumination under maximum power point tracking. Our study provides a promising and practical strategy to overcome the passivator-induced heterointerface energetics changes, avoiding the deteriorated efficiency and stability for the iodine-containing perovskite photovoltaics.
authors: Yi Zhang, Yujie Li, Xiaolong Geng, Guanhua Ren, Chunyu Liu, Wenbin Guo

10.1002/adfm.79081.title: Defect Engineering in Cesium Cadmium Perovskites Enables Multi-Stimuli-Responsive Luminescence for Temperature-Resilient X-Ray Radiography and Mechanosensing
10.1002/adfm.79081.abstract: ABSTRACT Halide perovskites have revolutionized optoelectronic technologies, yet their intrinsic defects are viewed as liabilities to be eliminated. Here, we challenge this paradigm by demonstrating that controlled manipulation of defect states in cesium cadmium perovskites transforms these inherent traps into functionally tunable charge carrier reservoirs. Using valence-engineered doping with Mn 2+ and multivalent ions, we systematically modulate the depth and capacity of carrier traps across 100 to 700 K. Comprehensive thermoluminescence spectroscopy reveals a hierarchical trap landscape, while first-principles calculations verify the intervalence charge transfer from Mn 2+ to the conduction band. These computational insights, combined with the experimental data, provide electronic-level validation of the charge trapping and release and offer a mechanistic framework for understanding the origins of trap states in the Mn 2+ -doped system. The resulting materials exhibit exceptional temperature resilience and tri-stimuli-responsive (optical/thermal/mechanical) luminescence, with 8- to 30-fold enhanced charge storage over commercial benchmarks (BaFBr(I):Eu 2+ and Y 2 O 2 S:Eu 3+ ). Remarkably, mechanical stimulation triggers immediate mechanoluminescence for real-time force monitoring while simultaneously storing residual charges for delayed thermoluminescent readout. This dual-mode functionality, enabled by control over trap population dynamics, establishes cesium cadmium halide perovskites as versatile platforms for adaptive X-ray radiography and wide-temperature-range mechanosensing, opening new avenues for smart sensing systems in extreme environments.
authors: Tianshuai Lyu, Haisong Li, Jingyan Peng, Bibo Lou, Zhanhua Wei

10.1002/adfm.78997.title: Doping-Vacancy Synergy in Iron Antimony Oxide for Efficient Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.78997.abstract: ABSTRACT We demonstrate the electronic structure engineering of iron antimony oxide (FeSbO 4 , FSO) through heteroatom (Ti, Zn) doping and controlled oxygen vacancy formation for efficient electrocatalytic water splitting. Heteroatom incorporation elevates intrinsic electrical conductivity to accelerate charge transfer during the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Simultaneously, surface oxygen vacancies polarize the local electronic environment at Fe active sites, optimizing the adsorption energetics of oxygen-containing intermediates to significantly boost oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance. Ti-doped FSO with moderate oxygen vacancies (TFSO 30 ) achieves outstanding HER activity (300 mV at 50 mA/cm 2 , Tafel slope of 119.38 mV/dec) due to vacancy-induced electronic modulation. In contrast, higher oxygen vacancy concentration (TFSO 60 ) drives superior OER performance (188 mV at 50 mA/cm 2 , Tafel slope of 76.18 mV/dec) compared to IrO 2, primarily driven by charge redistribution and the generation of high-valence active metal species. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that Ti doping and oxygen vacancies synergistically tune the electronic structure, promote charge transport, and lower reaction energy barriers to accelerate overall water-splitting kinetics. Overall, this work highlights Ti-doped FSO as an efficient, earth-abundant electrocatalyst and provides useful insights into defect-engineering strategies for catalytic energy conversion.
authors: Taewoo Lee, Balaji G. Ghule, Kyeong-Nam Kang, Bibhuti Kumar Jha, Hyunmin Kim, Ji-Hyun Jang

10.1002/adfm.79000.title: Bio-Inspired Tactile Reflex Architecture for Ultra-Fast and Context-Aware Human-Robot Interaction
10.1002/adfm.79000.abstract: ABSTRACT Robots operating in close proximity to humans must be capable of perceiving contact, reacting within milliseconds, and subsequently restoring stable task execution. However, existing proprioceptive or vision-based methods suffer from limited bandwidth, high latency, and poor reliability during dynamic interactions. Here, we propose a human-inspired tactile perception and reflex control framework that integrates a high-performance single-electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (STENG) tactile array, distributed microcontroller-based reflex processing, and impact-aware high-level motion generation. The STENG array, fabricated using optimized silicone and liquid-metal printing, provides high-bandwidth, high-resolution mechanical sensing and robust surface conformability. A lightweight neural classifier embedded directly in the reflex layer enables real-time discrimination between human and object contact from raw triboelectric waveforms. The distributed control architecture achieves a total reflex latency of 2.2 ms, outperforming the centralized controller by more than a factor of five. Experimental demonstrations show that the system can generate an immediate stop followed by high-level retraction under human contact, while selectively modulating motion during object contact, providing context-aware reflex actions. The proposed architecture bridges the gap between ultra-fast tactile sensing and high-level motion intelligence, enabling fast, safe, and human-friendly physical interaction for future human-robot interaction (HRI) applications.
authors: Jinhyeok Oh, Hun Jang, Jusung Choi, Heejun Moon, Joonbum Bae

10.1002/adfm.79078.title: A Phosphide Active-Hydrogen Valve: Redirecting Interfacial Hydrogen from Hydrogen Evolution into C-N Coupling for Efficient Urea Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79078.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic CO 2 /NO 3 − co-reduction offers a sustainable route to urea synthesis but remains constrained by mismatched carbon/nitrogen intermediate supply and uncontrolled competition between substrate hydrogenation and the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, interfacial active-hydrogen flux regulation is proposed as a design principle that matches *H generation with directional consumption within the C-N coupling network and is realized in Fe-doped Ni 2 P nanosheet arrays. The metal-phosphorus framework buffers and delivers *H, sustaining hydrogenation while suppressing futile recombination into H 2 . Fe incorporation simultaneously constructs electronically dichotomous microdomains: electron-deficient Fe sites activate CO 2 and stabilize *CO, whereas the electron-enriched Ni sites drive NO 3 − hydrogenation toward *NH 2 . Such synergistic regulation synchronizes *CO/*NH 2 supply with timely *H utilization, redirecting interfacial hydrogen from a competing HER precursor into a productive coupling resource. Operando spectroscopy and theoretical calculations corroborate enhanced precursor formation, a lowered C-N coupling barrier, and thermodynamic preference for substrate hydrogenation over HER. Fe-Ni 2 P delivers a urea Faradaic efficiency of 65.84% and a yield rate of 1820.31 µg h −1 cm −2 at −0.4 V vs. RHE in an H-cell, reaching 3688.91 µg h −1 cm −2 at 1.6 V in a membrane electrode assembly with a 50.69% Faradaic efficiency, offering a transferable design strategy for multi-reactant C-N coupling electrocatalysis.
authors: Pengyue Shan, Weimian Zhang, Chao Song, Haoliang Huang, Kaiyang Xu, Zhipeng Yu, Chenyue Zhang, Liyuan Zeng, Hang Cui, Yang Zhao, Laihong Shen, Lifeng Liu

10.1002/adfm.79028.title: Programmable Temperature-Capped Dressing for Enhanced Wound Healing, Bacterial Clearance, and Inflammatory Modulation
10.1002/adfm.79028.abstract: ABSTRACT Reconciling efficient bacterial eradication with tissue safety remains a challenge in photothermal therapy (PTT) because of open-loop thermal actuation. Herein, we propose a detachable bilayer hydrogel dressing comprising a poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM)-based protective upper layer as a self-regulating thermal cap, and a Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene/ciprofloxacin (CIP) therapeutic lower layer providing synergistic antibacterial therapy. Sequential replacement of the protection layer enables programmed temperature caps of 45°C for early infection control and 41°C for subsequent repair. Synergistic MXene/CIP effects achieve rapid and effective antibacterial activity (>99%) against both Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus . In an infected rat wound model, the programmable temperature-capped dressing shortens high-temperature exposure, attenuates TNF-α/IL-6/p-NF-κB p65 expression, modulates VEGF/CD31-associated angiogenic remodeling, and accelerates closure compared with controls. Furthermore, the percolated MXene network endows the therapeutic layer with stable negative temperature coefficient (NTC) behavior. To explore this extended electronic utility, we demonstrated the dressing's capability for in situ temperature monitoring. Additionally, a benchtop closed-loop laser control system was constructed to serve as a proof-of-concept for future autonomous feedback regulation. Overall, this bioelectronic hybrid platform advances PTT from conventional open-loop heating toward a thermally capped and feedback-compatible therapeutic strategy, offering a versatile paradigm for safer infected wound management.
authors: Zilu Hu, Fuhao Wu, Hongbin Su, Wenwu Wang, Dan Lu, Danni Hou, Nan Jiang, Xiyao Huang, Huimin Liang, Yibo Xiong, Yihao Long, Zeyu Ma, Qi Shao, Yixin Wang, Chengcheng Yuan, Chuntang Sun, Hongbo Yin, Liang He

10.1002/adfm.79093.title: Formation of Twisted Copper Phosphide on Cu(111) Surface Predicted by Machine Learning Simulations
10.1002/adfm.79093.abstract: ABSTRACT The fundamental interactions at surfaces and interfaces dictate the thermodynamic and kinetic pathways in the epitaxial growth of two-dimensional (2D) materials. The atomic-scale evolution of phosphorus (P) on Cu(111) serves as a representative example of interfacial complexity, where dynamic reconstructions and competing chemical interactions obscure the underlying growth mechanisms. In this study, we combine a rigorously trained Cu-P machine learning force field with atomically resolved scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the reaction of P on Cu(111) at atomic scale. Our results demonstrate that phosphorene is neither thermodynamically favorable nor kinetically accessible on Cu(111). Instead, strong Cu-P bonding drives the substitutional incorporation of P into the topmost Cu layer, forming a twisted copper phosphide (Cu 2 P) surface alloy - a phase that thermodynamically competes phosphorene over the experimentally relevant coverage regime. Formation of this Cu 2 P layer generates interfacial strain that organizes into a straight reconstruction network and transforms into spiral configurations upon annealing. With increasing P coverage, three-dimensional (3D) P islands, rather than flat phosphorene, are formed on Cu 2 P surface. These findings resolve a long-standing controversy regarding P growth on Cu(111) and highlight the crucial role of interfacial interaction between the precursor and the substrate in 2D material growth.
authors: Wenzhen Dou, Tianchao Niu, Liang Ma, Feng Ding, Jinlan Wang

10.1002/adfm.79103.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Anchored Metal-Free Cationic TADF Glassy Scintillators for High-Resolution Dynamic X-Ray Imaging
10.1002/adfm.79103.abstract: ABSTRACT Organic glassy scintillators offer a promising platform for scalable X-ray imaging owing to their optical transparency and melt processability. However, their performance is often limited by inefficient triplet-exciton utilization and poor condensed-phase stability. Although flexible side chains or rotatable units facilitate glass formation, they also increase molecular relaxation and nonradiative energy dissipation. Herein, we develop three single-component metal-free ionic thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) scintillators (C2-HI, C2-OHI, and C2-OMeI) using a hydrogen-bond-assisted side-chain anchoring strategy. Compared with the non-hydrogen-bonded analogues C2-HI and C2-OMeI, hydroxyl-functionalized C2-OHI forms directional O─H···I − interactions that rigidify the local molecular environment, suppress nonradiative relaxation, and stabilize the condensed phase without disturbing the emissive framework. Consequently, C2-OHI achieves a photoluminescence quantum yield of 93.69%, a radioluminescence intensity of 522% relative to commercial BGO, and an estimated relative light yield of 6.24 × 10 4 photons MeV −1 . Its melt-quenched glass retains efficient TADF scintillation with an estimated relative light yield of 2.00 × 10 4 photons MeV −1 , enabling X-ray imaging at 22.7 lp mm −1 and real-time imaging at 60 fps. This work establishes hydrogen-bond-assisted side-chain anchoring as a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating excited-state dynamics and condensed-phase stability in metal-free organic glass scintillators.
authors: Xiaocong Xu, Qiangwen Qiu, Shanyuan Zhong, Yanan Zhu, Hongming Chen, Xin Fang, Mei-Jin Lin

10.1002/adfm.79125.title: Site-Preferential Trace Phosphorus Substitution Accelerates and Stabilizes the Activation of Lithium-Rich Cathode Materials
10.1002/adfm.79125.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides can access both transition-metal and oxygen redox, but activation of the monoclinic Li 2 MnO 3 component is usually sluggish and structurally unstable. Uncontrolled activation promotes irreversible lattice distortion, oxygen-related degradation, voltage decay, and capacity loss. Here we use trace phosphorus substitution to regulate the activation pathway of a Li-rich Mn-based cathode. Structural, spectroscopic, microscopic, and theoretical analyses show that P tends to incorporate at Li-layer sites near Ni-containing local environments. This site-selective substitution modifies the Li-slab structure and adjacent Ni─O/O electronic environment, enabling more effective activation of the Li-rich monoclinic component with a self-relaxing lattice response. As a result, the P-substituted cathode reaches a peak discharge capacity of 273.1 mAh g −1 at the 50th cycle and still delivers 270.5 mAh g −1 after 300 cycles.
authors: Tongen Lin, Gui Chu, Xiaobo Zhu, Shanshan Ding, Wei Chao, Mattia Colalongo, Tobias Schulli, Joanne Etheridge, Bin Luo, Lianzhou Wang

10.1002/adfm.79107.title: Lattice-Hydrogen Pumping in Ni2P@MoO3 Enables Self-Buffered and Scaling-Resistant Hydrogen Evolution in Natural Seawater
10.1002/adfm.79107.abstract: ABSTRACT Cathodic hydrogen evolution in natural seawater offers green hydrogen production, but rapid proton consumption and hydroxyl-ion accumulation cause local alkalinization and metal hydroxide precipitation. This study reports a reversible lattice hydrogen exchange strategy that suppresses Mg/Ca precipitation by regulating the local interfacial pH with a Ni 2 P@MoO 3 /CC heterostructure. During electrocatalysis, MoO 3 dynamically adopts an H x MoO 3 -like state, accelerating water dissociation and lattice-hydrogen transfer to Ni 2 P while buffering OH − - buildup and local pH rise. Electronic modulation at the heterointerface accelerates OH − diffusion and maintains the local pH below the precipitation limit of 9.5. As a result, the catalyst required an overpotential of only 49.3 mV at 10 mA cm −2 in simulated seawater and outperformed commercial Pt/C/CC at current densities above 200 mA cm −2 . Moreover, when used as the cathode in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer, with natural seawater in the cathode chamber and 1.0 M KOH in the anode chamber, the Ni 2 P@MoO 3 /CC cathode enables stable operation for over 1000 h at 100 mA cm −2 . This study demonstrates lattice hydrogen dynamics as a feasible strategy to construct efficient and scaling-resistant cathodes for the natural seawater hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), which can be coupled with the alkaline oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in an asymmetric seawater/alkaline electrolyzer.
authors: Bo Geng, Qingyang Song, Xinyi Yang, Zhengwei Yang, Gaojie Li

10.1002/adfm.78961.title: Photodynamic Therapy-Primed and Enzyme Cascade-Fueled in Situ Prodrug Self-Assemblies for Self-Amplifying Chemotherapy
10.1002/adfm.78961.abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor heterogeneity remains a major translational challenge for targeted therapies, particularly those employing multi-targeted precision strategies. To overcome this barrier and ensure both high tumor-specificity and robust clinical efficacy, we designed CBT-NM-PPa-cRGD, a photodynamic therapy (PDT)-initiated, self-amplifying prodrug engineered for potent, multi-cascade tumor therapy. This prodrug incorporates a cRGD ligand to actively target α v β 3 integrin-overexpressing cancer cells. Upon cellular internalization and laser irradiation, the elicited PDT effect activates caspase-3 (Casp3). Casp3-mediated cleavage combined with glutathione (GSH) reduction initiates a biocompatible click condensation to drive the intracellular self-assembly of nitrogen mustard (NM)-loaded nanoparticles, leading to a substantial enhancement in drug retention and local concentration. Subsequently, the azoreductase-triggered release of NM induces tumor inhibition while further elevating Casp3 levels, thereby establishing a self-perpetuating cascade that sustains the self-assembly process. Moreover, PDT-exacerbated tumor hypoxia accelerates azoreductase-mediated NM release, fueling this positive feedback loop. The systematic in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrate that this PDT-primed, enzyme-controlled self-amplifying strategy provides superior tumor suppression, exceptional targeting specificity, and minimal systemic toxicity, offering a transformative paradigm for precision cancer therapy.
authors: Qianzijing Zhang, Yifan Huang, Zian Yu, Zhiyou Lun, Sijie Yuan, Jiangli Li, Jiancheng Peng, Jiao Meng, Bensheng Qiu, Fenfen Li, Yue Yuan

10.1002/adfm.79053.title: Large-Scale, Homogeneous Solution Crystallization of 2D Covalent Organic Frameworks with Integrated Crystallinity and Solubility for Ultrafast Noble Metal Recovery
10.1002/adfm.79053.abstract: ABSTRACT Solution-processable covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are crucial for advancing practical applications, yet traditional top-down exfoliation into solvophilic nanosheets suffers from low efficiency and limited scalability. This study presents a large-scale homogeneous crystallization strategy to constitute a family of soluble 2D COFs with high crystallinity and exceptional solubility via a dissolution-recrystallization route. By employing transformation from 3D precursors into 2D frameworks, a highly symmetric D 3h building block, hexachlorocyclotriphosphazene, is adopted to construct a three-connected 2D framework via a [3+3] reaction pathway, simultaneously retaining the three unreactive P-Cl sites on each D 3h center. A monoamine-substituted short-chain modulator is thus covalently incorporated to enhance framework solubilization, enabling a homogeneous crystallization via dissolution-recrystallization. This process accelerates crystallization kinetics, achieves ultrahigh yields (89.7%) and concentrations (138.8 mg mL −1 ), and allows gram-scale synthesis. Given their superior solution properties, such materials exhibit ultrafast gold recycling (k 2 = 0.141 g mg −1 min −1 ) through redox adsorption, significantly outperforming bulk analogues. Mechanistic studies reveal that phosphazene ring protonation lowers binding energy with AuCl 4 − via electrostatic and coordination interactions, followed by reduction to Au(0)/Au(I) and accompanied by water oxidation. This work explores a homogeneous crystallization system for 2D COFs, advancing their solution processability for scalable applications.
authors: Jinyao Zhu, Yuanzhe Cheng, Wanting Xie, Changchun Wang, Xuesong Ding, Jia Guo

10.1002/adfm.78425.title: Electrochemical Reduction of Low-Concentration Nitrate to Ammonia: Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives
10.1002/adfm.78425.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia (ENRA) is a promising strategy for simultaneously achieving nitrogen resource recovery, ammonia production, and nitrate remediation. However, most existing studies focus on high-concentration nitrate systems associated with specific industrial wastewaters, limiting their applicability to more widespread nitrate-containing waters. In contrast, nitrate streams derived from groundwater, agricultural runoff, plasma-assisted nitrogen fixation, and electrochemical nitrogen oxidation reaction are typically present at much lower concentrations, where severe mass-transfer limitations and intensified hydrogen evolution reaction substantially hinder ammonia production. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in catalyst design, electrochemical engineering, and operational strategies for low-concentration ENRA, focusing on the regulation of interfacial substrate behavior, active-species utilization, charge-transfer processes, and reactor-level optimization through reactor architecture, flow mode, electrode design, and operating modes. Furthermore, emerging utilization pathways for dilute ammonia products, techno-economic assessments, practical performance metrics, and integrated ENRA-based nitrogen conversion frameworks are discussed, together with the potential roles of artificial intelligence and intelligent process control in catalyst discovery, reactor optimization, and sustainable nitrogen recycling.

10.1002/adfm.77600.title: Dynamic Self-Optimization in an Ordered L1 0 -PtCo Core-Shell Catalyst Decouples Activity and Stability for Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.77600.abstract: ABSTRACT The performance of electrocatalysts for acidic hydrogen evolution is limited not only by intrinsic activity, but also by the structural instability under operating conditions. While ordered intermetallic compounds offer superior thermodynamic robustness, their dynamic evolution during catalysis remains poorly understood and rarely exploited. Herein, we introduce a dynamic self-optimizing core-shell electrocatalyst, L1 0 -PtCo@Co-shell, consisting of an ordered L1 0 -PtCo intermetallic core encapsulated by an ultrathin Co-shell. In 0.5 m H 2 SO 4 , this catalyst delivers an overpotential of 13 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , with mass activity and turnover frequency (TOF) values 15.9 and 4.2 times higher than those of commercial Pt/C, and stable operation for over 450 h. Operando X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy reveals potential-driven surface reconstruction via inward Co migration to form a highly alloyed PtCo surface. In situ Raman spectroscopy directly captures the co-adsorption of hydrogen intermediates on adjacent Pt and Co sites, supporting a synergistic Volmer-Tafel pathway. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations identify the ordered L1 0 core imposes a high Co diffusion barrier, suppressing dissolution while enabling controlled surface reconfiguration. By deliberately harnessing, rather than suppressing, dynamic reconstruction, this work establishes a general design paradigm for designing highly active and durable electrocatalysts for acidic hydrogen evolution.

10.1002/adfm.79143.title: Sustainable Cellulose Chiral Photonic Films Enable Simultaneous Ultralong Room-temperature Phosphorescence and High Luminescence Dissymmetry With Multicolor Tunability
10.1002/adfm.79143.abstract: ABSTRACT Simultaneously achieving high luminescence dissymmetry factors ( g lum ) and ultralong lifetimes in circularly polarized room-temperature phosphorescence (CP-RTP) materials remains a fundamental challenge, as it requires reconciling well-defined chiral ordering, efficient triplet-state stabilization, and matched energy-level alignment within a single material system. Here, we report a versatile bio-based strategy to overcome this trade-off by incorporating phosphorescent chromophores and polymer matrices into chiral cellulose nanocrystal films via one-step co-assembly. The resulting bio-based materials exhibit an ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence lifetime of up to 4.242 s. Through targeted optical path engineering using a chiral photonic crystal filter, these long-lived films achieve a large g lum value of −0.7093, without compromising phosphorescence performance. To expand the emission scope, guest fluorophore doping enables broad spectral tuning of the chiral emission via Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), yielding multicolor CP-RTP and controllable white-light emission. Benefiting from their switchable, multimodal optical properties, these films show strong potential for advanced dynamic optical anti-counterfeiting. This work addresses the core trade-off between ultralong lifetime and high g lum in CP-RTP systems, and establishes a sustainable, general platform for the design of next-generation chiral luminescent materials.
authors: Shengzhe Jia, Guozhi Lv, Yan Liu, Liuyang Yu, Bo Wang, Jiaxuan Tang, Jikun Li, Zhihe Dou, Tingan Zhang, Junbo Gong

10.1002/adfm.79126.title: Polarity-Reconfigurable In1.5Mn0.5Se3 Photodetectors Enabled by Asymmetric Schottky Barriers Toward Optical-Electrical Logic Gates and Encryption Communication Application
10.1002/adfm.79126.abstract: ABSTRACT Ensuring information security at the device level is a critical demand in the era of ubiquitous sensing and communication. In this work, we design an asymmetric two-terminal Schottky photodetector based on Mn-doped In 2 Se 3 . The regulation mechanism of Mn doping on electronic structure, interfacial charge distribution, and carrier transport is systematically investigated, and high-performance optoelectronic logic operations and optical information encryption, decryption are realized. First-principles calculations reveal that Mn doping can effectively narrow the bandgap of In 2 Se 3 from 1.0878 to 0.8986 eV and introduce donor impurity levels, significantly improving carrier concentration and optical absorption. Benefiting from the polarity-tunable photoresponse enabled by asymmetric Schottky barriers, the device successfully implements multifunctional optoelectronic logic gates including XNOR, NAND, NOR etc. Furthermore, a complete optical information encryption and decryption system is constructed based on the XNOR logic, realizing secure encoding and accurate recovery of plaintext information. This work not only provides an effective strategy for doping modification and interface engineering of two-dimensional semiconductors, but also offers new concepts and experimental support for high-performance devices toward next-generation optoelectronic computing and optical communication security.
authors: Jianbin Zhang, Liangqiang Chen, Yuan Ha, Conghui Shang, Jianshe Wu, Hua Xu, Dan Tan, Rusen Yang, Xiaobo Li
