10.1002/adfm.79067.title: Interfacial Band Homogenization and Controlled Nucleation Synergistically Enable Vertical Monolithic Perovskite Films for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79067.abstract: ABSTRACT Buried-interface inhomogeneity remains a key limitation in inverted perovskite solar cells, where aggregated Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles can generate nonuniform interfacial potentials, local band inhomogeneity, charge accumulation, and nonradiative recombination losses. Here, we report a small-molecule-mediated Al 2 O 3 nanoparticle strategy that integrates interfacial band homogenization, gradient-permeation defect passivation, and crystallization regulation. 1,3-diamino-2-propanol (1,3-DAP) anchors onto Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles, suppressing nanoparticle aggregation through surface electrostatic repulsion and homogenizing the buried interfacial potential distribution. Meanwhile, unanchored 1,3-DAP molecules permeate from the buried interface into the shallow perovskite bulk, where they passivate defects and act as nucleation-regulating sites. This dual regulation promotes vertically oriented grain growth along the (100) direction and forms vertically interconnected large-grain perovskite films. Consequently, the modified devices achieve champion power conversion efficiencies of 26.00% under N 2 fabrication and 25.09% under ambient-air fabrication, together with reduced voltage loss and enhanced stability. The unencapsulated modified devices further retain 90% of their initial maximum power output after 700 h of maximum power point tracking under continuous one-sun illumination in N 2 . Comparative molecular studies further show that effective crystallization regulation requires cooperative amino-hydroxyl functionalities and appropriate precursor compatibility, highlighting the broader applicability of the nanoparticle-interface molecular regulation strategy represented by 1,3-DAP.
authors: Haohao Nong, Kuo Wang, Mingyang Gao, Qiaogang Song, Longxian Zhang, Juchuan Chai, Yu Zhuang, Chi Yang, Xintong Zhao, Yanlin Wang, Yu Chen, Junjie Gui, Shiying Li, Kailiang Meng, Shurong Wang, Wenhua Zhang

10.1002/adfm.79113.title: Framework Excavation of UiO-66 for In Situ Confined Cu3 Cluster Assembly Toward Nitrite Electroreduction
10.1002/adfm.79113.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterogenizing molecular catalysts requires the simultaneous preservation of structural precision, active-site accessibility, and long-term stability. To address the limited capacity of robust small-pore frameworks for molecular clusters and the susceptibility of large-pore hosts to guest leaching and structural degradation, we propose a “Framework Excavation” strategy. This strategy selectively creates local enlargements within the microporous framework to generate sufficient space for the in situ formation of metal clusters, while the retained narrow channels kinetically confine the as-formed clusters and allow substrates to pass through the pores to fully access the highly exposed cluster sites. As a demonstration, chemically stable UiO-66 was engineered with missing-Zr 6 -node defects and employed as a host for the ship-in-a-bottle assembly of Cu 3 molecular clusters, yielding Cu 3 @UiO-66-Exc. In electrocatalytic nitrite reduction, Cu 3 @UiO-66-Exc achieves an NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 98.7% and a yield rate of 19.21 mg cm −2 h −1 , with stable performance over 300 h of cumulative electrolysis. Mechanistic studies, including DMPO-H spin-trapping, in situ infrared spectroscopy and theoretical computations, reveal that the confined Cu 3 architecture promotes active-hydrogen generation and successive hydrogenation of nitrogen-containing intermediates. This work establishes a catalyst support design principle that enables the in situ generation, long-term retention, and high site accessibility of molecular clusters within a robust microporous framework.
authors: Zhaoling Li, Kangning Zhou, Fengdan Ruan, Ailijiang Tuerdi, Xiao Liu, Fangfang Pan

10.1002/adfm.79112.title: Phase-Selective NiCo Oxide Electrodes Enable Paired Electrochemical Conversion and Valorization of Nitrogen-Containing Wastewaters
10.1002/adfm.79112.abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional wastewater treatment generally focuses on pollutant removal while consuming energy and recovering little chemical value. Here, we report a phase-selective Ni-Co oxide platform for paired electrochemical conversion of nitrogen-containing contaminants, coupling cathodic acetonitrile (AN) hydrogenation to ethylamine (EA) with anodic hydrazine oxidation to N 2 . Annealing NiCo layered double hydroxide precursor under Ar and in air produces cubic NiCoO 2 and spinel NiCo 2 O 4 , respectively, which exhibit complementary catalytic preferences. NiCoO 2 achieves 90.4%-91.2% Faradaic efficiency toward EA over 50-200 mA cm −2 in 8 wt.% AN, whereas NiCo 2 O 4 approaches 100% Faradaic efficiency toward N 2 over the same current-density range. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that this catalytic complementarity arises from phase-dependent reaction energetics: NiCoO 2 favors H-assisted AN hydrogenation while enabling facile EA release, whereas NiCo 2 O 4 promotes hydrazine dehydrogenation and, critically, N 2 desorption and active-site regeneration. A 100 cm 2 membrane-electrode assembly maintains 88-93% EA Faradaic efficiency and stable paired operation for 120 h. The paired system was further demonstrated using separately collected industrial wastewaters, together with downstream EA recovery and a preliminary process-level assessment. These results establish crystal-phase regulation of reaction and product-release energetics as a strategy for matching distinct electrode reactions within paired wastewater valorization.
authors: Jiangzhou Qin, Pan Zhu, Yanyu Lu, Chenxi Li, Baojun Liu

10.1002/adfm.79120.title: Low Hydrogen Crossover Poly(Arylene Quinuclidinium) Anion Exchange Membranes for Renewables-Compatible Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.79120.abstract: ABSTRACT Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) represents a transformative approach to green hydrogen generation, combining the kinetic advantages of alkaline systems with zero-gap configurations and platinum-group-metal-free catalyst compatibility. Current implementations, however, face major challenges, including device durability, adaptability to fluctuating renewable energy sources, and safety concerns due to hydrogen crossover. In this work, we demonstrate that poly(arylene quinuclidinium) membranes address these challenges through an engineered polymer backbone featuring extended arene units, which effectively enhance dimensional integrity and inhibit gas crossover. Therefore, the hydrogen permeation suppression achieves a remarkably low H 2 -in-O 2 crossover of only 0.53 vol% @0.1 A cm −2 , and delivers a high current density of 8.5 A cm −2 @2.0 V with stable operation over 1250 h. The optimized PQTPQui-15 membrane demonstrates practical potential in a kilowatt-level, three-cell electrolyzer stack. Furthermore, photovoltaic-integrated systems maintain safe operation (H 2 -in-O 2 < 0.13 vol%) across 0-190% load fluctuations, and respond to sub-second power transients while sustaining current densities of 0.04−1.91 A cm −2 . These advancements underscore the critical need to enhance the gas barrier properties of anion exchange membranes and establish a new paradigm for durable, rapidly responsive electrolyzers compatible with intermittent renewables.
authors: Tao Wang, Weijie Chen, Xiaoli Qu, Li Yang, Jianguo Wang, Chao Liu, Ping Wang, Yunsheng Ding, Haibing Wei

10.1002/adfm.78998.title: Dirac Semimetallicity Enabled by Stripe Antiferromagnetism in Monolayer FeSe
10.1002/adfm.78998.abstract: ABSTRACT Monolayer FeSe is a central platform for iron-based superconductivity, yet the electronic phases emerging from its competing magnetic orders remain elusive. Here we identify a Dirac semimetal state in monolayer FeSe induced by stripe antiferromagnetism, which hosts symmetry-protected Dirac nodes near the Fermi level. We show that breaking a single mirror symmetry enables an odd inter-orbital coupling between opposite-parity Fe states, enforcing robust Dirac crossings with a nontrivial Wilson-loop topology and boundary-dependent edge modes. We further predict a strong orbital diamagnetic susceptibility as a direct experimental fingerprint of this Dirac phase. Our work establishes FeSe as a magnetically tunable route to topological quasiparticles in iron-based two-dimensional quantum materials.
authors: Darius-Alexandru Deaconu, Aneesh Agarwal, Sam Azadi, Rodion Vladimirovich Belosludov, Robert-Jan Slager, Mohammad Saeed Bahramy

10.1002/adfm.79055.title: Stacking-Tuned Phonon Renormalization and Effective Heat Transport in Moiré Semiconductor Superlattices
10.1002/adfm.79055.abstract: ABSTRACT Optically driven moiré semiconductor bilayers involve coupled phonon anharmonicity, interlayer interactions, and local heat dissipation, but experimental benchmarks across supported homo- and heterobilayers remain limited. Here, we combine temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy, excitation-power-dependent Raman thermometry, and photoluminescence to study twisted MoS 2 /MoS 2 , WS 2 /WS 2 , and MoS 2 /WS 2 bilayers. From 90 to 300 K, both homobilayers show conventional softening of Raman-active phonons with negative effective anharmonic coefficients. In contrast, the WS 2 -derived out-of-plane A -mode in the MoS 2 /WS 2 heterobilayer hardens with increasing temperature, exhibiting a positive linear temperature coefficient of +0.00700 ± 0.00029 cm − 1 K − 1 and a positive effective Balkanski coefficient of +1.28 ± 0.19 cm − 1 , while other modes remain softening-dominant. Photoluminescence reveals an interlayer excitonic channel only in the heterobilayer, indicating an interface-specific phonon renormalization pathway beyond equilibrium anharmonic decay. Using two excitation objectives with distinct laser-heating radii, the supported Raman thermometry resolves mode-dependent effective thermal-transport parameters and reduces covariance in extracting in-plane heat-transport and heat-sinking coefficients. We further develop a physics-guided monolayer-to-stacked neural-network framework to reconstruct Raman spectra across temperature and power conditions and identify optimal optothermal regimes. These results establish heterointerface-controlled phonon renormalization as a key factor in phonon dynamics controlling heat dissipation and provide a scalable platform for thermal design in moiré quantum devices.
authors: Choudhury Abinash Bhuyan, Antonio Cobarrubia, Shrawan Roy, Arik R. Ahmed, Nicholas Schottle, Ryan Palmares, Jaedan Ford, Vincent Juliano, Nate Webb, Carlos M. Torres, Steve Smith, Santosh KC, Mansour Mortazavi, Sanjay K. Behura

10.1002/adfm.79087.title: Core-Periphery Fullerene Architectures Engineer Catalytic Interfaces for Efficient Neutral Hydrogen Evolution
10.1002/adfm.79087.abstract: ABSTRACT Neutral hydrogen evolution is governed by coupled active-site and solvent processes, posing a great challenge for catalyst design. Here, ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters are anchored on a sulfonated fullerene scaffold (Ru/C 60 -S), exploiting its core-periphery architecture to couple active-site energetics with interfacial hydration. Electronic interaction with the fullerene cage polarizes Ru sites, facilitating water activation and moderating H/OH binding, while the sulfonated periphery establishes a less ordered and more field-responsive interfacial hydrogen-bond network. Ru/C 60 -S requires only 10 mV to reach 10 mA cm −2 , sustains 100 mA cm −2 for over 1000 h in phosphate-buffered solution, and exhibits minimal activity loss from alkaline to neutral media. Molecular dynamics simulations, operando Raman, in situ FTIR and local pH measurements corroborate this interfacial restructuring under neutral HER conditions. Targeted perturbation of the fullerene periphery rigidifies the hydrogen-bond network and is accompanied by increased isotope sensitivity, slower interfacial kinetics, and diminished HER activity. These results identify interfacial hydration as a kinetically important component of neutral HER and demonstrate a core-periphery molecular strategy for cooperatively regulating active-site energetics and solvent organization.
authors: Wenhao Yang, Jiashuo Fu, Liting Cui, Qi Huang, Shuqian Xie, Zengyuan Li, Jijie Li, Wen Li, Ping Peng, Haining Wang, Fang-Fang Li

10.1002/adfm.79076.title: Microfluidic ER-Targeted Photodynamic Vesicles Overcome Radioresistance and Boost Antitumor Immunity via Organelle Stress Amplification
10.1002/adfm.79076.abstract: ABSTRACT Radioresistance remains a significant obstacle in oncology, underpinned by adaptive cellular stress responses that attenuate radiation efficacy. We present microfluidically engineered, endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeted photodynamic vesicles designed to surmount radioresistance through a spatiotemporally controlled, phototriggered reactive oxygen species (ROS) cascade. Upon 660 nm irradiation, these vesicles elicit an organelle-confined oxidative burst, initiating a self-amplifying cycle of calcium efflux and acute proteotoxic stress. This photodynamic priming achieves a superior sensitization enhancement ratio (SER = 1.35 ± 0.16) versus non-targeted vesicles (SER = 1.01 ± 0.03), drastically reducing clonogenic survival to 1.3 ± 0.6% at 6.0 Gy X-ray. Mechanistically, this synergy disrupts multiple resistance pathways by exacerbating genomic instability, depleting glutathione defenses, and inducing concurrent apoptosis and pyroptosis. Transcriptomic analysis reveals the regulation of radiosensitivity-associated genes, confirming comprehensive reprogramming of cellular stress responses. Crucially, this cascade induces immunogenic cell death (ICD), elevating dendritic cell maturation to 39.5 ± 5.5% in tumor-draining lymph nodes. Combined with localized radiotherapy, this approach profoundly amplifies systemic antitumor immunity, increasing intratumoral CD8 + T cell infiltration and robustly suppressing distant metastasis. This work establishes organelle-targeted ROS cascade amplification as a paradigm-shifting radiosensitization strategy that extends beyond conventional DNA-centric approaches, thereby unveiling novel therapeutic avenues for intractable malignancies.
authors: Yuwei Wang, Ziyao Lu, Jiangnan Shi, Wei Wang, Xinyu He, Hui Chen, Huiyu Bu, Shaojie Hua, Yutong Shi, Lin Guo, Hui He, Zhengqing Guo

10.1002/adfm.79071.title: Ratiometric Copper Iodide Scintillators for Temperature-Resolved X-Ray Imaging
10.1002/adfm.79071.abstract: ABSTRACT Multifunctional X-ray imaging that simultaneously resolves structural and thermal information is highly desirable under thermally dynamic and extreme conditions. Yet conventional systems require separate temperature sensors, which increases complexity and limits direct spatial correlation between the two. Here, we report a structurally engineered copper iodide (Cu-I) cluster scintillator that integrates high-resolution x-ray imaging with ratiometric thermometry in a single material. Regulating the Cu-I cluster and ligand coordination environment yields dual-emissive Cu 4 I 4 (3F-py) 4 , which exhibits two well-resolved excited-state emissions and a high light yield of 40 000 photons MeV −1 . The two channels respond differently to temperature, producing a pronounced intensity-ratio change and continuous radioluminescence color evolution from orange to blue as the temperature decreases from 300 to 100 K. Excited-state analysis reveals that the electron-withdrawing substituent stabilizes ligand-centered frontier orbitals and lowers the barrier for interconversion from the cluster-centered state to the metal/halide-to-ligand charge-transfer state, enabling broad-range thermochromism. The resulting scintillation screen achieves a spatial resolution exceeding 13 lp mm −1 , while the Boltzmann-type temperature dependence of the emission ratio allows quantitative thermal information to be encoded directly into the spectral ratio and color of x-ray images. This work establishes excited-state engineering of cluster scintillators as a strategy for temperature-resolved x-ray imaging.
authors: Wentao Wu, Simil Thomas, Feng Gao, Xin Zhu, Osman M. Bakr, Husam N. Alshareef, Jian-Xin Wang, Omar F. Mohammed

10.1002/adfm.79034.title: Bistable Isochoric Chiral Metamaterials with Reprogrammable Multiaxial Responses
10.1002/adfm.79034.abstract: ABSTRACT Reprogrammable materials enable post-fabrication tuning of mechanical properties, yet existing concepts are largely confined to uniaxial responses. Engineering materials, on the other hand, are routinely subjected to loading in multiple directions, yet their mechanical responses along these directions cannot be tuned in situ. Here, we introduce a class of chiral metamaterials built from isochoric rotationally bistable units that unlock reprogrammable behavior across multiaxial loading states. Integrating theory, simulations, and experiments, we demonstrate that the bistable units can reversibly switch between open and closed states under clockwise or counterclockwise torque, enabling isochoric switching between soft and stiff responses without geometric reconfiguration of the surrounding architecture. Upon selective activation of given bistable cores, the metamaterial exhibits reprogrammable snap-through instabilities that alter in situ global buckling modes and energy dissipation pathways. Under multiaxial loading, a set of volume-dominated properties, including effective bulk modulus and volumetric instability, can be reprogrammed, enabling erasable and rewritable two-dimensional snapping sequences that encode complex mechanical memory within the material. Beyond property tuning, the work suggests a scalable, reprogrammable framework that can be extended to Cosserat media to achieve multiaxial multifunctionality in soft robotics, fluidic devices, and mechanically intelligent systems.
authors: Shujia Chen, Lei Wu, Jingran Liu, Damiano Pasini

10.1002/adfm.79036.title: Deciphering Anomalous Luminescence in Highly Doped Transition-Metal Phosphors: Spin-Exchange, Unusual Site Occupancy, and Trace Impurities
10.1002/adfm.79036.abstract: ABSTRACT Anomalous luminescence in phosphors highly doped with transition-metal ions (e.g., , ) has attracted significant interest for multifunctional optical materials and devices. However, rational optimization and materials design have been hindered by controversial mechanisms. Here, we establish a unified analytical framework for deciphering such complex emissions across a diverse range of host systems. Our framework categorizes the possible origins into distinct classes- transition-metal dimers or clusters, configuration-associated isolated transition-metal centers, and impurities. We demonstrate that the various anomalous luminescence phenomena observed in highly doped transition-metal phosphors cannot be explained by exchange-coupled dimers alone, but instead arise from a variety of configuration-dependent effects that arise at high doping levels (e.g., unusual site occupancy, defect-dopant complexes, or alternative valence states), or trace impurities. In particular, the intervalence charge transfer transition in transition-metal dimers is expected to be predominantly non-radiative due to the large structural relaxation energy involved. This study provides a generalizable framework for deciphering complex luminescence in highly doped systems, reconciling long-standing controversies and offering a mechanistic foundation for interpreting broadband near-infrared emissions in highly doped phosphors for multifunctional optical applications.
authors: Qiaoling Chen, Litian Lin, Qinshi Hu, Hui Wang, Chang-Kui Duan

10.1002/adfm.79096.title: Hydrocarbothermal Reduction Co-Upcycling of Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries via Waste Plastics for Enabling Efficient Water Purification and Lithium Resource Recovery
10.1002/adfm.79096.abstract: ABSTRACT The upcycling of spent lithium-ion batteries and waste plastics is critical for resource security and sustainable development. However, current recycling paradigms treat these waste streams separately, leading to energy-intensive battery recovery and low-value plastic downcycling. Here, we present a waste polyethylene-driven hydrocarbothermal reduction strategy for upcycling spent LiNi 0.6 Co 0.2 Mn 0.2 O 2 (NCM 622 ) cathodes by exploiting the dual functions of plastics as in situ carbon sources and reducing agents, making a breakthrough on their co-processing and joint upcycling, and constructing a closed-loop system integrating mixed-waste upcycling, water purification, and lithium recycling. Hydrocarbothermal reduction via polyethylene pyrolysis induces pronounced interlayer expansion and octahedral distortion within NCM 622 , triggering structural collapse and driving the formation of a stable NiCoMn alloy nanorod deposited on a carbon nanosheet (NiCoMn/C) catalyst. Kinetic analysis shows that Co sites act as the primary catalytic centers, while Ni and Mn mediate charge transfer. NiCoMn/C enables efficient peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation for bisphenol A degradation with a rate constant of 0.411 min −1 , demonstrating competitive catalytic performance among reported alloy-carbon catalysts. Meanwhile, this system achieves 87% lithium recovery, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, and strong economic viability. This work establishes a generalizable paradigm for integrated waste-to-resource conversion and environmental remediation.
authors: Shengjia Ma, Wei Jin, Yaping Zhao

10.1002/adfm.79109.title: A Starfish-Inspired Hierarchical Multimodal Flexible Sensor for Decoupled Thumb Motion Perception and Virtual Human-Machine Interaction
10.1002/adfm.79109.abstract: ABSTRACT Wearable human-machine interfaces (HMIs) require sensing systems that combine high accuracy, mechanical compliance, and low system complexity. Here, we present a starfish-inspired, hierarchically decoupled multimodal flexible sensor for high-fidelity thumb motion perception and virtual human-machine interaction. Inspired by the distributed sensing mechanism of starfish tube feet, the architecture integrates radially distributed strain channels with spatially isolated pressure nodes. This design enables simultaneous sensing of global deformation and localized tactile stimuli while minimizing mechanical coupling. Finite element simulations and experimental characterization demonstrate effective strain amplification, low interchannel coupling, stable electromechanical performance, and long-term durability. Combined with a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) classifier, the system achieves validation and test accuracies of 99.82% and 99.27%, respectively, for six thumb motions, with strong cross-subject generalization. The decoded motions enable intuitive, real-time control in a virtual environment without bulky sensor gloves or external tracking systems. This work establishes a bioinspired strategy for structurally decoupled multimodal flexible sensing and provides a promising platform for wearable HMIs and intelligent robotics.
authors: Lu Liu, Zengbai Ouyang, Mengze Zhang, Jiantao Yao, Xiaoli Jia, Peng Zhang, Bo Han, Yu Gu, Yundou Xu

10.1002/adfm.79075.title: Endosomal Escape of siRNA Polyplexes: A Molecular Dynamics Perspective on Underlying Mechanisms
10.1002/adfm.79075.abstract: ABSTRACT To achieve a therapeutic effect, nanoparticles delivering nucleic acids must facilitate endosomal escape (EE) of their cargo. Despite extensive research, the mechanisms that lead to an effective EE are not sufficiently understood. Herein, we compare the EE behavior of four polymeric formulations (polyplexes) and one lipid nanoparticle (LNP) in vitro. Simultaneously, we utilized molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in all atom (AA) and coarse grained (CG) resolutions to differentiate the interaction of those formulations with endosomal membranes. The identified interaction patterns were discussed in perspective with the in vitro performance of the formulations: On the one hand, the results emphasize the benefit of hydrophobic residues in the nanoparticles. On the other hand, the role of anionic lipids in the biological membranes is demonstrated by MD. Different interaction modes of polyplex formulations with endosomal membranes are visualized in simulation with the aim to distinguish potential EE mechanisms from one another. This work highlights the power of MD simulations for taking a big step toward explaining differences observed in vitro on a molecular level and toward better understanding EE efficiency.
authors: Katharina M. Steinegger, Min Jiang, Florian Belger, Fabian Link, Benjamin Winkeljann, Olivia M. Merkel

10.1002/adfm.78370.title: Structure-Activity-Stability Tradeoffs of Pt Cathodes in Alkaline Water Electrolysis
10.1002/adfm.78370.abstract: ABSTRACT Due to its high activity for the hydrogen evolution reaction at low overpotential in alkaline conditions, platinum is a promising cathode catalyst material for next-generation, high current density alkaline water electrolysis (AWE). However, its implementation in industrially relevant zero-gap AWE remains poorly understood, particularly regarding catalyst utilization, durability, and impurity tolerance. Here we establish electrode structure-activity-stability relationships for a series of Pt cathodes prepared by galvanic displacement, sputtering, annealing, and dealloying, allowing systematic control over microstructure and adhesion. Annealed sputtered Pt presents moderate intrinsic activity but maintains stable operation over 1000 h at 2 A·cm −2 . A leached nanoporous Pt cathode achieves a high electrochemically active surface area with sustained performance under industrially relevant conditions. Beyond intrinsic catalyst properties, we reveal that the presence of Fe impurities critically governs cathode behavior. Using a rotating disk electrode and single-cell studies, Fe is shown to deposit within the HER operating window, replacing Pt active sites and evolving into dendritic structures that dominate electrode performance. These findings demonstrate that the use of Pt cathodes in AWE is dictated not only by catalyst design but also by impurity management and establishing key design principles for next-generation high-current-density cathodes.

10.1002/adfm.77831.title: Sky-Directional Radiative Cooling Meta-Films for Daylighting Windows
10.1002/adfm.77831.abstract: ABSTRACT Radiative cooling of vertical surfaces is constrained by the trade-off between visible transparency and directional thermal emission. Existing asymmetric emitters suppress ground-directed radiation but are opaque, preventing window integration. Here, we present a transparent asymmetric emitter (TAE) that resolves this limitation via a geometry-mediated optical design. The TAE employs a microprism array featuring ground-facing facets with partial silver coverage, enabling decoupled control of visible transmittance and mid-infrared emissivity. Angle-resolved measurements show high visible transmittance (75%) and strong anisotropic thermal response, with sky-facing emissivity of 0.95 and near-zero ground-facing absorption. Controlled vacuum experiments demonstrate maximum temperature reductions of 26.4°C. Outdoor experiments using solar-transmittance-matched references confirm consistent cooling, with maximum temperature reductions of ∼10°C at ground temperatures of 31.5°C. A global energy model incorporating location-specific, angle-dependent optical properties and realistic ground temperatures is developed to capture radiative effects in vertical windows. The model predicts a latitude-dependent trend, where energy savings are maximized in low-latitude regions and gradually diminish toward higher latitudes. Notably, the TAE achieves energy performance comparable to the ideal limit of seasonal emissivity-modulation technologies. As a scalable platform, the TAE establishes a viable route for integrating radiative cooling into windows without compromising daylighting.

10.1002/adfm.76449.title: An Integrated Recycling Strategy for Selective Lithium Separation and Reconstruction of Mixed Spent Cathodes for Water Oxidation
10.1002/adfm.76449.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is critical for low-carbon development and responsible resource utilization. Here, we report a green recycling strategy that simultaneously processes spent ternary (s-NCM) and spent lithium iron phosphate (s-LFP) cathode materials with diverse compositions, enabling compatibility with a wide range of feedstocks. An electrochemical pre-delithiation step achieves highly selective lithium recovery with efficiencies above 99% and negligible transition-metal loss (<0.15%). The delithiated residues are subsequently reconstructed into oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts through a low-cost, low-energy process without external metal additives. Owing to the intrinsic Ni-Fe synergy derived from s-NCM and s-LFP, the resulting NiFe (rec-NCM955/LFP) pre-catalyst exhibits outstanding OER performance, delivering a low overpotential of 234 mV at 10 mA·cm −2 , a small Tafel slope of 28.4 mV·dec −1 , and stable operation at 500 mA·cm −2 for 200 h in an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer. Economic and environmental analyses further confirm the scalability and industrial feasibility of this approach. This work offers an integrated and practical solution for selective lithium recovery and direct cathode upcycling, advancing circular LIB recycling and green hydrogen production.

10.1002/adfm.77724.title: Thermoreversible In Situ Adaptive Biogel for Conformal Electrophysiological Interfaces with Long-Term Robustness
10.1002/adfm.77724.abstract: ABSTRACT Robust skin-electronic interfaces are essential for continuous epidermal electrophysiological monitoring, enabling real-time tracking of physiological states and early detection of abnormalities. An ideal skin-integrated interface should simultaneously provide adaptive conformability, robust adhesion, and long-term stability. However, interfacial state mismatch arises from the conflict between the adaptive state required for intimate skin contact and the durable state needed for stable long-term operation, making it exceedingly difficult to reconcile these attributes within a single interface design. Here, we report an in situ adaptive biogel that, enabled by thermoreversible liquid-to-gel transition of gelatin and synergistic interactions imparted by an ionic medium, rapidly establishes a skin interface with conformal contact, robust adhesion (7.06 N cm −1 ), and month-long stability. These properties endow the interface with low-impedance coupling, motion-artifact suppression, and sustained functional reliability, supporting acquisition of multiple electrophysiological signals, continuous high-fidelity electrocardiogram monitoring during 24 h of daily activities, and electrocardiogram recordings during a 30-day evaluation with a signal-to-noise ratio of 21.41 ± 2.34 dB. Furthermore, a soft chest patch integrating the biogel enables synchronous electrocardiogram and respiration monitoring for dynamic cardiorespiratory analysis and assessment of apnea-like respiratory interruptions. This work establishes a general strategy for engineering robust skin-conformal biointerfaces for long-term wearable bioelectronics.

10.1002/adfm.78268.title: Conjugated Coordination Polymer Aerogels with Disordered Interfacial Water Structures for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Oxygen Evolution Kinetics
10.1002/adfm.78268.abstract: ABSTRACT Beyond rational design of active sites, regulation of the local chemical environment of electrocatalysts to promote the reactant transport dynamics is crucial for enhancing the reaction kinetics, which faces significant limitations owing to the rigid hydrogen-bond networks formed by interfacial water molecules. Here, an entropy-derived regulation strategy was proposed to engineer disordered interfacial water structures, which induces a flexible and adaptive environment that can substantially enhance the reactant transport dynamics and reaction kinetics. Taking a conjugated coordination polymer aerogel with homogeneous single-atom metal active sites as the model system, a comparative study investigating high-entropy and low-entropy conjugated coordination polymer aerogels (denoted as HE-CCPA and LE-CCPA) was carried out. Our findings reveal that, relative to LE-CCPA, the inhomogeneity of electron density distribution and reactant adsorption across multiple different single-atom metal sites of the HE-CCPA profoundly disrupts the rigid hydrogen-bond network, resulting in disordered interfacial water structures that can appreciably facilitate the transport dynamics of hydroxide ion reactants to improve the alkaline oxygen evolution kinetics. These findings highlight disordered interfacial water engineering as a promising approach for performance enhancement in widespread aqueous electrocatalysis.
authors: Shuting Zhan, Shouhan Zhang, Xinyue Xu, Ziwei Ma, Li Hu, Yuhang Wan, Hui Zheng, Longsheng Zhang, Tianxi Liu, Yi Xie

10.1002/adfm.78181.title: Phase-Change Microcapsules Enable Polyoxymethylene-Fiber-Based Aerogels With Enhanced Sub-Ambient Radiative Cooling and All-Day Thermal Management
10.1002/adfm.78181.abstract: ABSTRACT Current radiative cooling materials face significant challenges in managing temperature fluctuations between day and night. Although phase change materials can provide a thermal management effect through reversible phase transitions, their high thermal conductivity leads to a fast thermal response, which hinders efficient radiative cooling and thermal insulation. In this work, a bilayer aerogel composite is developed by integrating a polyoxymethylene-fiber-based aerogel outer layer with a sodium alginate-based aerogel inner layer with phase-change microcapsules incorporated, thereby enhancing radiative cooling while providing thermal insulation and buffering. With such an integrated design, an average solar reflectivity of 93.53% over 0.3-2.5 µm and a high average emissivity of 96.11% within the atmospheric window (8-13 µm) are achieved in the outer layer, while a high latent heat capacity of 159.8 J g −1 and a low thermal conductivity of 0.0678 W m −1 K −1 are maintained in the inner layer. Owing to these characteristics, the bilayer aerogel composite exhibits maximum temperature differences of −18.3°C (daytime) and +9.3°C (nighttime) between the sub-ambient and internal cavity ambient temperatures. These values are 8.0°C lower and 4.4°C higher than those of the bilayer aerogel composite without phase-change microcapsules, respectively. Thus, the developed composite shows potential for sustainable and environmentally friendly thermal regulation in buildings.
authors: Yumeng Dong, Tao Shi, Mengyue Li, Yatao Wang, Huan Liu, Xiaofeng Ma, Xiaodong Wang

10.1002/adfm.78271.title: Reconfigurable In-Sensor Processing Based on Photo-Electric Tailored Photovoltaics
10.1002/adfm.78271.abstract: ABSTRACT Machine vision enables artificial intelligence and edge computing, yet its efficiency is hindered by energy-intensive data transfer between sensing and processing units. Two-dimensional (2D) optoelectronic neuromorphic devices provide an appealing route toward in-sensor vision, but existing approaches typically rely on high operating power, complex multi-terminal architectures, or elaborate fabrication, limiting scalability and practicality. Here, we demonstrate a simple two-terminal MoS 2 metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) photodetector that realizes reconfigurable and non-volatile photovoltaic responses through photo-assisted and electric-field-directed programming of native sulfur-vacancy-related defects, without intentional defect-inducing pretreatment or additional functional layers. Under simultaneous 650 nm laser illumination and voltage-pulse programming, seven stable short-circuit photocurrent states with reversible magnitude and polarity are deterministically programmed, a functionality unattainable under optical or electrical stimulation alone. Spatially resolved measurements indicate asymmetric contact modulation after photo-electric programming, which is supported by local photocurrent mapping, low-temperature PL defect-related emissions at ∼1.81 and ∼1.83 eV, KPFM surface-potential measurements, and TEM/FFT lattice-order analysis. Leveraging these programmable photoresponses, hardware-measured device outputs support proof-of-concept motion detection, edge extraction with 95% Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) and 22 dB Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), and front-end preprocessing for handwritten digit recognition with accuracies exceeding 97%, establishing a defect-engineered pathway toward energy-efficient in-sensor machine vision hardware.
authors: Qiaolin Gu, Daozhi Shen, Linglan Guo, Ran Tang, Yufan Mao, Feifan Wang, Dingyun Zhang, Gangli Zhao, Xinquan Zhang, Mingjun Ren, Limin Zhu

10.1002/adfm.78195.title: Revealing Exceptional Supercapacitive-Storage Performance: Atomic-Level Insight Into Cu-Incorporation Activated Amorphous CoNi Hydroxide
10.1002/adfm.78195.abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel-cobalt-based hydroxides have established their niche in stationary storage applications where high theoretical capacitance, affordability, and carbon footprint matter most. Nonetheless, realizing their high rate capability and enduring cycling stability are challenged, originating from sluggish electron transfer and inadequate mechanical strength. Here, we pioneered to leverage on atomically uniform Cu-incorporation via light illumination to optimize the electronic and atomic structure of amorphous CoNi hydroxide. Remarkably, the as-fabricated amorphous CuCoNi hydroxide electrode embraces an ultra-high rate capacity of 74.1% following a 50-fold increase of current density and an unprecedented cycling life (∼ 92.6% of the initial capacitance retention after 100 000 cycles at 10 mA cm −2 ), far exceeding performances reported in the literature. The exceptional electrochemical performance could be attributed to Cu introduction, which leads to the transfer of more electrons from Ni to Co during the energy storage process, facilitating Ni in achieving the tetravalent state and obtaining additional pseudocapacitance. Additionally, the Cu-incorporation could effectively induce the appearance of defect states and lower the adsorption energy of OH − , thus expediting surface redox reactions. This atomic structure tuning strategy may shed light on the electrode material design for high-performance energy storage devices.
authors: Baohong Zhang, Yanhong Li, Haoran Xu, Dongfeng Zhang, Zhi Cai, Lidong Li

10.1002/adfm.78231.title: Novel Stress-Evolution Model for NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 Cathodes: Determining Localized Accumulation and Diffusive Transfer Based on Tension-Compression Asymmetry
10.1002/adfm.78231.abstract: ABSTRACT O3-NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM) is a promising high-energy-density cathode for sodium-ion batteries. However, the long-term cycling performance is hindered by particle fracture caused by non-uniform stress distribution. The mechanisms of non-mechanical stress accumulation in intergranular and intragranular regions, as well as the long-range transfer of stress interactions, remain unclear. Herein, we used DFT calculations and mechanical parameter analyses at the unit-cell scale to identify SOC-dependent “tension-compression asymmetry” (Δ E SOC ) as a key descriptor. Correlation analysis reveals that Δ E SOC governs the continuity of intragranular strain and the magnitude of intergranular strain, enabling precise mapping of local stress accumulation. We developed a stress-transfer model to describe directional stress propagation, demonstrating that cumulative stress is the product-sum of Δ E SOC values along the transfer path. This model elucidates how intragranular stress drives microcrack formation. Guided by these insights, we employed Ca 2+ doping to regulate Δ E SOC , effectively reducing stress accumulation and enhancing cycling stability. After 1000 cycles at 1C, the Ca-doped NFM retained 62.1% of the initial capacity, significantly outperforming the pristine NFM (18.3%). This work unifies localized stress accumulation and diffusive transfer mechanisms, providing a deeper understanding of stress-induced failure in layered cathodes.
authors: Lingfeng Shi, Fanbo Wu, Ziwei Liu, Yehang Dou, Ke Li, Mengjie Zhang, Yongsheng Pan, Yulin Ma, Geping Yin, Shuaifeng Lou, Hua Huo

10.1002/adfm.78158.title: Atomically Thin 2D Perovskite/MoS2 Heterojunctions With Programmable Twist Angle for High-Performance Photodetection
10.1002/adfm.78158.abstract: ABSTRACT Twist angle provides a versatile geometric degree of freedom to engineer interfacial coupling and carrier transport in van der Waals heterostructures. However, deterministic control of twist and its quantitative correlation with device performance remain challenging in hybrid perovskite/2D systems. Here, we report a growth-integrated, in situ strategy to fabricate atomically thin 2D (PEA) 2 PbBr 4 /MoS 2 heterojunctions with programmable twist angles spanning 0° to 60°, establishing twist as a reproducible device parameter. Twist-resolved Raman and photoluminescence mapping reveal registry-dependent interlayer coupling, while x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density functional theory demonstrate twist-tunable charge transfer and electronic reconstruction. Photodetection and transport exhibit a pronounced nonmonotonic dependence on twist angle, with an intrinsic optimum at 30°. The 30°-(PEA) 2 PbBr 4 /MoS 2 heterojunction exhibits ultrahigh photoresponsivity of 34 A W −1 , a specific detectivity of ∼2.5 × 10 12 Jones, an I on /I off up to 4.5 × 10 6 , and effective field-effect mobility of 182.5 cm 2 V −1 s −1 under 405 nm laser illumination, reflecting maximized interfacial synergy. Our work provides theoretical insights into the design of perovskite/TMD heterojunction electronics by establishing a quantitative relationship between twist angle and optoelectronic performance in the (PEA) 2 PbBr 4 /MoS 2 system, offering guidance for the optimization of high-gain photodetectors and low-power switching devices.
authors: Damin Liu, Zisheng Tang, Kefeiyang Hu, Sicheng Luo, Jieheng Lv, Jun Zhang, Jianhui Li, Mai Mao, Xiaoqian Wang, Dafu Zhao, Tongle Bu, Zhaoyong Zou, Wenchao Huang, Yong Liu

10.1002/adfm.78358.title: Full Component Utilization: Targeted Separation of Mn/Li From Spent LiMn2O4 for Reconstructing High-Performance Single-Crystal Cathode Materials
10.1002/adfm.78358.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing green and sustainable regeneration technologies for spent lithium-ion battery cathode materials is of great significance for establishing a self-sufficient and sustainable production model. In this study, full utilization of all metal components in spent LiMn 2 O 4 cathode materials is achieved through a strategy involving the directional separation of manganese and lithium. Based on the Ostwald ripening principle, spent LiMn 2 O 4 is regenerated into high-performance single-crystal cathodes. The recycled single-crystal lithium manganate (R-LMO) cathode mitigates lattice strain, suppresses Jahn-Teller effect-driven irreversible phase transitions, and enhances structural integrity. Simultaneously, the introduction of oxygen vacancies (OVs) lowers the Li + diffusion energy barrier, thereby improving lithium storage performance in R-LMO. Compared to commercial LiMn 2 O 4 (LMO), the R-LMO cathode exhibits superior electrochemical performance at both ambient and elevated temperatures (55°C). After 1000 cycles at 1C, the capacity retention rate of recycled R-LMO reached 81.2%, surpassing that of LMO (68.6%). Moreover, this method avoids the introduction of external ions that could contaminate the final product and generates no chemical waste during the recycling process, eliminating the need for post-treatment of waste streams or effluents. This work provides new insights into component separation from spent cathodes and lays the foundation for sustainable, cobalt-free cathode production.
authors: Bao Zhang, Bowen Zhu, Zhen Liang, Le Yu, Zhongren Zhou, Chao Li, Fang Cheng, Hao Wu, Jing Feng, Peng Dong, Weili Song, Yingjie Zhang, Yannan Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78269.title: Perovskite Microwire Crystals Encapsulated by Nano-Grating Structured Small Molecular Film for Polarization-Sensitive and Highly Stable Photodetectors
10.1002/adfm.78269.abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskites have emerged as promising materials for high-performance photodetectors owing to their strong optical absorption, high carrier mobility, and long carrier diffusion lengths. However, their intrinsic instability remains a major obstacle to practical applications. Here, MAPbI 3 microwires are encapsulated with a nano-grating structured 2,7-dioctyl[1]benzothieno[3,2-b][1]benzothiophene (C8BTBT) film. The hydrophobic nano-grating layer markedly enhances stability, enabling the device to retain 94.0% of its initial photocurrent after 80 days in air. Benefiting from improved light harvesting and carrier transport, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.35 × 10 4 A W −1 and a detectivity of 4.85 × 10 11 Jones. Moreover, the combined anisotropy of the MAPbI 3 microwire arrays and the C8BTBT nano-grating yields strong polarization sensitivity with a dichroic ratio ( I max / I min ) of 1.87.

10.1002/adfm.78304.title: Machine-Learning-Decoded Dual-Channel Photoelectrochemical Fingerprinting at Porphyrinic MOF-on-MOF Heterointerfaces for Intelligent Molecular Profiling
10.1002/adfm.78304.abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate discrimination of structurally analogous sulfur-containing molecules with overlapping photoelectrochemical (PEC) responses remains a major challenge for conventional PEC sensors that rely on one-dimensional photocurrent readouts. Herein, we develop a dual-channel PEC fingerprinting platform that pairs Zn-TCPP with a rationally constructed Cu-TCPP@Zn-TCPP MOF-on-MOF heterostructure and integrates their paired responses with machine-learning (ML) algorithms. Unlike traditional single-signal approaches, Zn-TCPP and the layered Cu-TCPP@Zn-TCPP heterointerface serve as two distinct transduction interfaces that convert molecule-dependent interfacial interactions into dual-interface PEC fingerprints. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that these discriminative responses arise from coupled molecular and interfacial effects. These effects include molecular-size-dependent interfacial accessibility, frontier-orbital-influenced hole consumption, and, in the case of glutathione (GSH), Cu-S-related modulation of the cathodic oxygen-reduction-related electron-consumption pathway. These differences in molecular-interface interactions are used to establish a paired PEC fingerprint dataset. Subsequent ML-assisted decoding, particularly with an artificial neural network (ANN), resolves the overlapping response patterns. The platform achieves high-accuracy classification of five representative sulfur-containing molecules, discrimination among predefined GSH concentration levels, and recognition of binary mixtures and spiked real-water matrices. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF heterointerfacial chemistry with data-driven fingerprint decoding, providing an interface-design strategy for intelligent recognition of sulfur-containing molecules in complex aqueous environments.
authors: Yu Feng, Guoao Li, Chenchen Liang, Huining Chai, Jing Guan, Lijun Qu, Lei Su, Xueji Zhang, Guangyao Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78261.title: Linker Engineering in Flexible Metal-Organic Frameworks Suppressing Slipping-Off Effect for Efficient Xe/Kr Separation
10.1002/adfm.78261.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with guest-selective gate-opening behavior are attractive for gas separations because they combine high selectivity with high capacity, yet their dynamic separation performance is often compromised by slipping-off effects. Here, we report a series of tetrazole-pillared MOFs, Zn(pzdc)(L) (pzdc = 3,5-pyrazoledicarboxylate; L = tetrazole derivatives), for efficient Xe/Kr separations, in which linker engineering with polar methyl or amino substituents reprograms framework dynamics and confined microenvironments to suppress slipping-off and promote Xe capture at low pressures through an adaptive molecular-recognition mechanism. Breakthrough experiments reveal a clear evolution in separation behavior, from severe Xe slipping-off in Zn(pzdc)(tz), to partial suppression in Zn(pzdc)(mtz), and ultimately to enhanced Xe/Kr separation in Zn(pzdc)(atz). Consequently, Zn(pzdc)(atz) affords > 99.99% pure Kr with a productivity of 107.5 L L −1 and a dynamic Xe uptake of 71.3 L L −1 from a Xe/Kr (20/80) mixture, while enabling trace Xe capture from simulated used nuclear fuel off-gas. In situ single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that linker engineering reinforces the host-guest interactions governing gate opening and amplifies the guest-induced structural response, enabling framework opening at extremely low Xe partial pressures and sustained dynamic Xe capture.
authors: Qingxue Hui, Xiuyuan Feng, Yu-Hao Gu, Jiali Fu, Deli Li, Xiangyang Zhang, Kuan Lu, Ye Xu, Chaoyue Fang, Shuai Yuan, Qi Ding, Zhaoqiang Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78301.title: Defect-Engineered Dual-Functional UiO-67 Type Framework: Ultra-Sensitive Ratiometric Fluorescence Sensing of Spectinomycin and Long-Lived Room-Temperature Phosphorescence for Anti-Counterfeiting
10.1002/adfm.78301.abstract: ABSTRACT Spectinomycin (SPT) lacks native chromophores and exhibits only weak far- ultraviolet absorption, rendering its sensitive and selective detection highly challenging via conventional optical methods. Herein, we report a dual-functional optical platform based on a UiO-67 framework with missing-linker defects constructed through mixed-linker doping of H 3 bptc. After pore-confined loading of Nile blue (NB), the resultant NB@UiO-67-bptc functions as a ratiometric fluorescent sensor for SPT, driven by SPT-induced NB excimer formation within the confined pore environment. The sensor delivers an ultra-low detection limit of 3.7 nM, an ultrafast response within 5 s, and a distinctive capability to discriminate SPT from other structurally analogous aminoglycoside antibiotics. The defective MOF carries abundant uncoordinated carboxyl groups, which can form hydrogen-bonding with sodium alginate (SA). The resulting composite film (UiO-67-bptc@SA) emits bright cyan long-afterglow film with an average phosphorescence lifetime of 759.8 ms and a naked-eye-visible afterglow of up to 2 s. This work demonstrates that a single defect-engineering modification can integrate two heterogeneous optical functions into one MOF system, providing a straightforward strategy for constructing multifunctional MOF optical materials for sensing and anti-counterfeiting applications.
authors: Yi-Fan Xia, Zhi-Qiang Cai, Yuan-Lei Zhang, Ling-Yi Guo, Hua Yu, Lan Yang, Yao-Hong Wang, Hou-Qun Yuan, Guang-Ming Bao

10.1002/adfm.78262.title: Asymmetric Interfacial Demulsification Creates Functional Wettability Gradients in Microporous Layers for PEM Fuel Cells
10.1002/adfm.78262.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation of coupled liquid-water and gas transport in microporous layers (MPLs) remains a major barrier to robust proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) operation across wide temperature and humidity windows. Here, we report a scalable asymmetric interfacial demulsification strategy for constructing MPLs with a continuous through-thickness wettability gradient (Gi-MPL). The Gi-MPL integrates a more hydrophilic catalyst-layer-facing region with a hydrophobic bulk, thereby promoting directional water transport while preserving gas-accessible pathways. Structural characterization reveals a clear sulfur-content gradient across the MPL thickness, and transport measurements show anisotropic liquid-water breakthrough behavior consistent with directional transport asymmetry. In membrane electrode assemblies, the Gi-MPL substantially outperforms a homogeneous control MPL over a broad operating window. At 80°C, it delivers a peak power density of 2.2 W cm −2 and reduces the concentration-polarization loss by approximately 80% at 3 A cm −2 . More notably, under harsh operation at 105°C, the Gi-MPL also maintains a peak power density of 1.4 W cm −2 , together with a clear advantage in durability. Multiscale simulations further suggest that the wettability gradient enhances liquid-water permeability under weak driving forces. These results establish through-thickness wettability engineering as an effective materials strategy for high-current-density PEMFC operation.
authors: Aojie Zhang, Feng Cheng, Mengli Wang, Xuelin Wei, Rui Wang, Shengqiu Zhao, Junquan Chen, Tian Tian, Haolin Tang

10.1002/adfm.78163.title: Piezoelectric and Pyroelectric Materials in Advanced Biomedical Applications: Multifunctional Integration and Clinical Prospects
10.1002/adfm.78163.abstract: ABSTRACT Piezoelectric and pyroelectric materials are advancing a broad spectrum of biomedical technologies, the former interconverting mechanical and electrical energy and the latter converting thermal fluctuations into electrical signals. For biosensing and health monitoring, piezoelectric polymers such as poly(vinylidene fluoride) and selected bio-derived systems enable wearable and implantable devices that track cardiovascular, respiratory, and musculoskeletal parameters. Concurrently, pyroelectric temperature sensors offer passive, real-time detection of thermal transients associated with inflammation and metabolic activity. In therapeutic applications, ultrasound-driven piezoelectric antibacterial materials and piezoelectric wound dressings accelerate infection control and tissue repair. Furthermore, piezoelectric scaffolds provide wireless electrical stimulation for neural and bone tissue engineering. In oncology, piezocatalytic and pyroelectric catalytic therapies generate reactive oxygen species for tumor ablation and immunogenic cell death. Recent innovations, including defect engineering to enhance charge separation, subcellular targeting strategies, and the development of biodegradable transient devices, address the long-term safety concerns of permanent implants. Despite these advances, challenges remain in optimizing in vivo stability, establishing standardized biocompatibility protocols, and navigating regulatory pathways toward clinical translation. Future interdisciplinary efforts will be essential to realize the full potential of these intelligent, biointegrated systems in precision medicine.
authors: Shuning Liu, Ziting Lin, Jiankang Cheng, Run Zhang, Boxin Xue, Xingguang Li, Huijing Xiang

10.1002/adfm.78277.title: Powerful Electric Jet Flow for Programmable Robotic Actuation
10.1002/adfm.78277.abstract: ABSTRACT Fluid manipulation is fundamental to fluidic actuation systems, spanning a broad range from biological organisms to robotic systems. However, developing a universal fluid manipulation platform that simultaneously offers programmability, scalability, and high flowrate for robotic actuation remains a challenge. Here, we report a soft fluid manipulation platform powered by an electrokinetic jet, which is generated from a novel wedge-shaped heterocharge layer within a dielectric fluid. In contrast to conventional electroosmosis (∼10 −4 L/min) or charge-injection electrohydrodynamics (<0.35 L/min), this platform leverages a specific electrode architecture to spatially program charge distribution via molecular dissociation. This mechanism creates a highly directional body force, yielding a specific flowrate ∼4.4 L min − 1 g −1 and an absolute flowrate exceeding 3.5 L min − 1 . The underlying physics of this phenomenon are interpreted by a theoretical model with comprehensive experimental and numerical validation. The platform exhibits intrinsic scalability from millimeters to meters and enables programmable actuation. Finally, the utility of this platform is demonstrated through three distinct applications: a high-speed swimming soft robot (achieving 26.5 BL/s), a fluidic lens for smartphone zooming (featuring millisecond-level voltage control), and a tactile feedback device for human-machine interaction. This work provides a versatile and practical solution for advanced fluidic actuation in next-generation robotic systems.
authors: Pingan Zhu, Wei Tang, Xinyu Guo, Yu Hu, Yonghao Wang, Qincheng Sheng, Kecheng Qin, Yidan Gao, Yiding Zhong, Huayong Yang, Jun Zou

10.1002/adfm.78274.title: Butterfly-Wing-Inspired Pore Architecture Adaptation for Environment-Guided Radiative Cooling Film
10.1002/adfm.78274.abstract: ABSTRACT With frequent extreme heat events, cooling demand is no longer confined to traditional low-latitude hot regions. Passive radiative cooling is usually designed to achieve the high reflectivity and emissivity under fixed conditions, whereas actual cooling demand changes with latitude-dependent thermal boundaries. Inspired by the structural-spectral distribution rule formed by butterfly-wings in response to their habitats, this work proposes an environment-guided gradient porous radiative cooling film design strategy. In the TPU/PMMA/ZrO 2 system, thickness-direction gradient pore regulates photon transmission, PMMA dispersed-phase introduces secondary scattering on pore-walls, and ZrO 2 nanoparticles enhance local optical contrast. The optimized G-TPU/PMMA/ZrO 2 film achieves 96.4% solar reflectance and 98.5% infrared emissivity, exhibiting the lowest outdoor temperature and highest net cooling power. By adjusting the supercritical CO 2 foaming process parameters, the same material system can form large-pore-rich, balanced-gradient, and dense-small-pore-rich architectures to adapt to different thermal environments. Climate-chamber tests further verified that the optimal pore structure changes with the external environment. EnergyPlus simulations show that radiative cooling cannot be treated as a universal year-round cooling surface, while an appropriate cooling method should be selected based on climatic characteristics. This work advances porous radiative cooling from single-condition performance maximization to structural adaptation for different thermal boundaries within one material platform.
authors: Yushu Wang, Yunlan Yang, Hanyi Huang, Jiawen Tang, Wentao Zhai

10.1002/adfm.78192.title: Indium-Mediated Electrolyte with Efficient Mg2+ Transport and CO2 Pathway Selection for Highly Reversible Mg-CO2 Batteries
10.1002/adfm.78192.abstract: ABSTRACT Mg-CO 2 batteries present promising potential for integrated energy storage and carbon fixation, though their advancement is limited by slow cathodic CO 2 conversion kinetics and insufficient reversibility. Here, we report an In-mediated electrolyte that couples solvation structure regulation with cathodic pathway control to realize highly reversible Mg─CO 2 chemistry in a conventional electrolyte system. Experimental and theoretical analyses demonstrate that, in addition to stabilizing the Mg anode and ensuring Mg 2+ transport, In species serve as an “electron sink and relay” to accelerate CO 2 conversion kinetics. They undergo preferential reduction prior to CO 2 , generating in situ atomically dispersed active sites that subsequently activate CO 2 via electron injection. This process directs the conversion pathway toward the formation of more reversible discharge products with favorable transport morphologies. As a result, the Mg─CO 2 battery delivers a long-term cycling life of over 1300 h at 100 mA g −1 with a minimum voltage gap of 0.25 V during cycling, and maintains robust performance under extreme conditions, including 3000 mA g −1 rate capability and operation at −20°C. This concept of mediator-enhanced electrolyte provides an effective route for a high-performance Mg-CO 2 battery system.
authors: Linlin Xue, Tong Li, Zhibin Xu, Ruoqi Zhao, Zhenglin Hu, Qingtao Ma, Xingjiang Liu, Aoxuan Wang, Jiayan Luo

10.1002/adfm.78193.title: In Situ Self-Locked Crystalline-Amorphous ZIF-8 Composite Membranes for Ethylene/Ethane Separation via Sacrificial Coordination Disruption
10.1002/adfm.78193.abstract: ABSTRACT Metal-organic framework (MOF)-derived amorphous materials combine the processability of disordered solids with the molecular-sieving characteristics of crystalline microporous frameworks; however, controlling crystalline domain regeneration within a chemically compatible amorphous matrix remains challenging. Here, a sacrificial coordination-disruption strategy is introduced in which formic acid (FA) transiently perturbs the Zn-2-methylimidazolate coordination network of ZIF-8 through proton transfer and ligand exchange, producing a formic acid-treated ZIF-8 precursor (FZIF-8). Heat-only treatment converts FZIF-8 into a ZIF-8-derived amorphous intermediate (aZIF-8), whereas 2-methylimidazole (mim)-assisted coupled heat-and-pressure treatment promotes removal of FA-derived species, structural reorganization, and in situ crystallization, yielding self-locked crystalline-amorphous ZIF-8 composite membranes (scaZIF-8). Increasing mim content systematically modulates the extent of in situ crystallization, crystallite size, accessible microporosity, and domain distribution. The resulting crystalline-amorphous interfacial architecture is associated with attenuated gate-opening behavior and a narrower effective molecular-sieving window relative to crystalline ZIF-8. These features enable ethylene/ethane separation with an ethylene permeability of 2871 Barrer and an ethylene/ethane separation factor of 10.1 for equimolar mixtures at 0°C. This work demonstrates sacrificial coordination disruption as a route to crystalline-amorphous MOF composite membranes and highlights crystalline-amorphous structural design for tailoring molecular-sieving behavior and gas-transport properties.
authors: Yubin Jin, Ung Gi Hong, Ki Jin Nam, Mun Suk Seong, Donghui Jo, U-Hwang Lee, Dun-Yen Kang, Jong Suk Lee

10.1002/adfm.77734.title: Balancing Hydrophobicity and Hydrophilicity: Dual Filler-Engineered Proton Exchange Membranes for Durable, High-Power Fuel Cells
10.1002/adfm.77734.abstract: ABSTRACT Most filler materials in ion-exchange membranes have been employed primarily to increase water uptake, with limited control over polymer morphology. Here, we direct the structural evolution of perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) membranes through PFSA-filler interface engineering, using zirconium-based metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) with systematically tuned surface polarity. Hydrophilic MOF surfaces stabilize interfacial hydration layers that promote water-cluster expansion and interdomain bridging across the membrane, whereas hydrophobic MOF surfaces preferentially interact with the PTFE backbone, inducing parallel chain alignment, lowering bulk crystallinity, and generating compact water channels. A dual-filler Nafion membrane combining hydrophilic UiO-66 and hydrophobic UiO-67 integrates both effects, achieving a significantly enhanced proton conductivity (176 mS cm −1 at 80°C, 95% RH), peak power densities of 785.3 mW cm −2 (ambient pressure) and 1,456 mW cm −2 (200 kPa), and a threefold improvement in durability compared to Nafion. Because the total filler content remains below 4 wt.%, this polarity-guided strategy is compatible with industrial roll-to-roll fabrication and offers a general design rule for next-generation, high-performance and durable fuel-cell membranes.
authors: Yonghwi Cho, Yunseong Ji, Minkyu Choi, Junsu Kim, Yejin Kim, Su Jeong Lee, Wooyoung Choi, Choong Hoo Lee, Ju Yeon Kim, Ohchan Kwon, Hanim Kim, Du Yeol Ryu, Ki Chul Kim, Dae Woo Kim

10.1002/adfm.78196.title: Generation of Squarelike Skyrmion Bubbles and Configuration Manipulation in Rare-Earth DyFe11Mo Magnet
10.1002/adfm.78196.abstract: ABSTRACT Topological magnetic skyrmions with nanoscale particle-like characteristics and high manipulability have been intensively studied as promising candidates for next-generation high-density information units. Besides the chiral skyrmions determined by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), the energy competition between magnetic anisotropy and dipolar interactions has demonstrated rich freedoms for generating various topological spin configurations. Normally, circular configurations are favored for topological particles, leaving the square configuration only rarely observed in chiral antiskyrmions due to the anisotropic DMI so far. Here, we found that magnetoelectric manipulation can stabilize a variety of squarelike skyrmion bubbles at zero field in centrosymmetric DyFe 11 Mo magnet. Furthermore, by combining analysis of in situ Lorentz transmission electron microscopy (L-TEM) images and micromagnetic simulations, the configuration transition between squarelike and circular skyrmion bubbles has been realized with the underlying mechanism clarified . The magnetic competition mediated by significant 3d-4f electron interactions between rare-earth and transition-metal (RE-TM) elements serves as the microscopic origin for magnetic texture manipulation, highlighting the extended application of the RE-TM based magnets in exploring multiple topological spin textures and spintronic functions.
authors: Yunxiang Yang, Zhan Wang, Zhidong He, Zhengying Tian, Fengxia Hu, Shouguo Wang, Jun Shen, Ying Zhang, Baogen Shen

10.1002/adfm.78166.title: Synergistic Modulation of Molecular Orientation and Interfacial Compatibility via Pyrimidine-Induced Weak Interactions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.78166.abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation of molecular orientation and optimization of interfacial compatibility between the Ag/active layer and cathode interface layers (CILs) are pivotal for improving the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, two bay -modified perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives, PDINN-PeOO and PDINN-PemOO, are synthesized by introducing pyridine-ester and pyrimidine-ester groups via facile coupling. Compared with pyridine-functionalized PDINN-PeOO, pyrimidine-based PDINN-PemOO possesses stronger electron-withdrawing capability. Meanwhile, PDINN-PemOO can establish dual synergistic weak interactions, namely hydrogen bonding and π - π stacking, thereby inducing a dominant face-on molecular orientation with suppressed edge-on packing. More importantly, the optimized stacking configuration further enables PDINN-PemOO to achieve bidirectional interfacial optimization. At the Ag/CIL interface, pyrimidine-derived can reduce the work function of Ag, and the enhanced intramolecular charge transfer simultaneously promotes self-doping. At the active layer/CIL interface, dual weak interactions strengthen molecular binding, reduce interfacial energy, thus suppressing charge recombination. Such bidirectional interfacial modulation dramatically improves stability with a T 80 of 1400 h under N 2 . Consequently, the PDINN-PemOO-based device attains an outstanding PCE of 20.06% in the PM6: D18: L8-BO system. This breakthrough unravels the intrinsic mechanism by which hydrogen bonds and π - π stacking co-regulate molecular orientation and interfacial compatibility, laying a robust foundation for efficient, stable OSCs.
authors: Shuhua Wang, Zhentian Xu, Dan Zhou, Jingyun Huang, Hongxiang Li, Jiangang Ma, Zhiyou Ji, Qiugen Zhang, Bin Hu, Lin Hu, Lie Chen

10.1002/adfm.78317.title: Nanoembossing-Enabled Mechanical Interlocking of Monolayer Nanofibers for Device Integration
10.1002/adfm.78317.abstract: ABSTRACT The device integration of nanofiber architectures is limited by weak interfacial adhesion and inefficient load transfer at nanofiber-substrate interfaces, leading to poor mechanical robustness and restricted processing compatibility. Here, we report a nanoembossing strategy that enables the interfacial embedding of electrospun nanofibers into lithographically patterned thin frames. Gelatin nanofibers are electrospun onto a patterned OrmoStamp thin film and thermally embossed at 180°C for 1 min. During embossing, a thermally activated compliant surface layer of OrmoStamp undergoes surface-conformal viscoelastic flow, facilitating intimate contact and stress redistribution of the gelatin nanofibers during crosslinking. Upon cooling, the nanofiber structures transform into an ultrathin two-dimensional membrane that is mechanically stable due to nanofiber embedment on the surface of OrmoStamp. With the aid of a soft buffer layer, the process further enables curved and fused nanofiber geometries, resulting in well-defined three-dimensional nanofiber architectures. These nanofiber structures can subsequently serve as backbone for the self-assembly of hydrogels or proteins, forming ultrathin functional membranes that support cell culture and tumor spheroid co-culture under microfluidic conditions. Notably, the resulting membranes exhibit sustained structural integrity after drying and storage, highlighting the inherent robustness of the nano-embossed nanofiber architecture.
authors: Xinyue Lan, Duomei Tian, Carole Aimé, Juan Peng, Yong Chen

10.1002/adfm.202532064.title: Synergistic Bimolecular Passivation Stabilizing Surface States for High Performance HTL-Free Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.202532064.abstract: ABSTRACT The inevitable photothermal-induced desorption of functional molecules at the perovskite film surface would resurge the passivated surface defect states and cause severe recombination, thereby affecting both photovoltaic performance and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Here, we report a synergistic bimolecular passivation (SBP) strategy by employing 2-methylpropanimidamide hydrochloride (MPACl) to fix phenethylammonium (PEA + ) ligands extensively used at the perovskite film surface, achieving a stable and well passivated surface. As revealed, SBP strategy significantly inhibited the interface nonradiative recombination and enhanced the carrier transport, along with optimizing the interfacial energy level alignment. As a result, for the promising hole-transport layer (HTL)-free PSCs, the target device achieved a remarkable PCE of 26.51% (certified at 26.03%) with a V OC of 1.204 V, corresponding to a mere 356 mV deficit for 1.56 eV perovskites. This further boosts the record efficiency of HTL-free PSCs. Meanwhile, the encapsulated device can retain over 95% of their original PCE after 1300 h of light soaking. Our work addressed successfully the above thorny issue and provides an effective way to realize both high efficiency and stability PSCs.
