10.1002/adfm.79102.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Network Enables Near-Coplanar Fluorooxoborates with Large Deep-Ultraviolet Birefringence
10.1002/adfm.79102.abstract: ABSTRACT Deep-ultraviolet birefringent materials require simultaneously large optical anisotropy and wide bandgaps, yet these properties are often difficult to reconcile in fluorooxoborates because the incorporation of tetrahedral [BO 4− x F x ] units tends to distort otherwise anisotropic borate frameworks. Here we introduce a hydrogen-bond modulation strategy to suppress such structural distortion and promote near-coplanar alignment of optically active building units. Inspired by the tension-distributing architecture of spider webs, the planar π-conjugated cations, [C(NH 2 ) 3 ], were employed as multidirectional hydrogen-bond donors to construct a highly interconnected hydrogen-bond network throughout the crystal lattice. Guided by this concept, a new fluorooxoborate, Li[C(NH 2 ) 3 ]B 6 O 8 F 4 , was synthesized. The cooperative hydrogen-bond network effectively constrains the [B 6 O 9 F 4 ] FBBs into a near-coplanar arrangement, reducing the dihedral angle between adjacent B 3 O 3 rings to less than 7°. An interplay between terahertz spectroscopy and solid-state density functional theory calculations reveals substantially enhanced cation-anion vibrational coupling over the hydrogen-bond-free analogue α -KB 3 O 4 F 2 , providing direct evidence for the collective constraint imposed by the hydrogen-bond network. The resulting cooperative alignment of the π-conjugated cations and anionic chains generates pronounced optical anisotropy, yielding a birefringence of 0.15 at 546 nm and a wide bandgap of 6.87 eV. Hydrogen-bond-network engineering effectively regulates framework coplanarity and provides a general design principle for high-performance DUV birefringent materials.

10.1002/adfm.79135.title: Bio-Derived Polyurethane Ionoelastomers With Hierarchical Dynamic Networks for Ultrawide-Range Iontronic Pressure Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79135.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable flexible iontronics remain limited by the concurrent difficulty of reconciling mechanical robustness with dynamic adaptability, and achieving high sensitivity across a broad pressure range. Here, we address these challenges by synthesizing a bio-derived polyurethane ionoelastomer with a dual-crosslinked architecture. At operational temperatures, thermoreversible Diels-Alder covalent bonds maintain thermoset-like structural integrity, while ionic liquid-mediated ion-dipole interactions act as dynamic physical crosslinks. This design enables on-demand topological rearrangement upon heating, allowing for high-efficiency self-healing (90.62% stress recovery) and repeated reprocessing without sacrificing mechanical strength. By combining this robust ionoelastomer with a biomimetic random-rough interface, we fabricated an epidermis-inspired capacitive sensor. The device exhibits a high sensitivity of 3339.21% kPa −1 (0-200 kPa) and a broad working range up to 1 MPa. For practical wearable applications, the sensor accurately captures radial pulse waves for cardiovascular monitoring. Furthermore, when integrated into a smart insole and paired with a support vector machine model, it classifies daily human activities with near 100% accuracy. This work provides a sustainable and mechanically robust material platform for advanced flexible tactile sensors.

10.1002/adfm.78789.title: Paving the Way for Next-Generation Solid-State Waste Heat Recovery: A Thermomagnetic Materials and Systems Roadmap
10.1002/adfm.78789.abstract: ABSTRACT Nearly half of global primary energy is dissipated as low-grade waste heat, predominantly below 100°C. While thermoelectric technologies offer a pathway to recover such energy, their efficiency and scalability remain limited. Thermomagnetic (TM) energy conversion has recently emerged as a promising alternative, with breakthroughs in materials and system design pushing its performance toward practical viability. TM systems offer unique advantages, including scalability, high theoretical second-law efficiency, and adaptability across diverse thermal regimes. In this perspective, we examine the key challenges and emerging opportunities in thermomagnetic energy harvesting, with a focus on material selection, processing techniques, and system-level design. We propose roadmaps to guide the field's development, aiming to establish TM conversion as a versatile solution for sustainable low-grade waste heat recovery.

10.1002/adfm.77505.title: Noise-Limited Bit Precision in Ferroelectric Synaptic Transistors for High-Resolution Neuromorphic Computing
10.1002/adfm.77505.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic hardware requires synaptic devices with reliable multilevel states, yet the precision of emerging synaptic devices is often assessed through experimental demonstration rather than a quantitative principle, hindering meaningful comparison across platforms. Here, we introduce a methodology based on low-frequency noise (LFN) spectroscopy to quantify the multilevel limit of synaptic devices, while also proposing a new metric for evaluating bit precision. We apply this approach to ferroelectric transistors with three representative channel materials, single-crystalline Si (c-Si), polycrystalline Si (poly-Si), and amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS), which respectively offer a benchmark for high-performance transport, a scalable silicon platform compatible with 3D integration, and a platform for low-temperature and large-area electronics. It is demonstrated that bit precision is determined by the interplay between dynamic range and noise amplitude, rather than memory window alone. Furthermore, we demonstrate how differences in bit precision affect the performance of large-scale neural networks. This methodology establishes LFN-based signal resolution as a key reliability metric, enabling precise benchmarking and guiding the design of high-performance neuromorphic hardware across materials and device architectures.
authors: Jaehong Park, Yeonseop Shin, Changhyeon Han, Sangwoo Kim, Eunchan Park, Youngchan Cho, Jaehong Min, Hyunjun Ahn, Jaekyoung Park, Cheol-Woong Yang, Jangsaeng Kim, Daewoong Kwon, Wonjun Shin

10.1002/adfm.77654.title: 2D Heterointerface-Mediated Chemisorption Pathways Enable Selective Dual-Gas Detection at Room Temperature
10.1002/adfm.77654.abstract: ABSTRACT Heterointerfacial modulation in 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offers a unique route to introduce a portfolio of fascinating properties, allowing layered materials to manifest multi-dimensional features for advanced device applications. Herein, functionally distinct heterostructures of 2H-MoS 2 are engineered via controlled Ar and O 2 plasma treatments, resulting in 1T/2H-MoS 2 and MoO 3 /2H-MoS interfaces, respectively, which in turn facilitate selective gas chemisorption. The tailored heterointerfaces reshape local electronic and surface energy landscapes of 2H-MoS 2 , where electron transfer from metallic 1T domains strengthens n-type conductivity, while hole injection from MoO 3 reinforces p-type behavior. Experimental measurements, supported by density functional theory, indicate that carrier-density modulation, together with the formation of favorable adsorption sites, governs the chemisorption behavior of oxidizing NO 2 and reducing NH3 molecules. The 1T/2H-MoS 2 and MoO 3 /2H-MoS 2 sensors selectively detect NO 2 and NH 3 with minimum detection limits of 165 and 138 ppb, respectively, at room temperature. The practical applicability of the sensors, demonstrated by fabricating a portable sensor array, showcases effective NO 2 detection in vehicular exhaust and NH 3 sensing in spoiled meat, underscoring their potential for environmental and food-safety monitoring. By strategically engineering heterointerfaces, this study translates tunable TMD properties into chemisorption-controlled gas discrimination.
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala

10.1002/adfm.78589.title: Ultra-Strong, Ductile, and Corrosion-Resistant High Entropy Alloy With Multi-Scale Heterogeneous Microstructure
10.1002/adfm.78589.abstract: ABSTRACT Marine engineering materials require excellent mechanical properties and corrosion resistance to ensure safe service. However, balancing mechanical strengthening mechanisms with corrosion resistance in alloy design remains a considerable challenge. Herein, we design a multi-scale heterogeneous microstructure, characterized by partial recrystallization, a grain-size gradient, and L1 2 precipitates, by introducing different Al and Ti contents into a non-equiatomic single phase face-centered cubic (FCC) Co-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloy (HEA), followed by cold rolling and short-term annealing. The designed Co 15 Cr 20 Fe 28 Ni 30 Al 3 Ti 4 HEA with multi-scale heterogeneous microstructure exhibits an exceptional combination of mechanical and corrosion properties that surpass those of most reported alloys. It achieves a yield strength ( σ YS ) of 1980 MPa, an ultimate tensile strength ( σ UTS ) of 2005 MPa, and a total elongation of 12.1%. In terms of corrosion performance, it demonstrates a high corrosion potential ( E corr ) of −307.7 mV SCE , a low corrosion current density ( i corr ) of 145.7 nA/cm 2 , and a high pitting potential ( E pit ) of 854 mV SCE . The outstanding performance is attributed to the multi-scale heterogeneous microstructure, which enhances mechanical properties through HDI and precipitation strengthening and promotes the rapid formation of a stable Cr-enriched passive film. This work provides a viable pathway for designing high-performance corrosion-resistant alloys that simultaneously achieve high strength and good ductility.

10.1002/adfm.77506.title: 2D Tin Halide Perovskite Semiconductors: Fundamentals, Applications, and Future Perspectives
10.1002/adfm.77506.abstract: ABSTRACT Tin (Sn) halide perovskites have emerged as promising lead-free semiconductors for next-generation electronic applications due to their non-toxicity and exceptional optoelectronic properties. Among them, two-dimensional (2D) layered Sn-based perovskites incorporating insulating and hydrophobic bulky spacer cations offer distinct advantages over their three-dimensional (3D) counterparts. These include outstanding structural flexibility, reduced ion migration, enhanced exciton binding energy, and improved environmental stability. To advance the research in this field and enable the development of high-performance tunable optoelectronic devices, this review provides a comprehensive analysis of the fundamental properties of 2D Sn-based perovskites, including structure-property correlations, charge carrier dynamics, operational stability, and synthetic strategies. Then, the recent progress in diverse device applications, namely light-emitting diodes, field-effect transistors, and memristors, is critically discussed. Finally, it identifies the key challenges and limitations and provides perspectives to guide future research directions in the design and application of 2D Sn-based perovskite materials.

10.1002/adfm.79101.title: Interfacial Inner-Local-Enhanced Discharge Induced by Aligned Needle Electrodes for the Synergistic Collection of Tribo-Charges
10.1002/adfm.79101.abstract: ABSTRACT A corona-discharge triboelectric nanogenerator (CD-TENG) couples triboelectrification with air discharge to harvest mechanical energy. However, electrostatic energy in conventional structures is not fully extracted because of inner charge locking and discharge at the triboelectric interface (tribo-interface). Herein, we propose a charge-extraction strategy by designing an inner-aligned needle-electrode TENG (INE-TENG) to extract electrostatic energy simultaneously from the side and inner regions of the tribo-interface. Through systematic analysis of discharge fluorescence and electrical output under different operating modes, we elucidated the synergistic charge-collection mechanism. Compared with the side-electrode-only configuration with the inner electrode disconnected, the synergistic operation transferred an additional 1.73 µC to the external circuit, as inferred from mode-switching electrical measurements. At a 2.0 GΩ load, the INE-TENG yielded an output energy of 15.7 mJ, 4.02 times that of the side-electrode-only configuration with the inner electrode grounded (3.91 mJ), exceeding the sum of the individual side and inner electrode outputs. A high output energy density of 2.61 J m − 2 per cycle was achieved using the basic structural unit. This study clarifies interfacial electrostatic energy loss pathways in CD-TENGs and demonstrates an electrode-architecture-based approach to improving energy extraction through synergistic charge collection from the side and inner regions of the tribo-interface.
authors: Cuiling Zhang, Kaixian Li, Chuncai Shan, Siqi Gong, Shuyan Xu, Huiyuan Wu, Xue Wang, Chenguo Hu

10.1002/adfm.79065.title: Nitrobenzo Crown Ether Enables Stable Interphases in Lithium Metal Batteries
10.1002/adfm.79065.abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium metal anodes promise high-energy-density storage but suffer from unstable solid electrolyte interphases and dendrite growth in carbonate electrolytes. Here, 4-nitrobenzo-15-crown-5 ether (NBCE) is introduced as a multifunctional electrolyte additive that simultaneously regulates Li + solvation and interfacial chemistry. NBCE replaces ethylene carbonate in the Li + solvation sheath, increasing contact ion pairs and substantially lowering the Li + desolvation energy. Its preferential reduction on lithium, accompanied by conversion of the nitro group into Li 3 N, produces a dense LiF- and Li 3 N-rich SEI. Consequently, Li||Cu cells exhibit higher Coulombic efficiency (CE), lower nucleation overpotential, and dense, dendrite-free lithium deposition, while Li||Li symmetric cells cycle stably for over 1000 h. Li||NCM811 full cells retain 79.5% of their capacity after 300 cycles with an average CE of 99.5%, and deliver approximately 86 mAh g −1 at 5 C. NBCE also significantly suppresses leakage current at high voltages. These findings establish multifunctional solvation and interphase regulation as an effective electrolyte-design strategy for high-energy-density lithium metal batteries.
authors: Zihui Liu, Qiuyan Li, Huijuan Ma, Chao Peng, Xue-Feng Yu, Jiahong Wang

10.1002/adfm.78601.title: Biodegradable 3D-Printable and Coatable Antifouling Composites for Marine Applications
10.1002/adfm.78601.abstract: ABSTRACT The intensive use of conventional, non-biodegradable plastics in marine environments causes substantial ecological damage. Beyond releasing microplastics and toxic additives, these materials are highly susceptible to biofouling and often rely on biocidal antifoulants, increasing their environmental impact. Here are reported biodegradable antifouling biocomposites that provide tunable shapes and formats via conventional thermoplastic processing, like compression molding and 3D printing, and can be integrated as conformal coatings to retrofit existing structures. The materials pair non-toxic ingredients: a beeswax matrix, Tween 80 as antifoulant and calcium stearate or stearic acid fillers to tune rheology and improve stability. Tween-rich formulations demonstrate effective inhibition of Escherichia coli adhesion and, upon seawater immersion, maintain larger unfouled areas than conventional bioplastics. In seawater, the dip-coated variants adhere efficiently to glass, steel, and plastic substrates. Biochemical oxygen demand in seawater shows biodegradation during 30-days testing, supporting low persistence. Calcium stearate filler-reinforced formulations display improved mechanics, endure at least 10 recycling cycles, and can be 3D-printed into free-standing architectures. This platform combines structural or coating deployment with effective antifouling, offering potential for underwater applications where complex geometries, integration into existing structures, and minimal impact on fragile ecosystems are critical, such as underwater robotics and coral restoration.

10.1002/adfm.78689.title: Adsorption of Selected Chiral Small Molecules Preserves Stacking-Dependent Polarization at van der Waals Interfaces
10.1002/adfm.78689.abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral small-molecule modification provides an interfacial route for functionalizing sliding ferroelectrics. Herein, we systematically investigate four chiral molecules adsorbed on h-BN, 3R-MoS 2 , and γ-InSe. Across 48 adsorption configurations, the polarization changes range from −27.5% to +13.7%, with a median absolute variation of 10.0%, while 35 configurations show changes within ±15%. The polarization retains its original Up and Down sign in all relaxed configurations examined. The oppositely polarized states remain connected by finite-energy sliding pathways, although molecular adsorption modifies the barrier heights and endpoint energy asymmetry. Bader charge and charge density difference analyses reveal limited net charge transfer and predominantly localized electronic redistribution near the interface. The relationship between the interfacial charge-transfer dipole and the Berry-phase polarization modulation depends on the substrate. These results demonstrate that stacking-dependent polar states remain present in the investigated chiral-molecule sliding-ferroelectric interfaces, providing a microscopic basis for molecular functionalization of sliding ferroelectrics.

10.1002/adfm.79115.title: Programmed Curing Directs Nanophase Organization in Active Ester-Cured Epoxies for Strong Adhesion, Toughness, and Recyclability
10.1002/adfm.79115.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced electronic packaging requires dielectric materials that combine reliable adhesion and dielectric performance with end-of-life management. Practical anhydride-cured epoxy networks generally contain polar hydroxyls, which promote hydrogen-bond-mediated cohesion and adhesion but degrade dielectric performance and moisture resistance. Active-ester curing reduces hydroxyl density, yet it can weaken adhesion by diminishing these interactions. Here, we report a strategy of programmed curing to direct nanophase organization, which exploits the different apparent curing kinetics of two active-ester curing agents bearing dodecanoyl and furoyl termini (AE-D and AE-F, respectively). During stepwise heating, these kinetic differences create a structural evolution window before gelation, enabling C12-driven nanophase formation in the bulk and enrichment of oxygen-containing groups at metal oxide interfaces. Consequently, the optimized RE-D50F50 network achieves an aluminum lap-shear strength of 22.96 MPa and a tensile toughness of 25.5 MJ m −3 , while maintaining a dielectric constant of 3.39 and a dielectric loss of 0.019 at 10 MHz, along with stable performance under hygrothermal aging. Mild acid-triggered deconstruction further enables the isolation of small-molecule products and the recovery of encapsulated components. This work establishes programmed curing as a route to improve the adhesion and toughness of low-dielectric active-ester-cured epoxies while advancing sustainable epoxy materials for electronic packaging.
authors: Chenyang Xu, Jingkai Liu, Shuaipeng Wang, Kerong Yang, Ziyu Liu, Xin Wang, Jinyue Dai, Xiaoqing Liu

10.1002/adfm.79105.title: Dynamic Thermal Regulation of Li-Mg Batteries via Microencapsulated Phase Change Materials Embedded in High-Entropy MOF Matrices
10.1002/adfm.79105.abstract: ABSTRACT To address critical safety vulnerabilities in Li-Mg battery (LMB), particularly internal short circuits and thermal runaway, we report a novel smart gel polymer electrolyte (HEMOF@TP@DZC GPE) that synergistically enhances electrochemical performance and intrinsic safety. The innovation centers on a hollow high-entropy metal-organic framework (HE-MOF) microcapsule with a hierarchically porous structure and abundant oxygen vacancies, which significantly accelerates ion transport kinetics essential for high-performance operation. Its unique spherical morphology with smaller curvature effectively disperses interfacial stress, actively suppressing detrimental Mg dendrite growth. For intrinsic safety, the microcapsule encapsulates flame retardant triethyl phosphate (TEP), anchored by a phase change material (PCM) serving as a smart gatekeeper. Upon temperature increase, the PCM triggers rapid TEP release, generating phosphorus-containing radicals that efficiently terminate combustion chain reactions and prevent thermal runaway propagation. An LMB cell utilizing this multifunctional HEMOF@TP@DZC GPE demonstrated exceptional performance stability, delivering a specific capacity of 80.5 mAh g −1 at 80 C and exhibiting remarkable capacity retention with negligible degradation (only 1.55%) over an extraordinary 20 000 cycles. This work establishes a fresh, impactful avenue for designing multifunctional HE-MOF microcapsules that seamlessly integrate advanced thermal management with superior electrochemical performance, paving the way for the next generation of intrinsically safer, higher-energy-density Li-Mg batteries.
authors: Yongqin Wang, Lixuan Zhang, Yu Fu

10.1002/adfm.79149.title: Jahn-Teller Distortion Triggers Unconventional Molecular O2 Formation in P2-Type Na0.67MnO2 Cathodes
10.1002/adfm.79149.abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen redox chemistry offers a pathway to high energy density in sodium-ion batteries but is often accompanied by irreversible molecular O 2 formation, leading to voltage hysteresis and poor cycling stability. The origin of molecular O 2 formation is commonly attributed to high-voltage charging yet remains debatable. Here, we uncover an overlooked mechanism in P2-type Na 0.67 MnO 2 , where molecular O 2 formation is decoupled from the conventional high-voltage paradigm and instead originates from Jahn-Teller distortion during discharge. Combined experimental and computational results reveal that Jahn-Teller-induced lattice distortion shortens O-O distances and enhances the O-O dimerization tendency, leading to irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation. This finding establishes a previously unrecognized distortion-mediated pathway governing oxygen redox. To address this issue, an Al/Si co-doping strategy is developed to regulate the electronic structure and reinforce the lattice framework. The co-doping suppresses Jahn-Teller distortion, stabilizes O 2p states, and weakens the tendency toward O-O dimerization, thereby inhibiting molecular O 2 formation. Consequently, the optimized Na 0.67 Al 0.01 Si 0.01 Mn 0.99 O 2 exhibits superior cycling performance, retaining 95% capacity after 100 cycles within 4.4-2.0 V and 90% after 500 cycles within 4.0-2.0 V. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for oxygen redox chemistry and offer a practical design strategy for stabilizing high-voltage manganese-based sodium-ion batteries.
authors: Yang Yu, Huibo Wang, Qingyuan Li, Deniz Wong, Ruoyu Wang, Tianran Zhang, Lirong Zheng, Xiangfeng Liu

10.1002/adfm.79142.title: Solution-State Supramolecular Engineering of Self-Assembled Monolayers for High-Performance Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79142.abstract: ABSTRACT Carbazole-based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), exemplified by [4-(3,6-dimethyl-9H-carbazol-9-yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me-4PACz), are widely used as hole-selective contacts in efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, aggregation-driven intermolecular organization in solution adversely affects the homogenization of SAMs on the substrate, compromising the performance of tandem devices. Herein, a supramolecular co-assembly strategy is developed to modulate solution-state intermolecular organization and suppress aggregation by introducing 4-fluorophenylglycine hydrochloride, which co-assembles with Me-4PACz via dual-site non-covalent interactions. This strategy links solution-state modulation to the formation of uniform SAM films, simultaneously realizing optimized energy alignment and reducing residual stress at the buried interface. Champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.66% and 33.91% (certified 33.5%) are achieved for 1.67 eV wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells and 1 cm 2 two-terminal monolithic perovskite/silicon TSCs, respectively. Moreover, the optimized tandem devices exhibit excellent operational stability under the ISOS-L-2 protocol, retaining 91% of the initial PCE after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under one-sun continuous illumination.
authors: Yusong Zhou, Wan Li, Li He, Hongzhen Su, Lin Li, Huanpei Huang, Yuhui Guo, Yanting Shao, Delong Wu, Hong Liu, Zhewei Zhang, Enbing Bi, Wenzhong Shen

10.1002/adfm.79134.title: Responsive Dielectric Polarization Regulates Nonradiative Losses in Perovskite Solar Cells
10.1002/adfm.79134.abstract: ABSTRACT Nonradiative recombination in perovskite solar cells (PSCs) is fundamentally governed by carrier-defect interactions, yet existing strategies primarily focus on defect density reduction and interfacial passivation. Here, we establish a guanidinium-based dielectric strategy to regulate carrier-defect interaction kinetics in perovskite films. By incorporating guanidinium-based additives with systematically varied molecular dipole moments and polarizabilities, enhanced dielectric screening is achieved, which weakens carrier-defect interactions while simultaneously reducing nonradiative loss. Together with multifunctional chemical passivation, this leads to suppressed nonradiative recombination and reduced energy dissipation. As a result, the optimized devices achieve efficiencies of 26.15% and 26.39% for n-i-p and p-i-n architectures, respectively, along with 25.64% for large area (1 cm 2 ) devices and 23.11% for wide-bandgap (1.68 eV) PSCs. The devices also exhibit excellent operational, thermal, and ambient stability. This work identifies dielectric regulation of carrier-defect interactions as a general strategy to minimize energy dissipation and advance PSCs toward their radiative efficiency limits.
authors: Xing Zhao, Yuanxi Zhang, Huilin Yan, Yujie Qiu, Min Wang, Junjie Zhou, Lin Luo, Pengjun Zhao, Ludong Li, Xiaohang Hao, Bingbing Fan, Liang Li, Shengqiang Ren, Peng Cui, Meicheng Li

10.1002/adfm.79141.title: Unlocking Near-Unity Photoluminescence Quantum Yield for Cs3TbCl6 Perovskite Nanocrystals Via Fluoroquinolone Surface Engineering
10.1002/adfm.79141.abstract: ABSTRACT Rare-earth-based lead-free halide perovskite nanocrystals (NCs) are promising for optoelectronics due to their narrow-band emission and physicochemical stability. However, the intrinsic 4f-4f forbidden transitions of rare-earth ions result in limited absorption cross-sections. Furthermore, inevitable surface defects at the nanoscale trigger non-radiative recombination, limiting luminescence efficiency. Herein, a surface engineering strategy utilizing fluoroquinolone (FQ) molecules is proposed to construct a hybrid system. Specifically, by introducing norfloxacin (NFLX) as a surface ligand, NFLX-modified Cs 3 TbCl 6 nanocrystals (NCs) have been developed that achieve a near-unity photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of 99.67%. Experiments and theoretical analyses reveal that the organic ligands effectively passivate surface defects, thereby suppressing non-radiative transitions. Simultaneously, the ligand acts as an efficient antenna that amplifies excitation light capture and establishes energy transfer pathways to NCs. Notably, it is demonstrated that beyond energy level matching, the electronic effects, steric configurations, and absorption capacities of ligand are crucial factors for efficient antenna effect. Finally, the effectiveness of this strategy is validated through applications in extreme-environment-resilient fluorescent anti-counterfeiting fibers and high-quality white light-emitting diodes (WLEDs). This work overcomes the bottleneck limiting the luminescence efficiency of rare-earth halide NCs, paving a new technical pathway for the design of high-efficiency surface-coordinated hybrid rare-earth luminescent NCs.
authors: Hui Zeng, Sai Xu, Yuye Gu, You Li, Yuefeng Gao, Yichao Wang, Danyang Wu, Hongquan Yu, Baojiu Chen

10.1002/adfm.79167.title: Highly Permeable Polyamide Membranes Based on Hexafluoroisopropylidene Molecular Scaffold for Efficient Organic Solvent Nanofiltration
10.1002/adfm.79167.abstract: ABSTRACT Developing highly permeable polyamide (PA) thin-film composite (TFC) membranes is a critical pathway for advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) in industrial chemical separations. Herein, we reported a dual-regulation strategy utilizing a molecular scaffold to construct PA TFC membrane with enhanced solvent permeance. Acting as a “molecular scaffold”, the -C(CF 3 ) 2 - group of the 2,2-bis (4-aminophenyl) hexafluoropropane (BAFP) effectively modulates the packing behavior of PA chains through steric hindrance. Simultaneously, the fluorinated moieties reduce transport resistance by weakening solvent-membrane interactions. The prepared TFC-BAFP membrane exhibited an excellent methanol permeance of 20.3 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 , a 3.4-fold increase over conventional TFC membrane prepared with 4,4'-diaminodiphenylmethane (MDA). Furthermore, the enhanced rigidity of the BAFP monomer imparted great structural stability and solvent resistance, even under harsh chemical conditions. The TFC-BAFP membrane also demonstrated efficient sieving for photosensitizer/precursor mixture system and exhibited significantly higher concentration efficiency than the commercial oNF-2 OSN membrane. This work proposes a molecular engineering strategy for developing highly permeable polyamide OSN membranes by regulating monomer steric hindrance and surface properties, contributing to the advancement of sustainable separation technologies in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries.
authors: Yun Shen, Shideng Yuan, Fuping Han, Peijun Zheng, Xiang Ma, Xin Liu, Manshu Zhao, Yiming Li, Yue Chen, Zhining Wang

10.1002/adfm.79140.title: Hydrophobic Microenvironment Engineering of Single-Atom Nanozymes for Proteolysis-Driven Marine Antifouling
10.1002/adfm.79140.abstract: ABSTRACT Peptide bond hydrolysis is essential to biology, yet the kinetic stability of amide bonds makes efficient and selective artificial proteolysis challenging. Here, we report a biomimetic Cu single-atom nanozyme, Cu-NC HSA, that integrates mixed d 9 -d 10 Cu-N 4 active sites with a hydrogen-substituted graphdiyne overlayer for selective protein hydrolysis. Mechanistic studies indicate that the Cu centers provide balanced Lewis acidity for carbonyl polarization and water activation, while the hydrophobic H-GDY microenvironment preferentially enriches substrates bearing nonpolar residues. Under mild conditions (25°C, pH 6.0-10.0), Cu-NC HSA hydrolyzes bovine serum albumin with a marked preference for peptide bonds adjacent to hydrophobic residues (86%). Beyond catalysis, Cu-NC HSA shows potent antibiofilm activity, achieving biofilm removal in vitro and enabling sustained marine antifouling performance in a real marine environment. This work offers a multiscale biomimetic strategy for selective protein hydrolysis and marine antifouling applications.
authors: Wenhua Zheng, Sheng Zhao, Fanxiang Meng, Yudi Zhao, Shixia Bian, Zezheng Ye, Hongyu Lin, Wengang Liu, Ning Sui, Jun Deng, Zhiling Zhu

10.1002/adfm.79027.title: Switching Superconductivity with Uniaxial Strain in a high-Tc${\rm T}_{c}$ Cuprate Superconductor
10.1002/adfm.79027.abstract: ABSTRACT A hallmark of quantum materials is their strong response to external stimuli, which makes them attractive for technological applications. In particular, when modest perturbations can drive a system between two electronic states, this can be used in memory and switching device applications. Here, we show that the superconducting transition temperature, , in a copper oxide superconductor can be dramatically altered by applying compressive uniaxial strain. This sensitivity suggests a practical route to switching superconductivity on and off. Such control could be realized by integrating superconductors with piezoelectric substrates, providing a platform to engineer superconducting devices whose state is tuned simply by strain.
authors: Baizhi Gao, Qianli Ma, Bruce D. Gaulin, Young-June Kim

10.1002/adfm.79088.title: Transpiration-Driven Bionic Leaves With Conical Pores for Hyperspectral and Thermal Camouflage
10.1002/adfm.79088.abstract: ABSTRACT Camouflage materials that replicate leaf spectral signatures and surface temperature are urgently needed to counter hyperspectral and thermal infrared detection. However, current materials display slow moisture-exchange kinetics due to poor transpiration mimicry, causing hyperspectral and thermal infrared exposure. Herein, transpiration-driven bionic leaves based on conical-pore hydrogels are pioneered via acid-induced phase separation to accurately replicate spectral and thermal signatures of natural leaves. The constructed conical pores facilitate Laplace-pressure-driven directional liquid movement within the tapered pores and enhance water loading and mass transfer. Combined with hygroscopic salts and hydrophilic groups, the system achieves rapid moisture response and sustained water supply under fluctuating conditions. This transpiration-mimicking water regulation allows the bionic leaf to match natural leaves in spectral and thermal performance. The bionic leaf achieves spectral correlation coefficients of 0.983 in the visible-near-infrared band and 0.997 in the thermal infrared band, verifying outstanding dual-band camouflage performance. Moreover, the bionic and natural leaves display closely consistent emissive features and radiation temperatures, with deviations less than 0.007 and 0.98°C, respectively, to deliver effective thermal infrared concealment. This work establishes a general strategy for constructing bionic materials based on Laplace-pressure-driven water regulation, unlocking new opportunities for the design of advanced camouflage systems.
authors: Diandian Zhang, Yixin Fan, Linting Wei, Fangting Zheng, Ruitong Ge, Yanzhen He, Wen Zhou, Shaohai Fu

10.1002/adfm.79152.title: Giant Atomic Displacement Driven Reconstructive Molecular Martensitic Structural Phase Transition in 1D Hybrid Metal Halide Actuator
10.1002/adfm.79152.abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic molecular crystals driven by martensitic structural phase transitions can convert external stimuli into mechanical work, holding significant research importance in the fields of actuation and energy harvesting. However, the structural phase transition mechanisms in traditional martensitic actuators are primarily limited to small-amplitude atomic displacements or molecular motions, rarely involving the breaking and reforming of chemical bonds. Herein, we report a Z-type cyclic inorganic double-chain hybrid (BMPD) 8 Pb 11 Br 30 (BMPD = N -butyl- N -methyl-piperidinium). It undergoes an unprecedented reversible topological reconstruction that transforms the local face-sharing linkage of [PbBr 6 ] 4− octahedra into edge-sharing. Notably, the atomic displacement generated during the phase change exceeds 1.35 Å. This structural rearrangement induces interchain shearing and cooperative deflection of inorganic double chains, further triggering macroscopic deformation and fast (0.66 mm·s − 1 ) martensitic actuation behavior. Upon thermal stimulation, the crystal generates a kinetic energy of about 2.88 × 10 −10 J and a maximum thrust force of 3.97 × 10 −4 N. The corresponding average force density and work density are 6.39 × 10 6 N m −3 and 868.0 J m −3 , respectively. The actuator efficiency reaches 8.07 × 10 − 5 -2.63 × 10 − 4 . This work offers a promising strategy for the design of fast-responsive and high-efficiency molecular actuators.
authors: Chao-Yang Chai, Qiang-Qiang Bi, Cheng-Dong Liu, Zhao-Rui Hua, Shu-Yin Jia, Jia-Hang Wu, Fei-Yang Li, Shuo Tan, Zhong-Xia Wang, Wen Zhang

10.1002/adfm.78947.title: Noise-Driven Functionality in Neuromorphic Materials, Devices, and Systems
10.1002/adfm.78947.abstract: ABSTRACT Neuromorphic hardware turns the physical dynamics of functional materials into computation, enabling dense in-memory and probabilistic architectures beyond digital abstraction. Yet this advantage also makes neuromorphic systems highly sensitive to noise and variability, because analog device states directly encode synaptic weights, neuronal thresholds, membrane currents, and spike signals. While device-to-device variation, cycle-to-cycle variation, and drift have been widely discussed as critical non-idealities, temporal noise, particularly read-current fluctuations during sensing of analog states, has received less systematic attention. This review addresses this gap by positioning temporal noise within the broader landscape of device variability and by highlighting low-frequency noise spectroscopy as a mechanism-resolved tool for identifying fluctuation origins, spectral signatures, time scales, and computational consequences. We establish a framework that classifies neuromorphic noise according to its role: suppression, tolerance, and utilization: (1) noise suppression reduces intrinsic fluctuation sources to secure multilevel precision and computing accuracy; (2) noise tolerance maintains robust operation through device-to-system strategies; and (3) noise utilization transforms intrinsic stochasticity into primitives for stochastic neurons and synapses, entropy generation, probabilistic bits, Bayesian inference, and reinforcement learning. Across neuromorphic materials, devices, and systems, this review reframes temporal noise from a reliability-limiting imperfection into a hardware-native resource for adaptive neuromorphic intelligence.
authors: Jaehong Park, Youngmin Han, Jaechan Song, Youngchan Cho, Zhongyunshen Zhu, Hocheon Yoo, Wonjun Shin

10.1002/adfm.79054.title: Cation-Directed Solvent Inclusion in Zero-Dimensional Indium Halides for Tunable and Stimuli-Responsive Emission
10.1002/adfm.79054.abstract: ABSTRACT Solvent molecules incorporated within the crystal lattice of zero-dimensional (0D) metal halides play an important role in determining their structure and optical properties. However, achieving predictable control over solvent inclusion remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report five 0D indium halides, (TMPA) 2 InCl 5 , (Ch) 2 InCl 5 ·DMF (1·DMF), (Ch) 2 InCl 5 ·2H 2 O·MeOH (1·2H 2 O·MeOH), (Ch) 2 InCl 5 ·H 2 O·EtOH (1·H 2 O·EtOH) and (Ch) 2 InCl 5 ·H 2 O (1·H 2 O), synthesized using two structurally analogous organic cations: Ch + (choline), containing hydrogen-bonding functional groups (―OH), and TMPA + (trimethylpropylammonium) lacking hydrogen-bonding groups. Structural analysis reveals that the organic cation with an ―OH group can facilitate the incorporation of solvent molecules into the crystal lattice of 0D indium halides. These host materials are non-emissive, whereas Sb 3+ doping activates broadband self-trapped exciton (STE) emission. Among them, 1·2H 2 O·MeOH:Sb exhibits a single yellow STE emission band peaking at 603 nm, while 1·H 2 O·EtOH:Sb, 1·H 2 O:Sb and 1·DMF:Sb display excitation-dependent dual emission bands, consisting of a high-energy one in the 400-550 nm region and a low-energy band centered at 645, 660, and 675 nm, respectively. Excitingly, reversible transformation between yellow-emitting 1·2H 2 O·MeOH:Sb and orange-red-emitting 1·H 2 O:Sb can be induced through heating-cooling treatment and MeOH/H 2 O stimuli. This work provides new insights into the rational design of stimuli-responsive 0D metal halide luminescent materials.

10.1002/adfm.79123.title: Phase Diagram and Theoretical Calculation Guided Rational Design of Cu 6.26 Sn 5 /Sn Heterostructured Aerogel for Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
10.1002/adfm.79123.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesizing hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) from nitrite (NO 2 − ) promises a green alternative to the hazardous Raschig process, yet catalyst development is trapped in a persistent selectivity-activity dilemma. Excessively strong adsorption of intermediates on the catalyst drives the over-reduction of * NH 2 OH to ammonia, whereas overly weak adsorption depletes the interfacial reactant supply and yields to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, guided by binary phase diagrams and density functional theory calculations, we report a one-step co-reduction strategy for the general synthesis of 3D intermetallic/metal heterostructured aerogels with freely tunable components-bypassing the sacrificial templates required by conventional methods. The resultant aerogel comprises a porous Sn scaffold decorated with Cu 6.26 Sn 5 intermetallic nanoparticles that form stable heterointerfaces. With cyclohexanone trapping in 0.5 m Na 2 SO 4 , the Cu 10 Sn 90 heterostructured aerogel achieves a remarkable Faradaic efficiency of 79.7% and yield rate of 0.731 mmol h −1 cm −2 toward cyclohexanone oxime. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the Cu 6.26 Sn 5 phase accelerates interfacial NO 2 − accumulation and mass transport, whereas the Sn scaffold serves as the dominant active center to undergo the reduction of NO 2 − and boost * NH 2 OH desorption. This study delivers a novel material design strategy for heterostructured aerogels toward highly selective electroreduction of NO 2 − to NH 2 OH.

10.1002/adfm.79104.title: Suppression and Reemergence of Directional Transport across the Ferromagnetic Transition in SrRuO 3
10.1002/adfm.79104.abstract: ABSTRACT SrRuO 3 is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO 3 thin film on DyScO 3 , where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature T c ,on ≈ 165 K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below T c ,on , this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance ( MR ): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along below T 0 = 145 K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near , where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. These results establish ferromagnetic ordering as the primary driver of the observed directional magnetotransport in SrRuO 3 .

10.1002/adfm.79040.title: Sulfur Vacancies Enable Reversible NH 3 Chemisorption on Monolayer MoS 2 for Ultrasensitive Room Temperature Sensing
10.1002/adfm.79040.abstract: ABSTRACT Sensitive ammonia (NH 3 ) detection at room temperature (RT) is essential for environmental monitoring, industrial safety, and emerging energy technologies. However, developed semiconductor sensors often suffer from insufficient NH 3 response magnitude, slow response kinetics, and a requirement for elevated temperatures. In this work, we propose a controllable surface Sulfur-vacancy (V S ) induced physisorption to reversible RT-chemisorption transition for NH 3 on monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ). This transition facilitates the extensive formation of N─Mo bonds, narrows the band gap of MoS 2 substantially, and achieves highly sensitive NH 3 detection accordingly. Consequently, an optimized vacancy density of 8.0 at.% enables RT-NH 3 sensing with a theoretical detection limit of 2.2 ppb, a wide dynamic range up to 10000 ppm, a minimum response time less than 2 s, and a remarkable selectivity ratio of 12. Benefiting from large surface and enhanced charge transfer, our RT- NH 3 prototype portable detector can deliver a prominent response of 23.7 with response time of 12 s toward 50 ppm NH 3 , and reversible recovery under 40% relative humidity (RH). These results establish rational RT-chemisorption enabled molecular recognition as a route to superior performance RT-NH 3 sensing in two-dimensional monolayered materials.

10.1002/adfm.79001.title: Emergence of a Hexagonal Fe 2 S 2 Single Layer Without a Bulk Counterpart via Phase Transformation
10.1002/adfm.79001.abstract: ABSTRACT Two-dimensional materials can stabilize crystal structures that are absent from their bulk counterparts, offering opportunities for materials design. Here, we report the synthesis of a previously unknown hexagonal single layer with -CuI structure, a buckled layer of two vertically stacked FeS honeycomb lattices, realized by thermally induced transformation of single-layer mackinawite grown on graphene/Ir(111). In situ scanning tunneling microscopy and low-energy electron diffraction reveal a transition from a tetragonal to a hexagonal lattice accompanied by distinct morphological and electronic signatures. The hexagonal forms reproducibly upon annealing and represents a new structural motif within the Fe-S material family. First-principles calculations identify the -CuI structure as most consistent with experiment. The calculations suggest that on-site Coulomb interactions and magnetic order are relevant to understanding the stability of the new 2D Fe-S compound. The preferred nucleation of single-layer mackinawite, despite being energetically disfavored, is speculated to result from its low edge energy, analogous to the 3D case. Our results establish as a platform for exploring structural polymorphism in two dimensions and demonstrate that reduced dimensionality can stabilize crystal structures not accessible in bulk materials.

10.1002/adfm.79043.title: Synergizing Proton Transfer and Oxygen Activation via Brønsted/Lewis Acid-Site Regulation in K-Doped La 0.5 Sr 0.5-x K x Mn 0.9 Co 0.1 O 3-δ Air Electrode for Reversible Protonic Ceramic Electrochemical Cells
10.1002/adfm.79043.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient operation of reversible protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (R-PCECs) requires rapid oxygen-electrode kinetics in both fuel cell and electrolysis modes, which depend on the concerted coupling of oxygen activation and proton transfer at the surface of air electrode. Conventional compositional and defect regulation can enhance oxygen vacancies, electronic transport, and oxygen exchange, but rarely considers surface acid chemistry as a means of coordinating proton transfer with oxygen activation. Here, A-site K substitution within a Co-modified La0.5Sr 0.5-x K x Mn 0.9 Co 0.1 O 3-δ framework is used to bridge this gap by regulating Brønsted and Lewis acid sites responsible for proton transfer and oxygen activation, respectively. Coupled with modified metal-oxygen bonding and enhanced oxygen-defect chemistry, this coordinated surface environment facilitates proton-coupled-electron-transfer (PCET) processes and accelerates reversible reaction kinetics. Accordingly, the optimized electrode delivers a polarization resistance of 0.049 Ω cm 2 and a peak power density of 1.436 W cm −2 at 700°C, and reaches −2.19 A cm −2 at 1.3 V and 650°C in electrolysis mode under 20% H 2 O. These findings identify Brønsted-Lewis acid-site synergy as a useful basis for designing high-performance triple-conducting perovskite air electrodes for R-PCEC devices.

10.1002/adfm.79169.title: Hydrogen-Bonding/Steric-Effect Competition Drives Symmetry Differentiation Toward Antiferroelectric and Ferroelectric States in Homologous 1D Hybrid Lead Bromides
10.1002/adfm.79169.abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular hybrid materials often show competing dipole arrangements, making macroscopic polarity difficult to control. Parallel dipole ordering favors ferroelectricity, whereas antiparallel ordering can cancel macroscopic polarity and potentially give rise to antiferroelectric behavior. Herein, we employ stepwise N-ethylation as a molecular-design strategy to regulate interaction networks and symmetry evolution in a homologous series of 1D lead bromides. The structures evolve from chiral nonpolar (MTP)PbBr 3 ( 1 , MTP = thiomorpholinium , P 2 1 2 1 2 1 ) to centrosymmetric antiferroelectric (EtMTP)PbBr 3 ( 2 , EtMTP = N-ethylthiomorpholinium , Pbca ), and finally to polar ferroelectric (Et 2 MTP)PbBr 3 ( 3 , Et 2 MTP = N, N-diethylthiomorpholinium , P 3 c 1 ). Structural analyses show that ethyl substitution progressively weakens directional N─H···Br hydrogen bonding while increasing the steric demand of the organic cations, thereby shifting the balance between hydrogen bonding and steric effects. In 2 , antiparallel ordering of organic dipoles produces a compensated antipolar structure, while double P-E hysteresis loops confirm antiferroelectric behavior. In 3 , diethyl substitution removes the dipole-canceling packing mode and promotes parallel ordering, giving rise to macroscopic polarity. Compound 3 exhibits T c ≈ 400 K, P s ≈ 3.20 µC cm − 2 , and d 33 ≈ 15 pC N − 1 . This work demonstrates that hydrogen-bonding/steric-effect competition provides a molecular basis for regulating symmetry, dipole ordering, and multifunctionality in low-dimensional hybrid materials.

10.1002/adfm.79122.title: Charge-Regulating Two-Dimensional Interfacial Nanocoatings Enable Ultrahigh Discharge Energy Density in Layered Polymer Nanocomposite Dielectrics
10.1002/adfm.79122.abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer dielectric films are widely investigated for electrostatic energy storage in power electronics and pulsed-power technologies because of their high power density and rapid charge-discharge capability. However, under high electric fields, leakage conduction arising from electrode-induced charge injection and field-driven carrier transport limits the discharge energy density ( U e ) and charge-discharge efficiency ( η ). Herein, an interface-engineered layered polymer nanocomposite incorporating spatially differentiated two-dimensional nanocoatings is designed to regulate charge transport and improve breakdown resistance. Montmorillonite nanosheets (MMT NSs) are selectively assembled at the electrode-dielectric interfaces, whereas boron nitride nanosheets (BN NSs) are introduced between adjacent dielectric layers. The internal BN NSs interlayers confine carriers and impede through-thickness transport, while the external MMT NSs coatings promote lateral charge redistribution and reduce persistent electrode-side charge accumulation. This coordinated interfacial regulation suppresses leakage conduction, local electric-field intensification, and the development of electrical breakdown pathways. Consequently, the best-performing multilayer structure among the investigated configurations achieves a discharge energy density of ≈37.3 J cm −3 at 740 MV m −1 . It also maintains a variation in discharge energy density of less than 3% over 60 000 cycles at 200 MV m −1 . This design provides a framework for charge regulation in existing and emerging layered polymer nanocomposite dielectrics.

10.1002/adfm.77513.title: Optomechanical Microgripper Based on Dual-Mode Drive of Triazene Crystals
10.1002/adfm.77513.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of organic crystals capable of direct light to mechanical work conversion is essential for advancing soft micro robotics. In this work, we report a novel class of triazene based photomechanical crystals that achieve significant light driven effects by triggering irreversible chemical and physical processes. Specifically, the DMF solvate of BNE follows a path of lattice phase transition induced by the escape of solvent molecules-a physical process that is irreversible yet exhibits a rapid response. In contrast, DNE crystals undergo intramolecular photodecomposition upon irradiation, and this irreversible chemical process generates a high single use mechanical energy output, enough to drive a significant displacement of microspheres. These two crystals can be conceptualized as prototypes for an inherently functionalized light driven micro gripper. DNE is suitable for scenarios requiring high energy single triggers, while BNE is characterized by its rapid response. This study not only provides two high performance light driven materials but also reveals an effective strategy for tailoring irreversible photomechanical responses through crystal engineering of molecular packing. Our findings offer a new paradigm for the rational design of task oriented intelligent soft micro actuators, catering to needs ranging from high force single use triggers to rapid response systems.

10.1002/adfm.77306.title: Polyvinylpyrrolidone-Based Chemo-Mechanical Synergy Strategy Achieves Atomic-Scale Synchronous Removal of Co/Ti Interconnection Heterostructures
authors: Lifei Zhang, Zixin Gao, Xinchun Lu

10.1002/adfm.78078.title: Microscale Patterning of Ultrahigh-Viscosity Metallic-Polymer Composites via Embedded Droplet Writing
10.1002/adfm.78078.abstract: ABSTRACT The ability to digitally pattern metallic-polymer composites with microscale precision would substantially expand the functionality of soft materials by enabling spatially programmed magnetic, electrical, and thermal responses within compliant architectures. However, progress in this direction has been limited by the lack of manufacturing platforms capable of processing ultrahigh-viscosity, high-filler-loading pastes while maintaining microscale resolution and seamless integration with structural matrices. Here, we introduce a hybrid additive manufacturing platform that combines direct droplet writing with vat photopolymerization to fabricate heterogeneous soft structures incorporating ultrahigh-viscosity metallic-polymer composites. The hybrid platform enables deterministic deposition of composites with filler loadings up to 87 wt% (47 vol%) and viscosities approaching 1700 Pa·s, while integrating them into photopolymerized elastomer matrices with microscale precision. This capability spatially localizes magnetic composite domains within compliant polymers, effectively decoupling magnetic functionality from the structure's overall mechanical compliance. Leveraging this material's architecture, we demonstrate programmable magnetic soft actuators with tunable deformation, pressure-responsive magnetic microvalves exhibiting sequential shut-off behavior, and magnetically switchable adhesives capable of controlled pick-and-release operations. By enabling microscale patterning and multimaterial integration of ultrahigh-viscosity metallic composites, this strategy significantly broadens the design space for multifunctional soft materials with programmable, spatially resolved functionalities.

10.1002/adfm.77903.title: Coexistence of Real- and Momentum-Space Topology in Symmetry-Locked Bilayer Altermagnet
10.1002/adfm.77903.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of real-space topological spin textures and momentum-space topological electronic states within a single system remains challenging. However, the emergence of altermagnetism has changed this. Here, we introduce a symmetry-locked bilayer altermagnet that concurrently hosts d -wave altermagnetism, momentum-space topology, and stable antiskyrmions. In momentum-space, it enables strain-triggered transitions to an antiferromagnetic Weyl semimetal phase, where the Néel vector acts as a switch for spin-layer-polarized quantum anomalous Hall and Weyl states, alongside coupled topological states and valley polarization effects. In real-space, the formation of interlayer co-directional and locked in-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions facilitates the creation of coupled antiskyrmion pairs with compensated topological charges. This locking symmetry fully cancels the transverse Magnus forces, resulting in current-driven, strictly longitudinal motion of antiskyrmions without any Hall-like deflection. Our work establishes a symmetry-locked bilayer altermagnetic platform for dual-space topological magnetism and provides a theoretical route to suppressing the antiskyrmion Hall response in charge-neutral antiskyrmions, opening pathways toward low-power topological spintronics.

10.1002/adfm.78259.title: Hierarchical Bio-Composites With Nacre-Inspired Interfacial Design for Durable Multifunctionality and Upcyclable Sustainability
10.1002/adfm.78259.abstract: ABSTRACT Biobased polylactic acid composites show great potential as alternatives to petroleum-based polymer materials, but their practical use is limited by the difficulty of simultaneously achieving mechanical strength, service durability, and integrated functionality. To address this challenge, we developed a biomimetic interfacial engineering strategy inspired by nacre's rigid-inorganic/flexible-organic interfacial composition. The composite exhibits favorable mechanical strength (flexural strength increased by 3.8 times) and durability under harsh environments, and outstanding UV-blocking properties are imparted by the interior of the composite together with its biomimetic interfacial layer, effectively inhibiting the photodegradation of various water-soluble organic substances (degradation extent <6%). The composite also features ultrahigh solar absorption (>95%), enabling efficient outdoor deicing/snow removal and stable solar-driven desalination, combining high evaporation efficiency (>94%) with excellent cycling stability. More significantly, at the disposal stage, the porous and surface-functionalized residue can adsorb dyes and heavy-metal ions from water, supporting resource-oriented end-of-life utilization. The composite also shows antifungal rates exceeding 96%, long-term antifungal behavior, low toxicity in the tested aquatic plant system, and soil-burial degradation behavior. This work presents an interfacial-design route for high-strength, multifunctional, and recyclable bio-based composites for outdoor and water-treatment-related applications, which is anticipated to exhibit significant potential in sustainable polymer materials.

10.1002/adfm.78248.title: Multiple Hydrogen-Bonding Network Engineered Multi-Layered Polyurethane Aerogels for Absorption-Dominant Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
10.1002/adfm.78248.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid proliferation of 5G technologies and wearable electronics has intensified electromagnetic interference (EMI), posing a substantial challenge to device reliability and human health. Consequently, lightweight, flexible, high-performance, and multifunctional EMI shielding materials are urgently demanded. In this work, multi-hydrogen-bonded waterborne polyurethane (H-WPU) was synthesized via polycondensation and combined with MXene and MXene@CoFe 2 O 4 fillers. Using a layered freezing and freeze-drying strategy, (MXene@CoFe 2 O 4 /H-WPU, B)-(MXene/H-WPU, A)-(MXene@CoFe 2 O 4 /H-WPU) EMI shielding aerogels were fabricated. The densely crosslinked hydrogen-bond network reinforced the H-WPU and established strong interfacial interactions with MXene and MXene@CoFe 2 O 4 , thereby suppressing filler agglomeration, improving impedance matching, and facilitating the uniform distribution of conductive and magnetic loss pathways. As a result, the B-A-B aerogels achieved EMI shielding effectiveness of 81 and 83 dB in the X and Ku bands, respectively, with reflection coefficients as low as 0.14 and 0.11. Excellent absorption-dominant shielding performance was maintained over a wide range of incident angles. The aerogels also exhibited outstanding mechanical resilience, stable pressure sensing over 1000 loading-unloading cycles, low thermal conductivity (0.097 W·m −1 ·K −1 ), and robust infrared camouflage performance. This molecular engineering strategy provides a promising route toward next-generation lightweight, flexible, multifunctional EMI shielding materials integrating sensing and thermal management.

10.1002/adfm.77523.title: Integrating Structure-Dominated Shielding and Material-Dominated Absorption: A Highly Anisotropic Fabric for Adaptive EMI Protection
10.1002/adfm.77523.abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible textile platforms with tunable electromagnetic interference (EMI) attenuation capabilities hold considerable promise for scenarios with controlled polarization or field direction. Herein, a highly anisotropic plain-weave fabric is reported, in which conductive nanofiber-covered core-spun weft yarns prepared via conjugate electrospinning and subsequent surface functionalization are orthogonally interlaced with insulating cotton warp yarns. By introducing a pronounced conductivity contrast between the warp and weft directions, the polarization-dependent electromagnetic response of an anisotropic conductive network is engineered into a textile-compatible platform. Through simple in-plane rotation, the EMI shielding effectiveness can be reversibly tuned from approximately 0.7 dB when the incident electric field is aligned with the insulating warp yarns to 41.5 dB when it is parallel to the conductive weft yarns. Meanwhile, multiscale heterogeneous interfaces within the conductive weft yarns promote interfacial polarization, conductive loss, and multiple scattering, enabling a minimum reflection loss of −51.58 dB, an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.2 GHz covering the X-band, and a radar cross-section reduction of 20.5 dB m 2 . This strategy combines the tunable EMI response enabled by anisotropic textile architecture with microwave absorption induced by multiscale interfaces, providing a feasible pathway toward lightweight, flexible, breathable, and multifunctional electromagnetic regulation textiles for polarization- or direction-controlled applications.
